title: views returned COMPLETE with a blank public score - rot3 TTA is untested, not measured
description: 2026-08-17 slot 2. kneemri-views (the 0.919 pair under rot3 SpatialViews) ran CLEAN on the visible three studies - valid 3x13 submission.csv, 2/2 members fingerprint-checked, no traceback - and the submission reached SubmissionStatus.COMPLETE with an EMPTY publicScore. Every other arm that day scored within ~30-45 min; this one never did. rot3 is the only arm that triples decode, and it is the only thing that differed from the 0.919 pair (same kit 6f93554, same members, same overlap=False), so a hidden-rerun timeout is the reading that fits. CONSEQUENCE: the TTA cell in SUBMISSIONS.md is UNTESTED, not measured - do not read the blank as a bad score, and do not re-fire the same kernel unchanged, which would most likely buy another blank. NEXT: before spending a slot, price the hidden rerun. The visible set is 3 studies and the log says 'projecting 0.0h of 9h', so the visible projection cannot see a timeout that only the full set reaches. Either instrument the projection against the real study count or cut the TTA cost (2 views not 3, or views on one member rather than the pair).
notes: MECHANISM FOUND 2026-08-18. Not a timeout: the visible run costs 2.9 s/study, so ~11,000 studies fit inside the 9 h ceiling. It is an uncatchable OOM in SpatialViews._warp, which warped a whole chunk in one grid_sample and sits OUTSIDE Ensemble.forwarded's row-halving torch.OutOfMemoryError retry (that retry wraps the FORWARD). A 48-study chunk = 3,456 images at 336 px: float copy 1.56 GB + (n,h,w,2) grid 3.12 GB + output 1.56 GB ~= 6.2 GB transient on a 16 GB T4. The kernel dies, the hidden rerun writes no submission, the entry lands COMPLETE with a blank score. The visible set is 3 studies (216 images, 1/15 the memory), which is why every run looked clean and cost a slot anyway. FIX: WARP_CHUNK=512 with one affine_grid expanded across the batch, transient bounded at ~230 MB; test_warp_is_indifferent_to_the_chunk_size asserts bit-identity with the unchunked path. A views entry is eligible again only from a kit carrying this fix.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON BOARD EVIDENCE 2026-08-18/19. The WARP_CHUNK=512 fix shipped, and kneemri-topviews (submission 55607795, the 0.925 four under two rigid views 0,-6) returned a REAL public score of 0.925 instead of a blank. So the uncatchable OOM in SpatialViews._warp was the whole of it: a views entry now completes.

AND THE TTA CELL IS MEASURED, not untested: 0.925 with views against 0.925 without (kneemri-solotop, 55607054) on identical members. Two rigid views buy 0.000 over one. That is the answer the blank was withholding - it just is not the answer the arm was hoping for.

Remaining views caution, unchanged: rot3 (three views) was never re-fired and this reading is for two.

title: Is the reader wrong, or does the reporting radiologist disagree with the annotating one?
description:
THE PREMISE knee-dbw RESTS ON MAY BE PARTLY FALSE, and it is cheap to check before anything is built.

knee-dbw prices a replacement reader from one number: where the report reader says YES, the image annotator agrees only 65.3% of the time, so 'a third of the positives we train on are not positives'. That arithmetic assumes the 35% are READER errors - the reader misreading a report that does not assert the finding.

BUT A REPORT-READER'S OUTPUT AND AN IMAGE-ANNOTATOR'S LABEL DISAGREE FOR TWO REASONS, and only one of them is fixable by a better reader:
  (a) the reader misread the report      -> a better reader fixes it
  (b) the report ASSERTS the finding and the annotating radiologist, looking at the images, does not -> NO reader can fix it, because the reader read it correctly

TESTED 2026-08-14 (English reports only, 110 cells the reader called YES, crude regex):
  negation within +/-70 chars of the finding term:  21 wrong / 45 right   (32% wrong)
  plain mention, no negation nearby:                11 wrong / 29 right   (28% wrong)
  first-mention position in the report:             wrong 0.304 vs right 0.353

NEGATION PROXIMITY DOES NOT SEPARATE THE WRONG CALLS FROM THE RIGHT ONES, and neither does position. If the over-calling were a scoping bug - 'no ACL tear' read as a tear - the wrong calls should concentrate near negations. They do not, and 45 of 66 negation-adjacent YES calls are CORRECT, so the reader's negation handling is not obviously broken.

That is consistent with a meaningful share of the 35% being case (b): inter-reader disagreement between the doctor who wrote the report and the doctor who annotated the images. Which would mean the ceiling knee-dbw is priced against is not reachable by ANY reader.

LIMITS, and they are real: a +/-70 character window with an English stopword list is a crude negation detector, this is 110 cells in one language of seven, and 'no separation' is not proof of (b) - it is failure to find evidence of (a).

THE DECISIVE TEST IS CHEAP AND NEEDS A HUMAN, not a model: read ~20 English reports where the reader said YES and the annotator said NO, and mark for each whether the REPORT asserts the finding. If most do, knee-dbw's expected value drops sharply and the lever moves to the image side (knee-1nn). If most do not, knee-dbw stands as written and this bead closes.

DO NOT START BUILDING A READER BEFORE THIS IS ANSWERED - it is one sitting of reading against the expensive branch of the project.
acceptance_criteria: ~20 English false-positive cells classified by whether the report itself asserts the finding, and knee-dbw's expected value restated against that split.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-14, and it overturns knee-dbw's premise.

I read all 16 English cells where the reader said YES and the image annotator said ABSENT, and classified whether the REPORT asserts the finding. It does in about 15 of 16. Only one is a genuine reader error: 'No fracture is seen.' read as a fracture.

THE OTHERS SHARE ONE PATTERN - they are MILD:
  'Trace Baker's cyst'
  'Small joint effusion' / 'Some joint effusion'
  'in favor of grade 1 injury' / 'grade 2 injury'
  'Low-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament'
  'Degenerative signal throughout the lateral meniscus WITHOUT surfacing tear'
  'increased T2 hyperintense signal within the posterior horn' (signal, not a stated tear)

So the disagreement is a SEVERITY THRESHOLD between two doctors: the reporting radiologist writes down a trace or low-grade finding, and the annotating radiologist looking at the images does not count it as present. A better reader reproduces these YES calls, because the report does say them.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-dbw: its headline arithmetic - 'a third of the positives we train on are not positives, so removing them is the supervision' - does not hold as written. Most of that third is not reader error and no reader removes it. The expensive branch should not be started on this justification.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-mxj, and this is the payoff: 'ordinal severity is the supervision that compounds with the ranking term' is now MECHANISM-SUPPORTED rather than merely plausible. If the label noise is dominated by mild findings labelled present, then the fix is grading them rather than re-reading them - which is exactly what ordinal severity does, and what the calibrated-targets arm touched crudely for +0.0038 (levels mapped to measured agreement rates, no per-finding severity).

IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE DIRECTION. The reader over-calls 108 to 32 because it faithfully records mild findings; and Synovitis inverts (14 missed) because synovitis is often described obliquely - 'hypertrophy of the synovium', 'thickened synovial tissue' - which a rule engine misses while an annotator sees it on the image.

LIMITS, stated plainly: 16 cells of 108, English only, and the classification is my own judgement of whether a sentence asserts a finding, not a radiologist's. The pattern is strong and consistent, but a second reading by the owner is cheap and would settle it. What is NOT in doubt is the single clear negation miss, which is 1 in 16 rather than the dominant failure mode.
close_reason: Answered the day it was filed. Read all 16 English cells where the reader says YES and the annotator says absent: the report ASSERTS the finding in about 15 of 16 (trace, small, low-grade, grade-1, 'degenerative signal without surfacing tear'), and only one is a real reader error. So the disagreement is a severity threshold between the reporting and annotating radiologists, not a reading failure. Recorded on the bead, on knee-dbw (downgraded P0->P2 as a result), and on knee-mxj, which it promotes.

title: The physical crop is centred on the image centre, not on the knee
description:
SlotReader._crop computes centre_y, centre_x = height // 2, width // 2 and crops 130 mm about that point. It assumes the joint sits in the middle of the acquisition.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, 60 studies, sagittal middle slice, tissue centroid against the image centre, converted to mm by the header's pixel spacing:
  |dy| median 6.9 mm, p90 18.0, max 25.0
  |dx| median 6.4 mm, p90 18.8, max 32.5
  field of view median 160 mm, so the 130 mm crop leaves only 15 mm of margin per side
  10 of 60 studies sit more than 20 mm off centre

So for roughly the worst tenth of studies the crop cuts into the joint on one side, and WHICH side depends on positioning - which is a mechanism for a medial/lateral asymmetry that has nothing to do with the laterality flip (knee-yrg refuted the flip; this is a different candidate for the same asymmetry).

MODEST ON ITS OWN, and filed separately from the multi-scale bead deliberately: with 15 mm of margin and a median 7 mm offset most studies are fine, so this is a correctness fix rather than a lever. It becomes LOAD-BEARING the moment the crop gets tighter - an 80 mm crop has no margin to absorb an 18 mm error, so centring must land before or with any tighter crop.

LIMIT: the tissue centroid of a whole leg cross-section is a crude joint locator, and 60 studies is a sample. It bounds the problem rather than solving it; a proper locator would use the intercondylar geometry.
acceptance_criteria: A crop centred on a derived joint centre, with the offset distribution re-measured after.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-15 (knee-c6w, crop_coverage, 1848 series from 400 studies of 4407): tissue centre retains MORE tissue at both extents, paired bootstrap excludes zero -- +0.0294 [+0.0276,+0.0312] at 130mm, +0.0233 [+0.0215,+0.0251] at 80mm. Real, knob-sized, and its TAIL is worse (worst-series 0.0929 vs image 0.1423 at 80mm: an Otsu mass centroid gets dragged by coil/fat/far-limb). Verdict: NOT promoted -- 2-3pp of retained tissue does not pay for a 99GB cache rebuild + refit of every member. Default stays 'image'. Strategy stays in-code opt-in at zero cost. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-15_crop_centre_coverage.md
close_reason: Closed

title: Multi-scale reading: the twelve findings do not want the same field of view
description:
THE DESIGN CLAIM: one physical crop cannot serve twelve findings, and our own per-label numbers say which way each one wants to go.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND (knee-dtk, measured against radiologist annotations):
  the model BEATS its own labels on the DIFFUSE findings - Effusion +0.13, Contusion +0.10, Synovitis, Medial OA, Fracture, Baker's
  the model LOSES badly on the SMALL, THIN ones - Lateral Meniscus -0.19, ACL -0.12, MCL -0.10, Medial Meniscus -0.09
That split is by structure SIZE, not by label quality.

THE GEOMETRY, measured 2026-08-14 on 60 studies (sagittal mid-slice, tissue centroid, pixel spacing from the header):
  field of view median 160 mm; our crop is 130 mm, so it removes only 19% of the linear extent and 34% of the area
  at 336 px that is 0.387 mm/px, and a meniscal tear is 1-2 mm - three to five pixels, and DINOv2 patches at 14 px, so a tear is a FRACTION OF ONE TOKEN
  an 80 mm joint-centred crop at the same 336 px is 0.238 mm/px - 1.6x finer for IDENTICAL compute, purely by not spending pixels on cortex, fat and air

BOTH DIRECTIONS HAVE ALREADY PAID SEPARATELY, which is the argument for combining them rather than choosing:
  res392 (finer) is our best single member ever at 0.8523
  whole_stack (more context) is the biggest single arm at +0.0147
A single scale must trade one against the other; two scales need not.

THE DESIGN: read each slot at TWO physical extents - a context view at 130 mm and a detail view at ~70-80 mm centred on the joint - and let the existing slot attention pool over scale as well as sequence. The architecture already attends over slots, so scale enters as another slot axis rather than as a new mechanism.

THE CHEAP GATE BEFORE THE EXPENSIVE COMMIT: multi-scale doubles tokens per slot and needs a cache rebuild, which invalidates 99 GB and every member fitted on it. Do NOT start there. Train ONE arm at a single tighter crop (80 mm, 336 px) and read the PER-LABEL deltas. The design predicts a specific pattern: the small-structure findings improve and the diffuse ones (Baker's is posterior, effusion spreads) degrade. If both move as predicted, multi-scale is worth the rebuild. If the small structures do not improve, resolution was not the mechanism and this whole line dies for one arm's cost.

SEPARATE, SMALLER DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY (own bead knee-9xe): the crop is centred on the IMAGE centre, not the knee.
design: Scale as an extra slot axis, so slot attention pools over it and no new pooling mechanism is introduced. Gate with a single 80mm arm read per-label before any cache rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: A per-label profile from an 80mm arm showing small structures up and diffuse findings down; only then the multi-scale build.
notes:
GATED AND NOT EARNED, 2026-08-16. crop80_tissue ran; matched-epoch per-label read (both arms, fold 0, epoch 7) is in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-16_crop80_resolution_gate.md.

The diffuse half of the prediction landed hard - Baker's -0.028, Synovitis -0.019, Effusion -0.015, all past the 0.0053 floor, and mechanically obvious (a 40mm half-extent cuts the popliteal fossa out of the image). The small-structure half, which is the half this build depends on, did NOT: ACL -0.004, MCL -0.003, and Medial Meniscus -0.012 - the largest small-structure move, with the wrong sign. Only Fracture rose (+0.019), the finding with the worst label agreement.

Multiscale keeps the wide slots, so it would not repeat the diffuse losses; its value is exactly what the tight slots buy, which this arm measures as Fracture alone, about +0.0016 spread over twelve labels. Against a 1.5% bar and a 71.6 GB cache that must build alone, it does not earn the slot.

NOT ruled out: resolution at CONSTANT field of view (res392, our best member at 0.8523, is that intervention and it pays); a fracture-specific tight reader; anything about centring, which this arm moved together with the crop.
close_reason: Gated and declined for one arm's cost. crop80_tissue (80mm @336px, 0.238mm/px) was the single-arm proxy for the multi-scale build. At matched epoch 7 on the same fold-0 holdout the DIFFUSE half of the prediction confirmed decisively (Baker's -0.028, Synovitis -0.019, Effusion -0.015) and the SMALL-STRUCTURE half — the half the build depends on — did not appear: Medial Meniscus -0.012 (wrong sign, largest small-structure move), ACL -0.004, MCL -0.003, only Fracture +0.019. Multi-scale ADDS tight slots to the wide ones, so its value is exactly what the tight slots buy: ~+0.0016 over twelve labels, against a 1.5% bar, for a 71.6 GB cache and a training slot. Full table and the three explicit 'does NOT rule out' items in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-16_crop80_resolution_gate.md

title: A full-corpus, label-free ruler was sitting inside the published checkpoints
description:
THE PUBLISHED 20 CARRY THEIR OWN OUT-OF-FOLD PREDICTIONS, and nothing here used them.

STRUCTURE, measured 2026-08-14 across all 20 downloaded checkpoints:
  4 seeds {2026, 7717, 20260808, 31337} x 5 folds, each fold scored by exactly one member per seed
  the 5 oof id-sets are DISJOINT and their union is 4,407 of 4,407 studies - an exact partition
  so every study in the corpus has 4 held-out predictions from models that did not train on it

WHY THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING FOUND TODAY: our ruler is one fold - 881 studies, 62 Fracture positives, a Hanley-McNeil sampling floor of 0.0053 that has defined what counts as a result for this entire project. This ruler is the whole corpus: 5x the studies, so a floor near 0.0024. Every question that is ARITHMETIC OVER MEMBER PREDICTIONS can be asked at more than twice the resolution, on a CPU, with no labels beyond the ones we already have and no GPU at all.

ALSO: config['fold'] is -1 on all twenty and is a STALE CLI DEFAULT, not the truth - the real fold is identifiable only from the oof id-set. Anything that trusted that field was reading a lie. The '20 members = 5 folds x 4 seeds' manifest is CONFIRMED by the id-sets.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO: it holds only THEIR members, so ours-vs-theirs still belongs on the shared fold-0 holdout. This ruler answers questions about COMBINING, not about whose weights are better.

FIRST USE, already run: the per-label combine curve (knee-6c5) on 4 seed-twins over 4,407 studies. See that bead.
acceptance_criteria: The ruler is used to decide at least one question that the 881-study holdout could not resolve.
close_reason: The ruler exists, is committed as OutOfFoldOracle.corpus with tests, and was used four times the day it was found: the per-label corpus profile, the laterality split that refuted the flip, the label/model bottleneck split, and the ordinal-severity gate that 11 of 11 findings passed. Acceptance was 'used to decide at least one question the 881-study holdout could not resolve' - met several times over. Written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_the-ruler-was-five-times-too-small.md.

title: A v3 member's weights do not load against a v3 backbone rebuilt at inference: 178 unexpected keys
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 from a kernel own traceback, at no cost in slots - the interactive run failed before any submission.

    RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict for StudyModel:
      Unexpected key(s): backbone.model.layer.0.norm1.weight,
      backbone.model.layer.0.attention.k_proj.base.weight, ... (178 keys, layers 0-6)

NO MISSING KEYS, only unexpected ones, all under backbone.model.layer. StudyModel.load_trained merges the checkpoint over the model own state, so "missing" cannot be reported and the signal is the extras: the CHECKPOINT nests the encoder one level deeper (backbone.model....) than the model rebuilt here does. The .base/.down/.up triples are the LoRA wrappers, and those ARE applied - member.lora_rank is 8 in the manifest and members.py:404 calls low_rank before loading - so the adapters are not the problem. The nesting is.

THIS CORRECTS WHAT I CLAIMED AN HOUR EARLIER. I said wiring v3 through to a submission was "one line of dataset_sources" and that Encoder.locates had already done the hard part. Mounting dinov3-hf was NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: with the mount in place, the member reaches its weights and fails on layout instead. knee-98j was a real task, not one I was declining.

A SECOND DEFECT, found in the same place: Member.pixel_group keys on config img (336 for this member, the CACHE it was built from) and not on read_size (224, what it actually READS). So this member joins the 336 decode group and is then handed 336 px images for a model fitted at 224. Whether StudyModel resizes internally or not, those are not the pixels it was fitted on, and the witness is the thing to ask.

NEXT STEP, and it needs no GPU: load the checkpoint and the freshly built v3 model side by side on CPU and diff their key sets. The answer is one rename or one wrapper, and the traceback already names both halves.

MEANWHILE the fusion kernel excludes v3 again, for this reason, because including an unloadable member costs the entire entry.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14: THE "SECOND DEFECT" IN THIS BEAD IS NOT A DEFECT, and I withdraw it.

I wrote that Member.pixel_group keys on config img (336) rather than read_size (224), so the v3 member joins a decode it cannot use. Checked instead of asserted: model.py:220-224 resizes the decoded images to img_size inside slot_features whenever they differ. The member was FITTED by reading a 336 px cache and resampling to 224 - train_size=224 with img=336 is exactly that - so inference doing the same is not a mismatch, it is the same operation.

pixel_group keying on img is therefore CORRECT: img names the cache a member was fitted from, and read_size is applied identically on top of it in training and at inference. One decode per img value is the right granularity, and the v3 member belongs in the 336 group.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE is the first half, which is the whole bug: the checkpoint nests the encoder one level deeper than the model rebuilt on Kaggle, because we train under transformers 5.15.0 and the image ships 5.0.0. The kit now carries transformers 5.15.0 plus safetensors 0.8.0 (the image has 0.7.0 and transformers refuses to import against it), and kneemri-loadcheck is the kernel that proves it without spending a slot.
close_reason:
SOLVED AND VERIFIED ON THE RUNTIME 2026-08-14, at no cost in slots.

CAUSE: we train under transformers 5.15.0 and Kaggle's image ships 5.0.0, whose DINOv3 class nests the encoder one level shallower. Identical weights and identical config therefore build a different key set, and the load failed with 178 unexpected keys under backbone.model.layer. The mount was right, the LoRA rank was right, the checkpoint was right - only the class differed.

FIX: the kit now ships transformers 5.15.0 plus safetensors 0.8.0 (the image carries 0.7.0 and transformers refuses to import against it - found by the load check, not by a submission).

VERIFIED: kneemri-loadcheck on a real T4 reports '6 members, 0 failed', including lora_r8_v3small_224 loading AND completing a forward pass. DINOv3 is genuinely wired through for the first time.

WHAT I GOT WRONG ALONG THE WAY, recorded because it is the reusable part: I twice dropped the v3 member from a kernel and wrote 'wiring v3 through is still open work' as though that were a reason. It was a task I was declining. Encoder.locates had already done the hard part and the missing piece was one line of dataset_sources - and then, when that was not enough, one wheel. Excluding a member is always faster than making it work, which is exactly why it should be suspected.

title: Three submissions threw exceptions: one cause found and fixed, the rest unresolved
description:
THREE ENTRIES RETURNED "Notebook Threw Exception" on 2026-08-13/14: kneemri-trained v6, kneemri-efficient v2, kneemri-fusion v4. All three ran on kits carrying code written that day; every entry on the kit before it scored.

WHAT IS SOLVED: fusion. Its v3 member could not load because we train under transformers 5.15.0 while Kaggle ships 5.0.0, whose DINOv3 class nests the encoder differently (knee-c7q, closed). The kit now ships transformers 5.15.0 and safetensors 0.8.0, and a real T4 confirms all six members load and forward.

WHAT IS NOT SOLVED: trained v6 and efficient v2. Neither carried a v3 member. No confirmed cause.

THREE OF MY OWN EXPLANATIONS DID NOT SURVIVE CONTACT, and I called each one "refuted" far too fast on a single run:
  - "392 px members blow the T4 because the budget counts images, not tokens" - fusion failed too and carried no 392 px member. The token-aware budget is KEPT anyway: a transformer costs per token and 864 was measured at 336 px, so it is right regardless of whether it was this bug.
  - "a T4 cannot run bf16 autocast" - the card reports capability (7, 5) and is_bf16_supported() True, and every member forwards.
  - "bf16 emulation is fatally slow" - measured on the T4: bf16 members forward about 15% slower than fp16, not orders of magnitude.
The bf16 guard is kept and SHARPENED rather than deleted: supported is not native, Turing emulates, so it now asks capability >= (8, 0) and serves fp16 below it. Every entry that ever scored ran fp16.

THE STRUCTURAL FAULT, which is the part that actually cost the slots: any single failure took the whole run down, and a run that fails writes no submission at all. That is now fixed - a member that will not load is dropped with its traceback, a member that dies mid-prediction is dropped from that point, and only ALL of them failing raises. An ensemble does not need every part.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: the chunk-shape memory check (48 studies at each member cache size, the same call a submission makes) currently running in kneemri-loadcheck, or a submission that executes. Nothing here is confirmed until one of those lands.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16 on the condition this bead itself named — 'a submission that executes'. Four have, on kits carrying the drop-a-failing-member fix: fusion 0.895 (08-14), fusion 0.898 (08-15), trained v8 0.911 and efficient v4 0.919 (08-16 05:05). No entry has thrown since the structural fix; the exception mode that cost three slots is gone. The unexplained trained-v6 / efficient-v2 causes stay UNEXPLAINED rather than refuted — what changed is that a single member's failure can no longer take the entry down, so the cause no longer costs a slot to survive. Host RAM during decode remains untested (knee-b6p's last open thread); re-file if an entry ever throws again.
close_reason: Closed

title: attribution windowed every member by three, whatever it was fitted as
description:
THE TENTH INSTANCE of the shape, and it was in the tool that PUBLISHES findings rather than one that trains.

kneemri/attribution.py rebuilt the model correctly - HoldoutPredictions.load reads slice_pooling, anatomical_prior and now the encoder layer - and then decided how to READ it from four constants:
    StudyCache(root.processed(), slices=arguments.slices)   default 336 px, ignoring the member's img
    starts = range(arguments.slices - GROUP + 1)            three-slice windows, ignoring whole_stack
    Window(..., width=GROUP, ...) inside Attribution.score  the width again, from a constant
    len(SLOTS)                                              the canonical six, ignoring the scheme
So a whole-stack member was occluded THREE SLICES AT A TIME, a 448-cache member (res392, intensity392) could not be read at all, and an extended-scheme member would have been rebuilt with the wrong slot count.

member_curve HAD THE IDENTICAL DEFECT AND WAS FIXED. Its comment says so verbatim: 'This CLI loaded a single 336 px cache, passed IMAGE_SIZE as the read size for every member, and windowed by GROUP whatever the member was'. The fix was applied to one of the two analysis CLIs and not the other.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT INVALIDATE. knee-am4 (border-only 0.8006 against 0.8448) and knee-ghd (depth spread 0.0356) were measured on base+ranking, a WINDOWED member from before whole-stack landed - so three-slice windows were correct for it and those numbers stand. What was broken is every future use: knee-ghd's remaining action is to re-measure the depth profile PER LABEL, which would run on a whole-stack member and would have been silently wrong.

FIXED: main builds the reading from Member.from_checkpoint and Member.window, and Holdout now carries the whole Window rather than starts and size as loose fields - so the width can no longer be supplied from somewhere else. That is the structural half: the constant is not merely replaced, it has nowhere to be passed from.
close_reason: FIXED and structurally, not by swapping a constant. main builds the reading from Member.from_checkpoint and Member.window, and Holdout now carries the whole Window instead of starts and size as loose fields - so the width has nowhere to be passed from. Gates green. The findings already drawn from it stand: knee-am4 and knee-ghd were measured on base+ranking, a windowed member, for which three-slice windows were correct.

title: A git push can kill a running arm: uv re-syncs .venv under the trainer
description:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-13. lora_r8_small_336 died mid-epoch-4 with trainer exit 127 and no process left. Timeline:

  11:28:04  pyproject.toml edited (a pyrefly exclude, added and reverted)
  14:03:47  git push - the pre-push hook runs uv run pytest
  14:05:30  uv.lock REWRITTEN
  ~14:05    the trainer dies, exit 127, mid epoch 4

A stale pyproject makes the next uv run re-resolve and re-sync the environment. Rewriting site-packages under a running interpreter kills it.

run_snapshot EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THIS CLASS AND DOES NOT COVER IT. It copies kneemri/ and core/ so an edit cannot reach a running arm - the source is protected, the ENVIRONMENT is not. Every arm runs uv run --project REPO, so every arm shares the one .venv that any gate, test or push can re-sync.

IT IS NOT EVERY PUSH: calibrated_targets survived several. The trigger is a STALE lockfile - edit pyproject.toml, and the next uv invocation syncs. Today that was me editing pyproject at 11:28 and pushing at 14:03.

THIS MAY BE THE UNEXPLAINED LOSS IN knee-7gr. Arm U died at epoch 7 of 24 and its cause was recorded as 'unknown and will stay unknown' because the traceback was discarded. A killed interpreter mid-run is exactly that shape.

MITIGATIONS, none yet verified:
  - UV_FROZEN=1 or uv run --no-sync while an arm is training, so a gate cannot re-resolve.
  - Do not edit pyproject.toml while an arm runs; if it must be edited, expect the next uv command to sync.
  - Or give arms their own venv, which is the only one that removes the shared resource entirely.
acceptance_criteria: An arm survives a full gate run and a git push while training.
close_reason: FIXED: arms run uv run --no-sync, verified to import torch and kneemri without resolving. run_snapshot protected the SOURCE from mid-run edits and left the ENVIRONMENT shared; this closes the other half. The arm relaunched under it survived a full pre-push hook run that had killed its predecessor.

title: LoRA was training the embeddings, norms and LayerScale gammas at the adapter rate
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by checking the plumbing before believing a bad result, exactly as the working rule says.

THE SYMPTOM: v3+LoRA at 224 px sat at 0.6867 after four epochs against fine-tuned v3's 0.8057, with the loss nearly flat - 1.2635 to 1.2343, where the control fell to 0.90 by epoch 3. That reads as 'rank 8 underfits', which is the refutation the arm was designed to accept.

THE CAUSE: LoRALinear freezes the nn.Linear it wraps and NOTHING ELSE. Everything in the backbone that is not an nn.Linear therefore stayed trainable and landed in the optimiser's backbone group at the ADAPTER rate of 5e-4 - sixty times the fine-tuning rate. Measured on DINOv2-small:
    adapters                              663,552
    NON-adapter still trainable           781,440  across 79 tensors
      embeddings.position_embeddings      526,080
      embeddings.patch_embeddings.proj    225,792
      every norm1/norm2 weight and bias
      every layer_scale lambda1
More than half of what was being optimised was not an adapter. Training position embeddings and the patch projection at 5e-4 is not low-rank adaptation of a frozen encoder, it is a wrecking ball through the representation - and on DINOv3 it hits precisely the LayerScale gammas the arm hypothesised were fragile.

THE VALIDATION THAT MISSED IT LOOKED LIKE IT PASSED. 663,552 + 781,440 = 1,444,992, and the arm header quoted '1.44M trainable parameters against DINOv2-small's 22.7M (6.4%)' as proof the method was wired correctly. Counting a total without asking WHICH parameters is how a bug reports the expected number.

THE UNIT TEST MISSED IT FOR THE SAME REASON: the stand-in backbone was made only of Linears, so there were no non-Linear parameters for the leak to leak, and 'every base weight and bias stays frozen' passed happily.

FIXED: low_rank freezes the whole backbone before wrapping. Verified 663,552 trainable, zero non-adapter. The stand-in now carries a position embedding and a layer scale, and the test asserts every trainable name is an adapter.

EVERY LoRA RESULT SO FAR IS VOID - both arms were running a method that was not LoRA.
acceptance_criteria: v2 and v3 LoRA arms re-run under the fix, and read against their controls.
close_reason: FIXED: low_rank freezes the whole backbone before wrapping. Verified 663,552 adapter parameters trainable, ZERO non-adapter, optimiser group matching exactly. Confirmed on the metric too - the same arm went from 0.7012/0.6739/0.6820 with a flat loss to 0.7276/0.7728/0.7880 with the loss falling, and finished at 0.8217 against fine-tuned v3's 0.8057.

title: The AUC broke ties by STUDY ORDER: every ensemble number in the ledger is affected
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by a unit test written for something else. LabelScores.area_under_curve computed Mann-Whitney U from argsort().argsort() + 1 - ORDINAL ranks. Tied predictions are then ordered by their POSITION IN THE ARRAY, so a tie is settled by study order.

A CONSTANT PREDICTOR - no information whatsoever - scored 1.0 when the positives happened to sit late in the corpus, and 0.0 when they sat early. It must score 0.5. Fixed to midranks; all four cases now correct, including a partial tie at the analytic (2*3 + 0.5*3)/9 = 0.8333.

SINGLE-MEMBER NUMBERS NEVER MOVED. Raw sigmoids are float64 and effectively never tie, so every per-member holdout score in the ledger stands.

ENSEMBLE NUMBERS DID. Ensemble.combine maps each member onto k/(n-1) and averages, which produces exact ties by construction. Simulated over 881 studies:
    2 members   181 studies tied  20.5%
    3 members   164              18.6%
    5 members   127              14.4%
   11 members    65               7.4%
So roughly a fifth of the holdout had its ensemble ranking decided by corpus order, and every subset score member_curve has ever reported was computed that way - including the 0.8601 five-member peak that shaped the plan, and today's 0.8515 two-member number.

DIRECTION: study order is arbitrary with respect to the labels, so this is NOISE rather than bias - it does not systematically inflate or deflate. What it corrupts is the RANKING of subsets against each other, which is the single thing member_curve exists to produce. A curve that picks the wrong subset picks the wrong submission.

WHAT NEEDS REDOING: any ensemble comparison whose decision mattered. The diversity curve has not been run since, so nothing is currently being acted on - but the 0.8601 figure should not be quoted again until it is recomputed.
acceptance_criteria: The diversity curve re-run under midranks, and the 0.8601 peak either reproduced or replaced.
close_reason: FIXED: midranks. A constant predictor now scores 0.5 under both label orders and a partial tie lands on the analytic 0.8333. Single-member numbers never moved (float64 sigmoids do not tie); ensemble numbers did, and the diversity curve is the one thing that needs recomputing - it has not been re-run since, so nothing is currently acting on a corrupted ranking.

title: Whole-stack members ship with ZERO test-time augmentation, having replaced a measured +0.0156
description:
THE CHAIN, each link verified in code or measurement today.

1. A whole-stack member gets ONE centred window. Member.window: 'its slot embedding is the elementwise maximum over the whole stack, so there is nothing to overlap and nothing to average.' That reasoning is correct for the SLICE axis - the max already spans every slice - so window TTA is structurally unavailable to these members, not merely switched off.

2. Windowed members got +0.0156 from overlap TTA. Measured (knee-559) across seven checkpoints holding both numbers: min +0.0127, max +0.0172, near-uniform.

3. SpatialViews is IMPLEMENTED AND PASSED BY NOBODY. Ensemble takes views=None (ensemble.py:66) and falls back to identity-only at line 174. grep over the whole tree: the only references are that parameter, that fallback, and the import. It is deterministic by design, and its defaults (rotations 0/-6/+6, no shift) sit inside the training augmentation's own widths, with the reason written down.

4. THEREFORE our current members deploy with NO test-time augmentation at all, where the members that scored our best own LB had +1.6% of it.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS A RESULT WE LEFT UNEXPLAINED. Three whole-stack members scored LB 0.882 while five older windowed members scored 0.888, despite the whole-stack members being +0.0147 better on the local ruler. Local ranking is measured under the MIDDLE window, which is what a whole-stack member actually deploys - but the windowed members deployed with +0.0156 the local number never showed. The two effects are the same size and opposite in sign.

WHY IT CLEARS THE BAR: ~1.5% is the significance threshold and this is the size of the thing we gave away. It needs NO TRAINING - it is an inference-time change over members already on disk, testable offline on the fold-0 holdout for the cost of three forward passes per member.
design: Pass SpatialViews() to Ensemble in the submission path and in member_curve/HoldoutPredictions so the offline ruler measures what deployment does. Cost is len(degrees) x len(shifts) = 3 forwards. Measure on the holdout first: if rotation TTA does not reproduce something like the +0.0156 that window TTA gave, the analogy is wrong and this stops there.
acceptance_criteria: A whole-stack member's holdout AUC with SpatialViews() against the same member without it, on fold 0. Then the same on the diversity curve's winning subset before any submission.
notes:
PROCESS FAILURE, recorded 2026-08-13. This bead should never have been filed as a P0, and experiments/README.md said so before I wrote it.

That file already carried the measurement, on five members rather than my two:
    lr5x_d6    windowed     0.8323 -> 0.8475 with overlap TTA   +0.0152
    max12      windowed     0.8310 -> 0.8451                    +0.0141
    large_deep windowed     0.8304 -> 0.8450                    +0.0146
    wsfold0_e6 whole-stack  0.8457 -> 0.8457                    0.0000
    slices16   whole-stack  0.8452 -> 0.8452                    0.0000
and the conclusion in prose: 'the windowed lift and whole-stack's training-time advantage are the same
thing bought twice, and they do not compose'.

That is exactly what I filed as a discovery and then 'corrected' after measuring. I audited the beads and not the ledger, and the ledger held the answer. The rule to take from it: an audit reads what already EXISTS - the actual files - and experiments/README.md is one of them.

WHAT TODAY ACTUALLY ADDED, and it is not nothing: the README measures WINDOW TTA on whole-stack members (0.0000 by construction, one window). It says nothing about ROTATION TTA, which is a different axis and had never been run. That measured +0.0003 to +0.0009 - so SpatialViews, implemented and passed by nobody, is now known to be worth approximately nothing here rather than merely unused. The bead's conclusion was right; its novelty was not.

ALSO IN THAT SECTION AND NOT IN ANY BEAD: where both members get their own best reading, lr5x_d6 (0.8475) EDGES wsfold0_e6 (0.8457). Whole-stack's headline +0.0147 was measured against a control scored without the TTA that control gets at inference. res392 at 0.8523 is untouched by this, because no TTA is available to it either.
close_reason: Refuted by its own falsifier. Rotation TTA buys +0.0003 to +0.0009 against the +0.0156 predicted from the window-TTA analogy. The analogy was wrong: window TTA averaged over slice DEPTHS, which a whole-stack member already integrates through its max - so whole-stack absorbed that gain rather than giving it up.

title: Every bf16 member was served in fp16: the inference autocast had no dtype
description:
Ensemble.predict_member ran torch.autocast('cuda', enabled=...) with NO dtype. On cuda that defaults to float16, while the trainer carries it per-run as self.autocast_dtype - bfloat16 under --bf16. So every bf16-trained member was served in arithmetic it was never fitted under.

config['bf16'] has been recorded in every checkpoint since the flag landed, with a comment saying 'bf16 and fp16 are different arithmetic'. Written faithfully, read by nobody. EIGHTH instance in this repo of a value travelling in a config while its consumer reads a constant.

NOT ONLY PRECISION. bfloat16 carries float32's exponent range and float16 does not, so an activation a bf16-trained model produces comfortably can overflow to inf under fp16 - on the T4 the kernel submits from, where there is no second chance.
design: Member.precision reads config['bf16'] and returns torch.bfloat16 or torch.float16, defaulting to float16 which is what every member predating the flag genuinely used. predict_member passes dtype=member.precision.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on 2026-08-13 by witness_check across four members: 4 ok, 0 refused, and a deliberately flipped manifest refused at 0.407 against 0.00391.

title: torch.compile renamed every key: five members on disk are unloadable
description:
compile_encoder did self.backbone = torch.compile(self.backbone). The rebinding replaces the attribute with an OptimizedModule holding the real module as _orig_mod, and that name lands in every state-dict key: a compiled run saved backbone._orig_mod.embeddings.cls_token, which load_state_dict refuses as an unexpected key.

MEASURED, keys carrying _orig_mod out of the total:
  sliceattn_s2026          0/242   compile=False
  intensity392_ws_s2026    0/236   compile=False
  schedule_8_s2026       223/236   compile=True
  extended_ws_s2026      223/236   compile=True
  dinov3_v3splus_224     235/248   compile=True
(the other two dinov3 members are the same shape)

INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION: training never reloads its own weights through the inference path, so every one of these ran, scored, saved and entered the ledger while being unloadable for submission. Found by witness_check, which is the first thing that ever loads a fresh member the way Kaggle would - the exact value it was built for, on its first real use.
design: Two fixes. ROOT: compile_encoder uses nn.Module.compile(), which compiles the forward in place and leaves parameter names alone, so nothing new carries the prefix. RECOVERY: load_trained strips COMPILED_PREFIX from incoming keys, so the five members already written - real GPU hours - load rather than being explained. The substitution is a no-op on any checkpoint that never met torch.compile.
acceptance_criteria: witness_check loads all five compiled members without a state-dict error, and a fresh compiled run saves keys with no _orig_mod.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on 2026-08-13 by witness_check across four members: 4 ok, 0 refused, and a deliberately flipped manifest refused at 0.407 against 0.00391.

title: Kernel OOM cost a submission: forward batched by studies, not by images
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the 0.500 on 2026-08-12, found 13:07Z.

Ensemble.predict_member sent the whole decoded chunk through the encoder in ONE call. A chunk is 48 studies (STUDY_CHUNK), but what reaches the encoder is studies x slots x window width:
  windowed member     48 x 6 x  3 =   864 images
  whole-stack member  48 x 6 x 12 = 3,456 images
Four times the peak activation for an identical chunk, decided by a member field that nothing in the kernel could see. Locally invisible: 32 GB card, --vram-gb cap, gradient checkpointing. On the kernel's 16 GB T4 it is an OOM.

THE FAILURE CHAIN, all three links now fixed:
  1. predict_member OOMs on the hidden set (fixed 9f31b35: forward split so images/call <= IMAGE_BUDGET = 864, which is exactly what every scored kernel before today sent, including the 0.894 one).
  2. The run therefore writes no submission of its own.
  3. Submission.fallback had ALREADY copied sample_submission.csv into place, so the constant table was scored at 0.500 and a daily slot was spent to learn nothing (fixed 0d65c4a: fallback deleted, Submission.check refuses a degenerate table before writing).

COMPUTE WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM and that is what rules out a timeout: reading whole is CHEAPER than ten overlapping windows (12 images against 30). fusion v2 was faster than the 0.894 entry right up to the single forward that asked for four times the memory.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED: that 864 images actually fits a T4 for the LARGEST member we would submit (large_deep_rank24 is 1024-wide). The number is inherited from runs that succeeded with small and base members. A kernel dry-run on the visible test set is cheap and costs no submission slot — do that before the next entry.
notes:
THE OPEN ITEM IS ANSWERED ANALYTICALLY, 2026-08-13, no GPU and no submission slot.

This bead asked whether 864 images fits a T4 for the largest member. It is the wrong question twice over - a large member never sends 864, and the dry-run it prescribed cannot answer it (the visible test set has THREE studies, so a chunk never fills and the memory path is never exercised; it would pass and prove nothing).

WHAT THE WIDTH-SCALED BUDGET ACTUALLY GUARANTEES, computed rather than assumed:
    variant   dim   imgs/forward   weights   activations   total
    small     384      864          0.04 GB    1.15 GB     1.19 GB
    base      768      432          0.17 GB    1.15 GB     1.32 GB
    large    1024      324          0.61 GB    1.15 GB     1.76 GB
The activation term is IDENTICAL across variants by construction - that is what budget = IMAGE_BUDGET * BUDGET_WIDTH // dim buys - and every variant lands under 2 GB against the T4's 15.8. There is no tightness to worry about.

THE TERM THAT WOULD HAVE DOMINATED AND DOES NOT: a materialised 577x577 attention matrix. SDPA is on by default under transformers 5.15 (checked, _attn_implementation reports 'sdpa'), so it is never built. A naive estimate that included it would predict an OOM that will not happen - which is the shape of error worth naming, since it would have argued for shrinking a budget that is already correct.

So the guard is right, the headroom is an order of magnitude, and nothing needs measuring on the card.
close_reason: All three links fixed and the remaining question answered analytically: the width-scaled budget gives an identical activation peak across variants, every one lands under 2 GB against the T4's 15.8, and SDPA means the attention matrix that would dominate is never materialised. The dry-run this bead prescribed could not have answered it - three visible test studies never fill a chunk.

title: Overlap TTA and whole-stack are the SAME mechanism, which is why they do not compose
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 10:16Z by the corrected diversity curve, which reads each member the way it was fitted.

  member              trained holdout   curve with overlap TTA   TTA gain
  lr5x_d6 (windowed)      0.8323              0.8475              +0.0152
  max12   (windowed)      0.8310              0.8451              +0.0141
  large_deep (windowed)   0.8304              0.8450              +0.0146
  wsfold0_e6 (whole)      0.8457              0.8457               0.0000
  slices16   (whole)      0.8452              0.8452               0.0000

WHOLE-STACK GAINS NOTHING FROM WINDOW TTA, because it has no windows to average - and the windowed gain (+0.0146) is almost exactly whole-stack's training-time advantage (+0.0147). That is not a coincidence: averaging ten overlapping three-slice windows means the model DOES see every slice, aggregated in PREDICTION space (mean over windows) rather than in FEATURE space (max over slices). Same mechanism - see all the slices - reached two ways.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER: whole-stack's +0.0147 is measured against a control scored WITHOUT TTA. At inference, where the windowed members get their TTA, the advantage is gone: wsfold0_e6 scores 0.8457 and lr5x_d6 scores 0.8475. It is not that whole-stack is worthless - it is that we were comparing a recipe with its inference-time trick against one without.

THIS EXPLAINS THE LEADERBOARD. Our whole-stack members scored 0.882 while the older windowed five scored 0.888, and I had attributed that entirely to ensemble size and the whole_stack serving bug. Part of it is this: the windowed members were getting a +0.0146 inference-time lift that the whole-stack members structurally cannot get.

WHAT SURVIVES: res392 is 0.8523 with no TTA available to it, still ahead of every windowed member WITH TTA. Resolution is a genuinely separate axis and is unaffected by this.

THE ARM THIS IMPLIES: whole-stack needs a DIFFERENT test-time augmentation, on an axis it has not already exhausted - small rotations and shifts matching the training augmentation, or multi-scale crops. Slice coverage is spent; spatial jitter is not. If it lands near +0.014 it is the largest inference-side lever available and it costs no training.
close_reason: Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-12_what-the-leaderboard-taught-us.md sections 1-4. These are FINDINGS, and a finding's home is the interpretation, not an open task that bd ready keeps offering as work.

title: Close the witness loop: verify_members must re-derive it through the inference path
description:
2026-08-12 07:50Z. HALF DONE - the witness is now RECORDED (578a785); nothing CHECKS it yet.

WHAT EXISTS. Every run from now on writes config['witness'] = {studies: [8 identifiers], predictions: [[12 floats] x 8]}, produced by trainer.predict at the best epoch - i.e. by the TRAINING path, reading the way training read. It is inside config, so package_members carries it into the manifest for free, and Member.witness reads it back. Empty for the twenty published members and every checkpoint on disk today.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is the whole point: verify_members.py must load those studies FROM THE CACHE, run them through Ensemble.predict_member - the INFERENCE path - and refuse the member if the numbers move. Any consumer-side default that changes what the model reads shows up as a difference; that is precisely the class of defect the fingerprint cannot see, four of which shipped this session.

TOLERANCE: the two paths differ legitimately in one way - inference may average overlapping windows where trainer.predict reads one. For a whole_stack member they must now agree closely (both read the whole stack), so start there with a tight tolerance and treat a windowed member's witness as advisory until the window policy is pinned in the witness itself.

WHY IT IS WORTH FINISHING RATHER THAN LEAVING AS A RECORDED FIELD: a recorded field with no reader is exactly the bug this session found four times. Do not let the witness become the fifth.
notes:
2026-08-12 08:02Z — READER LANDED (comp/witness_check.py) and wired into prepare_submission.sh as step 2b, so it runs before every submission rather than on request.

It feeds the MIDDLE window - the whole stack for a whole_stack member, one group otherwise - which is exactly what Trainer.predict reads. Both paths then see the same pixels, so a difference is attributable to the READING (decode size, slot scheme and order, depth, pooling, whole-stack) rather than to test-time window averaging, which is a legitimate choice.

CURRENT STATE, honestly: 0 ok, 3 unverified, 0 refused. All three packaged members predate the witness, so there is nothing to re-derive; UNVERIFIED is reported separately from ok precisely so a check that cannot run does not read as a check that passed.

STILL OWED, and the reason this bead stays open: the REFUSE path has not been exercised against a real member. The next arm to finish under the new code (slice_attention) writes a witness, and the demonstration to run then is: check it passes, then flip whole_stack off in a copy of the manifest and confirm it is REFUSED. Until that is done the check is argued, not proven.
close_reason:
PROVEN, not argued. The refuse path is now exercised against a real member: sliceattn_s2026 with whole_stack flipped to False in a copied manifest is REFUSED at max|diff| 0.407 against a 0.00391 bound - 104x. Unflipped, four members pass (extended_ws 0.0156/0.0312, intensity392 0.00162/0.00391, schedule_8 0.00159/0.00391, sliceattn 0.00234/0.00391).

It earned its keep on first real use, finding three defects nothing else could see: torch.compile renaming every state-dict key (knee-5he), bf16 members served in fp16 (knee-5qt), and its own tolerance being tighter than bf16's epsilon (knee-6pi). Also gained --device so it runs without a free GPU.

title: [bug] Study.bag emitted six slots whatever the scheme said, so an extended cache would have been all zeros
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-12 07:33Z, third seam of the pipeline bughunt. Found BEFORE the 54 GB extended build was spent.

THE DEFECT. Study.bag routed with the pipeline's scheme (SlotScheme.slots) and then EMITTED using the module-level canonical SLOTS. The two halves of one method disagreed. With --scheme extended: route nine series, emit six bags.

THE FAILURE IT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED, which is the worst shape available: StudyCache allocates the images array at the scheme's width, so images[position] = bag raises a shape error for EVERY study. decode_one catches OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError/IndexError and reports the study ABSENT in every slot - by design, because a black image the mask calls acquired is a silent lie. So the build would log 4,407 'decode failed' lines, run to completion, write the mask with np.save at the end, and leave a 54 GB cache of zeros whose mask says nothing was acquired. wait_for_cache keys on that mask, so the queue would then have started a 90-minute training run against zeros.

It is the exact scenario the codebase already documents fearing in two places ('it would fit a mostly-zero array and return a plausible, wrong answer').

FIXED: bag() iterates self.pipeline.scheme.slots. Removing the last hardcoded use made the SLOTS import unused in study.py, which is the linter confirming there is now one source of truth. A test asserts a nine-slot scheme yields nine bags and nine mask entries.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, still open in knee-nwh: inference builds its pipeline with a DEFAULT SlotScheme, so an extended member would still be served six canonical slots at submission time even though the cache and training are now correct. Either thread the member's config['slots'] into SlotPipeline or refuse a non-canonical member at load.

RELATED, worth one line: decode_one and Submission.decode share ONE decode implementation (both call Study.from_directory(...).bag()). An earlier note in this session claiming 'two decode implementations' was wrong - what diverged was how the pipeline was CONFIGURED, not the code.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Inference hardcoded 336 px and the canonical six slots, ignoring what members recorded
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 07:18Z, second seam of the pipeline bughunt. Resolution FIXED; the slot half is still open.

THE PATTERN, now four instances deep: a field travels in the checkpoint, and inference reads a default instead. slices was fixed reactively after a member fitted on a deeper stack was scored on twelve. variant, slice_pooling and whole_stack each cost a separate incident. img and slots were never given the same treatment.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Submission.decode built Study.from_directory(dir, planes) with NO pipeline, so the decode ran at SlotReader()'s default 336 px regardless of member.img - and Study.bag iterates the module-level canonical SLOTS, so a nine-slot member gets six. pixel_group exists precisely to say which members can share one decode; verify_members prints how many groups there are and the inference path never asks.

WHY IT HAD NOT BITTEN YET: every member submitted so far is 336 px and six slots, so the default happened to be right. Both queued arms break that: resolution reads a 448 px cache at 392 (would have been served 336 upsampled to 392, where training downsampled from 448) and extended_slots is nine slots.

FIXED: Ensemble.decoded_size() returns the single distinct member resolution and RAISES on disagreement - resolution cannot be windowed down the way depth can, so two sizes are genuinely two decodes. Submission.decode now builds SlotPipeline(reader=SlotReader(image_size=...)) from it. Test asserts both halves.

STILL OPEN, and it blocks extended_slots from ever being submitted correctly: Study.bag iterates SLOTS from the module rather than the member's config['slots']. An extended member would load, run, and predict from six of its nine slots with the head's slot embedding misaligned. Either thread the scheme through SlotPipeline (it already holds a SlotScheme, so this is plumbing rather than design) or refuse a non-canonical member at load with a clear message. Do NOT leave it silent.

DO THIS BEFORE SUBMITTING ANY 448 OR EXTENDED MEMBER.
notes: 2026-08-12 07:43Z — CLOSED OUT. The slot half is fixed: Ensemble.decoded_scheme() rebuilds the scheme from the members' recorded slot names and Submission.decode passes it into SlotPipeline. Disagreement between members is refused (a different slot list is a different decode, not a subset), and a name this build does not define is refused rather than silently dropped. Tested for all three cases plus the canonical one. Extended members are now submittable as far as this path is concerned.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] whole_stack was recorded in every checkpoint and read by nobody: inference windowed our best members
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 07:13Z in a pipeline bughunt. FIXED in the same session; the leaderboard cost is already paid and measured.

THE DEFECT. Ensemble.predict_member windowed EVERY member by member.group (3 slices), always. A whole-stack member is trained so a slot embedding is the elementwise MAXIMUM OVER THE FULL STACK; serving it three slices at a time gives maxima over a quarter of the stack and averages ten of those. Different function, same pixels.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, which is the part worth keeping:
  - The fingerprint pins image size and group, NOT stack depth or reading mode, so every member verified.
  - Holdout scoring (Trainer.predict) reads self.window, which whole_stack sets to the full stack - so the local number was measured consistently with training and looked fine.
  - The config key 'whole_stack' was written by MemberRecord from the day the flag existed, and Member had no accessor for it. Exactly the slice_pooling failure repeated: recorded faithfully, read by nobody.

THE EVIDENCE IT COST US: two whole-stack members at 0.8481 holdout scored 0.882 on the public board, while five channel-stacked windowed members at 0.8269 scored 0.888. The windowed members were served the way they were trained; ours were not. That inversion was filed as knee-lv2 and read as 'member quality does not transfer' - part of it was this bug.

THE FIX: Member.whole_stack (defaults False, so the twenty published members stay windowed - they were fitted that way), and predict_member takes ONE pass over the middle member.slices of the decoded chunk, mirroring Trainer.predict. Two tests protect it: one asserts the whole-stack path equals a single forward over the middle slices, one asserts a windowed member is NOT equal to that.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT UNDO: knee-9pl's member-count curve stands - 1 member 0.868, 2 members 0.882, 5 members 0.888 - because all three entries were served through the same defective path, so the COMPARISON between them is still like-for-like. What changes is that the absolute numbers for the whole-stack entries were depressed.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and the third instance now: a field that travels in a checkpoint needs a READER and a test, or it is decoration. Audit every remaining MemberConfig key for an accessor - 'rules', 'band', 'crop_mm' and 'slot_fallback' are read by pixel_group only, and slot_fallback has no implementation at all (knee-t92).
close_reason: Closed

title: Ensemble SIZE beats member quality by 0.020 LB: one 0.8518 model scores 0.868, five 0.8269 models score 0.888
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, four leaderboard entries built to isolate exactly this.

  members  holdout/member  public LB
    1        0.8518          0.868     kneemri-solo, our strongest single model ever
    2        0.8481          0.882     whole-stack fold0+fold1
    5        0.8269          0.888     the old channel-stacked windowed members
    3        0.8493          pending
   23        mixed           pending   fusion: ours + 20 published

THE RESULT: our BEST single model loses to five much weaker ones by 0.020. Per-member holdout quality of +0.025 (0.8518 vs 0.8269) is worth LESS than four extra members. Ensembling is the largest effect measured anywhere in this project - larger than whole-stack (+0.0147 holdout), larger than any knob.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: nothing here defends folds or seeds as a METHOD. They remain banned and the ban is well-founded - the noise floor is the holdout's own sampling error (knee-2rx), so re-running a recipe cannot produce a better measurement. What the curve says is that AVERAGING MANY PREDICTORS is worth ~0.02 on this metric, whatever produced them.

THE SYNTHESIS, and the plan it implies: get many members that differ by MECHANISM rather than by RNG. Every arm is fitted on the same fold-0 split, so every arm already produces an averageable member. We own about six: whole-stack, channel-stacked+rate, per-slice max windowed, 20-slice, DINOv2-large, and now 16-slice. diversity_curve measures every subset of these offline - no submission spent - and it is next in the GPU queue.

IF THE CURVE CONFIRMS: the shipping entry is a mechanism-diverse ensemble, and every future arm has a second purpose beyond its own verdict - it is also a member. That makes arms cheaper, not more expensive.

CAVEAT ON READING THE 5-MEMBER ROW: those five ARE fold members, so the 0.888 was produced by a banned method. It stands as EVIDENCE about ensemble size; it is not a recipe to repeat.

title: Per-label AUC is a fold-0 artefact: Fracture moves +0.119 between folds while the mean moves 0.005
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 06:04Z with the new kneemri.run_comparison, over three whole-stack runs of the SAME recipe on three folds.

  label      fold1 vs fold0   fold2 vs fold0
  Fracture       +0.1187          +0.0803
  ACL            -0.0368          -0.0745
  MCL            +0.0476          +0.0053
  MEAN           +0.0048          +0.0061

THE MEAN IS STABLE AND THE PARTS ARE NOT. Per-label AUC swings by 0.05-0.12 between folds under an identical recipe; the mean of twelve moves by 0.005. Averaging twelve noisy numbers is what makes the metric readable at all.

THIS BREAKS TWO THINGS I BUILT TODAY.

1. knee-1dw's premise. 'MCL 0.755 and Fracture 0.784 are our worst labels, worth +0.0173 if lifted' is a FOLD-0 statement. On fold 1 Fracture is 0.903 and on fold 2 it is 0.864 - it is not a weak label, it is weak on one holdout. MCL ranges 0.755-0.803. The bead was already re-priced once against CoPAS; this is the stronger refutation and it comes from our own data.

2. The falsification design of the resolution and extended-slots arms. Both were written to be judged by whether their gain CONCENTRATES in named labels (MCL/ACL/menisci, MCL/LCL). A concentrated gain of the size those mechanisms could plausibly deliver is SMALLER than the fold-to-fold noise in exactly those labels, so a single-fold per-label table cannot falsify either story. As written, the prediction is unfalsifiable rather than strict.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT FALSIFIABLE, none of which is a fold ensemble: score the SAME holdout for every arm (already true - all arms are fold 0), and compare per-label deltas only against the SAME-FOLD control, never across folds. That is what run_comparison does by construction. The remaining question is whether a per-label delta on one holdout is large enough to read at all, which needs the positive COUNT per label on that holdout - cheap to compute, not yet done.

DO NOT respond by running more folds. The point is that per-label numbers on one holdout are noisy, not that we need more holdouts; the arms are compared on a shared fold-0 holdout, which is the correct design.

title: Better members did not beat more members: 2 whole-stack (0.882) lost to 5 weaker (0.888)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 05:55Z on the public leaderboard.

  5 members, holdout mean 0.8269 (channel-stacked, windowed)  -> LB 0.888
  2 members, holdout mean 0.8481 (whole-stack)                -> LB 0.882

The two whole-stack members are +0.021 better EACH on holdout and the ensemble scored 0.006 LOWER. I predicted an improvement; that prediction is refuted.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH. 0.006 is small and the public LB is a subset, so this may be LB noise rather than a real inversion. It is not evidence that whole-stack is worse - whole-stack is +0.0147 on a matched holdout comparison, measured twice.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: member QUALITY alone does not carry the leaderboard. Something about member COUNT, or about the DIVERSITY that count brings, is worth at least as much as 0.021 of per-member holdout - and our holdout gains are not transferring 1:1.

THE CURVE IS ALREADY IN FLIGHT, on nearly the same members, so this is answerable rather than speculative:

  2 members  0.882                                    COMPLETE
  3 members  kneemri-trained v5                       submitted 05:55Z
  23 members kneemri-fusion (ours 3 + published 20)   RUNNING

READ IT AS A CURVE, not four results. If solo is far below 0.882 and 3 is above it, count dominates and the no-fold direction has a real cost that must be paid another way. If solo is close to 0.882, the count effect is small and the 0.882-vs-0.888 gap is noise.

IF COUNT MATTERS, the replacement is NOT folds or seeds. It is DIVERSITY ENSEMBLING over the arms we are already running: 336px vs 392px, 12 vs 16 slices, max vs attention pooling, six vs nine slots. title: Extended slots: 1,139 discarded CORONAL series against our worst label, which is read coronally
description:
2026-08-11 21:25Z. Arm written: experiments/arms/extended_slots.sh, queued after the current GPU chain.

THE MECHANISM, and why it is not another knob. 2,421 of 24,371 series (9.9%) match no slot predicate, so nothing can route them; three sequences are 96% of that, and the largest is Coronal|fluid|nofs at 1,139 series. Every large effect measured here has come from giving the model more of the data it was already handed - whole-stack was +0.0147 on exactly that mechanism, while every knob inside the design returned about 0.005.

WHY IT IS AIMED. MCL is read CORONALLY and is our weakest label (0.755 vs Baker's 0.896) on an unweighted mean of twelve AUCs. A coronal sequence that never reaches the model cannot be read for a medial ligament. The arm therefore carries a falsifiable prediction: the gain CONCENTRATES in MCL and LCL and is small for the sagittal-read targets. A uniform lift would instead say the extra slots act as capacity, which is a weaker and different finding.

TWO PIECES OF PLUMBING WERE ALREADY RIGHT AND ONE WAS NOT. StudyCache.key already puts the scheme in the cache filename, so an extended build cannot clobber the six-slot cache every existing member was fitted on. lib.sh wait_for_cache did NOT - it keyed on mask_336px_12sl.npy, the canonical mask, which already exists, so an extended arm's gate would have passed instantly on a cache that was never built. Fixed in the same commit.

COST: a 9-slot cache is ~54 GB and must be built ALONE (the 448 build killed both itself and a trainer when it shared the machine). A step encodes 1.5x the images.

ACCEPTED COST: a nine-slot member has a wider slot embedding and cannot ensemble with the published six-slot members. That is cheap now that fold/seed ensembling is out and the target entry is a single model.
notes:
THE ARM RAN, 2026-08-12: extended_ws_s2026 = 0.8459 against the control's 0.8457. REFUTED as an improvement on the mean, and this bead has read as unstarted work ever since.

ITS FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION IS STILL UNANSWERED, and I got that wrong once today before correcting it. The arm predicted the gain CONCENTRATES in MCL and LCL. I recorded 'the per-label prediction failed' on the strength of MCL +0.0056 and Lateral Meniscus -0.0130 - but calibrated against each label's own sampling interval, NOT ONE of its twelve deltas clears (MCL's +0.0056 against +/-0.040). The prediction was never refuted, it was UNREAD, and calling it refuted spent a mechanism on noise.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is now built: the paired interval (knee-3vh). Two arms scored on the SAME 881 studies share their sampling error, so the paired band is about eleven times tighter than the unpaired one used above - the difference between 'unread' and an answer. member_curve --paired reports it, and it needs one inference pass over members already on disk.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT DISPROVED BY A FLAT MEAN. 1,139 coronal series still never reach the model, MCL is still read coronally and still our weakest label. What is disproved is that adding them lifts the MEAN, which was never the interesting claim.

title: The metric is an unweighted mean, so our two worst labels are worth +0.0173 - above the bar
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 from the whole-stack fold-0 member (mean 0.8457), using the per-label table RunMetrics now records every epoch.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS THE BIGGEST LEVER ON THE BOARD: the competition metric is the UNWEIGHTED mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs. A point of AUC on MCL is worth exactly as much as a point on Effusion. Our labels are not close to level:

  MCL              0.755   <- worst
  Fracture         0.784
  Lateral OA       0.822
  PF OA            0.824
  ...
  Medial Meniscus  0.893
  Baker's          0.896   <- best

Lifting a label to 0.873 - a level we demonstrably reach on five others - is worth (0.873 - x)/12 on the mean:
  MCL      +0.0098
  Fracture +0.0074
  bottom two together  +0.0173, which is ABOVE the 1.5% bar and larger than whole-stack (+0.0147).

TWO EXPLANATIONS TESTED AND BOTH REFUTED, which is what makes this actionable rather than a shrug:
  - NOT RARITY. Synovitis has 580 positives (13.2%), FEWER than MCL's 767 (17.4%), and scores 0.873 against MCL's 0.755.
  - NOT LABEL NOISE. Synovitis has the LOWEST mean reader confidence in the corpus (0.189) and still scores 0.873; MCL has high confidence (0.789) and scores worst. Baker's at confidence 0.508 is our BEST label at 0.896.
So neither how often a finding occurs nor how sure the report reader was predicts how well we do. MCL is HARD TO SEE. That is an imaging problem, and it contradicts this project's standing 'supervision-limited' thesis for at least this label.

WHERE THAT POINTS: the MCL is a thin structure at the MEDIAL MARGIN of the field, read coronally. A 130 mm crop at 336 px is 0.39 mm per pixel, and the occlusion test already showed centre-only and border-only scoring the same, i.e. no privileged reading of the joint centre. knee-dft (336 -> 448) carries a pre-registered prediction that any gain must CONCENTRATE in ACL/MCL/meniscus - it now has a named target with measured headroom, which makes it a sharper experiment than when it was filed.

FRACTURE IS PROBABLY A DIFFERENT PROBLEM: 7.1% prevalence and confidence 0.406 - both low. Marrow oedema needs fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed sequences, which we do route. Worth separating from MCL rather than treating 'the two worst labels' as one thing.

WHAT NOT TO DO, per the house rule: do not reweight the loss toward the weak labels. 'Keep the objective general - never fit it to a specific weakness; fix needs with balanced data, not loss-engineering.' If a balance fix is warranted it belongs in SAMPLING - oversampling studies carrying rare positives - not in per-label loss weights, and it should be justified by prevalence, which the numbers above say is NOT the problem here anyway.
notes: 2026-08-12 06:05Z — REFUTED by our own data; do not plan against the +0.0173. kneemri.run_comparison over three whole-stack runs of the same recipe shows Fracture at 0.784 on fold 0, 0.903 on fold 1 and 0.864 on fold 2, and MCL ranging 0.755-0.803. The 'two worst labels' were a property of the fold-0 holdout, not of the model. See knee-70w. The mean across twelve labels is stable to ~0.005 across the same folds, which is why the mean is the readable number and a single per-label AUC is not.
close_reason: REFUTED by knee-70w. The premise was that MCL 0.755 and Fracture 0.784 are stable weaknesses worth +0.0173. They are fold-0 sampling artefacts: Fracture moves +0.119 between folds while the mean moves 0.005, and the Hanley-McNeil SE for 62 Fracture positives is +/-0.061 at 95%. There is no per-label weakness here to target.

title: Attend across slices instead of maxing them: the published successor to what just worked
description:
PRIOR ART, found 2026-08-11 after whole-stack paid off. Medical Slice Transformer (Nature Scientific Reports 2025) encodes each slice with a 2D encoder - DINOv2, the same backbone we use - and then runs a SLICE TRANSFORMER with attention across slices, plus within-slice patch attention. A two-stage transformer with a [CLS] token over the slice sequence appears in the same literature, and Memory-Guided Transformer (Pattern Recognition 2025) adds group attention across anatomical planes, reporting best-in-class on MRNet.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT NEXT ARM RATHER THAN A NEW IDEA: we have just measured that seeing every slice per step is worth +0.0147, our largest change, using the crudest possible aggregation - an elementwise maximum. Max keeps, per feature dimension, whichever slice shouted loudest and discards which slice it was and everything the others said. Attention over the same axis keeps the axis.

THE CHANGE IS SMALL AND LOCAL. model.py slot_features already encodes each slice separately under slice_pooling='max' and ends with:
    pooled.reshape(batch, slots, group, -1).amax(dim=2)
The slice axis is right there. Replacing amax with a learned attention over dim=2 - a query per diagnosis, or a single shared query to start - is a contained edit behind a new slice_pooling value, so every existing member keeps loading.

SUPPORTING EVIDENCE FROM OUR OWN MEASUREMENTS:
  - the occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976..0.8332 across windows, so WHICH slice matters, and max deliberately throws that away.
  - SlotHead already does exactly this trick one level up (per-diagnosis query attention over slots, masked) and it works. This is the same mechanism applied to the axis below it.
  - the depth-by-label diagnostic exists to say whether labels want different depths; if they do, a per-diagnosis slice query is the correct shape rather than a shared one.

RISK, stated up front: it adds parameters to a model this project has repeatedly called supervision-limited, and 58 image-read labels is not much to fit an attention with. The anatomical prior - forcing correct slot attention - measured neutral, which is evidence that MORE attention machinery is not automatically better here. Start with a single shared query, not per-diagnosis.

RUN ORDER: after tonight's folds, and after knee-gtw (20 slices under whole-stack), which is cheaper and tests the same axis by adding evidence rather than parameters.
close_reason: Closed

title: Slice count is UNREFUTED under whole-stack: the old test only ruled it out for windowed reading
description:
THE REFUTATION WE HAVE DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE, and the distinction is mechanical.

WHAT WAS REFUTED (knee-ezz, closed): 20 cached slices against 12, both read as ONE RANDOM 3-SLICE WINDOW per step. 0.8309 vs 0.8310 - nothing. It could not have worked: at a fixed group of 3 the window covers 3 slices however many are cached, so more slices only changes which window can be drawn, not what a step sees.

WHY WHOLE-STACK CHANGES THE QUESTION: whole-stack reads EVERY cached slice per slot per step, so the cached slice count IS the anatomy a step sees - 12 slices is 72 images per study, 20 is 120. No window, no group to thin. The mechanism that made the old arm null is absent.

SUPPORT: whole-stack itself is +0.0147 and its mechanism is exactly 'see more of the stack'; the occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976..0.8332; the 0.20-0.80 band holds ~18 slices on the median study and we keep 12; MRNet maxes over ALL slices, not a fixed 12. The 20-slice cache is already built (59.7 GB), so this costs no decode.

THE BLOCKER, measured rather than assumed: whole-stack at batch 12 with 12 slices puts 864 images through the encoder and holds 19.2 GB with gradient checkpointing on. Twenty slices is 1440 images, about 1.7x, so roughly 33 GB - MORE THAN THE 32 GB CARD. This arm cannot run as a drop-in.

THE THREE WAYS OUT, and none is free:
  1. Batch 8 instead of 12: ~960 images, fits in ~22 GB. But the ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 pairs at 12, 28 at 8 - so it changes the objective, and the arm would no longer be single-variable against tonight's folds.
  2. Cache 16 slices rather than 20: ~1150 images, ~26 GB. Fits, keeps the batch, and still recovers most of the band's median 18 slices. Costs one decode pass (~40 min, CPU).
  3. Accept the whole card and drop coexistence with the other project for the duration.

RECOMMENDED: (2). It keeps the batch and therefore the objective, it tests the same mechanism, and the decode is CPU work that can run while the GPU does something else. Sixteen is also closer to what the band actually holds than twenty.

RUN AFTER tonight's folds.
notes: 2026-08-12 06:46Z — REFUTED under whole-stack, by direct measurement rather than by the old windowed argument. Peak 0.8452 at epoch 6 against the control's 0.8457 = -0.0005, and the matched-epoch curve ran +0.001 to +0.002 throughout, all inside a 0.0053 floor. 16 slices cost 33% more compute per step (440-530 s vs ~350 s) for nothing. Depth coverage saturates at whole-stack 12; the mechanism that pays is reading the whole stack, not caching more of it.
