title: Through-plane masked prediction: the SSL objective currently sees zero 3D structure
description:
MRI is volumetric and a study is THREE orthogonal samplings of the knee (SAG/COR/AX x contrast, 6 slots, 12-20 slices each) - strictly richer than the isotropic cube an SL-MAE reads. Our encoder is 2D by choice, because DINOv2's pretrained weights are the asset and a 3D encoder means training from scratch on 4,407 studies. Volume is recovered at the HEAD (--whole-stack pooling, slice_attention +0.0016, seated).

THE GAP: kneemri/training/pretrain.py:127 draws slices INDEPENDENTLY at random, deliberately, so a batch cannot contain near-duplicate neighbours the decoder copies. Correct for batch statistics and it means the self-supervised objective sees no through-plane structure at all - every slice is an island, and masking recovers in-plane texture only. Continuity across slices is how a tear is distinguished from a partial-volume artefact, and menisci/cruciates are exactly the labels the 58-study vision partition says we fail on (Lateral Meniscus -0.193, ACL -0.123, MCL -0.096, Medial Meniscus -0.094).

THE ARM: mask WHOLE SLICES and reconstruct them from their neighbours - sample an adjacent triplet, hide the middle, predict from the outer two. Same backbone, same decoder, same cache; only the sampler and the mask change. Second version hides a whole SLOT and predicts it from another plane, which is the cross-plane consistency no head-level pooling can supervise.

Blocked on encoder_adapt reading out - that arm is the clean one-variable test of the in-plane objective and this must not be folded into it.

title: Arms die at exit 127 when a push re-syncs the shared .venv underneath them
description: A trainer that is mid-run holds an interpreter open against .venv. Every pre-commit/pre-push entry is 'uv run --extra dev' or '--extra devtools', and alternating extras makes uv rewrite .venv IN PLACE. The running interpreter's files vanish and it dies with exit 127 and no traceback -- no error line, no CUDA message, nothing in the trainer log. lib.sh:324-328 already records the first occurrence (2026-08-13, mid epoch 4, traced to a push at 14:03 rewriting uv.lock at 14:05) and added --no-sync to run_train. That fix is one-sided: --no-sync stops the ARM from syncing, and cannot stop another uv process from syncing beneath it. It recurred 2026-08-20 10:32, killing severity_weight at step 182/291 of epoch 1 -- the push that did it was my own. FIX: arms run against a dedicated environment (.venv-arm, built with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, gitignored) so the shared .venv is no longer shared with a live run. lib.sh must set UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT in run_train -- BLOCKED until the current arm lands, because lib.sh is the file that arm's shell is executing and editing it mid-run is the depth_regions_span failure recorded at lib.sh:219-221. Until then: DO NOT PUSH WHILE AN ARM RUNS.
design:
ONE EDIT POINT, because all four uv sites in lib.sh (46, 329, 388, 464) already pass --no-sync and differ only in what they run. Export the environment once near the top of lib.sh, beside REPO/PROCESSED, and every uv call in every arm inherits it:

    # ARMS DO NOT SHARE AN ENVIRONMENT WITH THE GATES. uv syncs .venv to EXACTLY the extras it is
    # given, so 'uv run --extra dev' and 'uv run --extra devtools' rewrite it in opposite directions
    # -- in place, with no lock. A pre-commit or pre-push hook doing that under a live trainer
    # deletes the files its interpreter is running from: exit 127, no traceback, no error line.
    # Measured twice (2026-08-13 mid epoch 4, 2026-08-20 mid step 182). --no-sync below stops THIS
    # process from syncing and cannot stop another one, which is why the fix is a separate directory
    # rather than another flag.
    export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$REPO/.venv-arm"
    [ -d "$UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT" ] || uv sync --extra dev --extra devtools

WHY NOT --no-sync ON THE HOOKS INSTEAD: .pre-commit-config.yaml is template-owned (sdlc-scaffold), and
--no-sync there would make a gate silently run against a stale environment, trading a loud failure for
a quiet one.

WHY NOT A LOCK: hold_card already serialises the CARD, and a second lock over the ENVIRONMENT would
make every gate wait out a forty-minute arm. Two directories cost ~2 GB and no waiting.

VERIFICATION, and it must be a positive check rather than 'no crash': with an arm running, run
'uvx nox -s gates' (which alternates extras, the exact trigger) and confirm the arm reaches its next
epoch line. Second check: '.venv-arm/Scripts/python.exe -c "import torch"' still imports after the
gates finish -- the environment the arm holds was not touched.

BLOCKED ON: the current severity_weight run. lib.sh is sourced by that arm's shell and is re-entered
after the trainer returns (to write LIB/_mark, seat value, the best-holdout check). Editing it mid-run
is the depth_regions_span failure at lib.sh:219-221.

ALREADY DONE: .venv-arm built (uv sync with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, 2026-08-20) and gitignored with the
reasoning. Proven usable in both directions today -- the full AST gate batch and supervision_gap both
ran green against it while the arm held .venv.
notes: knee-z99y is the same race seen from the other side: it recorded gate flakiness, this bead records arm death. One .venv, no lock, two writers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Severity should set the loss WEIGHT, not just the target value: mild YES is right 37.8% of the time and trained at the same 0.95 as severe
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, from report_labels_v2.csv and targets.MEASURED_AGREEMENT.

THE DEFECT, in one table. The reader emits five levels. The value carries severity. The weight does not:

  value  meaning    weight(__conf)   cells    radiologist says POSITIVE
  0.08   NO             0.85         22,298      4.1%
  0.28   UNK            0.05         14,445     13.6%
  0.68   mild YES       0.95          6,461     37.8%
  0.82   moderate YES   0.95          6,427     68.8%
  0.94   severe YES     0.95          3,241     95.8%

The three YES levels are severity grades 1/2/3 (the verdict/severity bijection, audited 2026-08-20) and
they all carry conf 0.95, verified over all 52,872 populated cells (min == max == 0.95 at each level).
A mild-grade YES is correct 37.8% of the time and is trained at the SAME confidence as a severe YES that
is correct 95.8%. A 2.5x reliability gap that the loss cannot see.

SIZE OF THE DEFECT, with its denominator stated. 6,461 mild cells x (1 - 0.378) = ~4,020 cells that are
confidently wrong-signed at weight 0.95. Over the 52,872 populated cells that is 7.6% of the corpus —
about twice the 100-report contest pilot's 4.0% contested rate, and unlike the pilot's it is spread
across ALL TWELVE labels rather than concentrated in Fracture and Contusion.

WHY THIS IS NOT calib_span, WHICH LOST 0.0020, and this is the load-bearing distinction.
calib_span (--calibrated-targets, Supervision.applied) rewrites the VALUE to the measured rate:
0.68 -> 0.378. That is BELOW 0.5, so 6,461 mild cells FLIP SIGN — a mild tear becomes a negative target
under BCE. That is a destructive change and is the most likely reason it inverted every clause.
This arm rewrites the WEIGHT and leaves the value alone. The mild tear stays a positive target; it is
merely trusted less. The ordinal ladder 0.68 < 0.82 < 0.94 is preserved intact, so the pairwise ranking
term — the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms — keeps every pair it currently forms.
So the ledger's one refutation on this axis does NOT transfer: it refuted a value edit, not a weight edit.

THE DESIGN, derived rather than picked (no magic numbers). Weight = P(label is correct | level), which
MEASURED_AGREEMENT already holds:
  NO   0.08 -> correct 95.9%   (weight up slightly from 0.85)
  UNK  0.28 -> 13.6% positive, ambiguous by construction — leave at 0.05
  mild 0.68 -> 0.378
  mod  0.82 -> 0.688
  sev  0.94 -> 0.958
Every number comes from the 58 image reads, fitted there and scored on the fold-0 report holdout, which
is how Supervision already keeps the ruler independent. Gate on WEIGHT_FLOOR interaction: --weight-floor
is in the shipped RECIPE and clamps low weights, so the arm must state what floor it runs under or the
0.378 it is testing never reaches the loss. VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED IN THE CHECKPOINT CONFIG.

DENOMINATOR CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the whole design. MEASURED_AGREEMENT is computed over 684
annotated cells, 311 of them positive calls, so the three YES levels carry roughly 124 / 124 / 62 cells.
The severe rate 95.8% sits on ~62 cells. The per-level ordering is solid (monotone across a 0.58 span,
and the corpus-weighted mean 61.8% reconciles with the independently reported 65% positive agreement),
but no single rate should be treated as precise to better than a few points.

CONTROL: band_dense = 0.8578 at epoch 8, the settled operating point (4e-5 backbone, 20 slices, band
0.10-0.90, whole-stack, 336 px, batch 12, 12 epochs one-cycle). Single variable: the weight column only.

PRE-REGISTERED, written before the run:
  PREDICTION — peak clears 0.8578 by more than 0.0062, and the gain is NOT concentrated in the six
    label-bottlenecked findings (knee-dtk), because a weight change touches all twelve.
  REFUTATION — peak at or below 0.8578. Then reliability weighting is not what the head is missing, the
    flat 0.95 was not costing anything, and the severity axis is closed on the LOSS side as well as the
    value side (calib_span). Say so and stop reaching for supervision.
  THIRD OUTCOME — mean flat but the mild-heavy labels move. Medial Meniscus is 53.3% YES and Effusion
    60.5%; if their per-label numbers move while the mean does not, the mechanism is real and something
    else is absorbing it.

RISK TO THE SHIPPED RESULT: NONE. This is a fold-0 matched arm. It writes a new checkpoint, touches no
member in comp/champion.json, and champion_check still guards that the 0.925 entry rebuilds. The only
cost is GPU time, and the card is currently held for biohub.

NOT QUEUED. Needs the card and an explicit go-ahead.
notes:
2026-08-20 10:32Z — BUILT, SMOKED AND RUNNING. The card freed and the user said so; launched directly
(no sentinel — nothing was running). Commit 2fcfdcf. Log: logs/severity_weight.log.

DENOMINATOR CORRECTION — the "~124 / 124 / 62 cells" above was MY PROPORTIONAL ESTIMATE, not a
measurement, and it was wrong. The real per-level n and CIs are in the Calibration docstring
(kneemri/labels/targets.py:62-67) and were there the whole time:

    level   measured   95% CI            n
     0.68    0.378     [0.282, 0.474]    98
     0.82    0.688     [0.611, 0.764]   141
     0.94    0.958     [0.912, 1.004]    72

This makes the design STRONGER, not weaker: the three intervals DO NOT OVERLAP. 0.474 < 0.611 and
0.764 < 0.912. The ordering is not "solid but imprecise" as the caveat above hedges — it is resolved.
The severe rate sits on 72 cells rather than the 62 I guessed, and moderate on 141 rather than 124.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT, and it differs from the design above in one place:
  Supervision.severity (a bool) + Supervision.trusted() + Supervision.reliability(), consumed at
  targets.py:224 BEFORE applied(), because a calibration rewrites 0.68 to 0.378 in place and a grade
  looked up afterwards would match nothing and fall back to __conf silently. The two switches compose
  only in that order.
  Supervision.moves_the_ruler() now gates the second read in Targets.pair — it was `if calibrated`,
  which would have graded the HOLDOUT under this arm and moved the AUC by construction.
  --severity-weight on TrainingOptions, stamped through Request.wanted() into the checkpoint config,
  so "verify the flag landed" is a config read rather than an inference.

MEASURED ON THE REAL TABLE (52,872 populated cells, post-annotation-override so counts differ slightly
from the raw-table counts in the description above):
  scores byte-identical between arm and control — this is not a calibration
  0.08 NO       n=22,102   0.8875 -> 0.9693
  0.28 UNK      n=14,268   0.2875 -> 0.2875 (untouched, it asserts nothing)
  0.68 mild     n= 6,363   0.9625 -> 0.5335
  0.82 moderate n= 6,286   0.9625 -> 0.7660
  0.94 severe   n= 3,169   0.9625 -> 0.9685

TWO THINGS MOVE, WHICH THE DESIGN ABOVE DID NOT SAY. The NO bucket is the largest at 22,102 cells and
it rises +0.082, uniformly across all twelve labels. So the arm grades the positives AND strengthens
the denials, and a bare mean cannot say which paid. The pre-registered clause was rewritten in the arm
to separate them: the denial uplift can only produce a UNIFORM lift, so a uniform lift now REFUTES.
The grade effect can only appear on labels a report actually grades — meniscus, cartilage/OA, ligament
sprain-to-tear. A lift concentrated in MCL also refutes (the pilot found 0 rulebook errors there and
resolution.sh argues it is bounded by what we can SEE).

Gates: uvx nox -s gates successful; 879 unit tests pass. Four total-partition gates fired on the new
switch and each was answered rather than suppressed — switch_coverage (needs the arm script to exist),
Request/test_not_a_switch, member_record.NOT_IN_CONFIG, run_comparison.SUPERVISION_AXES.

title: A queue watcher dies with the session that launched it, and nothing notices until the card is idle
description: Measured 2026-08-20 06:22Z. aug_long finished and wrote its ARM DONE marker, and the card then sat at 5 percent for about five minutes because the after.sh watcher gating on that marker no longer existed. ps showed exactly one after.sh alive (the headlr one launched this session, PPID 1); the three older watchers for v3base_band, aprior_dense and rank0_dense - launched in a session that has since ended - were gone. Their log files still say 'waiting for ARM DONE ...' forever, which is the trap: the queue LOOKS armed. nohup gives PPID 1 but does not survive whatever ends the harness shell here. Recovered by relaunching one chained after.sh over all three arms; the marker was already present so v3base_band started immediately. WHAT IS MISSING is a check that answers 'is every queued arm still gated by a live process', in the family of arm_check/ledger_check. Cheapest form: read the after_*.log headers for the arm each claims to be waiting on, cross them against ps for a live after.sh with that marker in its argv, and report any arm whose watcher is dead. Second, progress.py already knows when nothing is producing - an idle card with arms still queued is exactly the state it could name in one line instead of leaving it to a manual nvidia-smi.
close_reason: Built as kneemri/experiments/queue_check.py in 84993e3. Crosses the after_*.log headers against ps -ef: an arm is stranded when its watcher log says it has not started and no live after.sh carries that marker in its argv. Reports stranded ARMS, not watches, because recovery relaunches a chain over the arms; an arm anyone has announced counts as covered, which the first live run earned when aprior_dense was training and a dead log still claimed it. Ten unit tests, listing injected so the crossing is pure. Added to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the eighth check.

title: final_fit.sh, the deliverable, is written against the pre-settlement operating point and its central geometry argument is now INVERTED
description:
Found by knee-aixw's enumeration on 2026-08-20. This is that bead's failure mode in the highest-stakes place it can occur: final_fit.sh runs with --fold -1, so NO STUDY IS HELD OUT, there is no score, and train.py keeps the last epoch by construction. A regression here ships unseen. The script's own header says 'EVERY CHOICE HERE IS NOW THE ONE THAT SURVIVED', and that sentence was true when written.

RESOLVED THE SCRIPT'S EFFECTIVE CONFIG BY PARSING ITS ACTUAL ARGV rather than reading its comments. final_fit.sh names neither --slices nor --band-low/--band-high, so it takes the parser defaults:

    slices     12     settled recipe: 20
    band       0.2-0.8    settled recipe: 0.10-0.90
    image_size 448 / train_size 392
    ema        True

The band widening paid +0.0039 and the ledger describes it as 'already in the recipe every arm inherits'. final_fit.sh does NOT inherit it: band and slices are per-arm flags, not part of RECIPE, and this script names neither.

THE GEOMETRY ARGUMENT IS INVERTED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. The header builds the whole 448/392 choice on res392 = 0.8523, 'our best single member' and 'the one coverage lever that whole-stack does not already contain', concluding that 'fitting the deliverable at 336 would ship a model measurably worse than a member we already have'. Read against the champion as it stands today:

    band_dense_s2026            img=336 slices=20 band=0.1-0.9   0.8578
    calib_span_s2026            img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    band_span_s2026             img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    depth_regions_narrow_s2026  img=336 slices=12 band=0.2-0.8

ALL FOUR MEMBERS OF THE 0.930 CHAMPION ARE 336 px. res392 is in none of them and no longer has a metrics file on disk. The best single member this project has is band_dense at 336 px and 0.8578, which BEATS the 392 px member the deliverable is built around by +0.0055. The sentence the geometry rests on is now false in its own terms.

SECONDARY, both real and both smaller:
  - --ema is justified by exactly one measurement, weight_average at +0.0003 against wsfold0_e6 - flat, and taken at the pre-settlement operating point. It is the only one of knee-aixw's six stale rows with a live consumer, and this script is that consumer. The argument FOR it (no holdout, so no best-epoch selection to fall back on) is sound independently of the number, so this is 'the number is stale', not 'the flag is wrong'.
  - The script hardcodes '--one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0' instead of sourcing RECIPE. That is precisely the copy-paste drift recipe.sh was created to remove, and its own header cites knee-7tq needing FOUR corrections for it. This is the arm that would ship, and it is the one still doing it.

DO NOT JUST ADD THE FLAGS. 392 px with 20 slices at band 0.10-0.90 is a configuration NOBODY HAS RUN, and the script's own header forbids exactly that: 'a deliverable is the wrong place to run an experiment: with --fold -1 there is no score, so a regression would ship unseen.' VRAM is a second reason to be careful - the measured 1.335 GB/slice + 0.22 rule puts 20 slices near 27 GB at 336 px, and 392 px is more.

THE OPTIONS, and choosing between them is a design call:
  (a) Re-base onto band_dense exactly: 336 px, slices 20, band 0.10-0.90, 4e-5. Ships the configuration that actually scored best, changes nothing unmeasured, and drops the 392 px argument that no longer holds. Cheapest and most defensible.
  (b) Keep 392 px and measure the missing pair first (392 with slices 20 / band 0.10-0.90 on fold 0), then ship whichever wins. Costs a card slot but is the only path that keeps the coverage lever without shipping an unrun config.
  (c) Ship 392 px as written. Requires believing res392's +0.0066 survives an operating point that has since moved twice, which is the exact belief knee-aixw exists to distrust.

Recommend (a) unless a slot is spent on (b) first. NOT EDITED UNILATERALLY: the deliverable's geometry is a decision, not a typo.
notes: 2026-08-20: the SAFE half is done in 7f1b9c1 -- final_fit.sh now sources $RECIPE instead of holding a private copy of --one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0 (verified config-identical by parsing both argv forms), and its header carries the audit plus a DO NOT RUN marker. The GEOMETRY half stays open and needs a decision: (a) re-base onto band_dense exactly (336 px, 20 slices, band 0.10-0.90), (b) measure 392 px at the settled band on fold 0 first, then ship what scores, or (c) ship as written. Recommend (a). Not edited here on purpose: naming the missing flags at the current 392/448 would ship 392 px x 20 slices x 0.10-0.90, which nobody has run, and with --fold -1 there is no holdout to catch a regression.

title: v3base_band: the settled data recipe on a different encoder family
description:
QUEUED 2026-08-20 behind aug_long. Asks whether the +0.012 of decode recipe this ledger bought since the v3 runs is a fact about the DATA or about DINOv2. Every v3 number we hold (best 0.8268, base-under-LoRA at 224) was taken at the OLD operating point — band 0.20-0.80, 12 slices — and got none of the span (+0.0039), density (+0.0014) or rate work. Single variable against dinov3_base_lora: --slices 20 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9 substituted, encoder/LoRA/rate/pixels all held.

TWO RULERS. Matched control dinov3_base_lora 0.8268. Seat value against comp/champion.json greedy4_v1 0.8679.

PRE-REGISTERED. Prediction: solo clears 0.838 AND earns a seat despite a solo score ~0.02 under every incumbent, on the deep24 mechanism (deep24 is the worst member in the roster at 0.8213 and greedy picks it anyway, because its errors are not shaped by the objective the other sixteen share). Refutation: solo at or below 0.8268 — the recipe does not transfer, which demotes every decode number here from a fact about knee MRI to a fact about DINOv2's feature geometry, and the span/density/crop chapter has to be re-read with that scope written on it. Third outcome: solo clears 0.838, seat value at or below zero — encoder diversity does not pay in a four-member RankAverage vote, retiring the axis and reading the roster's recipe-only diversity as a finding rather than a poverty.

WHY THIS AND NOT A DECODE ARM: knee-jk3 closed that family and its own logic leaves the label axis (knee-mxj) standing, which is gated. This is the other thing jk3 never named — seventeen mounted members and sixteen are DINOv2, so the pool's diversity is recipe diversity almost entirely, and roster construction is where today's 0.042 of board movement actually came from.

VRAM sized, not assumed: base_lora peaked at 16.1 GB with 12 slices, so 20 slices lands near 27 GB against band_dense's measured 26.9 on the same card. Train size stays 224 for exactly that reason — one variable, and the budget has room for one.
notes:
SEAT BASELINE MEASURED 2026-08-20, before the arm runs, so the clause is a number rather than a sign. `python -m kneemri.kaggle.seat_value` over all 56 same-split checkpoints against greedy4_v1:

  band_dense_long   for band_span             0.8691  (+0.0012)   <- the only real positive in the pool
  attend_dense      for depth_regions_narrow  0.8681  (+0.0002)
  crop80_span       for band_span             0.8680  (+0.0001)
  ...
  dinov3_base_lora  for band_span             0.8654  (-0.0025)   <- THIS ARM'S CONTROL

So v3base_band's control sits 0.0025 BELOW the champion in its own best seat, and the prediction's seat half is therefore worth stating as movement: the data recipe has to buy about +0.0037 of seat value to bring a v3 member from -0.0025 to break-even, and more than that to earn the seat outright. Note the module docstring quotes dinov3_base_lora at -0.0013; that was measured against a smaller pool and the champion has improved under it since, which is the same shrinking-edge effect champion.json's last principle records. The -0.0025 is the current number and the one this arm is read against.

SECOND READING OFF THE SAME TABLE, unrelated to this arm but measured here: 56 candidates, THREE positive seats, the largest +0.0012. The mounted pool is at its margin against greedy4_v1 — which is what makes an axis the pool does not contain (encoder family) the right thing to spend the card on rather than another occupant of the band seat. Note also that 13 of the top 15 displace either band_span or depth_regions_narrow, so the contestable seat is still those two and no candidate in the pool threatens band_dense or calib_span.

title: Roster search is NOT exhausted: the offline ruler picks the winner but not the field
description:
Five board entries (champion 0.928, slot 1 compound 0.927, slot 2 band_span 0.927, slot 3 depth_regions_narrow 0.928, slot 4 calib_span pending) show no relation between offline seat value and board score. Every offline edge in play is inside the 0.0062 noise floor, and the pool MAXIMUM over the sixteen mounted members is 0.8679, +0.0031 - itself inside the floor.

Consequence, recorded in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md 'Slots 2 and 3 result': an entry whose offline edge over the champion is inside 0.0062 is not worth a submission slot. Board movement now requires a member that does not exist yet, not a rearrangement of the sixteen that do.

Also retires the one-swap rule: slot 1's compound and slot 2's single both returned 0.927, so member count was never the separator. Slot 5's pre-registration was amended in place rather than read against the dead clause.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-19 22:56Z, by the fourth data point. This bead was filed on three seat occupants while slot 4 was still pending. Slot 4 (calib_span, offline seat 0.8670, +0.0022 over the champion and a third of the 0.0062 floor) returned 0.929 - the first entry above 0.928 and the new champion.

So the claim 'an offline edge inside the floor is not worth a slot' is withdrawn, and 'roster search is exhausted' with it: the pool produced a winner. What the four points support is narrower - the offline ruler picks the WINNER (highest offline seat value took the highest board score) and does not resolve the FIELD (second-highest offline, band_span, came last on the board). Cannot rank two candidates a thousandth apart; can identify the top one.

Consequence for how slots are chosen: fire the offline MAXIMUM, do not fire the offline second or third expecting the order to hold.
2026-08-20, THE SEAT WAS BEING PRICED AS A FIFTH MEMBER, and now is not. seat_value called MemberCurve.marginal, which adds the candidate as a fifth — a move comp/champion.json's FOUR MEMBERS principle says is negative return. MemberCurve.swap now holds the count at four and reports the best seat each candidate could take and whose it was (commit 0b330c8).

Nine candidates against calibspan_v1 (roster 0.8670):
  attend_dense           for lr4e-5_ws  0.8680  (+0.0010)
  depth_regions_narrow   for lr4e-5_ws  0.8676  (+0.0007)
  band_wide              for lr4e-5_ws  0.8674  (+0.0004)
  focal_dense            for lr4e-5_ws  0.8673  (+0.0003)
  band_density           for lr4e-5_ws  0.8672  (+0.0002)
  band_span              for lr4e-5_ws  0.8671  (+0.0001)
  depth_regions          for lr4e-5_ws  0.8671  (+0.0001)
  lr1e-4_ws              for lr4e-5_ws  0.8669  (-0.0001)
  res392_ws              for lr4e-5_ws  0.8668  (-0.0002)

THE RESULT IS THE FIRST COLUMN, not the ordering: EVERY candidate's best seat is the SAME one. lr4e-5_ws is the roster's weakest member by marginal contribution and no other seat is contestable by anything in the pool. That is a sharper statement than this bead had — 'the search is not exhausted' becomes 'there is exactly one contestable seat, and nine candidates are queued for it'.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE: a submission. The whole spread from best to worst is 0.0012, a fifth of the 0.0062 floor, and the best move is +0.0010. The seat experiment already showed this ruler picks the winner and does not resolve the field, and here the field is compressed into a sixth of a floor — so these nine are, on this ruler, indistinguishable. attend_dense leads and is the candidate to hold, not to fire.
2026-08-20 the one contestable seat MOVED and then reopened, which is the sharpest form this bead has taken. (1) Re-priced against the new champion greedy4_v1, the weakest seat is no longer lr4e-5_ws — it is band_span, and the whole nine-candidate field collapsed: best move fell +0.0010 to +0.0002 (attend_dense for depth_regions_narrow), only two of nine positive. On that reading the mounted pool was EXHAUSTED and no submission on it was worth a slot. (2) Hours later band_dense_long landed at +0.0012 for band_span's seat, six times the pool's best, from an arm whose own premise was refuted. So 'exhausted' is a statement about a pool at a moment, not about the search: one new checkpoint restored a move larger than any the nine could make. The bead's claim stands and its mechanism is now named — the contestable seat is whichever member the current four is weakest at, and it migrates as the four changes.
close_reason:
ANSWERED 2026-08-20 by firing the thing this bead was tracking. Its standing rule was 'fire the offline MAXIMUM, do not fire the second or third expecting the order to hold'. band_dense_long WAS the maximum — +0.0012 for band_span's seat, six times the runner-up over a sweep of all 56 same-split checkpoints — and it shipped as longseat and returned 0.930, a TIE with greedy4_v1. So the rule survives (firing the maximum has never lost a tick) and stops being a source of board movement: the pool's best move is spent, the second is +0.0002, and re-running seat_value now prints '0 of 34 clear +0.0015'.

The bead's own mechanism is what makes that a statement about a POOL and not about the search — the contestable seat migrates as the four changes, and one new checkpoint restored a move larger than any the previous nine could make. That is exactly why this closes rather than concluding 'exhausted': the answer to 'is roster search exhausted' is 'yes for the members currently mounted, and a single new arm can reopen it', which is not a question that needs its own open issue any more.

Continues as knee-825t (the ruler saturates above ~0.868, with the refutation written), and the finding is now enforced in code rather than remembered: MemberCurve.swap closes its table with the resolvable count against BOARD_RESOLVABLE (commit 3cc7c88). The next roster move worth a slot comes from an axis the pool does not contain — knee-22mt.

title: Gates fail at random when two uv commands run at once
description:
uvx nox -s test on 2026-08-19 21:12Z: two failures, tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py::test_drift_refuses_a_kit_built_from_a_dirty_tree and ::test_a_path_inside_the_repo_answers_the_same_as_its_root. The first fails at 'assert check.drift(_kit(tmp_path / "clean", current)) == []' - a kit built from a clean tree reported drift. Running that file alone immediately after, with the working tree clean, gives 8 passed. So it is order- or timing-dependent, not a code regression, and lint passed in the same run.

Leading hypothesis, cheap to test: _repo(tmp_path) makes the git repo AT tmp_path and _kit() writes its kit directories INSIDE that same tmp_path, so the kit dirs are untracked files in the repo under test. Whether the tree reads dirty then depends on which helper ran first, which differs between a full-suite run and a single-file run. If that is it, the fix is to build the kit outside the repo root (tmp_path/'repo' for the repo, tmp_path/'kits/...' for the kits) rather than to relax the assertion.

Second candidate, already suspected once: the bd daemon exporting .beads/issues.jsonl mid-run makes the OUTER tree dirty. A bead was created at 20:56Z, minutes before this run. That is the same race the pre-push hook flake was filed under - if both turn out to be one cause, close the other as a duplicate.

This matters because the merge gate is the thing that says the tree is good, and a gate that fails at random teaches the reflex of re-running until green.
notes: MECHANISM FOUND, 2026-08-20 — and it is not the kaggle overlay this bead had narrowed to. See knee-6tpb. Every gate entry is 'uv run --extra dev' or '--extra devtools'; uv syncs .venv to EXACTLY the requested extra set, so two invocations that name different extras rewrite the shared .venv in place, in opposite directions, concurrently. That is a race with no lock, and it explains the shape this bead recorded: random, unattributable, never reproducible on a re-run, and always while something else was running. The severity_weight arm died from the same race at 10:32 today (exit 127, no traceback, mid step 182) because the interpreter it held was in the directory being rewritten. The overlay build ('--with kaggle') is one instance of the general case, not the cause -- which is why refuting the two overlay-specific mechanisms did not close this. FIX is shared with knee-6tpb: stop sharing one environment between a long-lived run and the gates.

title: Every directional result taken before the rate and span settled has an unverified sign
description:
calib_span is the proof case. calibrated_targets measured +0.0038 against wsfold0_e6 on 2026-08-16 at the DEFAULT encoder rate and the 0.20-0.80 band, and it earned a seat in the 0.928 champion package on that number. Re-measured on the recipe the project actually ships — 4e-5, 0.10-0.90, whole-stack — it is -0.0020, and the per-label clause inverted (Effusion -0.0212*, PF OA +0.0170*, the exact opposite of the mechanism it was licensed by). The lever did not change; the operating point did.

That makes the sign of a lever a property of the operating point it was measured at, and it does not transfer. slice_attention (+0.0016 over wsfold0_e6 at 12 slices in the narrow band) is the same shape and is what attend_dense is re-reading now. Everything in the ledger dated before the rate and span settled is in the same position: a recorded delta whose sign has not been checked where we ship.

WORK: enumerate the arms in experiments/README.md taken at the pre-settlement operating point, and rank them by (a) whether anything downstream still depends on the sign — a champion member, a queued arm's premise, a closed bead's reason — and (b) cost to re-measure. Only the ones carrying a live dependency are worth a slot; a directional number nobody is standing on can stay recorded as what it was. Do NOT bulk re-run: the point is to find the ones where a wrong sign is currently load-bearing, and calibrated_targets sitting in the champion package while measuring negative at our recipe is the first of them.
notes:
2026-08-20: caught one before it cost anything. unfreeze_depth had sat unrun since 2026-08-11 with its control named as wsfold0_e6 (0.8457) — default rate, 0.20-0.80 band. Queuing it as written would have measured a throughput lever against a control from before the rate and span settled, which is this bead's exact failure and the one calib_span had just paid for. Re-based onto band_dense (0.8578, 4e-5 / 20 slices / 0.10-0.90) so it is a single-variable pair on --unfreeze-last, commit 37ff6d0. THE GENERAL RULE THIS BEAD NOW HAS TEETH FOR: an arm script's named control is part of its recipe and goes stale with it, so a script written before the operating point moved must be re-based before it is queued, not read as if its comment were still true.
2026-08-20, CORRECTION to the note above: unfreeze_depth had NOT sat unrun. It ran 2026-08-19 as unfreeze4_s2026.pt and is refuted in the ledger as row `unfreeze_4` — 0.8320, -0.0137 vs wsfold0_e6, 2.2x the floor, converged, eleven of twelve labels negative. The check that missed it grepped the ledger for the SCRIPT name; the ledger indexes runs by their OUTPUT name (`unfreeze`, eight mentions). A watcher had it queued behind band_dense_long and would have overwritten that checkpoint; killed, and the script now carries the refutation at the top (commit 370e8ea).

The general rule in the note still holds and the re-basing is kept. What changes is which way this case cuts FOR this bead: the refutation itself was taken at the stale operating point, so unfreeze_4 is not an example of a re-basing that saved a slot — it is another entry on this bead's OWN list, a recorded sign measured before the rate and span settled. It is a weak entry: nothing downstream stands on it (no champion member, no queued arm's premise), and -0.0137 with eleven of twelve labels negative is far enough past the floor that an operating-point flip is not the live reading. Recorded, not planned.

METHOD NOTE for this bead's enumeration WORK: grep the ledger by OUTPUT name, not script name. The two differ for at least this arm, and an enumeration that uses script names will report arms as unrun that are refuted on disk.
2026-08-20, ENUMERATION DONE. The bead asked to list the arms taken at the pre-settlement operating point and rank them by live dependency. Six rows in experiments/README.md are read against wsfold0_e6 and none against rank24_s2026 by name: encoder_layer 9 (-0.0227), unfreeze_4 (-0.0137), pair_memory (-0.0302), per_label_loss (-0.0043), weight_average (+0.0003), centre_tissue (-0.0048).

NONE IS LOAD-BEARING IN THE CHAMPION, and that was checked against the recorded recipes rather than assumed. All four members of the 0.930 entry read centre=image, ema=False, layer=None, unfreeze_last=6, per_label=None - so every axis those six rows measured is at its default in everything that ships. Four of the six are also far enough past the 0.0062 floor (-0.0227, -0.0302, -0.0137) that an operating-point flip is not the live reading, which is the same argument this bead already recorded for unfreeze_4.

EXACTLY ONE HAS A LIVE CONSUMER: weight_average (+0.0003, flat) is the only measurement justifying --ema, and experiments/arms/final_fit.sh carries --ema. That consumer turned out to have a much larger problem than the flag, filed as knee-5895: final_fit.sh names neither --slices nor --band-low/--band-high, so it takes the parser DEFAULTS of 12 slices and band 0.2-0.8 against the settled 20 and 0.10-0.90, and its central 448/392 geometry argument is inverted - all four champion members are 336 px and band_dense at 336 beats the 392 px member the script is built around by +0.0055. With --fold -1 there is no score, so none of that would be caught by the run.

CONCLUSION FOR THIS BEAD: the ledger's stale rows are safe to leave recorded as what they were. The stale thing that mattered was not a row at all - it was a SCRIPT whose named recipe went stale, which is the general rule this bead already wrote down after unfreeze_depth. That rule has now caught two arms, and the second one was the deliverable. The enumeration half of the work is done; what remains under this bead is only to re-check any FUTURE script's named control before queueing, which is a standing habit rather than a task.

title: calib_dense: the only untested corner of the span x density x calibration cube
description:
THE ARM IS WRITTEN AND CHECKED: experiments/arms/calib_dense.sh, arm_check --as-queued reads 1 checked / 0 refused / 0 uncached. It is band_dense's exact invocation with --calibrated-targets added.

WHY. Three levers are measured separately against lr4e-5_ws (0.8525): span 0.10-0.90 +0.0039, density 20-over-the-span +0.0014, additive on the mean with interaction ~0.0001. band_dense (0.8578) is the corner carrying both and is the best single member the project owns. calib_span is measuring the third lever on the SPAN corner right now. calib_dense is the corner carrying all three and the only cell of the cube nobody has run.

NOT A KNOB: each lever answers a different question (what anatomy is covered / how the pooled budget splits inside it / whether what we tell the model about a cell is true), and knee-jk3 leaves the label axis standing after decode-geometry closed at ~+0.005 total.

PREDICTION (in the arm header, written before the run): if calibration is a third independent lever, its delta against band_dense equals its delta against band_span within the floor. Per-label clause inherited unchanged from calib_span - MCL and Effusion move most, PF OA barely.

REFUTATION: a mean at or below band_dense with MCL and Effusion flat = calibration and density are substitutes, the depth_regions_span shape a third time, and the label-on-decode stack retires outright.

BLOCKED ON knee-ey1c BY DESIGN. If calib_span reads flat or negative on the span corner, this corner is dead by the same measurement and the slot belongs elsewhere. Do not launch before calib_span lands.
close_reason: Dead by its own pre-registered blocking condition. calib_dense.sh's header says DO NOT LAUNCH THIS BEFORE calib_span LANDS — if the calibration is flat or negative on the span corner, this corner is dead by the same measurement. calib_span came back -0.0020 with the per-label clause inverted, so the condition fired and the arm was never launched. The script stays in the tree as the record of a refused cell; the slot went to attend_dense.

title: DeviceBudget.needed() was a 336 px fit applied at any resolution, so the derived cap forbade the 420 px rung
description: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-19 while choosing the arm after calib_span. needed() returned GB_PER_SLICE*(slices+1)+RESIDENT_GB, a function of SLICES ALONE, and GB_PER_SLICE's own docstring says it is a 336 px constant fitted on 12- and 20-slice rows. The two facts never met in code. THE HARM IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT BLOCKED THE ONE REMAINING NON-KNOB AXIS. --vram-gb was stripped from every arm precisely so the cap would be derived (knee-ylp0), which means resolution.sh at 420 px would have derived 16.28 GB against a rung MEASURED at 23.42 GB (experiments/README.md, the rung table: 392/12 = 20.46, 420/12 = 23.42, 448/9 = 20.00). A cap UNDER a measured demand is the one thing DeviceBudget.capped's own docstring names as preventing nothing and guaranteeing the failure - it says so about clamping to DEFAULT_SHARE, and the size-blind fit was doing the same thing from the other direction. Worse, the docstring deferred consuming the size term 'until a run at a second resolution has logged a peak to check it against', and the 420 run is what would have logged that peak - it could not, because it would have OOM'd first. THE FIX consumes the derivation the docstring already contains: FITTED_SIZE = 336 is named, needed() multiplies by (size/FITTED_SIZE)**2, and DeviceBudget gains size defaulting to FITTED_SIZE. Exact at 336 by construction, so no existing caller's number moves; 420 now derives 27.34 GB, which OVERSTATES the measured 23.42 rather than understating it - the safe direction, costing await_headroom polling instead of an immediate OOM on a recipe that fits. Both construction sites pass the size the step actually encodes, train.py as 'train_size or image_size', the same expression member_record and members already read. TESTED: test_needed gains the fitted-size identity, the square law, and the assertion that the cap clears the 420 rung; 845 unit tests pass and arm_check reports 51 arms, 0 refused, 0 OVERSTATED. CLASS: faulty PLUMBING - a value derived under one condition and consumed under another, with the condition recorded only in prose.
close_reason: Closed

title: calib_span: the label calibration has never been measured on the recipe we ship
description: calibrated_targets scored 0.8495 vs wsfold0_e6 0.8457 (+0.0038, inside the 0.0062 floor) at the OLD operating point - default backbone rate, 0.20-0.80 band. The settled recipe is now 4e-5 with the span closed on 0.10-0.90 (band_span 0.8565, an interior optimum). So the calibration has never been measured on what we ship, and the calibrated_targets_s2026 member inside the 0.928 champion package was fitted on a recipe no later arm reads from. knee-jk3 names the label axis as the one thing its own logic leaves standing after the decode-geometry family totalled about +0.005. THE QUESTION IS SUBSTITUTION: calibration answers a different question from span, so the prior is additive - but that was exactly depth_regions_span's prior and it lost -0.0049. experiments/arms/calib_span.sh is written and passes arm_check (51 arms, 0 refused, 0 uncached). Single variable against band_span. Pre-registered: the gain must concentrate in MCL and Effusion (most 0.68-skewed) and PF OA must barely move; refutation is a mean at or below control WITH MCL and Effusion flat.
close_reason: calib_span landed 0.8545, -0.0020 vs band_span. Flag verified single-variable (calibrated_targets False->True). The pre-registered clause INVERTED rather than missed: Effusion -0.0212* and MCL +0.0029 were the two predicted risers (negative and flat), while PF OA, predicted to barely move because it is nearly calibrated already, is the largest positive row at +0.0170*. Structure scale focal +0.0037 / regional -0.0099 — the mirror of what the span bought. Transferable lesson recorded in the ledger: calibrated_targets scored +0.0038 on 2026-08-16 at the default rate and the 0.20-0.80 band and is a champion member on that number; re-measured at the shipped operating point it is negative. A lever's sign is a property of its operating point.

title: Rotate a re-run's checkpoint and .holdout.npz with its epochs
description: RunMetrics.begin rotated only the metrics file; the checkpoint and .holdout.npz were overwritten, so a ledger row quoting an earlier run's best had no file behind it. Cost depth_regions_span its run-1 predictions on 2026-08-19 when the arm re-entered run_train mid-flight. Fixed: begin() now moves the weights and predictions aside as <run>_run<n>.pt / <run>_run<n>.holdout.npz under the same index as the epochs.
close_reason: Fixed in RunMetrics.begin: the checkpoint and .holdout.npz rotate to <run>_run<n> under the same index as the epochs, chosen from the epochs alone so a run killed before its first checkpoint still consumes a number. Two unit tests: the artefacts move together, and an absent checkpoint neither shifts the index nor raises. ledger_check.reran now points the reader at _run<n> and says an absent sibling means the run predates the fix.

title: An arm launched from the repo tree runs unsnapshotted, so editing it mid-run re-enters run_train
description:
run_train re-sources lib.sh when the lib blob changes (the drift-refresh added under knee-yn6j option a). On 2026-08-19 I edited lib.sh (heartbeat in take_card) while depth_regions_span was training. The log then showed 'line 39: ,: command not found', 're-sourcing before depth_regions_span', and 'epoch 0' — the completed arm re-entered run_train and re-ran from scratch, truncating its .metrics sidecar (recovered from the rotated .metrics.1.jsonl) and overwriting its .holdout.npz.

The arm script itself did NOT change (mtime 19:52, before the run; its line 39 is a comment), so a byte-offset theory does not explain the syntax error — the refresh re-reads the LIB mid-execution and the shell resumes at a stale offset in the new blob.

Operating rule adopted immediately: do NOT edit experiments/lib.sh while an arm holds the GPU lock.

The fix worth designing: the refresh should be gated on the arm not being mid-run — snapshot the lib at run_train entry (run_snapshot already exists for the arm script; the lib needs the same treatment), or refuse to re-source once a training process has started. Re-running a finished 45-minute arm and destroying its per-study predictions is a strictly worse outcome than running one arm on a stale lib.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-19 from the log itself, and it inverts this bead's theory - which changes the fix. logs/depth_regions_span.log lines 28-33 read in order: the seat-value block (roster of 4: 0.8648, +depth_regions_span +0.0009) so THE ARM HAD ALREADY FINISHED AND REPORTED; then 'experiments/arms/depth_regions_span.sh: line 39: ,: command not found'; then the re-sourcing message; then 'epoch 0' again. Two things follow. (1) The syntax error is in the ARM SCRIPT, not lib.sh, and it PRECEDES the re-source line - so the re-source is a CONSEQUENCE of a shifted byte offset, not its cause. Gating the re-source would not have prevented this incident; it would only have stopped the second training run from starting. (2) The description's 'the arm script itself did NOT change' is false. Line 39 of that arm is the header prose arguing '18 clears the measured peak and stays under what will be free' - that IS the --vram-gb 28 -> 18 edit, made while the arm was executing. Bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset, so editing the file under a running shell shifts every later offset: execution resumed inside a comment (the bare ',' is a fragment of one), and the shifted offset then re-entered the run_train line. THE RULE WAS TOO NARROW. 'Do not edit lib.sh while an arm holds the card' does not cover the file that actually broke. The rule is: do not edit ANY file bash is currently executing - the running ARM SCRIPT above all. THE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE TREE AND WAS NOT USED: run_snapshot copies the arm per run and every arm honours 'source ${ARM_LIB:-...}' for exactly this reason, but this arm ran from the repo path (the error names experiments/arms/..., not a snapshot path). So the fix is to make the snapshot path the ONLY way an arm is invoked - queue.sh runs 'bash experiments/arms/<arm>.sh' directly - rather than to gate the staleness refresh. Snapshotting the LIB as this bead proposed is still worth doing but it is the second half, not the cause.
FIXED 2026-08-19 in experiments/lib.sh, one point below every caller. The root cause as corrected: depth_regions_span ran UNSNAPSHOTTED (its log names the repo path), a header edit shifted the byte offsets bash reads a script by, execution resumed inside a comment and re-entered run_train for a second training run. run_snapshot has existed since 2026-08-12 and every arm carries a comment naming it, but only after.sh actually called it - queue.sh:40 ran 'bash experiments/arms/<arm>.sh' directly, and so does every hand-launched arm, which is how most arms start. Fixing the callers was rejected: it is the same class of miss that produced the bug, and a caller invented tomorrow inherits nothing. THE GUARD SITS AT 'source lib.sh', the one line every arm has and every path crosses - the identical argument that puts hold_card in run_train rather than in run_snapshot. If ARM_LIB is unset AND $0 resolves under $REPO/experiments/arms/*.sh, lib.sh calls run_snapshot on itself and exits with its status. ARM_LIB is an exact signal rather than a heuristic: run_snapshot sets it when handing the copy to bash, and arm_check sets it to the stub, so the child never recurses and the checker never re-execs. The $0 test keeps after.sh and queue.sh - which source lib.sh with $0 pointing elsewhere - out of the re-exec entirely. TESTED without spending GPU by launching a RETIRED arm, which exits before run_train: 'bash experiments/arms/multiscale.sh' printed the re-run line ONCE, wrote experiments/multiscale.running.sh, and propagated the retired exit 1. arm_check then ran 51 arms with 0 refused and the guard line absent from its log, which is the stub path proving it does not fire where it must not. NOT fixed by gating the staleness re-source, which was the bead's original proposal: that re-source is a CONSEQUENCE of the offset shift and gating it would only have stopped the second training run, leaving the corrupted first one.
close_reason: Closed

title: VRAM caps are hand-typed guesses, and a co-tenant turns each overstatement into a wait then a crawl
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19 from every arm's own 'peak memory X GB reserved' line against the --vram-gb its script asks.

  arm                     ask   measured peak   overstated by
  band_dense               28       26.92           1.1
  band_density             28       26.92           1.1
  depth_regions            28       26.92           1.1
  band_wide                26       21.57           4.4
  focal_pool               26       16.59           9.4
  weight_average           22       16.35           5.7
  centre_tissue            20       16.24           3.8
  slot_mean                20       16.24           3.8
  band_full                26       16.24           9.8
  band_span                26       16.24           9.8
  per_label_loss           26       16.24           9.8
  rate_wholestack          26       16.24           9.8
  depth_regions_narrow     28       16.24          11.8

THE PEAK IS A FUNCTION OF SLICE COUNT, not of the arm. Every 12-slice whole-stack arm peaks at exactly
16.24 GB, every 20-slice one at exactly 26.92, and band_wide at 16 slices sits at 21.57. Fitting the two
endpoints gives 1.335 GB per slice plus 0.22, which PREDICTS 21.58 at 16 slices against band_wide's
measured 21.57 - a third point held out and matched to 0.01 GB. That is what activation memory linear in
stack depth looks like, so this number is derivable and none of the asks above were derived.

WHY IT ONLY NOW HAS TEETH: DeviceBudget.await_headroom waits up to CONTENTION_WAIT_SECONDS for
free >= vram_gb and then starts anyway. On an empty card an overstated ask is free - the wait passes
immediately. With a co-tenant it is not: biohub_kaggle began training at 19:37 today and holds ~13 GB of
the 32, so a 12-slice arm asking 28 polls for memory it never needed, burns the bound, and then starts
into the PCIe-paging crawl the class exists to prevent. The ask is being read as the NEED, and for most
arms it is 6-12 GB above it.

CAUGHT LIVE: depth_regions_span was queued at 28 and is a 12-slice recipe. It was stopped, re-capped to 18
and relaunched (fa634cd) before it took the card. depth_regions_narrow shows how it happens - it is
depth_regions with the slices dropped to 12 and the 20-slice cap copied along unchanged.

THE FIX is to stop hand-typing it: the trainer knows --slices before it allocates, so DeviceBudget can
default its cap from the recipe (1.335 * slices + 0.22, plus a margin) and an arm names a number only to
override. That removes the whole class rather than correcting thirteen literals, and it is the
'derive parameters with an argument, no magic numbers' rule applied to the one constant that has been
guessed every time.

NOT URGENT FOR CORRECTNESS: the cap bounds the allocator and not the batch size, so no past result is
affected and no arm is mismatched to its control by any of this. It costs wall-clock and risks the driver
reset that took both projects down on 2026-08-17, which is why it is P1 and not P2.
notes:
THE FIT IS 336 px ONLY, and it cannot be extended from the logs we have.

Checked every arm off 336 px for a peak line - resolution_392, resolution_448, intensity_392,
dinov3_v3small_224, extended_slots, lora_r8_small_336 - and NONE of them records one. The
'peak memory X GB reserved' line postdates those runs, so the resolution axis is unmeasured and the
1.335-GB-a-slice line is fitted at one image size. slices16_ws is the only extra point it has, at 21.57
against the predicted 21.58, and that varies SLICES rather than pixels.

THE PHYSICAL FORM extends it without new data, and is what the implementation should use rather than the
1-D line: activation memory scales with the token count a stack presents, which is slices x (size/patch)^2,
so cap = k * slices * size^2 + c. Solving on the two 336 px endpoints gives k = 1.1825e-5 and c = 0.22,
which reproduces 16.24 at 12 slices, 26.92 at 20 and 21.58 at 16. It is the same line at 336 px by
construction and it is a PREDICTION everywhere else.

SO THE FIX SHIPS AS A DEFAULT AND SAYS SO: an arm that names --vram-gb still overrides, the derived number
only replaces DEFAULT_SHARE * whole, and the first 392 px run under it is the measurement that confirms or
corrects k. Being approximately right from a mechanism beats a hand-typed 26 that is 10 GB wrong, but the
docstring must not claim the resolution term was measured, because it was not.
close_reason: Stripped --vram-gb from all 36 arms that carried it; DeviceBudget.needed() derives the cap from --slices. arm_check reports 0 overstated, 0 refused across 50 arms. The three headers that argued a specific number keep the measurement and drop the prescription.

title: An accidental same-recipe rerun diverged 0.0163 at epoch 1 — the 0.0062 floor may not cover training nondeterminism
description:
band_full was launched twice on 2026-08-19: the first run died at epoch 2 when its parent was killed, the second is the arm that will land. Identical recipe, identical seed, identical cache, same machine, ~10 minutes apart. They do not agree.

  epoch   run 1     run 2     diff
  0       0.7389    0.7364    -0.0025
  1       0.7591    0.7754    +0.0163

This is FREE evidence nobody planned for and it points at the ruler rather than at any arm. The 0.0062 noise floor every ledger row is marked against is a PAIRED SAMPLING bound: it answers 'how much do two scores on these 909 holdout studies differ by chance given the studies', and it is computed from the label counts, not from re-running training. It does not contain a term for the training path being nondeterministic — cuDNN kernel selection, non-deterministic reductions, dataloader ordering — and here that term alone is 2.6x the floor at epoch 1.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW, and the distinction is the whole bead: these are MID-TRAINING epochs, which are the unstable part of the curve, and the ledger quotes a run's BEST epoch after 12. Arms may well converge to within a fraction of this by the end. The measurement that settles it is one same-recipe rerun to completion, read best-against-best — which is not a seed study (seeds and folds are banned and this changes neither): it is the same seed twice, and it asks what our own harness's reproducibility is.

IF the converged spread is anywhere near this, every sub-floor delta in experiments/README.md is reading a number whose bar is drawn too narrow, and the honest fix is to widen the floor rather than to re-argue the arms. Cheap to check: no new recipe, no new cache, one 50-minute slot on the card behind work that already matters.

NOTE the nondeterminism is independently corroborated: knee-djk8 measured seven members re-deriving their own witness at 0.6-2.5x bf16 eps on cuda with the arithmetic matched, i.e. the forward pass is not bit-reproducible on this card either.
notes:
EPOCH 2 LANDED AND IT WALKS THE CLAIM BACK: 0.8046 vs 0.8040, a spread of 0.0006. The three paired epochs are -0.0025, +0.0163, -0.0006, so epoch 1 is an OUTLIER on this pair rather than the typical gap, and the honest reading of the run so far is that the divergence is transient early-training instability that the curve re-converges from. Two of three epochs sit well inside the 0.0062 floor.

That does not retire the bead — n=3 mid-training points cannot bound a converged spread in either direction, and one 0.0163 excursion is still 2.6x the floor at a point where the two runs are supposed to be the same computation. It DOWNGRADES it: this is no longer 'the floor is probably too narrow', it is 'we have never measured our own harness's run-to-run reproducibility and we have one accidental hint that it is not zero'. Same measurement settles it, lower urgency.
2026-08-19 18:05 UTC — the replicate is on the card (pid 68145, epoch 2 of 12, ~246 s/epoch, ~35 min left). Run 1's artifacts are preserved beside it as depth_regions_span_s2026_run1.{pt,metrics.jsonl,holdout.npz}.

The metrics sidecar is GOOD (7928 bytes, the rotated .metrics.1.jsonl, 13 lines = header + 12 epochs), so the per-epoch mean-AUC curve for both runs is intact and that is what bounds the nondeterminism term on the mean.

The run1 .holdout.npz is NOT run 1's: it was copied at 20:57, after the replicate's epoch 0 had already overwritten the live file at ~20:54. So the per-study predictions in it are the replicate's epoch 0, not run 1's epoch 9. Do not read it.

BUT run 1's CHECKPOINT is safe (depth_regions_span_s2026_run1.pt, 20:49, 89 MB), so the per-study predictions are REGENERABLE by inference rather than lost — a per-label paired read of run1 vs replicate is still available, it just costs one holdout forward pass. Do that only in a gap between arms.
2026-08-19 18:10 UTC — INTERIM, the replicate through epoch 4 of 12, matched-epoch against run 1:

    epoch  run1     replicate  delta
      0    0.7457   0.7455     -0.0002
      1    0.7708   0.7696     -0.0012
      2    0.8106   0.8011     -0.0095
      3    0.8246   0.8226     -0.0020
      4    0.8355   0.8355      0.0000

Two things this already says, both against the bead's own title.

(1) THE 0.0163-AT-EPOCH-1 FIGURE DOES NOT REPRODUCE HERE. This pair is 0.0012 at epoch 1 and 0.0002 at epoch 0. Whatever produced the 0.0163 that opened this bead, it was not the generic run-to-run term of this recipe — so that number should not be quoted as the nondeterminism bound until the arm it came from is named and re-read.

(2) BUT THE MID-CURVE EXCURSION IS REAL AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE EFFECT IT HAS TO ARBITRATE. Epoch 2 diverges 0.0095, twice depth_regions_span's -0.0049 and above the 0.0062 paired-sampling floor. So at a SINGLE epoch, training nondeterminism alone can produce a delta larger than either. That does not yet transfer to the ledger's number, which is a max over twelve epochs and has its own bias and its own variance — and the curve reconverges to 0.0000 by epoch 4, which is the pattern of a shared trajectory with per-epoch jitter rather than two diverging runs.

THE NUMBER THIS BEAD ACTUALLY NEEDS is |best(run1) - best(replicate)|, run1's best being 0.8505 at epoch 9. Epochs 5-11 are where it is decided; the run has ~30 min left.

title: RunMetrics.rows() picks a KILLED run's epochs over the ones that made the checkpoint
description:
ledger_check reports 'UNRECORDED slices16_ws_s2026: best 0.8411'. The ledger records 0.8452, and the checkpoint agrees: slices16_ws_s2026.pt holds epochs_done 12, holdout 0.84518, backbone_lr 8e-06.

MECHANISM. slices16_ws_s2026.metrics.jsonl holds TWO appended runs: run A epochs 3-11 peaking 0.8452 at epoch 6, then run B epochs 0-8 peaking 0.8411. rows() returns the LAST non-empty group by design -- 'a re-run to the same --out appends and the checkpoint beside it holds only the newest one' (run_metrics.py:166). That premise fails when the re-run is KILLED: run B never wrote a checkpoint (a leftover slices16_ws_s2026.partial is the tell), so the .pt on disk is still run A's, and best() now quotes 0.8411 for a member that scores 0.8452. Every consumer of best() -- ledger_check, arm comparisons, any seat read that prices a member by its recorded best -- reads the wrong number, silently and plausibly.

WHY IT IS NOT A BOOKKEEPING NIT. The failure mode is the one the ledger exists to prevent: a number that describes a different run than the artefact it is attached to, differing by 0.0041 -- large enough to reorder members, small enough to look like a normal reading.

THE ORACLE IS ON DISK. The checkpoint records its own holdout. If no row in the last group matches the checkpoint's holdout, that group did not produce the checkpoint, and the group that contains it did. That rule keeps the pair_memory_s2026 case rows() was written for (a COMPLETED re-run, whose checkpoint holdout is in the last group) and fixes the killed-re-run case.
notes:
FIXED FORWARD, not by loosening the reader: RunMetrics.begin(recipe) opens a run's record and moves any previous run's epochs to <run>.metrics.<n>.jsonl, so one live file describes one run and rows()' last-group guess can no longer be asked the ambiguous question. Fitting calls begin(); describe() stays an append because metrics_recipe BACK-FILLS a recipe onto finished runs.

The two mixed files already on disk (slices16_ws_s2026, pair_memory_s2026) are NOT rewritten -- editing recorded measurements to satisfy a checker is the wrong direction. slices16_ws's killed re-run peaked at 0.8411 and that number gets WRITTEN INTO experiments/README.md beside the 0.8452 the checkpoint holds, which is what ledger_check is actually asking for and leaves both runs on the record.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ring 0.05 scores 0.634 on a champion member: reproduce it before believing it

This is NOT a re-file of the 2026-08-11 border result. That one (border-only 0.8006 vs whole 0.8448 on rankbase24) was filed as a possible periphery shortcut and then reinterpreted in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11_what-actually-moved-the-number.md as a weak model leaning on coarse global context, with the ambiguity named explicitly: the border is 75% of the area and still holds joint. BEFORE BELIEVING IT, three benign readings to separate, because the ring is joint-free but NOT anatomy-free (5% of a 336px side at 130mm crop is ~6.5mm, still inside the leg on many slices):

  (b) scanner/protocol appearance (FOV, coil shading, noise texture) -> correlates with SITE, and the same interpretation already established that the language gap is a site gap and sites differ in label prevalence. This one IS a confound and would inflate the holdout.

NEXT STEP, cheap and already available: rerun attribution on a second champion member with a different recipe (one GPU pass, no training) and check whether ring 0.05 reproduces. Rule out (c) first. Then separate (a) from (b) by scoring ring-only predictions by scanner/vendor, which this repo has already done once for the language-gap analysis.

DENOMINATOR NOTE: 400 studies, one member, one fold. Chance is 0.5.

title: GPU lock's exit trap deleted locks held by other chains, so two arms could share the card
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-19 (d657b6c), by observation rather than by search: experiments/gpu.lock did not exist while per_label_loss was mid-epoch, which should be impossible.

MECHANISM. hold_card armed 'trap "rm -rf '<path>'" EXIT' with the path expanded at lock time. That removes the lock when the shell EXITS, not when the shell still HOLDS it. release_card set LOCK_DIR="" but could not disarm the trap, so any shell that had ever held the card wiped whatever lock existed at its exit. Chain A takes the card, releases after its arm, chain B takes it, chain A's shell exits and deletes B's lock, chain C is then free to start an arm on top of B's.

WHY IT MATTERS: two arms on one card is the 31.9 GB of 32.6 overflow that Windows pages over PCIe, running both at a tenth of throughput at ~180 W of 575. That is the failure knee-jyvv diagnosed, and this made it reachable BETWEEN OUR OWN ARMS with no second repository involved. The serialiser was producing the thing it exists to prevent.

FIX: removal is conditional on this shell being the recorded holder (drop_own_card), in the trap and in release_card alike. An ownership test rather than 'trap - EXIT' on release, because clearing only covers shells that reach release_card while the trap exists for the ones that are killed. Three classes tested: own lock released, foreign lock survives our exit, killed shell still drops its own.

RELATED: knee-jyvv (the same overflow, arrived at from the other side — a foreign CUDA process — fixed by a free-VRAM gate in hold_card at 6b63b9f and a stall watchdog in kneemri.training.heartbeat at 8ce2643).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Two-project GPU sharing pages over PCIe: 183 W of 575 W at '99% util', 10x slower
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19 06:20 UTC while per_label_loss was training.

SIGNATURE: nvidia-smi reports 99% utilisation and 31949 MiB of 32607 used, at 183.71 W against a 575 W limit. Throughput collapsed mid-epoch-4 from ~1090 img/s to 30-170 img/s and has not recovered — 10x, sustained, with no error anywhere. Epoch 4 took 749 s against ~287 s for epochs 1-3.

CAUSE: two CUDA tenants. pid 93308 is ours (kneemri.training.train, started 08:29 local); pid 177224 is D:/personal_projects/biohub_kaggle's celltrack.training.joint_detector, started 08:34 and holding 12.59 GB working set. The collapse tracks the second start. Their sum exceeds the card, and Windows pages GPU memory over PCIe rather than failing — which is the exact pathology experiments/lib.sh already documents for two arms of OUR OWN queue ('reports 99% utilisation at a third of the power budget and simply takes fifteen times longer'). hold_card()'s mkdir lock serialises kneemri arms against each other and CANNOT see another repo's process.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY 'KILL ONE': biohub sharing this card is sanctioned. So the fix is to make sharing SURVIVABLE rather than to claim exclusivity: cap our own process so the pair fits in 32 GB instead of thrashing. Paging costs 10x; a smaller batch costs 10-20%.

CANDIDATE FIXES, cheapest first: (a) torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction on a budget read from a flag, so an arm declares its ceiling and OOMs honestly instead of paging silently; (b) a throughput WATCHDOG in the trainer — img/s below a fraction of its own warm median for N steps is a logged warning, since the failure is invisible today and cost most of an arm before anyone looked; (c) teach hold_card to notice a foreign CUDA process before starting an arm and wait, which only helps arms not yet started.

(b) is the one that generalises: this failure produced no error, no log line and a correct-looking 99% util. Nothing in the repo would ever have reported it.
notes:
COEXISTENCE MEASURED 06:37 UTC, and it changes the shape of the fix. biohub's trainer is on the card again (celltrack.training.joint_detector, same invocation) WHILE our per_label_loss arm trains, and there is no pathology: 20068 MiB of 32607 used, 573.98 W of 575, our arm at 1092 img/s against its own peak of 1260. Two tenants share this card fine. The failure is not sharing, it is the sum crossing the card.

THE TENANT'S FOOTPRINT GROWS DURING ITS RUN. The same biohub process holds ~4-5 GB now (20068 total minus our ~15-16) and held 12.6-14 GB during the 05:xx collapse. So the overflow can arrive at an arm that started with plenty of room, which means a start-time check CANNOT be the whole fix and the heartbeat watchdog is not redundant with it. Prevention stops us starting into a full card; detection is the only thing that catches a card that fills up underneath us. Both landed (6b63b9f, 8ce2643).

This also says the 18432 MiB start threshold is not over-tight: our own arms peak ~16 GB, so the guard only blocks when a foreign tenant already holds more than the card can spare, and the common case (a 4-5 GB neighbour) starts immediately.
close_reason: Closed

title: witness_check on CUDA (the earlier CUDA refusal was a missing uv run, not a defect)
description:
prepare_submission.sh invokes 'uv run python comp/witness_check.py' with NO --device, so it runs on CUDA, where tolerance() returns the tight MATCHED_TOLERANCE=2e-3. On 2026-08-19 that refused 7 of 12 members with max|diff| 0.00495-0.0193, including calibrated_targets_s2026 and lr4e-5_ws_s2026, which are two of the four members in the 0.925 champion. The 2026-08-17 baseline recorded in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md is '--device cpu: 6 ok, 1 unverified, 0 refused', so the documented invocation (CLAUDE.md says --device cpu) and the script's own invocation disagree about whether a submission may proceed.

THE SPLIT IS NOT SIMPLY bf16. All 7 refused members are bf16, but crop80_tissue_s2026 is ALSO bf16 and reproduces its witness EXACTLY (max|diff| 0), as do the two fp16 members. So 'bf16 eps 7.8e-3 exceeds the 2e-3 bound' explains why the bound is too tight to be met, but not why three members meet it exactly. Exact reproduction means identical kernels and identical reduction order; the other members differ in op order somewhere between the training path and Ensemble.

WHAT TO SETTLE BEFORE TRUSTING EITHER VERDICT: (a) is the CUDA diff stable across two runs (a reading difference) or does it move (kernel nondeterminism)? (b) does it spread evenly over the twelve labels (arithmetic) or concentrate in a few (the defect class this check exists for -- those moved 0.05-0.5)? (c) what does crop80 do differently from calibrated. Do NOT loosen MATCHED_TOLERANCE before (a) and (b) are answered; a bound raised to admit an unexplained 0.019 is the gate switching itself off.
notes:
LEG (b), FIRST READING (cpu, --batch 12, 2026-08-19). witness_check now prints the residual's SPREAD -
how many of the twelve labels carry at least half the widest label's residual - on the PASSING verdicts
as well, because a shape is unreadable without a control and cpu passes the same members cuda refuses.

  calibrated_targets 3/12   sliceattn 5/12   intensity392 6/12   extended_ws 4/12
  lora_r8 8/12              crop80_tissue 8/12   lr4e-5_ws 5/12   lr1e-4_ws 4/12
  band_dense 4/12           band_wide 4/12

Nothing concentrates into one or two labels. That is the shape a rounding has; the four reading defects
this check exists for moved a FEW findings by 0.05-0.5. It is NOT yet the answer to (b): these are the
cpu residuals (float32 against a half-precision witness), and the refusals live on cuda. The cuda run
needs the card, which band_density holds until ~14:20 UTC. Run `--device cuda --batch 12` after it and
compare the two spread columns member by member.
LEG (b) MEASURED 2026-08-19, cuda batch 12, full roster: 3 ok / 2 unverified / 7 refused. The bead's premise 'refuses every bf16 member on CUDA' understates and overstates at once — it does not refuse every member, and the three that pass do so at max|diff| EXACTLY 0, exact in every label, not merely inside tolerance.

  ok        sliceattn_s2026            0.00000
  ok        intensity392_ws_s2026      0.00000
  ok        crop80_tissue_s2026        0.00000
  REFUSED   band_dense_s2026           0.00495   0.63x bf16 eps
  REFUSED   band_wide_s2026            0.00540   0.69x
  REFUSED   extended_ws_s2026          0.00790   1.01x
  REFUSED   lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026  0.00915   1.17x
  REFUSED   lr1e-4_ws_s2026            0.01470   1.88x
  REFUSED   calibrated_targets_s2026   0.01610   2.06x
  REFUSED   lr4e-5_ws_s2026            0.01930   2.47x

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE WITNESS'S DTYPE, and witness_check's own tolerance docstring supplies the key: it names extended_ws as bfloat16 and sliceattn/intensity392 as float16. Every float16 member re-derives bit-exactly on cuda; every refusal lands at 0.6-2.5x of bf16's eps (2^-7 = 7.8e-3) — the SAME 1.6-2.4x band the CPU calibration measured for this check, on the same arithmetic.

SO THE CUDA BRANCH'S PREMISE IS THE DEFECT, not the members. tolerance() reasons 'on cuda the re-derivation runs under the member's own autocast dtype, so the arithmetic MATCHES and any remaining difference is kernel nondeterminism' and applies the tight 2e-3. That holds for float16 (observed: exactly 0) and is false for bfloat16, where kernel nondeterminism is ITSELF at eps scale because seven mantissa bits accumulated over twelve blocks is where the reordering shows. CROSS_PRECISION_FACTOR exists for exactly this and is applied only on the cpu branch.

NOT YET CHANGED, deliberately: this is a safety gate and loosening it needs the discrimination argument stated, not just the calibration. The argument is available — the four reading defects this check exists for moved predictions 0.05-0.5, so a bound at 4x bf16 eps (0.031) still refuses them by 1.6-16x. Wants its own bead and a test before the constant moves; NOT to be done in passing while an arm is landing.
LEG (b) ANSWERED 2026-08-19 on the card, and this bead's premise was both too strong and too weak. Not 'every bf16 member fails': three pass, and they pass at EXACTLY 0, not merely inside tolerance. The refusals sit at 0.63-2.47x bf16 eps. Root cause is filed separately as knee-9084 - the cuda branch skips CROSS_PRECISION_FACTOR because it assumes arithmetic matches, which is true of fp16 and false of bf16. Deliberately not fixed here: it is the pre-submission safety gate and wants its own test. Leg (c) still open.
LEG (c) NARROWED 2026-08-19, and it REFUTES the clean dtype story that leg (b) proposed. Read the config flag straight off the checkpoints: crop80_tissue is bf16=True and re-derives at EXACTLY 0, same as the two fp16 members. So the dtype is NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT — every fp16 member is exact, and among bf16 members one is exact and seven are not.

  crop80_tissue        bf16=True   0.00000   crop_mm 80, centre tissue
  calibrated_targets   bf16=True   0.01610   crop_mm 130
  band_dense/wide, lr4e-5_ws, lr1e-4_ws, extended_ws, lora  bf16=True  refuse
  sliceattn, intensity392_ws  bf16 unset (fp16)  0.00000

SECOND HYPOTHESIS REFUTED IN THE SAME PASS: not a stale witness recorded before the autocast-dtype fix. If it were, the residual would track recency, and it does not — crop80_tissue is 08-16 while band_dense (08-19 03:10), band_wide (08-19 01:32), lr4e-5_ws (08-18) and lr1e-4_ws (08-18) are all NEWER and all refuse.

WHAT IS LEFT is the only field that differs: crop_mm 80 / centre tissue against 130 / image. The tensor shapes are identical after the resize, so the kernels are the same and the opportunity for reordering is the same; what differs is the CONTENT — a tighter crop drops the background air, so the activations it produces may simply be small enough that seven mantissa bits round the reordering away.
