title: The cache band 0.20-0.80 has never been widened - whole-stack reads every slice we cached and no slice we did not
description:
THE LAST LIVE FORM OF 'we discard data' (see the 2026-08-18 re-audit on knee-jk3, which refutes the other three).

The cache samples slices from the 0.20-0.80 fraction of each series. Whole-stack reading, our largest measured win (+0.0147), shows the model every slice IN THE CACHE - and therefore no slice outside that band, in any arm we have ever run. knee-ezz varied the DENSITY inside the band (12 vs 20 slices, deconfounded with max pooling: -0.0001) and closed as refuted. Density inside a band and the width of the band are different questions, and only the first was asked.

MECHANISM, and why it can plausibly clear the 1.5% bar where the density arm could not: the band was chosen to skip the empty end-slices of a sagittal series, which is a sound default for a mid-joint finding. Five of the twelve targets are meniscus/ligament and the meniscal horns sit toward the PERIPHERY of the joint, not its middle - anterior and posterior horns, and the medial/lateral extremes, are exactly what a centred 60% crop of the stack is most likely to clip. That is a targeted anatomical prediction, not 'more data is better': it predicts the gain concentrates in the meniscus labels and is near zero on the central ones, which is a checkable claim the per-label holdout can settle.

COST is on the cheap axis by the cache's own docstring - bytes are linear in slices, quadratic in resolution - and a wider band at the SAME slice count costs nothing at all in bytes, only in what each slice covers. Two variants worth one cache each: (a) same 12 slices spread over 0.10-0.90, which is free and isolates band width from slice count; (b) more slices to hold density constant while widening, which prices the two together.

CONSTRAINT that PROVES it: per-label deltas, not the mean. The mechanism names WHICH labels should move (meniscus/ligament, the peripheral findings) and predicts near-zero on the rest. A uniform lift across all twelve would refute the stated mechanism even if the mean rose, and should be read as something else - most likely the encoder simply liking a different field of view.

BLOCKED ON GPU for the arm; the cache build itself is CPU/IO and can run whenever.
design: PRE-REGISTRATION IS HARDER THAN ScaleProfile AND MUST NOT BE GUESSED. The proving constraint (per-label deltas: peripheral structures move, central ones do not) needs a table like anatomy.ScaleProfile's FOCAL/REGIONAL split, written before the arm runs. It does not transfer, because the band trims a DIFFERENT anatomical direction per plane: sagittal slices run medial-lateral, coronal anterior-posterior, axial superior-inferior. So a peripheral/central class is a property of (finding, the planes it is READ on), not of the finding — the MCL is the most medial structure in the knee and is still CENTRAL for this arm, because ANATOMY reads it on coronal only and a coronal band cut removes anterior and posterior slices, not medial ones. A first pass over the twelve puts menisci, both OA compartments, effusion, Baker's, contusion and fracture on the peripheral side and only ACL, MCL and synovitis on the central one. A 9-3 split with the majority peripheral cannot produce a two-sided prediction, so the arm would read as a UNIFORM LIFT whichever way it went — which is precisely the unfalsifiable shape ScaleProfile's docstring was written to avoid. Do not ship a table under time pressure. Either derive the classes from the measured per-slot geometry in kneemri/corpus/band_coverage.py (cut mm per slot, already computed) rather than by eye, or drop the per-label constraint and prove the arm on a per-slot ablation instead.
notes: ANSWERED 2026-08-19 by the band_wide arm. 0.20-0.80 -> 0.10-0.90 at constant mm-per-slice (16 slices) reads 0.8553 against the control's 0.8525: +0.0028, directional on the mean, and the per-label pattern is the substance — MCL +0.0133, Synovitis +0.0083, Fracture +0.0074, Contusion +0.0072, ACL +0.0071, menisci flat, Medial OA -0.0088. The outer tenth at each end of a medial-to-lateral band is the COLLATERALS, not the menisci. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-19_the-outer-band-holds-the-collaterals.md. Follow-up band_dense (20 slices, same band) is running to test whether the OA loss is max-pool dilution.

description:

WHAT THE POOL ACTUALLY VARIES:
  member                        scheme     train_size  variant   slice_pooling
  calibrated_targets_s2026      canonical      0       small     max

WHY THAT IS THE P1: the decode path is the only ensemble axis measured to transfer to the board at MORE than the usual compression — collapsing three members onto one pixel group cost 0.0059 offline and 0.014 on the board, 2.4x (README, knee-7d1). Every other axis is now measured and closed: count saturates at four (+0.0008 for a sixth member), per-label selection has NEGATIVE oracle headroom (knee-vjmw), and the combiner is flat within 0.0005 (knee-qhzd). See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md.

THE ARMS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE WRITTEN AS ACCURACY ARMS: experiments/arms/crop80_tissue.sh and centre_tissue.sh. They should be read as DIVERSITY arms too, and that changes the keep/kill rule. crop80 predicts small structures UP and diffuse findings DOWN — a member that fails differently BY CONSTRUCTION. Its ensemble value does not require it to win solo: a member scoring below res392 on its own can still add more than a seventh canonical member, and the curve says a seventh canonical member is worth +0.0008.

SO THE READ IS: score crop80/centre_tissue by their MARGINAL contribution to the ensemble (member_curve with and without), not by solo AUC. A solo regression with the predicted per-label SHAPE is a pass on this axis, not a fail.

COST: each needs its own cache — 'experiments/arms/build_cache.sh 336 12 canonical 6 80 tissue' (and 130/tissue for the other) — which is the reason neither has run. That decode is the real price of this axis, and it is the price of the only lever left.
notes:
UPDATE 2026-08-19 (later) — the band reading survives a doubled pool, and gets an argmax-blind confirmation.

The holdout backfill landed, so the card-free greedy now runs over 22 same-split fold-0 members rather than
10. The ceiling moved +0.0004 (0.8661 -> 0.8665), a fifteenth of the 0.0062 floor, so the subset search is
spent over the larger pool too.

The part that matters for THIS bead: the first three greedy picks are all band-axis members —
band_dense (0.8578), then band_wide (0.8633), then depth_regions (0.8648) — worth +0.0070 together before a
single non-band member is chosen. Every other axis in the pool competes for the fourth seat onward at a few

ninth and is the first pick that does NOT raise the ensemble, sliceattn tenth at -0.0003,
lora_r8_v3small_224 sixteenth. res392_ws was a member of the 0.925 champion four.

Still unrun: centre_tissue.sh.
STATE 2026-08-19: the band half of this bead is now SERVED and measured, the crop/centre half is not. Band members that exist at fold 0: lr4e-5_ws (0.20-0.80 @12), band_span (0.10-0.90 @12), band_density (0.20-0.80 @20), band_dense (0.10-0.90 @20), band_wide, and band_full (0.00-1.00 @12) training now. The 36-record re-search then put band_dense first and band_span second in the greedy roster, so the axis paid where the bead predicted.

CROP/CENTRE REMAINS UNVARIED IN THE POOL: crop80_tissue (80mm, tissue centre) is the only member off 130mm/image, and it is not in the shipped four. That is the half of this bead still open, and it is the cheaper half — the arm exists, the cache exists, and no seated member reads it.

depth_regions_span (queued behind band_full) is the pooled wide-span cell and adds a group nothing occupies, but it is a POOLING x BAND cell, not a crop one; it does not close this bead.
MEASURED AND REFUTED 2026-08-19 by crop80_span, which is the arm this bead asked for. The all-ours pool's missing crop/band/centre axis was filled at the settled operating point: 80 mm tissue-centred crop on top of the 0.10-0.90 span, single variable against band_span (run_comparison names 'crop_mm 130.0->80.0, centre image->tissue' and nothing else). Result 0.8466, -0.0099 against its control. The pre-registered clause required the regional group to reproduce at 80 mm AND a positive seat; the group came out NEGATIVE on all four (ACL -0.0263*, Contusion -0.0198*, Baker's -0.0164*, Effusion -0.0079, three clearing the pair's own +/-0.0314), so the refutation condition fired. Seat value is +0.0015 (roster 0.8648 -> 0.8663), positive but an ADD as a FIFTH member, and comp/champion.json's FOUR MEMBERS principle records the best subset falling monotonically past five - so it is not a seat, and a swap is unavailable because the member loses to its own control. MECHANISM: in-plane extent and through-plane span are ANTAGONISTS, not independent diversity axes. The band widening buys regional findings by covering more anatomy along the stack; an 80 mm crop removes anatomy across the plane, and the two largest losses are the structures at the field margins - MCL -0.0265* and ACL -0.0263*, exactly what the widening had bought. Cropping in gives back what widening out paid for. Same substitution shape as depth_regions_span on a different pair of axes, the third time this family has produced it. CONSEQUENCE for this bead: crop/centre is not the free diversity axis it was filed as, and the 2.4x transfer argument never gets to apply because there is no seat to transfer. Diversity has to come from somewhere other than decode geometry.
2026-08-19 CLOSING. Both halves are answered: the band half was SERVED (band_dense first and band_span second in the greedy roster) and the crop/centre half was REFUTED by crop80_span at -0.0099 against its own control, with the mechanism named - in-plane extent and through-plane span are antagonists, so cropping in gives back what widening out paid for. centre_tissue.sh stays unrun deliberately: it is the same axis the refutation covers, and running it would price a variant of a mechanism already measured backwards. The question this bead leaves standing - diversity has to come from somewhere other than decode geometry - is knee-jk3's, not a fifth cell of this one.

that discards ~90% of the data' has to be re-read at 0.032. The design argument is untouched — we still

by member pool and ensembling rather than by data-per-step. Whatever remains is a smaller and more
specific target than the bead states.
notes:
REMEASURED 2026-08-19 07:44 from the live public leaderboard (1945 teams, downloaded not inferred).

US: rank 63 of 1945 = top 3.2%, score 0.928, 30 submissions, team 'Dimitar Terziev' / dimiturnt. Previous reading on this bead was 0.919 = rank 84 of 1758.

THE FIELD MOVED FASTER THAN WE DID, and this is the finding rather than our rank:
                 2026-08-11      2026-08-19
  teams            1095            1945
  leader           0.942           0.952
  top ten          0.928           0.941
  top 1%           0.928           0.937
  median           0.823           0.885
We went 0.919 -> 0.928, +0.009. The median went +0.062. OUR CURRENT 0.928 IS THE SCORE THAT WAS RANK 10 EIGHT DAYS AGO. A held score loses roughly fifty places a week at this rate, so 'keep the champion and be careful' is itself a losing move.

THE BOARD IS DENSE WHERE WE SIT: 0.928 -> 63, 0.930 -> 45, 0.932 -> 37, 0.935 -> 26, 0.938 -> 16, 0.940 -> 12, 0.945 -> 4. About 7-9 places per thousandth. Eight teams are tied with us at 0.928 exactly.

AND THE GAP IS SMALLER THAN OUR RULER. Leader 0.952 is 0.024 board above us; at the median 4.7 board-points-per-holdout-point transfer that is ~0.005 offline, UNDER the 0.0062 holdout noise floor. The whole remaining distance to first place is inside our measurement error, which is knee-7d1 restated with numbers: past this point the holdout can rank neither our candidates nor our distance to the front, and only the board arbitrates. Caveat on the 4.7: it was measured on member swaps and is a median over few points, so it is an order-of-magnitude argument, not a conversion constant.

title: RunComparison reads a recipe from one source, so a checkpoint-stamped control reads as unmatched
description: run_comparison.unmatched()/reader_change() call RunMetrics.recipe() only. 50 of 69 members wrote no metrics file and 36 of those stamp the full recipe into the checkpoint, so those pairs print 'recipe unrecorded, so nothing here can say the two runs are matched' when the fact is on disk. This is knee-bot limit (2): wsfold0_e6 is the control its argument rests on and it has NO metrics file at all, so metrics_recipe (which globs *.metrics.jsonl) can never reach it. Backfill.of already resolves both sources inline; that logic has no home. Fix: one resolver in kneemri/runs/metrics_recipe.py reading metrics-first then checkpoint stamp, used by run_comparison, holdout_backfill and holdout_metrics. PROOF: run_comparison --control wsfold0_e6.pt names the moved axes instead of refusing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cross-step pair memory: the ranking term sees 66 pairs, the metric ranks the whole corpus
description:
RankedObjective enforces ordering only INSIDE a batch of 12 (66 pairs from twelve neighbours the sampler happened to co-locate), while the competition scores one ROC AUC per label over the entire test set. A model can order every batch perfectly and order the corpus badly. Batch size is a VRAM decision here (864 images/step fills 26 GB), so the pair pool is set by the card rather than by the statistic.

RememberedRanking keeps the last 8 steps' DETACHED readouts (144 floats x3 per step) and forms the cross-step pairs in both directions, summing numerator and denominator before dividing so a pair counts the same whichever side of the memory boundary it falls on. ~17x the pair mass for kilobytes. Gradient flows only through the live step (MoCo-style fixed-target queue).

STATUS: code landed (1508d62), 16 unit tests incl. the empty-memory equality oracle, arm script + config field landed (f5157f5), smoked (loss 1.3792 vs memory-off 1.3438 — the term fires), queued behind final_fit.

FALSIFIABLE: gain must show in AUC and be LARGEST on rare labels (Fracture 314 pos, Synovitis 580) whose separating pairs a batch of twelve most often fails to contain. A falling loss with flat AUC = it found an easier objective, not a better ranking. Control wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457.
notes: Correction: no code fix was needed. kneemri.runs.metrics_recipe had already backfilled the recipe from each checkpoint's options block, appended at the END of the file; my scan read only line 1 and concluded the controls were undescribed. The comparison ran as-is.
close_reason: Refuted on the mean AND on its own per-label prediction. 0.8353 @ e6 vs wholestack_s2026 0.8457 (-0.0104). Per-label at matched best epochs: predicted rare-label gain absent (Fracture +0.0044 against a +/-0.061 interval, Synovitis -0.0144), damage lands on Lateral Meniscus -0.0426* and Medial Meniscus -0.0304* (* clears its own 95% interval). Confound reported: compile_encoder False->True. Unblocking it needed a code fix, not a run: RunMetrics.recipe() now falls back to the checkpoint's options block, so every pre-recorder run is matchable again. Recorded in experiments/README.md.

title: Published CC0 members are now a COST: all-ours beats the 24-member fusion by 0.013-0.021
description:
MEASURED on the leaderboard 2026-08-16. efficient v4 (2 all-ours whole-stack members) 0.919; trained v8 (strongest 5 all-ours) 0.911; fusion v10 (our 6 + the published 20, 24 members) 0.898. Both all-ours entries clear the mixed fusion by more than the 1.5% bar, so the jump belongs to the post-LoRA member POOL and not to the two-member configuration.

CONSEQUENCE: the fusion kernel is no longer the accuracy entry, and a slot spent on more published members is a slot spent going backwards. The 'diversity beats quality' rule that six earlier entries supported is BOUNDED rather than refuted: it earned its number while our members were weak and while half of them were somebody else's. What survives is about the spread — a member worth adding fails differently AND scores nearly as well — and the published CC0 members no longer clear the second half.

OPEN: the local ruler and the board now disagree in SIGN on member count. Holdout ranks the five above the pair (0.8610 vs 0.8581); the board ranks the pair above the five (0.919 vs 0.911). See knee-7d1.
notes: CONFIRMED ON THE BOARD 2026-08-17, submission 55583385: fusion x25 (our 5 + their 20 CC0) scored 0.894 against 0.919 for the all-ours pair — -0.025, four times the 0.0062 noise floor and the only delta of the day that clears the 1.5% bar in either direction. The offline penalty this bead measured (0.013-0.021) lands on the board with the same sign and a LARGER size, so the 2.4x transfer compression does not rescue grafted members: the holdout was not under-pricing diversity here, it was under-pricing the cost. The CC0 pool is closed as a source of members; every remaining entry is all-ours. Recorded in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md and comp/board.jsonl (fusion25_v2).
close_reason: Closed

title: kneemri/ is 76 flat modules: give the package a structure that can be gated
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-15: kneemri/ holds 76 modules in one directory, and 33 of them define main() — the package mixes CLI ENTRYPOINTS with LIBRARY code and groups neither by subject. core/ holds one module (paths). The reference layout in this portfolio is biohub's celltrack/{analysis,data,detectors,edges,eval,linkers,losses,models,postproc,training} plus core/{data,metrics}: subpackages by subject, with each entrypoint beside the subject it drives rather than bucketed into a cli/ folder (bucketing by KIND is the thing the code principles forbid).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: import-linter can only express a directional contract between NAMED layers. With one flat package there are no layers to name, so the one gate that catches architectural erosion has almost nothing to say — the 1078-edge graph is ungoverned. A structure is what makes the gate able to fail.

TARGET (8 subpackages, subject-based, entrypoints beside their subject):
  corpus/     what a study is and how pixels are read: acquisition anatomy laterality slots slot_reader slot_ties study study_cache cache_flags window_reader crop_centre prefetch folds build_cache dry_run decode_bench crop_coverage stack_coverage diagnose_laterality
  labels/     the target tables and the rulers: targets confident_labels label_combine label_power label_stability reader_agreement report_language ruler_check ruler_transfer supervision_gap
  models/     backbone model slot_head slice_attention lora ema
  training/   train trainer fitting objective patience report_supervision heartbeat head_trial
  inference/  holdout_predictions holdout_slab prediction_cache test_time members ensemble holdout_backfill member_readings
  evaluation/ scores holdout_record run_metrics run_comparison member_record member_curve metrics_recipe paired_floor ordinal_signal tie_divergence encoder_drift oof_oracle attribution ledger_check arm_check
  embeddings/ embedding_cache build_embeddings report_embeddings
  kaggle/     submission kernel_run mounts mounted_kit kit_check package_members

BLAST RADIUS (audited, all text-substitutable): tests/unit/kneemri/* mirror the module path and must move with it; experiments/*.sh and experiments/lib.sh; comp/kernels/*.py, comp/kernel_bootstrap.py, comp/verify_*.py, comp/witness_check.py, comp/*.sh; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; docs and interpretations that quote a command. THE KERNELS ARE THE RISK: they run against the UPLOADED kit, so a rename is only safe once the kit is re-uploaded — which knee-wgx already requires before any submission (kit_check --mounted must exit 0).

METHOD: one subpackage per commit, gates green each time, import-linter contracts extended as each layer becomes nameable.
close_reason: Landed in d02b6f6 (eight subject subpackages) + e1edc9b (five import-linter contracts, three modules moved to make them true) + kit-finder repoint and coverage-omit update in the same commits. Gates green, 558 tests. What the structure was FOR is now real: corpus/models/embeddings/kaggle/training all carry enforced directional contracts. The two axes still unwritable are filed separately.

title: Run the back-fill over the 65 checkpoints on disk, then re-read the ledger's per-label claims
description:
kneemri.holdout_backfill exists and is unit-tested (a49d033); what remains is the PASS. python -m kneemri.holdout_backfill --checkpoints <runs>/*.pt --device cpu walks each run, refuses the ones with no recipe or --fold -1 with a printed reason, and writes a DERIVED record beside every other one.

Cost and where it lands: an inference pass over ~880 studies per run, keyed through PredictionCache, so runs sharing a reading policy pay the decode once. CPU is enough - that is the point of the bead - but it is hours, so run it in the background and report which runs were refused and why (a silent '45 skipped' is the failure mode this project keeps paying for).

THEN the part that has value: run_comparison over the back-filled arms and state plainly which previously-reported per-label deltas survive their own paired floor and which do not. Every such floor prints INDICATIVE, because a re-derivation is accurate only to ~4x eps, wider than the +/-0.016 half-width being quoted - so a delta that only just clears is not settled by this. That is knee-3vh's second acceptance clause.
notes: 2026-08-15 18:55Z: the unordered 55-member walk was killed and relaunched in PRIORITY ORDER (pid 273172, log /tmp/bf_ordered.log): wsfold0_e6, extended_ws, intensity392_ws, slices16_ws, schedule_8 first — the four arms knee-3vh names as each 'improving' Fracture by +0.012..+0.037 against a +/-0.061 unpaired bound, plus their shared whole-stack control. All 69 checkpoints follow, but the acceptance clause only needs those five, and a CPU pass is ~hours per member (909 holdout studies, 336 px, dinov2-small), so a walk in list order would have spent a day before reaching the arms in question. The walk now announces each member before its pass (7f8a4c5) — the old one printed only on completion, which reads identically to a hang.

title: Back-fill holdout predictions for the arms already run, so their per-label claims can be re-read
description:
knee-mx17 makes every FUTURE arm pairable. The 65 runs already on disk predate the record, so run_comparison still marks them against the unpaired bound and the ledger's per-label findings remain UNREAD rather than kept or killed - which is knee-3vh's second acceptance clause.

The fix is an INFERENCE pass, not a training one: kneemri.holdout_predictions already loads a checkpoint and reads a fixed study set through the submission path, and PredictionCache already stores the (studies, 12) array keyed by checkpoint identity and reading policy. What is missing is a CLI that walks a run's checkpoints, re-derives each one's holdout, and writes it through HoldoutRecord so run_comparison finds it.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT. (1) The holdout must be the run's OWN split, taken from its recorded recipe, or the array is for the wrong studies and the join silently shrinks to whatever overlaps. (2) A re-derivation is NOT the training array - it lands within a tolerance, and on CPU that tolerance is the cross-precision one (4x eps), which is wider than a paired half-width of +/-0.016. So a back-filled record must SAY it was re-derived, and a paired interval computed from one is indicative, not exact.

Runnable without the card (device cpu), which is the point.
close_reason: Closed

title: A run throws away the per-study predictions it already computed
description:
knee-3vh's blocker is one line of I/O. Fitting.ranked computes the best epoch's holdout predictions (881x12) in memory; keep() persists EIGHT of those studies as a witness and drops the rest. So every per-label delta this project quotes is compared against a floor measured on someone ELSE's seed twins, because our own arms have no per-study predictions on disk.

Cost to fix: 881x12 float32 = 42 KB per run, zero extra compute, and the array is EXACT - it is the same one that produced the ledger's per-label numbers, not a re-derivation that could disagree with them.

What it unblocks: each arm's OWN paired interval (knee-3vh), instead of the 2.2x upper bound borrowed from a null pair of twins. Retro-filling the 65 runs already on disk needs an inference pass (kneemri.holdout_predictions + PredictionCache) and is a separate question; this makes every FUTURE arm free.
close_reason: Closed

title: The knee-1nn gate is eyeballed: encode structure scale so the crop arm's two-sided prediction is computed
description: knee-1nn gates a 99 GB multi-scale rebuild on ONE 80mm arm, and its prediction is two-sided and specific: millimetre-scale structures (ACL, MCL, menisci, cartilage) up, centimetre-scale ones (effusion, synovitis, Baker's, contusion, fracture) down. A uniform lift is a confound and a uniform fall refutes the mechanism. Today that prediction lives in prose in experiments/arms/crop80_tissue.sh and the readout is twelve per-label deltas a human eyeballs — which is post-hoc pattern-fitting waiting to happen on the one arm that decides the rebuild. Put the structure scale beside the anatomy table it belongs to (a physical property of the finding, argued in mm, NOT fitted to knee-dtk's observed split — cartilage lands on the focal side by physics even though it measured label-bottlenecked, which makes the test sharper), and have run_comparison print the two group means and the pattern the arm actually matched.
close_reason: Closed

title: ruler_check scores every member under one reading, not its own
description: ruler_check builds each checkpoint with len(SLOTS) slots, reads at IMAGE_SIZE, windows by GROUP and predicts in the fp16 default, from one cache named by CLI flags. That is the fifth site of the member-driven-load defect already fixed in member_curve, attribution, the serve path and Ensemble: a whole-stack member is scored three slices at a time, a 448 px member cannot be scored at all, a bf16 member is ranked as a function it was never fitted as, and an extended-scheme member gets the wrong head width. It is the tool that decides whether the local ledger can rank recipes at all, so a wrong reading here invalidates the ruler verdict itself. Fix: group checkpoints by Member.cache(root).key exactly as member_curve does, refuse a cache whose study order disagrees, and score through HoldoutPredictions.cached with member.window/precision so the stored holdout predictions are shared with member_curve instead of recomputed.
close_reason: Closed

title: attribution CLI names its cache by hand, dropping the member's crop and band
description: The fourth member-driven cache load. knee-jrvy fixed the oracle, the witness check and the curve; attribution.py built StudyCache from slices, image_size and routing only, so a member fitted on any other crop or band was occluded against the DEFAULT arrays. It publishes findings (border-only, depth spread) and the ring widths it blanks are fractions of a crop it was not reading.
close_reason: Closed

title: Every member-driven cache load ignores the crop and band the member records
description:
AUDITED 2026-08-15, immediately after the band became configurable (knee-5jse).

StudyCache.key now carries the crop and the band, so a differently-read cache cannot clobber the historic arrays. That closed the BUILD side. The SERVE side is still open: every consumer that loads a cache FOR A MEMBER resolves it by size + slices + routing only, and never passes the member's reading — so it silently resolves to the DEFAULT key and hands the member 130 mm about the image centre over the 0.20-0.80 band, whatever it was fitted on.

  oof_oracle.py:244    StudyCache(root.processed(), slices=member.slices, image_size=member.image_size, routing=member.routing)
  comp/witness_check.py:94   same shape, same omission
  member_curve.py:254  builds from scheme alone

This is load-bearing NOW, not hypothetically: the 80 mm cache is on disk for knee-1nn, and it is the next arm to run. A member fitted on it and scored through any of these three would be scored on pixels it never saw, with the fingerprint and the witness both passing — the fingerprint fixes size and group only, and the witness replays the training path.

oof_oracle.agrees(member, checkpoint) has the same defect in its purest form: it TAKES a Member and never touches it, comparing the published config against the module constants CROP_MM / SLICE_BAND / SLOTS. That answered 'does their reading match our DEFAULT', which was the same question as 'does it match this member' only while nothing could differ. It no longer is.

FIX: a Member.reading property (its Crop and its Band, the pair StudyCache already takes), passed at every member-driven load; agrees() compares against that instead of the constants.
close_reason: Closed

title: Slice band is the last reading rule recorded from a module constant
description:
member_record.py:217 stamps "band": list(SLICE_BAND) — the MODULE CONSTANT — while every neighbouring field (crop_mm, centre, tie, pool, slice_pooling, slot_pooling) deliberately takes the RUN's own value, each with a docstring saying why the constant was a bug. The serve path READS this field (Member.band -> MemberConfig.band -> submission read.band), and ensemble.py:94 documents that a band mismatch is invisible to every fingerprint.

Latent today only because nothing can configure the band: DecodeRequest has no band field, StudyCache.decode_one builds SlotReader without one, build_cache exposes no flag, TrainingOptions has no field. So SlotReader's band parameter is unreachable and the recorded constant happens to be true.

The hazard: StudyCache.key = f"{image_size}px_{slices}sl{crop.suffix()}{routing.suffix()}" carries NO band, so the first run that ever varies it writes to an existing cache's path — the same silent clobber the key's docstring already documents for slot count and crop, on the axis it does not cover. knee-c5n's unlabeled SSL corpus is exactly the consumer that would want a wider band. Tenth instance of the repo's named failure class, caught before it fires.

Fix: give the band the same treatment the crop got. A Band value object beside SlotReader with a suffix() that is empty for the historic (0.20, 0.80); Band in DecodeRequest, StudyCache (init + key), build_cache --band-low/--band-high, TrainingOptions.band_low/band_high + band property, and member_record stamping options.band. Serve side already reads it.
close_reason: Closed

title: ledger_check gives a clean bill of health computed over 15 of 69 runs
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15, no GPU. ledger_check globs *.metrics.jsonl only. On disk: 69 checkpoints, 21 metrics files, 50 runs with a checkpoint and NO metrics file. So the check reports '15 finished runs, 0 unrecorded' — a pass computed over 15/69, the wrong denominator, which is the failure class this repo keeps paying for.

Widening the scan to the checkpoints (each carries a 'holdout' float alongside its stamped 'options') and matching on the same 4-decimal quote:
  - 24 checkpoint-only runs are quoted in an interpretation but NOT in experiments/README.md
  - 11 are quoted in NO document at all: aug_fold0 0.8201, base_s7_fold0 0.8180, deep24_s2026 0.8213, labaug_fold0 0.8203, lr20x_s2026 0.7524, member_fold1 0.8305, member_fold3 0.8325, member_fold4 0.8306, nf13_fold0 0.8158, nf7_fold0 0.8121, shallow24_s2026 0.8143

NOT all 11 deserve a ledger row — member_fold1/3/4 are ensemble members whose 5-fold mean 0.8269 IS quoted, and nf7/nf13 are the runs made meaningless by the seed-derived-split bug. The defect is that the check cannot SEE them, so that judgement was never made by anyone; a run that finishes with no metrics file is invisible forever.

WORK: LedgerCheck gathers finished runs from metrics files AND checkpoints (metrics wins where both exist, NaN dropped as now), then the 11 get read one by one and either written into the ledger or explicitly recorded as not worth a row.

Found while checking whether report supervision had ever run: report03_s2026/report10_s2026 have checkpoints, no metrics file, and ARE in the ledger (rows 87-88) — invisible to the check but recorded by hand.
close_reason: Landed f59d0f4/44bae23. finished() counts a run on its checkpoint, record = ledger + interpretations/. 15/69 -> 65 finished runs; the 11 written down nowhere are now in experiments/README.md with the ruler caveat (nf7/nf13 are recorded at overlap-TTA scores while their checkpoints hold raw ones, so match-on-number cannot separate 'never recorded' from 'recorded under the other ruler').

title: A metrics file does not say which recipe produced it, so a per-label comparison cannot tell a matched control from an unmatched one
description: kneemri/run_metrics.py writes epoch rows only: epoch, loss, auc, seconds, per_label, vram_peak_gb. The recipe lives in the checkpoint (member_record.payload stamps vars(options)) and in the arm shell script, but NOT beside the numbers being compared. RunComparison then subtracts a control's per-label scores from an arm's with nothing checking that the two differ only in the arm's intended axis — the same shape as the config-recorded-consumer-defaults class, moved into the analysis layer. It matters now: knee-1nn's gate is a per-label read of the crop80 arm against the 130mm whole-stack control, and the control's own file cannot say it was 130mm. Fix: RunMetrics records the recipe as a header line, RunComparison names the options that differ.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing checks that a Trainer policy the run asked for is actually ATTACHED
description: kneemri/train.py:444-469 builds the Trainer as eight hand-written 'if self.flag: trainer.method()' lines. The design and reading ratchets both check the MANIFEST — a flag recorded faithfully and then never attached trains the OLD recipe and stamps the new one, which is the nine-defect failure class with the config half correct. A policy method added to Trainer and never wired into the builder is silent. Needs a ratchet that walks Trainer's policy methods rather than naming today's six.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two rebuild-from-config paths with complementary blind spots: the ranking tool cannot load focal or LoRA members
description: MemberPackage.load and HoldoutPredictions.load each rebuild a trained model out of a recorded config, and each spells the defaults itself. HoldoutPredictions.load reads slice_pooling, slot_pooling, anatomical_prior and encoder_layer but NOT pool and NOT lora_rank, so a member fitted with cls_mean_focal is rebuilt two parts wide and a LoRA member is rebuilt with no adapters -- both fail on load_state_dict, which means the tool that decides WHICH members we submit cannot score two member classes the trainer can now produce. One rebuild (StudyModel.from_config) used by both paths, with the defaults spelled once beside StudyDesign.
close_reason: Closed

title: slice pooling: three names, six spellings, and an unknown one silently stacks channels
description: StudyModel.per_slice returns slice_pooling in {max, attend} - so any name that is neither is treated as channel stacking. That is the whole failure class: members.py:277 and holdout_predictions.py:61 read the string out of a manifest and hand it straight to StudyDesign with no vocabulary to check it against, so a stale or misspelled name rebuilds a DIFFERENT function on different pixels and loads cleanly. The names are spelled raw in six places: the design default, per_slice's set, the module guard at model.py:157, the trainer's choices tuple and default, and build_embeddings. Its own docstring records that this already happened once - the guard branched on max while the module branched on attend, so adding attention left one site refusing a model the other supported. Give the vocabulary one home as a table, look the name up where the model is BUILT so an unknown one raises there, and read the trainer's choices off it.
close_reason: Closed

title: pool: the trainer cannot select the focal pooling, and the manifest stamps a literal
description: model.StudyDesign.pool selects how patch tokens become one vector per slice (cls_mean = class token + patch mean; cls_mean_focal adds the per-channel upper tail). Only the embedding path can choose it: build_embeddings and head_trial both take --pool, but train.py has no pool field and never passes one into StudyDesign, so every trained member is cls_mean and the focal variant is unreachable from the trainer. member_record then stamps the string cls_mean as a LITERAL, three lines under the comment explaining why crop_mm must be the run's own value - and members.py:252 reads that field back to REBUILD the design at serve. Wire the run's pool through, name the two strings beside POOL_PARTS, and give the argv sites choices off the table. Also: an ATTEND definition was inserted between POOL_PARTS and its docstring, so POOL_PARTS carries none and the orphan string is a dead expression.
close_reason: Closed

title: --print-key writes to stderr, so every cache build reports ARM FAILED with an empty key, and wait_for_cache still rebuilds the key in bash
description: Two defects on the same seam, both found by running the 80mm decode. ONE: build_cache prints the key through logging, which writes to stderr, so KEY=$(uv run ... --print-key) captures the empty string. The 2026-08-15 decode of 336px_12sl_80mm_tissue completed - 4407 studies, mask written, no slot-less study - and the arm reported ARM FAILED build_cache_ (no mask written) because it checked mask_.npy. A build that succeeds and reports failure is worse than one that fails. TWO: wait_for_cache reassembles the key from size, slices and scheme in bash, ignoring crop, centre and tie - so an arm waiting on 336px_12sl_80mm_tissue watches mask_336px_12sl.npy, which exists, and proceeds instantly against a cache that was never built. Its own comment says that is the failure it exists to prevent; it prevents it on one axis of four. Fix: the key is DATA, so it goes to stdout while logs stay on stderr, and wait_for_cache asks --print-key for the full reading instead of spelling it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two arms wait on caches nobody has decoded, and one of them gates the multi-scale line
description:
arm_check --require-caches now reports it: of 34 arms, crop80_tissue wants 336px_12sl_80mm_tissue and centre_tissue wants 336px_12sl_tissue, and neither exists. crop80_tissue is the gating arm for knee-1nn, so the P0 that survived the knee-jk3 audit cannot start until a decode has run.

EACH IS 33.4 GB and about the size of images_336px_12sl.npy; 965 GB free, so disk is not the constraint. THE CONSTRAINT IS RAM AND CO-TENANCY: build_cache.sh says RUN IT ALONE, because on 2026-08-11 a build beside a trainer had the OS kill both silently at 2200/4407 studies with no error and no resume — open_memmap(w+) recreates the file zeroed, so a kill costs the whole decode. On 2026-08-15 the card was at 16.4/32.6 GB and 51 percent with 57 GB of system RAM free, i.e. the other project was training, so a six-worker decode was NOT started.

RUN, when the machine is ours: experiments/arms/build_cache.sh 336 12 canonical 6 80 tissue, then the same with 130 image for centre_tissue (which is the disambiguation arm, so it is second). No GPU needed for either — this is CPU decode, and it can be done before any training permission.
notes: Both decodes done 2026-08-15. 336px_12sl_80mm_tissue and 336px_12sl_tissue: 4407 studies each, zero studies with no slot, coverage 42.5-98.5% per slot (identical to the canonical cache's, as expected - the router is unchanged, only the crop). arm_check --require-caches: 34 arms, 0 refused, 0 UNCACHED. The cache line no longer blocks anything.
close_reason: Closed

title: arm_check proves an arm PARSES but not that the cache it reads exists
description: arm_check exists because this project's expensive failures are arms that fail LATE, and it currently catches exactly one of them: a flag the parser refuses. It does not catch the other, which has the same cost — an arm whose reading names a cache that is not on disk. --image-size, --slices, --crop-mm, --scheme and --tie together pick a cache key (StudyCache.key), main resolves the card BEFORE it maps the cache (train.py:469 then :479), so the arm holds the GPU, raises FileNotFoundError on a memmap, and the queue slot is discovered burned. That is precisely the shape arm_check was built for, and multiscale makes it live: knee-1nn's implementation landed, its arm reads a twelve-slot cache, and no such cache has ever been built.\n\nThe check is free: parse the flags that already parse, build the StudyCache the run would build, and ask whether images/mask/index are there. It cannot be a hard failure by default — paths.yaml is gitignored so CI has no data root, and a queue legitimately builds a cache in an earlier slot — so it reports by default and refuses under --require-caches, which is what to run immediately before arming.
close_reason: Closed

title: The multiscale scheme is never driven from argv: nothing proves --scheme reaches the model
description: knee-1nn's implementation landed at b1384e1 (MULTISCALE_SLOTS = the six read wide plus the same six at DETAIL_MM=80), and the arm that gates it is blocked on the GPU. What is NOT blocked is proving the flag lands. --scheme decides three separate things in main — the CACHE the run reads (StudyCache.key carries the routing suffix), the SLOT COUNT the model is built with (len(SCHEMES[scheme]) at train.py:519), and the slot NAMES recorded on the member (train.py:523), which is what MemberPackage.scheme later matches to find the cache at serving time. Three consumers of one flag is exactly the shape of this repo's nine recorded config-vs-consumer defects, and the newest feature has the fewest eyes on it. argv_to_checkpoint drives main end to end already and runs in four seconds; it asserts the CANONICAL slot count and never varies the scheme. Add the multiscale case: twelve slots on the model, twelve names on the member with the tight half present, from a cache written under the multiscale key.
close_reason: Closed

title: KernelRun.run is untested: the loop that spends a submission slot
description: kneemri/kernel_run.py sits at 69% and the uncovered lines are 107-138 - the whole of run(): choose members, find each encoder mount, load, DROP a member that will not load, refuse an entry where none loaded, and hand the ensemble to Submission with the entry's overlap flag. description: TrainingOptions.fitted_trainer gated report supervision on 'if self.report_weight and self.report_vectors', so a run given a weight and no vectors file attached nothing and trained the plain recipe under the report arm's name, config and ledger row. Fixed: TrainingOptions.reports() raises when the weight is set without vectors. test_reports covers it; test_fitted_trainer extended to the switches it never asserted (bf16/fp16 autocast dtype + scaler, EMA, report supervision).

title: strongest() ranks a member with NO holdout FIRST, and the full-data fit is exactly that member
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15, cold, no GPU: sorted([0.85, nan, 0.84, 0.88, 0.80], reverse=True) returns [nan, 0.88, 0.85, 0.84, 0.80]. NaN compares False against everything, so Timsort leaves it wherever it started and reverse=True puts it at the FRONT. MemberPackage.strongest (kneemri/members.py:437) is exactly that sort, keyed on member.holdout.

WHO CALLS IT: every submission kernel. kneemri-solo is strongest(1) ('the single strongest member'), kneemri-efficient is strongest(2), kneemri-trained is strongest(5). So this decides which weights a submission slot runs.

WHY IT IS LATENT AND ABOUT TO STOP BEING: no packaged member carries NaN today. knee-7tq (P0) ships a single full-data fit, and a full-data fit has no holdout BY CONSTRUCTION - fitting.NO_HOLDOUT writes nan deliberately, because the alternative (recording the standing-in epoch index) had a final fit advertise 'holdout 6.0' and beat every real member. That fix moved the defect rather than removing it: 6.0 sorted first because it was large, nan sorts first because it is unordered.

CONSEQUENCE: strongest(1) returns the unranked member instead of our best, silently; strongest(2) returns [unranked, best] and drops the second-best; with TWO final fits the order between them is arbitrary. Every one of those loads, fingerprints, and predicts - the failure class this repo keeps paying for.

FIX: a member with no recorded holdout cannot be 'strongest'. Rank NaN LAST and say so in the log, so a caller asking for the best members never receives an unranked one by accident; naming a final-fit member for a submission stays an explicit choice.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that packages members including one with NaN holdout and asserts strongest(1) is the best REAL member.
close_reason: Closed

title: The epoch loop is untestable: extract it from train.main so the training pipeline is checkable without a GPU
description:
TrainingOptions.fitted_model and fitted_trainer were both extracted from main() because setup and loop are two jobs and only setup grows per flag. The LOOP was left behind, and it now carries every decision that decides what a run PRODUCES:

  best-epoch tracking (best/best_state, and the clone taken INSIDE trainer.evaluated() so the number that ranks an epoch belongs to the weights that epoch would write)
  the empty-holdout mode (--fold -1): mean = float(epoch) so 'keep the best' keeps the LAST, and reported must come back NaN or a final fit advertises holdout 6.0 and wins strongest()
  patience, which must stop the loop without compressing the schedule
  the witness travelling with the weights it was produced by
  save_partial on every improvement, with the SAME payload the final save writes

None of that is reachable from a test: main() needs a parsed argv, a mapped cache, a downloaded encoder and a DataRoot. Every one of those five behaviours is a silent-wrong-answer failure, and four of the five have already gone wrong once in this repo.

Extract the loop into its own object (kneemri/fitting.py) taking the trainer, the record, the metrics and the patience, and returning the best score, the state and the witness. main() then assembles and calls it. Unit-test the five behaviours on the fake backbone, and add tests/integration/corpus_to_checkpoint.py for the joint the unit tests cannot see: fit a tiny model, write the payload, reload it the way the kernel does, and re-derive the witness through the INFERENCE path — the claim comp/witness_check.py makes for real members, made in CI on a synthetic one so a reading defect fails a gate instead of a submission.
close_reason: Closed

title: Does a DELTA between two arms survive changing the ruler? Measurable now, no GPU
description:
knee-7d1's own follow-up, and the first version of it that costs nothing: 'compression is a claim about DELTAS BETWEEN MODELS, and one ensemble's LEVEL agreeing on both rulers says nothing about how a gap between two models transfers. Testing that needs two arms scored both ways, which is now possible for the first time.'

WHAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE WITHOUT A GPU. The published members carry out-of-fold predictions for every study and were fitted on report_labels_v2.csv with no annotation weighting, so the 58 radiologist-annotated studies are genuinely held out for them (knee-7d1 notes, supervision_gap.py). Arms therefore do not need to be trained - they can be built by COMBINING different subsets of members, which is a real quality axis: the ledger already shows 20 published members at 0.8355 where a single one sits far below.

THE MEASUREMENT. For a ladder of arms (1, 2, 4, ... members combined), score each arm twice over the SAME studies - once against the report labels, once against the radiologist annotations - and compare the DELTAS, not the levels. Bootstrap over studies, paired, because both rulers see the same 58.

WHAT IT ANSWERS. If the annotation-ruler delta tracks the report-ruler delta with slope ~1, the local ledger is choosing recipes on the right axis and only its LEVEL is biased. If the slope is far from 1, part of what the ledger has 'measured' is a property of the label reader. Either way it prices the instrument every number in this project is reported on.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ANSWER. The local-to-LEADERBOARD compression knee-7d1 measured (0.0107 local -> 0.020 LB). That needs the leaderboard. This is the ruler half of it - report-vs-annotation - which is the candidate mechanism supervision_gap.thresholds already named (our ruler calls 45.5% of cells positive against the radiologist's 34.4%).

LIMIT STATED UP FRONT: n=58 studies. Paired deltas are tighter than the +/-0.034 the level carries, but this ruler still cannot see a knob, and the arms must be far enough apart to clear it.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-15, no GPU, no slot. kneemri/ruler_transfer.py; interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-15_the-two-rulers-return-the-same-delta.md.

THE MEMBER LADDER CANNOT ANSWER IT: 1->2 is +0.0021 [-0.0087,+0.0142] on the report ruler and 2->4 is +0.0043 [-0.0037,+0.0124]. Four seeds of one recipe are not far enough apart at n=58, exactly as this bead's own limit warned.

So the arms were pushed apart on purpose - an arm blended toward a permutation of itself, a ruler being indifferent to HOW an arm got worse. Averaged over five permutation seeds:

  share   report    annot    ratio   seed range
  0.05   +0.0006  +0.0017   +0.97   [0.97,0.97]
  0.10   +0.0010  +0.0032   +0.98   [0.75,1.22]
  0.20   +0.0078  +0.0114   +1.17   [0.75,1.64]
  0.40   +0.0577  +0.0635   +1.15   [0.79,1.70]

ANSWER: a delta measured against the report labels transfers to the radiologist annotations at a ratio near 1, every seed range spanning 1. The local ruler is biased in LEVEL and unbiased in DELTA, which is the property that decides whether the ledger can pick a recipe.

AND ONE SEED NEARLY SAID THE OPPOSITE. The default seed alone gave ratio 1.70 with a paired bootstrap interval of [1.07,3.48] - excluding 1, and matching the ~1.9x compression knee-7d1 inferred from two leaderboard rows. Four other permutation seeds gave 0.90, 1.14, 1.21, 0.79. The bootstrap was honest about the STUDIES and silent about the PERMUTATION, an axis nothing in the harness was watching. The module now reports the seed range by construction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-7d1: report-versus-annotation labelling is REMOVED as the mechanism for the local-to-leaderboard compression - both rulers saw the same predictions on the same studies and returned the same delta. The compression, if real, comes from elsewhere (different studies, 20 members at submission against 4 out-of-fold, hidden-set composition) or is two points of scatter. Unchanged: only the board can settle it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Re-paste the three fixed kernel scripts into their Kaggle notebooks
description: e0ae10a fixed an unpruned /kaggle/input walk in kneemri-fusion (manifest search), kneemri-graft and kneemri-graft-verify (DINOv2 search, and graft's sample_submission search). Kernel scripts are NOT shipped in the kit — they are pasted into the notebook by hand — so the repo being fixed changes nothing about what Kaggle runs until each notebook is updated. title: The 248-second rglob the kernels fixed is still in the package, once PER MEMBER
description:
comp/kernels/*/find_kit prunes the competition mount by name and bounds its depth, after an unpruned rglob of /kaggle/input was measured at 248 s. The package never learned it. Three walkers remain, and rglob prunes NOTHING - the {train_series,test_series} filter runs after the walk has already descended and statted every DICOM:

- KernelRun.run:133 rglobs INPUT for sample_submission.csv - another full walk.
- MemberPackage.find (members.py:449) rglobs base for manifest.json - another.

That is >=23 walks before a single study decodes, on a hidden set far larger than the visible three studies the 248 s was measured against. It fits knee-b6p's signature exactly (COMPLETE, blank publicScore, slot consumed) and it is the cheapest of the three promoted causes to remove.

description:
Measured 2026-08-15 by 'python -m kneemri.kit_check --mounted': dimiturnt/kneemri-kit carries 4faac3d while HEAD is c302305, five shipped-package commits ahead.
