title: Oracle ensemble: measure the CEILING of member combination before building another member
description:
Stolen from biohub_kaggle 7b982b0, which advanced every cell by its GROUND-TRUTH velocity to ask what a perfect Kalman filter could rescue - answer 0 of 35 - and closed a whole lever for the cost of a diagnostic instead of an implementation.

OUR VERSION. On the fold-0 holdout, with member predictions we have already paid for:
  (a) PER-LABEL ORACLE: for each of the twelve labels take the ranks of whichever member scores it best. That is the ceiling of ANY per-label member weighting scheme.
  (b) PER-STUDY ORACLE: for each study, the best ranking any member gives it. A looser ceiling on any combination rule at all.
Compare both against the best subset member_curve finds by plain rank-averaging.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT NEXT MEASUREMENT. Diversity, not member quality, is what moved our leaderboard - five weak members scored 0.888 and two members 0.021 better EACH scored 0.882. Every plan we have (v3 as a diversity member, extended slots, LoRA) is a bet that combination has headroom left, and none of them has ever been priced against a ceiling. If the per-label oracle sits near the plain average, member weighting is dead before it is written and the diversity story is exhausted; if it sits far above, weighting is the cheapest gain on the board and no new member is needed to collect it.

COSTS NO TRAINING - inference over the holdout for members already on disk, the same pass member_curve makes.
design: Extend kneemri.member_curve, which already loads holdout predictions per member and groups by cache. The oracle is argmax over members of the per-label AUC, not a fit - no risk of the oracle itself overfitting beyond the obvious (it is an upper bound BY CONSTRUCTION and must be reported as one, never as a score we could achieve).
acceptance_criteria: Two numbers against the plain best subset: per-label oracle and per-study oracle, both stated as ceilings. The verdict is which of 'build another member' and 'weight the members we have' is worth wall-time.
notes: AUDIT 2026-08-17: part (a) is ALREADY BUILT - MemberCurve.oracle (kneemri/evaluation/member_curve.py:119) takes the per-label max over members and logs it beside the plain rank-average and the best single, with the headroom delta, and MemberCurve.logged prints it on every member_curve run. So the per-label ceiling costs nothing extra to obtain; it comes out of the 7-member run started 06:16 UTC today. What remains of this bead is (b) the per-study oracle, and (b) is worth re-examining before it is written: 'the best ranking any member gives each study' selects with the answers at study granularity, which drives the ceiling toward a number near 1.0 and prices no reachable scheme. A ceiling that no rule could approach does not gate work the way the per-label one does. Proposal: close this bead on the per-label number when the run reports it, and only open a successor if the per-label headroom is large enough that a finer ceiling would change a decision.
close_reason: MEASURED 2026-08-17: per-label oracle 0.8590 vs plain rank-average 0.8588 over seven members - headroom +0.0002, two orders inside the 0.0062 floor. Per-label member weighting is dead, and so is another member of the same kind as a route to it. Part (b), the per-study oracle, is deliberately NOT built: selecting per study uses the answers at a granularity no rule approaches, so its ceiling prices nothing. Recorded in experiments/README.md and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the-oracle-ceiling-is-the-average.md.

title: The witness tolerance was tighter than bf16's own epsilon
description:
witness_check carried TOLERANCE = 2e-3, inherited from the fingerprint and documented as 'above GPU noise' - true when training ran in float32 or float16, false the day bf16 landed. bfloat16 keeps float32's exponent and spends seven bits on the mantissa, so its eps is 2^-7 = 7.8e-3, FOUR TIMES the gate.

The check would refuse every bf16 member, correctly by its own rule and wrongly in fact. A gate that cries wolf is a gate someone switches off before a real refusal arrives - and this one runs as step 2b of prepare_submission.sh, so it blocks entries.

MEASURED on sliceattn_s2026 (fp16 witness) re-derived in float32: max 2.34e-3 over all 96 numbers, mean 4.3e-4, median 2.7e-4, nothing above 1e-2, every label moved about equally. The shape of arithmetic noise. The four reading defects this check exists for moved predictions 0.05-0.5 and concentrated in some labels while sparing others.
design: tolerance(precision) derives the bound from torch.finfo(dtype).eps rather than a constant. Open question the multi-member run answers: 2.34e-3 is 2.4x fp16's eps, so a single eps is the wrong model for a 12-block transformer's accumulated rounding - the bound may need a measured multiple.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on 2026-08-13 by witness_check across four members: 4 ok, 0 refused, and a deliberately flipped manifest refused at 0.407 against 0.00391.

title: v3+LoRA: the one axis the DINOv3 verdict never varied
description:
Every DINOv3 run inherited DINOv2's adaptation recipe (six blocks rewritten at 8e-6). The 2026-08-13 interpretation ruled out patch grid (441 patches vs 196 bought 0.0023, inside the floor) and capacity (v3-S+ scored 0.0045 WORSE than v3-S), leaving ADAPTATION as the untested axis behind a -0.038 deficit.

MECHANISM: v3 carries LayerScale (per-channel learned gain, init small) and RoPE; v2 has neither. A backbone rate chosen for v2 is not obviously the right step for v3, and an oversized step on those gammas degrades exactly the fine local structure the per-label table says v3 lost - Baker's -0.115, lateral meniscus -0.077, against effusion -0.014. LoRA freezes gammas, RoPE and base weights bit-identical and confines the update to rank 8.

BONUS PROPERTY: LoRA makes the rate comparable ACROSS encoders where fine-tuning could not - the adapters are zero-init new parameters in both cases, so 5e-4 means the same thing on v2 and v3.
design: lora.sh gains variant/size arguments; run is v3small at 224 (its native read, 104s/epoch, ~21 min for 12 epochs). Control is dinov3_v3small_224_s2026 = 0.8057, same encoder, same read, fine-tuned recipe. Second control is lora_r8_small_336 on DINOv2, which says whether rank 8 carries enough capacity at all.
acceptance_criteria: Near 0.84: the encoder was never the problem, our fine-tuning was destroying it - a finding that applies back to DINOv2 and reopens the committed interpretation. Still near 0.80: the representation verdict hardens and the scope caveat closes.
notes: FINAL 2026-08-13: best 0.8217 at epoch 9 of 12, against fine-tuned v3's best 0.8057. +0.0160, three times the 0.0053 floor - better than the interim +0.0136.
close_reason: CONFIRMED and measured: v3+LoRA reaches 0.8217 against fine-tuned v3's 0.8057, +0.0160, three times the floor, and ahead at every matched epoch. The hypothesis was right - DINOv3's deficit was PARTLY our adaptation recipe, and freezing the base (gammas, RoPE, patch embedding, norms) recovers about a third of it. It does not overturn the DINOv2 verdict: 0.819 is still 0.027 short of 0.8457. Recorded in the interpretation and the ledger. The contrast with DINOv2, where the same method is BEHIND at every matched epoch, is the finding: our recipe is right for v2 and wrong for v3.

title: The three-group entry FITS: 1708 units/study against 4140 that already completed
description:
2026-08-12 15:46Z. The last entry died on a resource limit nobody had computed (knee OOM, fusion v2 -> 0.500), so this one is costed before it is built.

THE UNIT is one 336-px image-forward through a 384-wide encoder. A member's cost per study is (slices if whole-stack else 3 x windows) x slots, scaled by (read/336)^2 for pixels and by width/384 for the encoder:

  wsfold0_e6              72     whole-stack, 6 slots
  sliceattn_s2026         72
  slices16_ws_s2026       96     16 cached slices
  lr5x_d6_s2026          180     windowed, 10 overlapping windows
  max12_s2026            180
  max20_s2026            324     20 slices windowed
  large_deep_rank24      486     180 images x 2.7 for a 1024-wide encoder
  res392_ws_s2026         98     72 x (392/336)^2
  intensity392_ws_s2026   98
  extended (9 slots)     108
  TOTAL                 1708 units/study

THE ENTRY THAT COMPLETED, for scale: 23 windowed members x 180 = 4140 units/study, and that is the all-small assumption — if the published members are base it was 8280. So a THREE-GROUP entry with everything we own costs 2.4x LESS than one that already ran inside the limit.

COMPUTE IS THEREFORE NOT THE CONSTRAINT, and that inverts the question: we are not choosing members to fit a budget, we are choosing them because the curve says more than five stops helping (0.8601 at five, 0.8596 at six, 0.8590 at eight). Diversity is the scarce thing, not time.

WHAT IS STILL UNCOSTED: decode. Three pixel groups is three passes over the test set at roughly 1 s/study each in the preview run, so ~75 minutes for a 1,500-study hidden set against a 9-hour limit. Comfortable, and it is the number to re-check if a fourth group ever appears.

MEMORY IS SEPARATELY HANDLED: the forward is now bounded by IMAGE_BUDGET scaled by encoder width (864 for small, 324 for large), which is what the fusion v2 OOM cost us.
notes:
AN ALL-OURS ENTRY IS PACKAGED AND COSTED, 2026-08-13, using this bead's own unit model. It sits at D:/data/.../all_ours (512 MB, 6 members), built with no GPU and no slot.

    member                units/study
    res392_ws                      98
    intensity392_ws                98
    calibrated_targets             72
    sliceattn                      72
    extended_ws                   108
    lora_r8_v3small_224            32
    TOTAL                         480

480 against the 1,708 this bead judged would fit, and against 4,140 that ALREADY COMPLETED on the T4. Eight and a half times the headroom, so neither OOM nor timeout is a live risk. It is that cheap for the same reason the efficiency entry is: a whole-stack member reads ONE window (72 units) where a windowed member costs 180.

WHY THESE SIX. The leaderboard evidence says DIVERSITY beats member quality - a third member of our own recipe bought nothing while a different recipe bought +0.006 - so they are chosen to differ by MECHANISM rather than by score. They differ on five axes at once:
    read size      336 / 392 / 224
    slot scheme    6 slots / 9 slots (extended sees 83,297 slices no other member can reach)
    pooling        max / attend
    encoder        DINOv2-small / DINOv3-small (a different pretraining family)
    supervision    standard / calibrated / intensity-jittered
Three decode groups, which is exactly the three-group case this bead costed.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the field moved. The median rose 0.021 in two days while our best rose 0.006, so we fell from the 34th percentile to the 31st while gaining. And none of the whole-stack or 392 px work - about +0.021 offline - has ever been on the board; our best entry is still the mostly-grafted fusion.

STILL GATED on the offline curve (knee-uff), which must be re-run under midranks before it can rank subsets. The package existing is not permission to submit it.

title: Cached-embedding harness: a frozen-encoder proxy that makes a head experiment cost seconds
description:
THE ARITHMETIC. Whole-stack fold-0 is 4,407 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices = 317k images. Encoding them ONCE at the measured 940 img/s is ~5.6 minutes, and 317k x 384 dims x 4 bytes = 487 MB — it fits in RAM, let alone on disk. After that, training the head alone is a few matrix multiplies per epoch: SECONDS, against 320 s now.

WHAT IT BUYS. Every question that does not change the pixels or the encoder becomes ~free to ask: slot-head design, the anatomical prior, rank weight, weight floor, loss shape, slice pooling over cached per-slice vectors, report supervision weight, slot attention. Those are currently 66-minute arms each and they are exactly the class the ledger says returns ~0.005 — a knob-sized answer for an hour of card time. At seconds each they can be swept instead of chosen.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is a PROXY, not the model: a frozen encoder is a different function from one whose top six blocks adapt, and a head tuned on frozen features may not transfer. THE HARNESS IS ONLY WORTH BUILDING IF THAT CORRELATION IS MEASURED FIRST — take three head variants whose fine-tuned scores we already know, run them frozen, and check the ORDERING survives. If it does not, the harness answers a different question than the one we ask and should be dropped rather than trusted.

WHY NOW. It also unblocks the thing the ledger keeps asking for: the metric rewards diverse members, and a cached-embedding harness can fit dozens of heads on the same features in minutes. Head diversity is weaker than encoder diversity, but it is nearly free, and 'nearly free' is a different budget line from 'an hour each'.

COST TO BUILD: one encode pass writing a memmap keyed like StudyCache (size, slices, scheme, variant), plus a Trainer path that reads vectors instead of pixels. The slot/mask plumbing already exists and is shared.
notes:
2026-08-18: slot_mean RAN (the arm this bead was gated on). 12 epochs, best 0.8406 at epoch 6, against whole_stack fold-0 0.8457.

WHAT SLOT ATTENTION IS WORTH: +0.0051, one floor-width (0.0053). It is a knob, not a lever — which is
itself the number this arm existed to set: a future pooling scheme beating mean by 0.01 is now clearly
interesting, and one beating it by 0.002 clearly is not. Mean-pooling is also a near-free diversity
member (same parameter count, same everything else, 0.005 behind).

THE PROXY'S SECOND PAIR IS STILL NOT RESOLVED, honestly read: the fine-tuned delta is +0.0051, which is
INSIDE the 0.0053 floor, so the correlation gate should exclude it for the same reason it excluded
slice_pooling — scoring it would manufacture agreement out of noise. head_trial --correlate can be rerun
now that the fine-tuned side exists, but n stays 1 unless the gate is loosened, and loosening it to
admit a floor-width pair is exactly the move that would make the proxy look validated when it is not.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire a v3 member through to a submission: kit rebuild, dataset_sources, witness
description:
The encoder side is done (knee-8hn). What remains is untested because no v3 member exists yet.

1. THE KIT. comp/kit/kneemri_src is a built copy and still holds the old find_dinov2. It must be rebuilt before any kernel runs a v3 member, or the kernel will not find the mount it now has.
2. DATASET_SOURCES. Every kernel-metadata.json lists model_sources for the two DINOv2 mounts. A v3 entry needs 'dimiturnt/dinov3-hf' in dataset_sources instead — it is a dataset, not a Kaggle model.
3. THE WITNESS. The refuse path has never been exercised against a real member (knee-qws), and a v3 member is the first one whose encoder differs from the training default, so it is the strongest test the gate will ever get.
4. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. The DINOv3 licence requires acknowledging the materials in any published result, so the README must carry it if a v3 member ever scores.
notes: 2026-08-17 member_curve, seven members: dinov3_base_lora_s2026 (DINOv3-base + LoRA, 0.8269 alone - our best v3 member) does not earn an ensemble slot. best 4 = 0.8612 excludes both v3 members; best 6 including them = 0.8603; best 7 = 0.8588. The diversity argument for v3 does not show up as ensemble gain on this holdout, so wiring a v3 member through to a submission would ship a subset we have measured to be worse. Hold this bead until a v3 member either beats 0.8462 (the weakest CURRENT member) alone or a run shows it failing on studies the v2 members miss.

title: Submission budget: gate every entry behind the offline member curve
description:
2026-08-12 06:55Z, at the owner's instruction to start saving submissions.

STATE: 3 of today's 5 spent (3-member, 1-member solo, 23-member fusion). Two left. No auto-submitter is armed - checked; the only background waiters are training queues.

THE MECHANICS, stated because 'saving up' does not mean what it sounds like:
  - 5 submissions per day, reset 00:00 UTC. UNUSED SLOTS DO NOT ROLL OVER, so nothing accumulates by abstaining. Saving only avoids waste.
  - Only TWO Final Submissions are judged (rule 2.2.b). Those are the scarce resource, and they are chosen at the deadline - not automatically the last two submitted.

THE GATE, from now on: no entry is submitted until it has been justified OFFLINE. kneemri.member_curve scores every subset of members on the shared fold-0 holdout and costs no slot; every arm is fitted on that same split, so every candidate ensemble is rankable before it is submitted. Submit only when
  (a) the offline number predicts a gain over our best LB (0.888), or
  (b) the question cannot be answered offline at all - i.e. holdout-to-LB transfer for a recipe that has never been on the board.

WHY THIS IS NOW AFFORDABLE, where it was not yesterday: the member-count curve (knee-9pl) is measured, so we no longer need the leaderboard to tell us that more members help. The remaining open question - WHICH members - is exactly what the offline curve answers.

WHAT IS PENDING AND MUST BE READ BEFORE ANY NEW SPEND: the 3-member entry and the 23-member fusion entry. Fusion in particular sets the top of the count curve and decides whether mixing the published members with ours is worth keeping.
notes:
THE GATE WORKED, 2026-08-15, and it refused an entry I had been ready to argue for. The 24-member fusion - our two best-on-paper members finally admitted after the read-group fix - prices at +0.0001 over the 22-member shape on 48 fold-0 holdout studies. This bead exists to stop slots being spent on 'maybe it is better', and that is exactly what it did: yesterday's verified, fingerprint-checked, kernel-tested entry does not clear the bar.

Also worth recording as evidence this bead's premise is right: our FIRST two members buy +0.022 over the published twenty and the next two buy nothing, so the marginal value of a member collapses fast and enthusiasm about a member's own holdout number is not a substitute for pricing the ENSEMBLE it joins.

title: DINOv3 is permitted by the rules and blocked only by a license click
description:
2026-08-12 06:25Z.

RULES VERDICT (comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt, saved verbatim). Not banned.
  2.6.b  external data and models are acceptable unless the Host prohibits them, subject to 'reasonably accessible to all' and 'minimal cost'. DINOv3 is free and every participant can obtain it on identical terms - a license click on a free HF account. Passes both tests.
  2.5.a  explicitly contemplates 'pretrained models with an incompatible license' and does NOT require an open-source grant for them.
  3.6.c  constrains open source CODE, not model weights; 2.5.a is the specific provision for weights.

STATE: the HF token at D:/life/creds/machine/hfpat.txt is VALID (account mitkoTrz, read scope). The repos still 403 because the ACCOUNT has not accepted Meta's DINOv3 license. That is an agreement for the owner to accept, not the agent: https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m -> 'Agree and access repository'.

WHY IT IS WORTH A RUN. Published benchmarking (arxiv 2509.06467) finds DINOv3 beats medical-specific foundation models (BiomedCLIP, CT-Net) on several medical tasks despite natural-image-only pretraining, which also deflates knee-zkz's 'swap to a medical encoder' plan. DINOv3 is a straight upgrade of the encoder we already use rather than a domain gamble.

CHEAP TO TRY: patch 16 divides our 336 px cache exactly (336 = 16 x 21), so no re-decode is needed - only an entry in ENCODERS and a train run.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE BEFORE IT COULD WIN, neither blocking the experiment:
  1. The scored kernel has no internet, so the weights must be mounted from a Kaggle dataset. Kaggle carries only community re-uploads of DINOv3, no official metaresearch mirror; uploading our own copy is a Meta-license redistribution question.
  2. Winner obligation 2.8 wants the final weights as a public Kaggle dataset. For a DINOv3-derived model that means publishing OUR fine-tuned weights, which 2.5.a's carve-out addresses for licensing but Meta's terms govern for derivatives.

DO NOT use a third-party mirror to skip the license click: rule 3.14.a warrants that a Submission infringes no third-party IP, and the click is free.
notes:
2026-08-13 — CAPACITY IS REFUTED TOO. DINOv3 sits at ~0.80 whatever we vary.

  v3small @336   0.8080   441 patches, 1.5x native
  v3small @224   0.8057   196 patches, native resolution
  v3splus @224   0.8012   28.7M parameters against 21.6M, same everything else
  DINOv2-small   0.8457   control

Three runs, spanning a 2.25x range in tokens and a 33% range in parameters, land within 0.007 of each other and 0.045 below the control. Read size does not explain the gap (both directions tried) and neither does student size — S+ is if anything slightly WORSE than S, comfortably inside the floor.

WHAT IS LEFT is that our adaptation recipe was fitted around DINOv2 and does not transfer: 8e-6 on six unfrozen blocks suits an encoder whose blocks are already close to what the task wants, and v3 is a distilled model with RoPE and LayerScale. The owner ruled out spending card time self-tuning that rate, which is the right call — a rate sweep is our hyperparameters, not the data.

SO DINOv3 STOPS HERE AS A LEVER and continues as a MEMBER. 0.8057 is our weakest checkpoint by a distance and the only one from a different encoder family; it reads 224 off the 336 cache, so it shares that decode and costs nothing extra to serve. It is in the diversity curve, which is the only thing that can say whether failing differently is worth 0.04 of individual score.
close_reason: Done: licence accepted, weights mirrored as private dataset dimiturnt/dinov3-hf, three v3 arms trained and scored.

title: The 0.0062 noise floor is holdout SAMPLING error - more seeds cannot lower it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 06:08Z, kneemri.label_power over report_labels_v2.csv.

Hanley-McNeil standard error per label, on an 881-study holdout (one fold of five):

  Fracture          62 positives   SE 0.0311   95% +/-0.061
  Synovitis        116             SE 0.0230   95% +/-0.045
  MCL              153             SE 0.0202   95% +/-0.040
  ...
  Effusion         533             SE 0.0126   95% +/-0.025

  mean of 12       SE 0.0053

THE PREDICTED FLOOR IS 0.0053 AND THE MEASURED SEED SPREAD IS 0.0062. They agree. The floor is therefore not mainly initialisation variance - it is the sampling error of the holdout itself.

FOUR CONSEQUENCES.
1. Multi-seed cannot lower this floor. Averaging seeds removes seed variance, which is the SMALL part; the holdout stays the same 881 studies with the same 62 Fractures. This independently supports the standing ban on seed work, on a mechanism rather than a preference.
2. Any arm delta below ~0.006 is not measurable on this holdout, whatever it does to the model. That is not a statement about the method, it is the resolution of the instrument.
3. Per-label deltas need +/-0.03 to +/-0.06 error bars. Every per-label claim made so far was quoted without one, and two of them shaped a plan (knee-70w, knee-1dw).
4. The project's 1.5% bar is about 3x the floor, which is why it is the right bar and should not be relaxed.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY IMPROVE PRECISION: more held-out studies per evaluation, i.e. a LARGER holdout fraction, which trades training data for measurement precision - or accepting the mean as the only readable number and never planning on a single label. The second is free.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cut folds 2-3: k-fold was spending GPU that three untested mechanisms were waiting on
description:
2026-08-11 20:40Z. wholestack_folds.running.sh was running folds 1-2-3 sequentially, ~70 min each.

WHAT FOLD 1 BOUGHT AND FOLDS 2-3 DID NOT. Fold 1 (0.8505 against fold 0's 0.8457) turned whole-stack from a single-seed number into a replicated one AND gave a second ensemble member - that is the 'harden a number that already works' case. Folds 2-3 buy only ensemble variance reduction: they answer no question, and the standing rule is that k-fold is a PERFECTING tool, not a finding tool.

Against that, resolution (448 px), slice_attention and 16-slice whole-stack were all unrun, and each tests a mechanism that could plausibly clear the 1.5% bar.

title: publish.py exists because 'the kaggle CLI cannot run here' - that premise is now false
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while trying to submit, and it cost the first attempt.

WHAT publish.py SAYS IN ITS OWN DOCSTRING: 'the official kaggle CLI authenticates with a username + key pair, which is a different credential from the KGAT_* access token this project holds, so the documented kaggle datasets version / kaggle kernels push flow cannot run here at all. The REST endpoints take the bearer token directly.'

That justified an entire hand-rolled module: a three-step dataset upload protocol, a kernel push, and a bearer-token auth path.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE NOW:
  - ~/.kaggle/access_token holds a KGAT_* token that EXPIRED ON 2026-07-23, nineteen days ago. credentials.json records access_token_expiration: 2026-07-23T19:17. Kaggle answers an expired bearer token with its marketing HTML rather than a 401, so publish.py fails with a wall of HTML and exit 1 - which is what happened tonight.
  - ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json holds a username + key pair which AUTHENTICATES FINE. KaggleApi().authenticate() returns OK as dimiturnt and lists our three submissions.

So the credential publish.py was written to avoid is the one that works, and the one it was written to use is dead.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, tonight: the official CLI, which pushed both datasets and the kernel without trouble. One Windows quirk worth writing down - kaggle datasets version -p comp/members fails with a mangled temp path ('comp/members_manifest.json.json') because the CLI concatenates directory and filename; running from inside comp/ with -p members works.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, and it is not obvious:
  (a) refresh the KGAT token (credentials.json carries a refresh_token) and keep publish.py, which has the drift gate wired into it - _refuse_if_stale runs before authentication, and that gate has real value;
  (b) retire publish.py for the CLI and move the staleness gate into prepare_submission.sh, which already calls verify_kit;
  (c) keep both and document which to use when.
I would not delete publish.py reflexively: its VALUE was never the transport, it was refusing to publish a stale kit. That belongs somewhere regardless of which client pushes the bytes.

NOT URGENT - the CLI path works and is now proven end to end. But the docstring is actively misleading, which is worse than an absent one.

title: torch.compile and bf16: the last throughput levers, and why they must land at a boundary
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-11 of what we do and do not use, prompted by the owner asking directly.

IN USE:
  - Gradient checkpointing (--recompute-activations, added today). MEASURED: 32 GB -> 19 GB with the loss untouched, and it is what let the whole-stack arm fit at all.
  - SDPA fused attention - already on by default under transformers 5.15 (_attn_implementation reports 'sdpa'), so attention matrices are never materialised. Checked before assuming.

NOT IN USE:
  - bf16. We run fp16 autocast plus a GradScaler, which is autocast's CUDA default rather than a decision anyone made.
  - torch.compile. Nowhere in the tree.
  - TF32. Never set.

WHAT EACH IS WORTH, on this hardware and this loop:
  - bf16: SAME matmul throughput as fp16 on Blackwell. The win is robustness - no GradScaler, no scale-collapse - not speed. We have seen no NaN trouble, so this is insurance rather than a fix.
  - TF32: affects fp32 matmuls only, and under autocast the encoder already runs fp16. Near zero here.
  - torch.compile: the ONLY remaining double-digit lever. 10-30% is typical for a ViT. Compatible with our checkpointing because use_reentrant=False was chosen deliberately.

RISKS FOR COMPILE, to check rather than assume: the final batch of an epoch is partial, so the shape change triggers a recompilation every epoch unless batches drop_last or pad; and the supervised() two-readout path returns a tuple from one encoder pass, which is exactly the sort of graph that can force a break.

WHY NONE OF THIS LANDS MID-QUEUE: every control in the ledger - the 0.8272 baseline, arm Q at 0.8310, the whole-stack arm now running against them - was measured under fp16 with eager kernels. Changing precision or kernel fusion changes numerics, so an arm run afterwards is no longer strictly matched to the control it is quoted against. This project has already paid for one unmatched comparison when a 'new best' turned out to be a seed change.

THE PROTOCOL: land them together at a natural boundary, then run ONE matched arm (same fold, same seed, same recipe) under the new settings and confirm the score is unchanged within the 0.0062 noise floor. If it moves, the speed is not worth an unexplained score change. Record the seconds-per-epoch delta in experiments/README.md so the cost of the guarantee is visible.

Pairs with knee-5f0 (the batch/VRAM sweep): both are throughput work that must be measured on an idle card, and both should be done in one sitting rather than trickled in.
notes: OUTCOME 2026-08-13: both landed and both shipped a defect the audit did not predict. This bead worried about recompilation on the partial final batch (handled: batches drops it) and a graph break in the two-readout path (did not occur). What it missed was that torch.compile REBOUND over the module attribute, renaming every state-dict key to backbone._orig_mod.* and making five members unloadable - knee-5he. And bf16's arrival made the inference autocast's missing dtype a live bug, knee-5qt, plus put the witness tolerance below bf16's own epsilon, knee-6pi. All three are filed and fixed; closing this as the audit it was.
close_reason: Both levers landed (compile -21% at batch 2 measured, bf16 in use). The three defects they brought are filed separately as knee-5he, knee-5qt, knee-6pi.

title: Give VRAM back to the other project: find the smallest batch that still saturates compute
description:
OWNER'S FRAMING, 2026-08-11, and it is the right one: VRAM is a HARD partition (oversubscribe it and Windows pages over PCIe, which is how a 32 GB run ended up at 145 W of 575 doing nothing), while compute is time-sliced. So the objective is the SMALLEST memory footprint that still saturates the SMs - the free space is worth real money to the other project on this card, and the utilisation is shared anyway.

WHERE WE ARE, measured under whole-stack at batch 12 with checkpointing and an 18 GB cap:
  VRAM 19.2 GB | utilisation 95-100% | power 540-556 W of 575 (96%) | CPU 12%
That is COMPUTE-limited, unambiguously. A memory-limited run looks like the uncapped version of the same arm: 100% 'utilisation' at 145 W with 1% memory-controller traffic.

THE SWEEP, to run when the GPU is free: batch 12 / 8 / 6 / 4 at fixed everything else, recording peak VRAM, power, utilisation and seconds per epoch. Expected shape - VRAM falls sublinearly because weights, optimiser states, CUDA context and the checkpoint boundaries are fixed costs, so batch 6 lands near 12-13 GB rather than 9.6; power and utilisation hold until the batch gets small enough to go launch-bound.

MUST BE MEASURED ALONE. A second process on the card time-shares the SMs, so both would report ~100% utilisation and the reading would say nothing about either.

THE CAVEAT THAT STOPS THIS BEING A FREE KNOB: batch size is not neutral to the OBJECTIVE. The ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 pairs at batch 12, 15 at batch 6 - so shrinking the batch weakens the exact term we added deliberately. Any batch chosen for memory reasons has to be re-measured on score, not assumed equivalent. The lever that IS free is gradient checkpointing, already applied: 32 GB -> 19 GB with the loss untouched.

OUTPUT: a recommended (batch, vram-gb) pair per arm shape, recorded in experiments/README.md so arms declare a budget rather than taking what they find.
notes:
TWO THINGS MEASURED TODAY THAT CHANGE HOW THIS SHOULD BE RUN, neither of which needs the card.

1. THE CAP DOES NOT PARTITION THE DEVICE. --vram-gb bounds PYTORCH'S ALLOCATOR, and driver context plus kernel workspaces sit on top of it. Set to 30 on a 32.6 GB card it left no headroom and Windows paged GPU memory over PCIe rather than raising OOM: the run crawled at 40 img/s against ~1000, reporting 100% utilisation, 1.75 hours per epoch. A cap only converts thrashing into a clean OOM if it leaves the driver its room, and set too high it PERMITS the thrashing it exists to prevent. 26 is what every healthy arm uses. So 'VRAM is a hard partition' is true of the device and NOT of the number in the flag - the flag is a soft bound with an unmodelled overhead on top, which is exactly the thing this sweep is trying to calibrate.

2. expandable_segments IS A NO-OP ON THIS MACHINE. Torch prints 'expandable_segments not supported on this platform' at startup on Windows. Three arms carried it and none was helped; any fragmentation it was credited with reclaiming was never reclaimed. Do not include it as a variable in the sweep, and do not credit a result to it.

AND A CAVEAT ON THE SWEEP AS DESIGNED: batch 12 / 8 / 6 / 4 does not hold the objective fixed. The ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 at batch 12 against 15 at batch 6 - so a smaller batch is a different loss, not merely a smaller memory footprint. The sweep answers 'what fits' honestly and 'what scores' only if --rank-weight 0 is used, or if the score is read as confounded.

title: Runs are compared by grepping logs: no metrics file, no experiment tracker
description:
RAISED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-11, asking about mlflow/tqdm/periodic logging.

WHAT LANDED IMMEDIATELY: kneemri/heartbeat.py. One line per epoch could not distinguish a slow run from a wedged one, and that cost a quarter of an hour today - a whole-stack arm sat thrashing on a VRAM overflow and the only evidence was the card's power draw. The heartbeat reports step, loss and images/s every 30 seconds, paced by SECONDS because step cost varies ~20x across arms.

TQDM WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, on a specific ground rather than taste: every arm's output is redirected to a file. A progress bar in a file is a trail of carriage returns - the HuggingFace weight-loading bar already litters every log we own, and it is the reason grepping arm logs needs a 'grep -v Loading weights'. A log line is the right instrument when the reader is a file, not a terminal.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING, and what it costs: there is no machine-readable record of a run. Comparing arms today means grepping 'best holdout' out of a dozen log files scattered across /tmp and processed/experiments, by hand, and the ledger in experiments/README.md is maintained by ME rather than by the runs. That is how a result gets misattributed - it already happened once, when a 'new best' turned out to be a seed change.

THE CHEAP FIX, and the one I would do first: a metrics.jsonl beside each checkpoint - one line per epoch with {epoch, loss, auc, seconds, lr, vram_peak}. No server, no daemon, nothing to run; it is greppable, diffable, and plots from pandas in three lines. Data stays out of the repo like every other artefact.

ON MLFLOW SPECIFICALLY: it would give run comparison and a UI, and it costs a local server plus a tracking directory plus a dependency, and it wants to own the run lifecycle. For a single-machine project whose arms are already committed shell scripts, that is a lot of machinery for what a JSONL and pandas provide. I would only reach for it if we start running many arms per day and need to slice them by hyperparameter interactively. Worth revisiting then, not now.

NOT URGENT while the queue is one arm deep - it is a workflow cost, not a score cost.
close_reason: Closed

title: Three arms lost in one afternoon: one unexplained, one unproven, one I killed by editing it mid-run
description:
THREE LOSSES on 2026-08-11, stated separately because they have different causes and only one is actually understood.

1. ARM U (composed shipping candidate) died at epoch 7 of 24 and PRINTED 'ARM U DONE'. Cause unknown and will stay unknown: it ran from the old /tmp script, which piped into grep with no tee, so the traceback was discarded. The tee fix had been committed hours earlier and was never applied to the arm already in flight - a fix that does not reach running work is not yet a fix.

2. THE 448 px CACHE BUILD was killed at 2200 of 4407 studies. Its log simply stops - no traceback, and it was a plain redirect with 2>&1, so an exception would have been captured. That means the OS killed it. 93.6 GB RAM, 31 GB free at inspection, no OOM event in the System log. RAM pressure from a 63.7 GB memmap write beside a ~27 GB trainer is the suspicion and it is UNPROVEN. I checked VRAM headroom carefully before parallelising and never checked system RAM at all.

3. WHOLE_STACK died with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote' at line 21. THIS ONE I CAUSED. bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset as it executes; a sweep that rewrote every arm's trailing marker truncated whole_stack.sh under the running shell, which resumed at a stale offset and died. It took a two-hour arm with it, and I did it while fixing the marker defect from loss 1.

WHAT IS FIXED, each verified by breaking it:
  - run_train reads PIPESTATUS[0], so a crashed trainer cannot be reported by a contented grep.
  - The completion marker moved INSIDE run_train and fires on success only, where success also requires a 'best holdout' line to exist - a trainer can exit 0 having produced nothing quotable.
  - Verdicts tee into the arm's OWN log. They used to go only to stdout, so the resolution arm was gated on a marker in a file that could never contain it; that gate would have waited forever with the GPU idle and nothing reporting an error.
  - run_snapshot copies an arm to <name>.running.sh and runs the copy, so the repo stays editable while long work runs. ARM_LIB carries lib.sh's path into the snapshot.
  - wait_for_cache gates on the cache MASK, which build() writes only after the decode loop returns. The images .npy is allocated at build START, and a build killed by the OS leaves no log line to grep for.

COST: roughly 50 minutes of GPU on arm U, a 2200-study decode, and a two-hour arm - against an afternoon whose entire measured yield was sub-bar anyway.

THE RULE WORTH KEEPING: never edit a file that is currently executing, and when a fix lands in shared plumbing, check what is running under the old copy.
close_reason: The postmortem is written and every fix is verified by breaking it: PIPESTATUS[0] so a crashed trainer cannot be reported by a contented grep, the completion marker inside run_train gated on a 'best holdout' line, verdicts teed into the arm's own log, run_snapshot copying the arm AND (since 2026-08-12) the package, wait_for_cache keyed on the mask. Loss 2's cause - OS kill during a 63.7 GB memmap write beside a trainer - stays UNPROVEN and is recorded as such rather than as a conclusion.

title: Experiment definitions lived in /tmp - every number in the ledger came from an unversioned script
description:
RAISED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-11, and correct. Twenty-two chain scripts under /tmp produced every measurement this project reports. They were unversioned, unreviewable, absent from any diff, and one reboot from gone - so 'how was this number produced' had no answer in the repo.

This is the same failure the no-notebooks rule exists to prevent: a one-off run must become a committed entrypoint. A shell script in /tmp is a REPL session that happens to be a file.

FIXED: experiments/ is now in git.
  - experiments/lib.sh      shared plumbing, sourced by every arm
  - experiments/after.sh    queue an arm behind another's completion marker
  - experiments/arms/*.sh   one file per hypothesis, each carrying its control number and its result
  - experiments/README.md   the ledger

Three defects were fixed by the move rather than merely copied:
  - The data root is resolved through core.paths instead of a hardcoded D:/data, so an arm is runnable
    on another machine. paths.yaml is gitignored and machine-specific; the old scripts spelled it out.
  - run_train TEES full output to <processed>/experiments/<arm>.full.log before grepping. The old
    scripts piped straight into grep, so any traceback whose wording missed the filter vanished and a
    failed run looked merely empty.
  - wait_for exists so the completion-marker rule (knee-a9b) is encoded once rather than re-derived.

THE DIVISION: arms are CODE and live in git; logs and checkpoints are DATA and stay under processed/.

STILL TO DO: the arms that ran before the move (chains 1-15) exist only as their results in the ledger
and in interpretations/. Not worth reconstructing each as a file - but nothing new gets run from /tmp.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit: experiments/ is in git with lib.sh, after.sh, arms/ and a README ledger; all eight live arms syntax-checked and the path resolution verified against core.paths. New arms run from the repo, never /tmp.

title: Depth spread across windows is 0.036 - larger than every method change combined, and we sample uniformly
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 by occlusion on base+ranking (experiments/arms/attribution.sh), each 3-slice window scored ALONE over 400 holdout studies:
  best single window starts at slice 7 = 0.8332
  range 0.7976 .. 0.8332 across the ten windows, SPREAD 0.0356

For scale: the whole model with all ten windows averaged scores 0.8448, and the best SINGLE window gets to 0.8332 on its own. The spread across depth is larger than every method change this project has ever measured put together (rate +0.0051, pooling +0.0038, ranking +0.005, base encoder +0.0085).

WHAT WE DO WITH THAT TODAY: nothing. trainer.py draws ONE uniform random window start per batch, so steps are spent evenly across depths - including the ones worth 0.798. And Trainer.predict scores epochs on the MIDDLE window, which is not the best window (slice 7 of a 0..9 start range is off-centre).

THREE CANDIDATE MOVES, in increasing cost and increasing risk of fooling ourselves:
  1. INFERENCE, free: weight the ten TTA windows by their measured value instead of averaging uniformly. Risk: the weights are fitted on the holdout, so they must be cross-validated per fold or they are just holdout overfitting. Do NOT ship a weighting fitted on the same fold it is scored on.
  2. TRAINING, cheap: sample window starts non-uniformly toward the informative band. This is a curriculum, not a leak - the model still sees every depth, just not equally.
  3. UNDERSTAND IT FIRST. Is slice 7 special because of anatomy (the intercondylar notch, the cruciates) or because of the 0.20-0.80 band's geometry? The profile should be re-measured per LABEL - a meniscus finding and an effusion have no reason to share a best depth, and a per-label profile would say whether one window can serve all twelve.

(3) gates the others: a single global best-window is only worth acting on if the labels agree, and per-label profiles cost one more occlusion pass with no training.

RELATED: this is the same evidence that motivates whole-stack reading (knee-hek), from the opposite direction - that arm removes the window choice entirely rather than optimising it.
notes:
INSTRUMENT BUILT 2026-08-15 (ac98a6b), MEASUREMENT NOT YET RUN. The remnant question this bead was left open for -- does the max over depth concentrate on a few slices, and do the twelve labels agree -- had no instrument: depth_by_label scores each WINDOW alone, and Member.window gives a whole-stack member exactly one window, so it returns a single row on the very member that collects the finding.

Attribution.slice_importance takes one slice OUT of the stack instead, per label, and Attribution._slice_cost reports the two numbers that decide it (share of total cost on the dearest slice, and how many distinct depths the twelve labels pick). The slice is replaced by its NEIGHBOUR rather than blanked -- a black slice is an input the encoder never sees, so blanking would measure the model's reaction to a novel image rather than the value of what was removed; same reason slot_importance withholds through the presence mask.

WHY IT IS NOT MEASURED YET: the pass is ~26 forwards over the holdout (12 slices + 6 slots + 3 regions + 4 rings + depth). On CPU at 336 px x 6 slots x 12 slices that is ~15k image forwards even at 8 studies, and 8 studies puts the per-label AUC in the +/-0.2 Hanley-McNeil regime -- an unusable ruler. Needs a GPU slot: run experiments/arms/attribution.sh against a whole-stack checkpoint (e.g. calibrated_targets_s2026.pt) with --studies 400.
close_reason: Ran on band_dense_s2026, 400 studies. Slot spread 0.0213 with AX_FLUID_FS at +0.0260 (consistent with the 2026-08-11 rankbase24 reading, not degenerate). Rings produced for the first time: ring 0.05 = 0.6343, filed as knee-im48. Depth window sweep degenerate at 1 window, filed as a defect.

title: A training step sees 18 of ~180 slices: one window, never the volume
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-11, and it is the largest single change this project has measured.

THE CHANGE: read all 12 cached slices per slot per step instead of one random 3-slice window. A step goes from 18 images to 72 per study; with batch 12 that is 864 images through the encoder.

MEASURED, fold 0, small encoder, max pooling, rate 4e-5, against arm Q (identical recipe, WINDOWED read, best of 24 epochs) = 0.8310:
  whole-stack, 24 epochs   0.8413  peaked at epoch 6, then declined
  whole-stack, 12 epochs   0.8457  peaked at epoch 6 (still running at time of writing)
  +0.0147 on the control, and +0.0188 on the five members that produced our 0.888 leaderboard entry.

PRIOR ART SAYS THIS IS THE CANONICAL OPERATION, not an invention: MRNet (Stanford, PLOS Medicine 2018) combines per-slice features by an element-wise max over ALL slices of a series. Our three-slice window was the deviation. Found by looking outward BEFORE running the arm, which is how it should have been done for the knobs that preceded it.

WHY IT WORKS, in terms the earlier failures make sense under: the model was seeing 18 of ~180 acquired slices per step. The occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976 to 0.8332 across windows - larger than every method change measured here - so which window a step happened to draw was a bigger lever than any knob being tuned. Whole-stack removes the draw.

DOES NOT RESURRECT SLICE COUNT as previously tested: that arm was refuted under WINDOWED reading, where more slices at a fixed group of 3 means each group spans less tissue. Under whole-stack the mechanism is different and untested - see the new bead.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately not claimed: single fold, single seed. The fold ensemble now training is what turns this into a number worth quoting.
close_reason: LANDED and it is the control. Whole-stack reading is wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457, +0.0147 over the windowed arm Q, and every arm since is measured against it. The 'still open: single fold, single seed' caveat is void by policy rather than unmet - folds and seeds are both banned (owner, 2026-08-11/12), so the fold ensemble that was going to harden this number is not going to be run.

title: 9.9% of series match NO slot predicate, and three missing slots are 96% of it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 over all 4,407 studies (kneemri/slot_ties.py --lost, one DICOM header per series, no pixels).

THE PREMISE OF THIS ISSUE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. It claimed 17.4% of series 'never reach a slot'. That number conflated two very different losses:
  - STRUCTURAL: the series matches no slot predicate at all, so nothing can ever route it. This is 2,421 of 24,371 = 9.9%.
  - COMPETITIVE: the series matches a slot but loses to a denser stack, since one slot holds one series. That is the rest, and it is a different problem with a different fix (knee-evn).

THE CENSUS, and the reason it is actionable:
  Coronal|fluid|nofs   1139
  Axial|t1|nofs         621
  Axial|fluid|nofs      575
  Axial|t1|fs            57
  Sagittal|t1|fs         18
  Coronal|t1|fs          11
  83,297 slices in unrouted series - about 19 slices per study of imaging the model never sees.

NONE OF THESE ARE LOCALISERS. Coronal PD without fat suppression is a standard meniscus sequence; axial T1 reads patellar cartilage and the retinacula. These are diagnostic acquisitions the six-slot scheme simply cannot express.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND EXACT: the scheme covers three planes x two weighting axes only partly - there is no COR_FLUID_NOFS, no AX_T1 and no AX_FLUID_NOFS. Adding those three slots captures 2,335 of 2,421, or 96.4% of the structural loss. The remaining 86 are odd fat-suppressed T1s and can stay unrouted.

COSTS, stated honestly:
  - The cache gains a slot axis: 6 -> 9 slots is 35.8 GB -> 53.7 GB at 336 px and a full decode pass (~40 min).
  - A step costs 50% more encoder passes.
  - Every existing member has n_slot=6 and cannot load against a 9-slot head. The graft's 20 published members are 6-slot by construction, so the graft path must keep the 6-slot scheme - this forks the two, which is a real maintenance cost rather than a free win.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE WORTH HOLDING: a 2025 multi-plane study found single-plane sagittal beat three-plane fusion for ACL (0.976 vs 0.949), and our own anatomical-prior arm was neutral. More sequences is not automatically more signal, and this model already collapses its attention onto one slot (knee-1zk). The mechanism here is different - it adds sequences that are ABSENT rather than reweighting present ones - but the prior should temper the expectation.
notes:
2026-08-12 06:33Z — RE-PRICED DOWN by a coverage audit, before the arm spent a 54 GB cache build plus a 90-minute train.

CURRENT SLOT COVERAGE, from mask_336px_12sl.npy over all 4,407 studies:
  SAG_FLUID_FS    93.5%     SAG_FLUID_NOFS  62.6%
  COR_FLUID_FS    95.5%     COR_T1          64.1%
  AX_FLUID_FS     98.5%     SAG_T1          42.5%
  slots filled per study: 2->38, 3->391, 4->1350, 5->2287, 6->341

WHAT THAT DOES TO THE ARM'S ARGUMENT. The header said the extended scheme 'recovers 1,139 discarded CORONAL series against MCL, which is read coronally'. That overstates it: 95.5% of studies ALREADY have a coronal (COR_FLUID_FS) and 64.1% already have an ANATOMICAL coronal (COR_T1), which is the contrast MCL is actually read on. The 1,139 Coronal|fluid|nofs series therefore mostly add a THIRD coronal view to studies that already have two, not a first coronal to studies that have none.

WHAT SURVIVES: 83,297 slices are genuinely unseen, the three added sequences do cover 96.4% of the structural loss (2,335 of 2,421), and it remains in the 'more data' family that produced the only large effect here (+0.0147). But the expected size is now well below what the header implied, and the cost is high - a 9-slot cache is ~54 GB, must be built ALONE, and produces members with a wider slot embedding that cannot ensemble with anything else we own.

DECISION: keep the arm, run it AFTER the cheap ones (resolution 392, slice_attention), and stop describing it as aimed at MCL.

A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME AUDIT: 'slot_fallback' is a config field with NO IMPLEMENTATION. member_record.py writes it as a hardcoded False and members.py reads it back; no code anywhere routes a fallback series into an empty slot. It documents the published members' rule rather than one of ours. If a fallback is ever built, note the semantic cost the audit surfaced: the head learns 'slot k is this view', so substituting a different sequence into slot k makes that slot mean two things, and the presence mask stops distinguishing absent from substituted.
close_reason:
THE ARM ALREADY RAN AND WAS REFUTED, and this bead did not know it. experiments/README.md:79 - 'extended_slots | nine slots, +1,139 coronal series | 0.8459 | +0.0002 | refuted on the mean'. The bead's live decision line still read 'keep the arm, run it AFTER the cheap ones', which is exactly the failure the project rule names: a bead is the work queue, the ledger is where measured results live, and a bead can sit silent about a number settled days earlier.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT MEANS, since it is worth more than the bookkeeping. The nine-slot scheme put 83,297 genuinely unseen slices in front of the model - 96.4% of the structural routing loss, about 19 slices per study - and bought +0.0002 against a 0.0053 floor. That is a real refutation of 'more sequences' as an axis on this data, and it stands beside the 2025 multi-plane result the bead already held as counter-evidence (single-plane sagittal beat three-plane fusion for ACL) and beside knee-1zk (attention collapses onto one slot anyway).

IT DOES NOT REFUTE 'more data' generally: whole-stack reading, which shows the model more DEPTH of the sequences it already had, remains the largest change ever measured here at +0.0147. The distinction that survives is DEPTH of an existing view, not BREADTH across views.

The 9-slot cost the bead priced honestly (54 GB cache, 50% more encoder passes, members that cannot ensemble with any 6-slot weight we own) is now cost with a measured near-zero return, so the fork is not worth opening.

The separate slot_fallback finding is re-filed on its own rather than closed with this.

title: comp/ is outside the enforced lint scope - 115 findings, and the submission path lives there
description:
PROGRESS 2026-08-11: the unambiguous half is done and committed. Fixed in comp/: unsorted imports (2), RUF010, SIM117 (urlopen + file are now one with-statement), E501, PLR2004 (0x2000 is now _PRINTABLE_CEILING with a docstring), and MissingToken -> MissingTokenError (N is in our select; the rename crosses publish.py). Verified by RUNNING verify_kit, publish's guard and survey's CLI, not just the linter. comp/ now passes ruff's enforced select except T201.

TWO POLICY CALLS REMAIN, each a decision rather than an edit:

1. T201 (84 prints). print is the interface of an operator CLI (verify_kit, build_kit) and the output mechanism of a Kaggle kernel, where the notebook log IS the console. kernel_run.py already uses logging, so conversion is possible. Options: convert everything, or widen lint_paths with a documented per-file-ignore for comp/kernels/** and the operator CLIs. The second is honest and cheap; the first is the house rule taken literally.

2. pyrefly missing-import x2. publish.py does 'from survey import ...' and 'from verify_kit import ...' - correct at runtime because the script's own directory is sys.path[0], unresolvable to a checker without a search-path entry. That entry lives in template-owned [tool.pyrefly] config, so it is a copier/upstream change rather than a local edit; adding them to ignore-missing-imports would be a suppression hiding a real structural fact - comp/ is a set of sibling SCRIPTS, not a package.

Only after those two can lint_paths gain 'comp'. comp/kit needs no exclusion: it is gitignored and both ruff and pyrefly already skip it.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-13, and comp is now INSIDE the enforced gate - lint_paths reads 'core kneemri tests comp'.

T201: all 79 prints converted to logging (probe 50, graft-verify 17, survey 10, build_kit 2). The decision recorded here was already right for a reason I had not noticed: FIVE kernels - efficient, fusion, graft, solo, trained - were ALREADY logging, so the 'a kernel's stdout is its interface' exemption was dead on its own evidence, not just on kernel_run.py's.

THE CONVERSION BROKE THREE CALLS AND RUNNING THEM IS WHAT FOUND IT: print(..., flush=True) became logger.info(..., flush=True), which is a TypeError - logging takes no such kwarg. The linter was perfectly happy. This bead's own instruction to verify by RUNNING rather than by re-linting is what caught it. (StreamHandler flushes per emit, so behaviour is preserved.)

THE OTHER BLOCKER IS GONE: pyrefly's missing-import on publish.py's 'from survey import ...' no longer fires - 5 suppressed, and the 5 REAL errors it did find are fixed in code rather than ignored: a missing @override on Fused.package, two unannotated empty containers (mis-annotated as list[str] when passed holds slack FLOATS - the checker caught my guess), a None-narrowing pyrefly could not follow through all(), and a dict[str, object] subscript in witness_check.

ONE NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING: narrowing witness['studies'] with a bare isinstance gave an empty list on a malformed witness, which would have reported 'ok over 0 studies' - a silent PASS from the gate whose entire job is to refuse. It returns UNVERIFIED now.

24 further findings resolved: 13 PLC0415 and 4 S603 waived with real reasons (the kit is not on sys.path until install_wheels runs; pip installing wheels we mounted, fixed argv, no shell), 1 BLE001, 3 E501 wrapped, the rest stale noqa and import sorting. Verified by running build_kit, verify_kit, survey and both converted kernels' module level + output helper.
close_reason: comp passes the full enforced ruff select and pyrefly strict, and is now in lint_paths. Verified by running the tools, not by re-linting.

title: Capacity is not the constraint - but 'capacity is spent' overstated it, and the rate prediction was refuted
description:
MEASURED, fold 0, 24 epochs, matched: large + every block trainable + ranking = 0.8304, against base + ranking = 0.8283. +0.0021 for 3.5x the parameters and 185s/epoch against ~50s. Inside noise, far inside the 1.5% bar.

THE MORE INTERESTING NUMBER IS THE CURVE: large peaks at EPOCH 10 and falls to 0.8211 by epoch 23, on a one-cycle schedule still decaying. small and base peak at 13-15 and hold. A model that peaks a third of the way in and then gives back 0.009 has more capacity than the supervision can constrain.

READING: the binding constraint has moved from capacity to SUPERVISION. 98.7% of our labels are read out of report text; 58 of 4,407 studies carry an image-read annotation.

PREDICTION LEDGER, recorded before the arms landed - kept open because two entries are still unresolved:
  - REFUTED 2026-08-11. 'The encoder-rate bracket should be neutral to NEGATIVE - a faster encoder is more capacity to fit noise.' Measured +0.0044 at 5x the rate (knee-3om). Wrong in DIRECTION. The magnitude is sub-bar, so this refutes the prediction without overturning the thesis - but the thesis is now weaker than when it was written, and the honest statement is that the encoder was frozen too hard, not that capacity is spent. A rate that HELPS is not what a supervision-limited model does.
  - OPEN: slice coverage should still pay - it adds EVIDENCE, not parameters. (Refuted for slice COUNT at fixed GROUP, -0.0016; the real test is whole-stack pooling, knee-hek / chain20.)
  - OPEN: the full-data fit should pay - 4,407 studies against 3,527 is more supervision (knee-7tq).
  - HELD: a large encoder, if used at all, wants a SHORTER schedule than 24 epochs.

DOES NOT resurrect label filtering - refuted on two matched seeds. Supervision-limited means more or better-READ labels, never fewer.

PRACTICAL: large is NOT the recipe to ship. base + ranking at 0.8283 costs a third of the wall-clock for a difference inside noise.

CLOSE THIS when whole-stack and the full-data fit have both reported - the thesis stands or falls on them, not on the capacity number that opened it.
notes:
THE OPEN PREDICTION IS RESOLVED, and it was right. 2026-08-13.

  'slice coverage should still pay - it adds EVIDENCE, not parameters'
CONFIRMED by whole-stack reading: +0.0147, the largest single change this project has measured, and it adds no parameters at all. Resolution followed on the same axis: 336 -> 392 px, +0.0066, also evidence rather than capacity. The two together are +0.021 against the original control while LARGE bought +0.0021 for 3.5x the parameters.

So the prediction ledger closes 1 confirmed, 1 refuted-in-direction, and the THESIS SURVIVES ITS OWN REFUTATION. The encoder-rate result (+0.0044) said the encoder had been frozen too hard, not that capacity was the constraint; and the two levers that have since cleared the bar by a wide margin both add EVIDENCE. The binding constraint is supervision and coverage, not parameters, and that is now measured on three arms rather than argued from one.

WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR knee-f0a (DINOv2-large), which is still a P0 on the opposite premise: that bead says 'capacity and training time are the only two levers that have ever cleared the noise floor'. That was true when written and is not now.

title: The geometry laterality rule is unvalidated on the vendors that never write the tag
description: Header sweep over all 24371 series: the Laterality tag is absent on 50.7 percent of series and 50.0 percent of studies, and it is NOT missing at random - present on 84.3 percent of Siemens studies, 38.3 percent of Philips, and 0.0 percent of GE (868 studies), Toshiba (181) and Canon (45). So the geometry fallback is the SOLE laterality rule for about 24.8 percent of the corpus, and the 98.6 percent tag-vs-geometry agreement that validated it was necessarily measured only where the tag exists - Siemens and Philips. It has never been checked on GE or Toshiba. A left/right error there would suppress exactly the medial/lateral targets and is invisible to every check run so far. ALSO: this confounds the earlier refutation of the laterality hypothesis, whose first leg compared 'tag-resolved vs geometry-resolved' subgroups - those are near enough vendor subgroups. The second leg (rules agree 98.6 percent; asymmetry SMALLER on mirrored knees) is unaffected and remains the stronger argument. Cheap check: render a few GE and Toshiba coronal mid-slices after normalisation and confirm the medial compartment lands on the expected side.
close_reason: CHECKED AND THE RULE HOLDS. Population test with no eyeballing: after normalisation the mean coronal image of each vendor should resemble the tag-resolved reference and not its mirror. Correlation against the Siemens mean, straight vs mirrored - Philips 0.904/0.709, GE 0.925/0.730, Toshiba 0.913/0.721, with the floor set by Siemens against its own mirror at 0.780. A mirrored population would score at or below 0.780; every vendor scores 0.90+ upright. So the geometry rule agrees with the tag-resolved orientation on exactly the vendors that never write a tag. LIMIT: population-mean test, detects a systematic flip and not a sporadic one - a rule mirroring a random 5-10 percent would leave these numbers about where they are.

title: Test whether label CONTENT moves our score, before porting a 2000-line lexicon
description: REQUEUED at 24 epochs. The first attempt ran at 8 epochs and was killed mid-flight: 8 epochs is the regime just shown to be undertrained (24-epoch small scores 0.8205 vs 8-epoch 0.8081, +0.0124), so a label-content test there would have read as noise for the same reason eleven knobs did, and the whole point was a keep/kill on an expensive port. Design now: confident-only labels at seeds 2026 and 7, control full-labels at seeds 2026 (0.8205, already have) and 7, all 24 epochs, all scored against the FULL table so the struck-out arm earns no self-agreement credit. Two-vs-two against a 0.0062 floor is still thin but it is the right regime.
close_reason: Refuted with two matched seeds: striking the reader's own UNK calls (27% of pairs) costs -0.0073 (s2026) and -0.0056 (s7), same sign both times. Soft low-weight targets already extract the residual signal; filtering deletes real supervision. Written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11_what-actually-moved-the-number.md. Does NOT rule out a BETTER reader - that resolves UNKs rather than striking them - so knee-crl stays open at P2.

title: The slot head does not localise - it picks one axial slot for everything
description: RESOLVED to neutral. Corrected Baker's row (axial co-primary) scores 0.8073 vs baseline 0.8081 - indistinguishable at the measured 0.006 noise floor, where the first version scored 0.8005. One wrong row was worth 0.0068 of the 0.0076 regression. The structural finding STANDS and is the valuable part: the baseline head routes nearly every finding to AX_FLUID_FS (attention/anatomy correlation +0.127), so it is not localising evidence to the sequence that shows it. Forcing correct anatomy (+0.809 correlation) neither helps nor hurts, which says the slot choice is not where this model's accuracy comes from. Prior stays opt-in, default off: costs a parameter, buys nothing measurable.
close_reason: RESOLVED to neutral and recorded: forcing correct anatomy is 0.8073 vs 0.8081, indistinguishable. Prior stays opt-in, default off. The structural finding (attention routes nearly everything to AX_FLUID_FS) is preserved here and its live follow-up is knee-1zk, whose first step - quantifying the collapse as a score delta via attribution.slot_importance - is chain19.

title: Rebuild the ablation ledger on the recovered ruler
description: Noise floor is RULER-DEPENDENT and must be re-measured on report_labels_v2. On the old (lost) ruler two seeds spread 0.0012 (0.8233/0.8221, 30 epochs). On report_labels_v2 at 8 epochs, seed 2026 = 0.8081 and seed 7 = 0.8121, a spread of 0.0040 - 3x larger. If that holds with seed 13, per-slice max (+0.0018) is unambiguously noise and the anatomical prior (-0.0076) is ~2x noise rather than 6x. Do not restate either arm's verdict until the third seed lands.
notes:
2026-08-17 — REMAINING WORK DONE. Swept every absolute AUC quoted in code and docs.

.py (23 hits across 14 files, `0.8xxx`): all but one are internally-MATCHED pairs quoted to carry an
argument about a delta, and a matched argument survives a ruler change — the absolutes move together.
The one exception was kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py:47 (border-only 0.8006 against whole-image
0.8448), introduced 2026-08-11, i.e. sitting exactly on the ruler-rebuild boundary. It is now labelled:
the 0.0442 between them is readable, neither absolute is comparable to a ledger number quoted since.
ensemble.py:57 (0.8450, 08-12) and model.py:423 (0.8057, 08-13) are current-ruler and need no label.

.md: comp/SUBMISSIONS.md carries a date on every row, so each number states its own ruler — nothing to
do. The two READMEs were stale in a way that outranks ruler labelling and is now fixed:

  - README.md "Where it stands" still said our best was 0.888 against a board best of 0.895 that was
    mostly not ours. Since 2026-08-16 the board best IS all-ours (0.919 two-member, 0.918 four-member),
    both clearing the mixed fusion by more than the bar. Updated, with the diversity paragraph extended

title: The measured ledger's ruler was unreproducible: the label table had no fetch step
description: Every ablation number (0.8092 baseline through 0.8221 floor) was scored against a report-derived label table that was NOT on disk anywhere - a drive-wide search for csv/parquet written since Aug 5 under D:/data returned nothing, and no copy existed in the repo or the kit.
