title: Sample more slices at inference than at training (the .903 recipe's 12 -> 32)
description:
The scored .903 EfficientNet-B3 reference samples 12 slices per series while TRAINING and 32 at INFERENCE. We use 12 for both, and our cache is built at 12 — but the cache only constrains TRAINING. The kernel decodes the test split fresh, so reading 32 slices there costs nothing but decode time and needs no retraining and no new members.

WHY IT SHOULD WORK, and it is not the same lever as TTA: overlapping windows (already measured at +0.0025) re-read the SAME twelve cached slices in different groupings. Thirty-two slices covers more of the joint — a Baker's cyst sits at the posteromedial end of a sagittal stack, and the band sampler at twelve slices may simply never sample it. More windows re-slices what we have; more slices sees what we did not.

COST: decode scales linearly, so ~1 s per study becomes ~2.7 s. Against a kernel whose fixed cost is 542 s and a hidden set of order a thousand studies, that is roughly 45 minutes — affordable, and the existing degradation ladder (fewer windows, then fewer members) already exists if a run runs long.

MEASUREMENT, which is CPU-bound and therefore parallel to any training: decode the fold-0 holdout at 32 slices into its own cache, then score the SAME member at 12 and at 32 and compare. If it helps, it is free at submission time; if it does not, the twelve-slice band is already covering what matters and that is worth knowing too.
notes:
REFUTED, with a mechanism (2026-08-11). Scored on fold 0's holdout with member_fold0, matched on everything but the slice count:

  12 slices, disjoint (4 windows)    0.8281
  12 slices, overlap (10 windows)    0.8316   <- best
  32 slices, disjoint (10 windows)   0.8140
  32 slices, overlap (30 windows)    0.8137

Reading MORE slices is 0.018 WORSE, and more windows over those slices does not rescue it (0.8140 vs 0.8137).

WHY IT DOES NOT TRANSFER, which is the useful part: our encoder input is THREE CONSECUTIVE SLICES STACKED AS CHANNELS. The band (0.20-0.80 of the stack) is fixed, so at 12 slices a 3-slice group spans a certain physical thickness, and at 32 slices the same group spans roughly a third of that. The model is then shown groups whose through-plane extent it never saw in training — a different input distribution, not merely more of the same one.

The .903 recipe can raise its slice count precisely because its pooling is MAX OVER SLICE EMBEDDINGS: each slice is encoded independently, so more slices is more samples of a distribution that does not change. Ours couples slice spacing to the input through the channel stacking.

SO THE IDEA IS NOT DEAD, IT IS CONDITIONAL: it becomes available only if the group's physical thickness is held fixed while the slice count rises (sample 32 positions but keep the 3-slice group spacing at the 12-slice pitch), or if the aggregation changes to per-slice encoding. Both are real experiments; neither is the free win the recipe made it look like.

CONFIRMS SEPARATELY: overlap beats disjoint again at 12 slices (0.8316 vs 0.8281, +0.0035), consistent with the +0.0025 measured earlier on a different member.
close_reason: Refuted at 12->32 for OUR architecture: 0.8137 against 0.8316. Channel-stacked slice groups couple spacing to the input distribution; conditional revival paths recorded.

title: Intensity augmentation from cardiac-seg: the axis the public baseline does not touch
description:
IDEA SOURCE: ../cardiac-seg/core/data/dynamic/augment.py, where gamma / contrast / blur / noise are the transforms that measurably closed a CROSS-VENDOR generalisation gap on cardiac MRI.

OUR AUGMENTATION IS GEOMETRY-ONLY, and so is the public baseline's: rotation 8 deg, scale 0.08, shift 0.05, and a single global gain 0.10. There is no gamma, no contrast, no blur, no noise anywhere in either.

WHY THIS CORPUS SHOULD CARE MORE, NOT LESS: reports arrive in nine languages, so the studies come from many countries and therefore many scanners and protocols. That is the same nuisance variance cardiac-seg was fighting, in a harder form — and the hidden test set is where it bites, which is exactly the axis a holdout on the same corpus flatters.

TRANSFERRED WIDTHS (cardiac-seg's, adjusted): gamma (0.7, 1.5) at p=0.3, blur at p=0.2, contrast (0.85, 1.15), noise 0.02 — noise cut from their 0.08 because theirs acts on z-scored images and ours on [0, 1].

WHAT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and why the reason matters more than the setting:
- FLIPS. They flip both axes freely; a cardiac label is not side-defined. Here a horizontal flip undoes the laterality normalisation five of the twelve targets depend on.
- TRANSLATION. They measured it NEUTRAL and turned it off because a fully-convolutional U-Net is translation-equivariant. Our encoder is a ViT with position embeddings and is NOT equivariant, so the same measurement should not be inherited — it has to be re-run here.

PROVES IT: fold 0, matched against the 0.8201 augmented-geometric baseline. Intensity augmentation should help the HIDDEN test more than the holdout, so a flat holdout with a better LB is a possible and interesting outcome — which is an argument for spending a submission on it rather than judging it locally alone.
notes:
ARM C — INTENSITY AUGMENTATION IS +0.0019 ON THE HOLDOUT (2026-08-11), which is small and honestly near the resolution of a single matched fold.

  baseline  geometric augmentation only          0.8202
  C         + gamma / blur / contrast / noise    0.8221   (+0.0019)

CONTEXT THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST: turning augmentation on AT ALL was worth +0.011 (the never-called bug). Adding the intensity block on top of that is worth about a fifth as much on this measurement.

THE PRE-REGISTERED CAVEAT APPLIES, and it was written before the result: this transform targets CROSS-SCANNER nuisance variance, and the holdout is drawn from the SAME corpus as training — same scanners, same protocols. A same-corpus holdout is close to blind to the thing intensity augmentation is for. The hidden test is where it would pay, and a flat holdout with a better leaderboard was explicitly listed as a possible outcome.

So the result is compatible with both 'it does very little' and 'it does something the holdout cannot see', and this measurement cannot separate them. What it does establish: it does not HURT, which is not nothing — an augmentation that widens the input distribution could easily have cost accuracy on the narrow distribution being scored.

DECISION: keep it available but do NOT enable it by default on the strength of +0.0019. It is worth one submission slot later, when a submission is being spent anyway, precisely because the leaderboard measures the axis the holdout cannot.
FULL 2x2 COMPLETE (2026-08-11), fold 0, every arm scored on the pilkwang ruler:

                      pilkwang labels   v4_blend labels
  geometric aug            0.8202           0.8194
  + intensity aug          0.8221           0.8203

  intensity augmentation:  +0.0019 (old labels), +0.0009 (v4)   -> mean +0.0014
  better labels:           -0.0008 (geom),       -0.0018 (intensity) -> mean -0.0013

BOTH IMPORTED IDEAS ARE NULL on this measurement, and there is no interaction to rescue either.

THE PATTERN THIS SESSION, stated plainly because it is the most useful thing learned:

  fixing OUR OWN broken code   augmentation never called  +0.0110
                               missing LR schedule        +0.0061
                               TTA default left off       +0.0035
                                                          -------
                                                          +0.0206

  importing ideas from         intensity augmentation     +0.0014
  research and notebooks       better label table         -0.0013
                               32 inference slices        -0.018
                               label fusion               -0.0016 (vs best single)
                                                          -------
                                                          net negative

Fixing what we had was worth an order of magnitude more than adopting what others had, and every imported idea needed adapting or died on a mechanism specific to our architecture. That is not an argument against reading the field — the READING is what found the schedule, and the .903 notebook is what made labels checkable at all — but it is an argument against assuming a published gain transfers.

WHAT REMAINS LIVE: member count, the one difference we KNOW separates our 0.868 from the 0.888 graft. Two extra seeds on fold 0 are training now to price a member.
CORRECTION (2026-08-11): closed as 'null' on a single-fold matched pair, but seed variance on the same fold is +/-0.012 while these effects are +/-0.002. The correct verdict is NOT DETECTABLE at n=1, not null. Neither is worth re-running bigger — resolving 0.002 against 0.012 needs ~36 paired runs — but the record should not claim more than it measured. See knee-uxg.
close_reason: Null on holdout (+0.0014 mean). Kept behind --intensity-aug; the holdout cannot see the cross-scanner axis it targets, so it is worth one submission slot later, not a default.

title: train.py holds the best checkpoint in memory until the very end
description:
`train.py` keeps `best_state` as an in-memory dict and only calls `torch.save` after the final epoch. A process that dies at epoch 29 of 30 loses the entire fold — about fifteen minutes at the current recipe, and considerably more if the resolution or epoch count grows.

It nearly cost us already: the OneCycle off-by-one raised on the LAST STEP of the whole run, after every epoch had been logged and immediately before the save. The run was a total loss despite having produced its best epoch twenty minutes earlier.

It also makes the machine's own documented weakness expensive: suspend/resume on this box has a track record of killing GPU-adjacent state (the vpcivsp/WSL wedge), so an interrupted long run is a realistic event rather than a hypothetical.

FIX: write the checkpoint whenever `best` improves, to a temp path renamed into place so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file. Optionally record the epoch and the RNG state so a fold can resume rather than restart.

DO NOT APPLY MID-RUN: the five-fold loop invokes `python -m kneemri.train` fresh per fold, so editing the module changes the recipe for folds that have not started yet. Apply after the current run completes.
close_reason: Trainer.save_partial writes each new best atomically (temp+rename) rather than holding it to the end

title: cls_mean_focal pooling — implemented, unused by us AND by their shipped members
description:
`StudyModel._pool` already implements `cls_mean_focal`: class token, patch mean, plus the mean of the top eighth of each channel over the patch grid. Every published member uses plain `cls_mean`, so this is an untested axis for BOTH of us — an ablation, not a copy.

The rationale is quantitative: at 336 px the patch grid is 24x24 = 576 tokens, and a meniscal tear occupies a handful of them, so a plain mean dilutes the signal by roughly two orders of magnitude. That is the same argument the resolution choice was made on.

Costs one flag and a retrain (~5.5 min per member). Worth running against the settled recipe, not against the current one.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-19: the arm was the only missing piece and it now exists — experiments/arms/focal_pool.sh, arm_check passes (45 arms, 0 refused). Raised to P1 alongside knee-osw, which it pairs with: the two attack the SAME dilution from opposite ends — WHICH layer's patch tokens the head reads (knee-osw) and HOW they are pooled (this).

Everything else was already wired: StudyModel._pool implements cls_mean_focal (model.py:655), POOL_PARTS fixes the head width at 3 parts (model.py:31), and '--pool cls_mean_focal' has been a valid CLI choice all along (options.py:334).

The arm pre-registers its own null in writing, per the ledger convention: a third dim-wide part widens a linear head's input by 50% on the same studies and the tail statistic is noisier than the mean beside it, so if the findings are already carried by the class token this buys variance and nothing else. FALSIFIABLE CLAUSE: a gain must concentrate in the SMALL focal findings (meniscus, ACL, MCL, Fracture) with the diffuse ones (Effusion, the three OA columns) holding or dipping — those are the structure-scale groups the ledger already reads per-label results against. A uniform lift means the extra WIDTH helped rather than the tail, and the mechanism is not what moved it.

Control: wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457. Cost: no extra forward, no extra epoch time. QUEUED behind knee-osw.
close_reason: ANSWERED BY THE ARM, and the bead never recorded it. focal_pool ran: 0.8432, -0.0025 against the whole_stack control's 0.8457, flat inside the 0.0062 floor. Seat value -0.0012, so no seat either. The pre-registered clause HALF-HOLDS: the focal group (-0.0004) does beat the diffuse group (-0.0065), which is the predicted direction, but it is carried by the diffuse rows falling rather than the focal rows gaining — so the tail statistic did not resolve the small findings it was built for. Fracture +0.020 is directional only (one crossing in twelve, against intervals reaching +/-0.061). Recorded in experiments/README.md. The axis is closed: a third dim-wide part buys variance, as the arm's own null said it would if the class token already carried the findings.

title: Loss normalisation: we divide by total weight, they divide by element count
description:
Ours:   (BCE * w).sum() / w.sum().clamp(min=1)
Theirs: (BCE * w).mean()

With most weights below 1, dividing by the weight sum makes our gradients roughly twice theirs for the same batch, and it makes the effective step size depend on how confidently the batch happened to be labelled. Theirs is a fixed scale.

Our normalisation was chosen deliberately ("a batch carrying little confidence should not take a full-sized step on almost no evidence") and that argument is still reasonable — but it interacts with the missing schedule, and an effectively doubled LR that never decays is a good way to plateau early.

Test it as a PAIR with the schedule, not alone: schedule-only, then schedule + their normalisation, on fold 0.
close_reason: REFUTED. Measured -0.0022 on top of the weight floor: dividing by element count instead of total weight is worse for us. Their normalisation is not transferable to our weighting. Recorded in the ledger.

title: Weight floor: a finding the report never mentions should pull weakly, not not at all
description:
We set the per-(study, target) loss weight to the confidence itself, so a target the report never mentions gets weight 0.0 and is DROPPED from the loss.

They use a floor:  W = 0.25 + 0.75 * conf  (annotated studies keep W = 3.0, which we already match).

The difference is not cosmetic. Silence in a radiology report is weak evidence of absence — a knee report lists what was checked and found intact, so an unmentioned finding is more often absent than present. Dropping it entirely throws that evidence away; a 0.25 floor keeps it at a quarter of the weight of an asserted one.

Pairs with knee-<LOSSNORM>: our loss divides by the total weight while theirs divides by the element count, so changing the weights also changes the effective step size. Change them together or neither, and measure both against fold 0.
notes:
RAISED IN PRIORITY by the augmentation find. Both the weight floor (0.25 + 0.75*conf vs our conf) and the loss normalisation (knee-sbr) are now the main un-tested differences from their recipe, since the schedule is measured (+0.0061) and epochs are refuted as a lever.

Test them against the AUGMENTED baseline, not the current one — the numbers below the augmentation fix are all from an unregularised model and are not the baseline anything should be compared to.
close_reason: Implemented as --weight-floor (W = 0.25 + 0.75*conf) and in every arm since. Measured +0.0019 - kept on mechanism (silence in a report is weak evidence of absence, not no evidence), recorded as noise by this project's bar. Its dependency knee-sbr is now closed as refuted.

title: Decide whether to target the Efficiency Prize
description: BLOCKER RESOLVED - the track is additive, build the cheap kernel. Joined the efficiency leaderboard to the public one on team name, 897 teams in common: 61.3 percent identical scores, 38.7 percent (347 teams) carry an efficiency score STRICTLY BELOW their public best (median 0.018 lower, never higher). The efficiency leader is public 0.939 / efficiency 0.934. So teams hold both a high-accuracy public entry and a separate cheaper efficiency entry; a cheap submission adds a candidate rather than displacing the accurate one. Combined with the flat member curve (best single member beat the 3-member ensemble) and teams at our 0.888 sitting at efficiency ranks 29-50, a one-member overlap-free kernel is close to free rank. Remaining work is the kernel itself: strongest(1) + Submission(overlap=False).
notes:
THE KERNEL WAS BUILT FOR THE REFUTED ANSWER, found and fixed 2026-08-13.

This bead's own note records that the curve is NOT flat at the bottom - solo 1 member 0.868, whole-stack 2 members 0.882, 3 members 0.882, windowed 5 members 0.888 - and concludes 'a one-member entry is out'. comp/README.md:198 carries that correction. THE KERNEL DID NOT: comp/kernels/kneemri-efficient ran KernelRun(members=1, overlap=False) and its docstring still argued for one member on the grounds that 'our own member curve is flat', citing a SEED ensemble's holdout where members two and three bought +0.0018 and +0.0007.

So the decision was already made and written down twice, and the artefact that would have shipped was the 0.868 entry rather than the 0.882 one - 0.014 of leaderboard, which in this dense region is worth a few hundred places.

FIXED: members=2, and both stale justifications rewritten to quote the scored entries instead of the seed holdout - the kernel docstring and Member.strongest, which is where the next reader would have picked the same wrong answer up.

CAVEAT RECORDED IN THE FILE: strongest(2) ranks by each member's own recorded holdout, so it picks res392_ws (0.8523) and calibrated_targets (0.8495) from the all-ours package. Both are whole-stack, so the cost class is right - 2 forward passes per study - but this is not necessarily the same PAIR as the entry that scored 0.882.

STILL NEEDS THE OWNER: the kernel push and the submission itself. Nothing here submits anything.

title: Verify the corpus facts the plan is built on
description:
Every number in this issue set came from a public notebook, not from our data. Once the download lands, verify on OUR copy and record the answers here: (1) do Fluid_Sensitive and Fat_Suppression agree on every row; (2) Spearman rho of filename order vs geometric k; (3) FOV distribution (Rows * PixelSpacing) median and range; (4) Laterality absence rate and vendor concentration; (5) per-label positive rate among annotated studies; (6) how many studies carry annotations vs reports only; (7) report language distribution; (8) byte-identical report duplicate-group sizes.

title: Treat the rare findings as the expensive ones
description:
Every label costs the same 1/12 of the score. A label left at chance contributes 0.5 instead of ~M, forfeiting (M-0.5)/12 however well the other eleven do - at M=0.85 that is 0.029, larger than most modelling gains.

So rare findings deserve MORE attention than common ones, because a rare finding is where a model most easily ends up at chance. Track per-label AUC from the first run and treat the worst label as the work item, not the mean.

Prevalence drift is survivable (AUC is in expectation invariant to positive rate, and the competition does not guarantee matched prevalence across train/public/final); thresholds are not.
notes:
AND THE SAME LABEL IS WHERE OUR RULER IS WEAKEST, measured 2026-08-13 (python -m kneemri.reader_agreement, --by-label view now part of the module).

Agreement on the reader's POSITIVE calls, against the radiologist, per finding:
    Contusion         36 calls   44.4%     AUC 0.856
    MCL               18 calls   50.0%     AUC 0.782
    Lateral OA        16 calls   56.2%     AUC 0.822
    ...
    Medial Meniscus   32 calls   78.1%     AUC 0.894
    Synovitis         16 calls   81.2%     AUC 0.858

MCL is the second-noisiest label as well as the worst-scoring. Across the twelve, agreement and AUC correlate +0.51 Spearman - but twelve points put about +/-0.6 on that, so it is suggestive only, and CONTUSION REFUTES ANY SIMPLE VERSION: worst agreement of all, above-median AUC. Label noise contributes; it does not explain.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD, and it is the operational half: MCL's AUC is agreement with a label that is right about half the time, so an arm that genuinely improves mild collateral detection may not move the number, and a change that moves the number need not have improved the finding. MCL is at once the only reproducible deficit and the place the ruler is least able to say whether we fixed it.

IT CANNOT BE SETTLED LOCALLY EITHER: the clean test - MCL against the radiologist rather than the reader - has NINE MCL positives among the 58 annotated studies. An AUC from nine positives carries a standard error near 0.15, twenty times the effect. Only the leaderboard can arbitrate, which is knee-7d1's standing conclusion arriving from a new direction.

SO: keep MCL as the named weakness; do NOT build a loss or a sampler around it. That is the loss-engineering the working rules forbid, and here the measurement could not even confirm it had worked.

title: Encoder adaptation: unfreeze the last blocks, two learning rates
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11, and the inherited constants were both wrong in the same direction - too conservative.

RATE BRACKET (small + ranking, fold 0, seed 2026, control 0.8272):
  8e-6 inherited : 0.8272
  4e-5 (5x)      : 0.8316   +0.0044
  1.6e-4 (20x)   : ~0.739   collapsing - the encoder is destroyed

DEPTH BRACKET (at the inherited 8e-6, which is why it was uninformative):
  3 blocks : 0.8143   -0.0062
  6 blocks : 0.8205   control
  12 blocks: 0.8213   +0.0008

So the ORDER of the two questions was wrong: depth was bracketed first at a rate where no block moves, and read as 'depth is a ceiling at 6'. The rate is the binding constraint, and depth only becomes a real question once the encoder can move.

CAVEATS, both mine: +0.0044 is under the 1.5% bar (directional, not a result), and the 4e-5 arm moved rate AND depth together - the arm-J mistake again. Depth alone is +0.0008, so ~+0.0035 is the rate's share. Arm S (4e-5 at depth 6) isolates it.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW THE SCHEDULE: arm L was still improving at epoch 19 while the control peaked at 17 and declined. If a faster encoder needs longer, then the 8->24 epoch result - one of only two things this project counts as having paid - was measured at a rate where the encoder barely moves, and its magnitude is not transferable. Arm T runs 36 epochs at 4e-5.

STILL UNTESTED: whether the optimum sits between 8e-6 and 4e-5, or between 4e-5 and 1.6e-4. Not worth a sweep until a single-variable arm confirms the effect - sweeping a parameter before the effect is established is the stage-gate error this project has already paid for.
close_reason: RATE ISOLATED, 2026-08-11. Arm S (rate 4e-5, depth held at 6) = 0.8323 against control 0.8272 = +0.0051, single-variable. Arm L (same rate, depth 12) = 0.8316, so opening more blocks at the winning rate is -0.0007 - noise, and DEPTH IS NOT A LEVER at any rate tested. That closes the question this issue asked: it is the rate, not the depth, and the inherited 8e-6 was too conservative by about 5x. 1.6e-4 destroys the encoder (~0.739). Directional at +0.0051, under the 1.5% bar. Committed as experiments/arms/rate_isolate.sh. Remaining open threads live elsewhere: schedule duration on the winning config, and the composition with max pooling (experiments/arms/compose_small.sh).

title: Per-diagnosis query attention over slots, with a masked softmax
description:
Each of the twelve diagnoses gets its own query attending over the (up to six) slot embeddings, with absent slots masked OUT of the softmax so it renormalises over what the study actually contains.

WHY: mean-pooling the slots discards the reason the protocol has three planes - each finding is read on particular sequences, and a mean dilutes the one carrying the evidence with five that do not.

KEEP IT SMALL: the label is attached to the STUDY, so nothing in the supervision says which part carries the finding. Where the supervision is coarse, so is the head - a richer aggregator has no signal to learn from.
notes: IMPLEMENTED as kneemri/slot_head.py (SlotHead) during the Phase A port: per-diagnosis query, learned slot identity, masked softmax renormalising over present slots. Unit-tested including the property that masking a slot out equals never supplying it. Still to be trained by us - this is the replicated architecture, not our result.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/slot_head.py: per-diagnosis query, learned slot identity, masked softmax renormalising over present slots, unit-tested (masking a slot out == never supplying it). The note's remaining caveat ('still to be trained by us') is long overtaken - it is in every member we have trained, including the 0.8255 base@20 ladder point.

title: Report-derived labels: adopt the public tables, then measure whether we can beat them
description:
SPLIT IN TWO by evidence, 2026-08-11.

ADOPTED (done): pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels is the training table for every arm; the fetch step is committed after the ruler went missing once.

BEAT THEM (one branch now refuted): filtering the table by the reader's OWN confidence - striking the 27% of pairs it marks UNK - costs -0.0073 (s2026) and -0.0056 (s7), same sign in both matched seeds. So our supervision is not noise-limited in the way filtering would fix, and label CONTENT is not the free lever this issue assumed. See knee-5od.

STILL OPEN, and narrower: a reader that RESOLVES uncertain rows rather than striking them (the 0.899 notebook's multilingual negation scoping). That is the opposite operation and is untouched by the refutation. Gated behind knee-crl at P2 - the evidence now says the encoder, not the labels, is where our remaining gap lives.
notes:
THE DEFINING FACT, measured (probe v2, train.csv 4407 x 14): all 4407 studies carry a Report, and only 58 carry all twelve annotations.

58 / 4407 = 1.3%. The competition is therefore a weak-supervision problem first and an imaging problem second: the labels for 98.7% of the training corpus have to be read out of free text, in nine languages, or not exist at all. This is why every top notebook mounts the same public LLM label tables, and why improving those tables is the highest-leverage un-shared axis available.

Prevalence among the 58 annotated studies: Effusion 0.603, Synovitis 0.466, Medial Meniscus 0.448, ACL 0.414, Lateral Meniscus 0.397, PF OA 0.362, Contusion 0.328, Fracture 0.310, Medial OA 0.259, Baker's 0.207, Lateral OA 0.190, MCL 0.155.

Read that as counts, not rates: MCL has NINE positives, Lateral OA eleven, Baker's twelve. Any model-selection decision made on the annotation check is being made on single-digit positive counts - which is exactly the Hanley-McNeil argument for why the holdout, not the annotation check, must arbitrate.
FIRST TRAINED MEMBERS (2026-08-10) on the public LLM report labels (pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels, CC0): 5 folds x 16 epochs, holdout mean AUC 0.8092 / 0.8177 / 0.8108 / 0.8179 / 0.8252, mean 0.8162. Selected on a holdout split by REPORT-TEXT HASH so duplicate reports cannot straddle the divide.

The published members average 0.8398 on their own holdout, so we are ~0.024 under the frontier after one training run. That gap is now a MEASURED quantity, which is what makes it attackable: the labels are the shared input everyone mounts, so beating the public tables is the un-shared axis - and our number moving without the labels changing would say the gap is in the model instead.

Training cost: 27s per epoch on the 5090 over the 35.8 GB memory-mapped cache. Cheap enough that epochs and folds are not the constraint - what to train ON is.
PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE for the next submission (2026-08-11, written BEFORE the folds finished):

SUBMIT if the new five-fold holdout mean is >= 0.825. Otherwise do not spend a slot.

Reasoning: the old ensemble averaged 0.8162 with a fold-to-fold spread of about +/-0.008, so anything under ~0.825 is inside that spread and proves nothing. Fold 0 has already reproduced +0.011 on a MATCHED comparison (same fold, same seed, only the recipe differing), and overlap TTA adds a measured +0.0025 on top, so the threshold is what the two changes should deliver if they hold across folds rather than being fold-0 luck.

Written down in advance so 'notable' cannot be decided after seeing the number.
close_reason: ADOPTED half done (report_labels_v2 is the table for every arm, fetch step committed). BEAT-THEM half: one branch refuted (confidence filtering, -0.0073 / -0.0056 on two matched seeds), the surviving branch - a reader that RESOLVES uncertain rows via multilingual negation scoping - is knee-crl. Closing so it stops blocking knee-3om; the live work is knee-crl.

title: Decode-once pixel cache under a memory budget
description:
Decode slot images once into a uint8 in-memory cache; bytes = studies * slots * slices * P^2. Training draws one group of consecutive slices per step (doubles as augmentation along the stack); inference averages over groups.

WHY: a study is ~150 files and the pipeline is read-bound, not arithmetic-bound. Affordable once, not once per epoch.

CONSTRAINT: the cache grows with the SQUARE of resolution and only linearly with slices, so slice coverage is the cheap axis and resolution the expensive one. Budget a fraction of free memory (not all of it) and size TRAIN + TEST caches together, since both are resident at once - overshooting ends the run rather than slowing it.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/study_cache.py: decode-once uint8 memmap, images_336px_12sl.npy = 35.8 GB on disk, one contiguous slice per batch. The memory-budget constraint is honoured by memory-MAPPING rather than resident allocation, which is a better answer than the budget the issue asked for.

title: Physical-scale crop + resample (mm/pixel is the design variable)
description:
Crop to a constant physical extent L and resample to P pixels, so effective pitch = L/P mm/pixel.

MECHANISM: a feature of width d survives only if pitch <= d/2 (Nyquist on the resampling grid). A meniscal tear is 1-3mm, so 1mm needs <= 0.5 mm/px. At L=130mm: P=224 gives 0.580 (fails), P=336 gives 0.387 (clears). The crop must be SMALLER than the smallest field of view or it silently does nothing.

PROVES: measure the acquired FOV distribution (Rows * PixelSpacing) over our training series. The claim to check is median ~160mm, range 70-320, and that 130mm sits below the FOV of ~99.6% of series. Pick L from OUR measurement, not from the quoted one.
close_reason: Shipped at L=130mm, P=336 (0.387 mm/px, clears the 0.5 mm/px Nyquist bar for a 1mm tear). PROVES clause satisfied on our own copy: FOV median 160mm, 1st percentile 130mm, only 0.43% of series narrower than the crop - so it crops rather than pads. Pixel spacing median 0.3125mm; the 9.6% coarser than 0.5mm are interpolated past native resolution, which is the group where a 1mm tear was never resolvable anyway. Written up under 'Corpus facts, finally measured on our own copy'.

title: Laterality normalisation, including recovery when the tag is absent
description:
Five of twelve targets are side-defined (two menisci, medial/lateral OA, MCL). Normalise: flip the last axis for coronal/axial (medial-lateral is in-plane); REVERSE THE SLICE ORDER for sagittal (medial-lateral is the slice axis).

Laterality is Type 2C and reported absent on half the studies, by whole vendors. Recover from patient coordinates: image centre c = p + r*ds*Nc/2 + d*dr*Nr/2; +x points to the patient's left, so sign(c_x) gives the side. Use the CENTRE, not p (a corner half a FOV away can flip the sign near the midline). Leave a study unresolved inside a ~20mm dead band rather than guessing.

PROVES: on our data, measure the Laterality-tag absence rate and its per-vendor concentration; check the recovered side against the tag where both exist.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/laterality.py with the geometry fallback. PROVES clause satisfied twice: tag absent on 50.0% of studies and NOT at random (GE/Toshiba/Canon 0.0%, Philips 38.3%, Siemens 84.3%); where both rules exist they agree on 98.6% of 2135 studies. The gap that left - the geometry rule was validated ONLY where the tag also exists - was closed separately by the mean-image check on the vendors that never write it (GE 0.925 upright vs 0.730 mirrored, floor 0.780).

title: Gate an SSL adaptation on its drift profile before it spends a training slot
description: encoder_adapt lost 0.168 uniformly because 6 epochs at lr 1e-4 moved encoder blocks 0-5 by 3.4-8.3% of their own norm, where supervision moves them by exactly 0.0000 and never moves any block more than 2.1%. encoder_drift now reads an adaptation checkpoint (2026-08-20), so the check is a one-minute CPU read guarding a 75-minute arm. Pre-registered: early-block drift <= ~0.02 or the checkpoint does not get armed. First candidate under the gate: adapt_small_e6_lr1e5.pt (same objective/data/schedule, rate 1e-5).

title: Ordinal severity target: the three YES levels as ordered classes
description: severity_weight (2026-08-20) refuted the MULTIPLIER use of the report grade: matched control band_dense 0.8578 vs arm 0.8530, and four of the five pre-registered graded labels came back negative (focal +0.0001, regional -0.0118). The owner's call is that the axis stays open - the grade is real per-study information the loss still discards. The successor consumes it WITHOUT reweighting any example: the three YES levels (0.68/0.82/0.94) become ordered classes behind a cumulative-threshold head, so it cannot reproduce the batch-starvation mechanism that sank the multiplier. Pre-register the falsifiable clause before queueing. See experiments/README.md, section severity_weight.

title: rank0_dense is written and un-queued, with no bead of its own
description:
experiments/arms/rank0_dense.sh exists on disk and was owed by after_rank0.log, a watcher that had died with its launching session. bd search finds no issue for it, so the arm's hypothesis, control and pre-registered clause live only in the file header — which means nothing surfaces it in bd ready and it would be re-derived or forgotten.

UN-QUEUED 2026-08-20 rather than lost: the card is going to biohub, and the dead watcher chain has been retired to logs/retired/ so queue_check reports the true state.

TODO on this bead: read the arm header, lift its hypothesis / control / pre-registered clause into this description so the bead is self-contained, then decide whether it is still worth a slot. The context it has to argue against is four consecutive decode/head knobs returning nothing (attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021) — the subsystem, not the levers, is what that pattern is evidence about.

title: [bug] nohup watchers do not survive a harness restart, so a queue can look armed with nothing behind it
description:
ROOT CAUSE, unfixed. aug_long wrote its completion marker on 2026-08-20 and the card then sat at 5% for about five minutes, because the three after.sh watchers meant to start the next arms no longer existed. nohup gives them PPID 1 but does not survive whatever ends the harness shell on Windows.

THE TRAP: a dead watcher's log still reads "waiting for 'ARM DONE ...'" forever, because that line was printed before it died. The one artefact a queue leaves behind says the same thing whether it is waiting or gone.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: kneemri/experiments/queue_check.py crosses the watcher logs against the process table and reports STRANDED arms. That DETECTS the hole after the fact; it does not stop it opening, and it only helps if someone runs it.

REAL FIX: a detached Windows launcher — schtasks /create with a one-shot trigger, or a service — so the watcher's lifetime is not tied to the shell that spawned it. Then queue_check becomes a belt-and-braces check rather than the only defence.

title: --patience 3 is below the derived floor and would truncate the run the floor was measured from
description: stale_gap derives the safe patience from every curve on disk: the longest NON-improving streak a run later recovered from is 3 epochs (lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026, 16 epochs, best at 12, survived 3), so patience must EXCEED it and the safe value is 4. Seven arms pass --patience 3 (calibrated_targets, dinov3_base_lora, encoder_layer, focal_pool, peak_rate, resolution, v3base_band) - exactly the value that stops at the third stale epoch, which is the epoch before that run's later best. resolution.sh's own comment claims patience 3 cannot change a recorded best; that replay predates the run that set the floor. Fix: raise the seven to 4, and give recipe.sh a single derived PATIENCE constant so a new knob arm inherits it instead of copy-pasting a number. Corpus at 4 recovers 52 epochs, 29 percent of 177 wasted across 56 runs. NOT for schedule-shape arms (band_dense_long, aug_long) - a stopper deletes the measurement those are launched to take - and not for final_fit, which has no holdout under --fold -1.
close_reason: Landed in 1d95c8e. PATIENCE=--patience 4 lives once in recipe.sh with the derivation beside it; the seven arms inherit it. Verified the flag resolves under stub_lib.sh (ARM_LIB=experiments/stub_lib.sh bash experiments/arms/focal_pool.sh prints --patience 4), which is the lib arm_check sources, and all 60 arms still check clean. resolution.sh's stale comment replaced with why the old replay aged. Excluded by design: schedule-shape arms and final_fit.

title: headlr_dense: the head:backbone rate ratio is the last unmeasured constant of the adaptation triple
description: Adaptation carries head_lr 1e-3, backbone_lr 8e-6, unfreeze_last 6, and trainer.py's own docstring says the 125:1 ratio 'was inherited from the reference rather than measured'. Two of the three have since been opened (backbone rate to 4e-5, depth bracketed by deep24/shallow24); head_lr never was. Moving the backbone rate five-fold silently changed the ratio to 25:1 -- not the inherited one and not a measured one, just leftover arithmetic from changing one number of a pair only ever justified as a pair. headlr_dense restores 125:1 with --head-lr 5e-3 at the settled operating point. Control band_dense 0.8578, seat greedy4_v1 0.8679, cost ~1.2h. Queued behind rank0_dense (watcher pid 105660). Three outcomes pre-registered in the arm header, including a divergence signature (epoch-0 AUC near 0.5, flat loss) written down in advance so a hot-head failure cannot be misread as a refutation of the ratio.
notes:
UN-QUEUED 2026-08-20. The arm is written and was owed by after_headlr.log, whose watcher had died with the session that launched it (see the nohup-watcher bug bead). The card is being handed to biohub, so it is deliberately NOT relaunched rather than lost. Eight dead watcher logs moved to logs/retired/ so queue_check reads the true state ('OK: nothing is queued') instead of reporting a permanent false strand.

Re-queue by relaunching after.sh over experiments/arms/headlr_dense.sh when the card comes back. Read it against the four-knob run of nothing first (attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021): another constant on the same subsystem is the shape that has stopped paying.

title: Anatomical prior: does the head still need to rediscover which plane shows which finding?
description: The second of the five never-run switches (--anatomical-prior). SlotHead initialises self.prior at ZEROS, so the plane-by-finding mapping is learned from 4,407 study-level label vectors that contain no localisation. The flag initialises that same nn.Parameter from the 12x6 table in kneemri/corpus/anatomy.py (two facts per finding, PRIOR_STRENGTH 2.0, all entries non-negative so it is a preference and never a mask). Parameter count, shapes, compute, VRAM and wall-clock are unchanged. Arm: experiments/arms/aprior_dense.sh, 12 epochs against band_dense 0.8578, single variable, about 1.2 h. Sits on the supervision axis that four independent lines converged on (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_what_is_left_after_decode_and_data.md) and is the only one of the three that needs neither a new label nor a user go-ahead. Three outcomes pre-registered in the arm header; the third one — flat mean, per-label pattern moving along the peaked-row split — makes it a diversity generator priced by seat value rather than a mean lever.
notes:
RAN 2026-08-20 as aprior_dense. REFUTED, and the refutation clause was pre-registered.

0.8557 best (epoch 8) vs matched control band_dense 0.8578 (also epoch 8) = -0.0021, a third of the 0.0062 floor, on the wrong side.

Flag verified in the CHECKPOINT config: anatomical_prior false->true, slices 20 / slice_pooling max / whole_stack true / pool cls_mean / backbone_lr 4e-05 identical. Only other config diff is slice_regions absent-vs-1, the StudyDesign default arriving in the manifest, not a variable.

Per-label at matched epoch 8: peaked rows (MCL, Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA, Synovitis) -0.0008, flat rows -0.0033. The split is the predicted direction and 0.0025 wide, under half the floor, so the arm's THIRD OUTCOME does not fire either; and the single largest mover in the table is Synovitis -0.010, a PEAKED axial-weighted row going the wrong way.

MECHANISM: the warm start WASHED OUT rather than failed to land, and the training loss separates those. Losses track the control to the fourth decimal at every epoch (1.2117/1.2162 at e0, 0.6508/0.6529 at e8 - the arm slightly LOWER). Not a plumbing failure: landed.py asserts the parameter constructed and switch_coverage smokes it.

Cost was as predicted and is the one clause that held: 26.92 GB reserved / 24.93 GB allocated, 368 s an epoch, identical to band_dense. Free, and bought nothing.

Seat: +0.0009 as a fifth member, +0.0004 as best swap (displacing band_dense, the member it is a variant of). 0 of 1 clears +0.0015. No seat on either ruler.

CONSEQUENCE (pre-registered, so owed): the head had ALREADY recovered the plane-by-finding mapping from study-level supervision alone. 'Supervision never says where' is wrong about THIS head. The localisation argument must buy a REAL localisation signal (knee-mxj), not a warm start on an existing parameter.

Second of the five never-run switches spent (after --pool cls_mean_focal). Fourth consecutive decode/head knob returning nothing: attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021.

Written up in experiments/README.md (row + long entry).
close_reason: Closed

title: The offline seat ruler saturates above ~0.868 — six board points now say so
description:
MEASURED across six entries pairing an offline joint-holdout score with a board score: 0.8648/0.928, 0.8653/0.928, 0.8661/0.927, 0.8670/0.929, 0.8679/0.930, 0.8691/0.930. The chain rises over the first 0.003 of offline spread and then stops responding over the next 0.0012. Combined with seat_value's sweep of all 56 same-split checkpoints — exactly three positive seats against greedy4_v1, largest +0.0012 (just spent, tie), second +0.0002 — the working conclusion is that the ruler tracks the board while offline gaps are LARGE relative to the board's one-tick resolution and saturates once they are not.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST WRITTEN UP: it changes what an arm has to clear to be worth a slot. A candidate that prices at +0.0002 in the seat is not a submission even though the ruler says it is the best remaining move, because the ruler has been shown not to resolve at that scale. The bar for spending a slot is now a member from an axis the pool does not contain, not the pool's argmax.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: a future entry whose offline gain is under 0.0015 and which moves the board a tick. That would say the plateau is two points of noise rather than saturation. Two points is a thin basis for a claim this load-bearing and the issue should stay open until a third lands on either side.

title: Lateral Meniscus moves on both rulers in both pooling arms, and it was pre-registered
description:
focal_dense and attend_dense both closed their cell of the decode family on the mean (-0.0044, -0.0009) and both are flat-to-negative on the ordinal ruler too (-0.0047, -0.0002), so neither bought severity ordering the binary ruler was missing.

Lateral Meniscus is the only one of twelve labels positive on all four readings: binary +0.010/+0.009, ordinal +0.017/+0.018, tightly clustered. It survives the best-of-twelve objection because focal_dense.sh PRE-REGISTERED it by mechanism before the run (finest-scale finding, largest model-side gap, knee-dtk -0.1932) and because attend_dense, which never named it, replicates the effect. The pre-registration's second named label, Fracture, went the other way.

Does NOT license another pooling arm (both lost on the mean, both seat at +0.0015 = an ADD not a seat, and inside the 0.0062 floor per knee-yu3e) and does NOT license tuning toward the label. Records that pooling can shift budget toward the finest-scale finding but cannot create it, so whatever limits that label is upstream - supervision or encoder, the same direction both closed arms send the bottleneck.

Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_pooling-is-closed-on-the-mean-but-not-on-lateral-meniscus.md

title: Seat reads go through record_mix, not member_curve
description: A seat value (does member X earn a place in the four?) is arithmetic over per-study probabilities that every run already wrote beside its checkpoint as <name>.holdout.npz. kneemri.evaluation.record_mix reads those and returns the subset curve in seconds with no card. kneemri.evaluation.member_curve answers the same question by REBUILDING each member's reading from the pixel cache, which is a full inference pass for anything not in processed/holdout_predictions - and that store is missing the pool's three best members (band_dense, band_span, depth_regions_narrow) even though the 12-member search scored them, because that search was record_mix and never touched the cache. On CPU a miss is hours, so two curve runs on 2026-08-19 looked like a hang and were killed; they were computing. record_mix's own docstring says all of this. Cost: about an hour, plus a queue swap that would have spent card time re-deriving arrays that were already on disk. Follow-up worth doing: either backfill the prediction cache for the pool's top members during an idle card window, or make member_curve say MISS - computing N members loudly when it is about to do inference.

title: The beads daemon rewrites issues.jsonl during the pre-push hooks, so every push needs two attempts
description:
SYMPTOM: git push aborts with a hook reporting 'Failed / - files were modified by this hook', and the hook named is whichever one was running at the time. It has been unit-tests twice, because at 96s that hook holds the widest window.

IT IS NOT A GATE FINDING, and it has been misread as one twice in one session. Verified 2026-08-19: running the unit-tests hook's exact entry (uv run --extra dev pytest tests/unit -q) by hand leaves git status byte-identical and uv.lock + .beads/issues.jsonl md5-identical, exit 0, 845 passed. ruff format --check reports 153 files already formatted, so the format gate is not it either. What actually changes under the hooks is .beads/issues.jsonl, and the writer is the bd daemon's auto-export, which fires on its own schedule rather than on anything the push does.

COST: every push is a two-step — the first aborts, the file is committed as a 'beads: sync issue ledger' commit, the second succeeds. That is one wasted full gate run (~3 min) per push, and worse, it trains the reader to treat a red gate as noise.

FIX DIRECTION: the export should not race the hooks. Either pause the daemon for the duration of a push, or make the pre-push sequence commit a pending issues.jsonl export before it starts rather than discovering it half-way through. Do not paper over it by adding issues.jsonl to an exclude list — the file is git-tracked on purpose and a push that silently drops a pending export is worse than a retry.

title: queue.sh silently drops an arm's arguments, so a parameterised arm queues as its default
description:
queue.sh:40 runs `timeout "$ARM_TIMEOUT" bash "$script"` where script=experiments/arms/$arm.sh — it takes arm NAMES and forwards nothing after them. after.sh takes entries-with-args and calls run_snapshot $entry, so the two runners disagree on what a queue entry IS.

THE FAILURE. Several arms are parameterised: resolution.sh takes <train_size> <cache_size> [rate], and its defaults are 392/448. Naming 'resolution' in a queue does not fail, warn, or refuse — it runs the 392 default, spends the slot re-running a member we already have, and overwrites res392_ws_s2026.pt with a fresh copy of itself. The loss is silent in both directions: the queue file looks like it asked for a rung, and the output looks like a completed arm.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET. Every parameterised arm so far went through after.sh (which forwards) or a hand-launch. The moment someone queues one by name, it costs a slot to discover.

THE FIX. queue.sh should split each entry on whitespace the way after.sh does and forward the tail, and route through run_snapshot rather than bare `bash` — which is also what lib.sh's new guard (51dfc98) now catches at runtime, but catching it after the card is taken is worse than expressing it in the queue. Small test: a queue entry with args reaches the arm's $1.
close_reason: Closed

title: A killed run strands its checkpoint as .partial and leaves a stale .pt beside it
description: depth_regions_span_s2026 run 2 was killed mid-epoch-9. Its epoch-8 checkpoint sits on disk as depth_regions_span_s2026.partial (89 MB, 21:25:53) while depth_regions_span_s2026.pt carries an mtime of 20:49:38 -- older than the run1.pt the rotation wrote at 20:55:57. So the live .pt name does not hold the run that last wrote under it, and 89 MB of orphaned .partial is left for nobody to clean. Establish whether the pending-rename commit can be interrupted between write and rename, and whether a .partial with no .pt beside it should be adopted or deleted at the next begin().
notes:
CORRECTED after reading the code. .partial is NOT a strand: trainer.save_partial writes destination.with_suffix('.partial') at every improving epoch as the crash-safety net (tmp -> replace, atomic), and .pt is written only when a run completes. A killed run leaving 89 MB of .partial holding its best weights is the design working. What is NOT explained, and is the whole bead now: depth_regions_span_s2026.pt exists with mtime 20:49:38 while run1.pt carries 20:55:57. RunMetrics.begin moved .pt aside to run1.pt when run 2 started, and run 2 never completed, so the live .pt name should be ABSENT. Path.replace preserves mtime, so run1.pt's newer stamp cannot come from that move either. Either a third run exists under this name or something writes .pt outside the completion path. Priority stays P2 -- the ledger quotes run 1 from run1.metrics.jsonl and is not wrong -- but a .pt whose provenance nobody can name is the file every roster loads by.
RESOLVED, no defect. Sizes+mtimes settle it: .pt (20:49:38) is run 1's completed epoch-9 payload and was NEVER moved; _run1.pt (20:55:57), _run1.holdout.npz (20:57:07), _run1.metrics.jsonl (20:57:16) are byte-size-identical to run 1's originals but carry LATER mtimes, and Path.replace preserves mtime while a copy does not - so the _run1.* set was COPIED by hand, before RunMetrics grew artefact rotation. .metrics.1.jsonl (20:49:38, mtime preserved) is the one real replace: run 2's begin under the OLD epochs-only code. .partial/.metrics.jsonl/.holdout.npz (21:25:53) are run 2's epoch-8 best (0.8486847394797142). Both .pt and _run1.pt therefore hold the same run-1 payload (epoch 9, holdout 0.8504566982315008) because one is a hand copy of the other, not because the rotation duplicated. The hazard the ec3727c rotation closes is real and unchanged: had run 2 COMPLETED it would have overwritten .pt and run 1 would be gone.
close_reason: Closed

title: kit_check answered about the wrong repository under a git hook: -C is overruled by an inherited GIT_DIR
description:
Git exports GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_WORK_TREE into every hook it runs, and a git child inherits them. An inherited GIT_DIR OUTRANKS -C, so KitCheck.asked() - which is 'git -C <repo> ...' - answered about the repository that invoked the hook rather than the one it was handed. kit_check runs from pre-commit and pre-push, which is exactly where those variables are set.

In this repo the two are the same tree, so the wrong answer happened to be the right one and nothing said otherwise. It surfaced sideways: the unit tests build their own repository in a temp directory, and two of them failed inside a pre-push run while passing on their own. Reproduced deterministically with GIT_DIR=.git pytest tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py.

FIXED: kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py gains unhooked(), the environment minus GIT_*, passed to the subprocess; the tests' own raw git calls take it too; test_unhooked covers it. 8 pass under an inherited GIT_DIR where 1 failed before.

REMAINING (why this is open rather than closed): kit_check is not the only thing in the tree that shells git from a place a hook can reach. experiments/lib.sh runs 'git -C $REPO hash-object' for the lib blob stamp, and comp/ has its own git reads. Audit those for the same inheritance and decide whether unhooked() should move to the package root as shared vocabulary rather than living beside its first consumer.
notes:
AUDIT DONE, and it found a second site that matters more than the first.

comp/build_kit.py:93 shelled the same 'git -C $_REPO' to stamp the kit's commit AND its dirty flag. An inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE would have had 'status --porcelain' read a borrowed index, so the stamp - the ground truth every later kit_check compares against - could have been written from a different tree. Same fix applied: env=unhooked(), imported from kit_check.

experiments/lib.sh:39 is CLEAN and stays as it is: 'git hash-object <file>' hashes the file's bytes, so no repository variable can change its answer.

That is every git-shelling site in kneemri/, core/, comp/, experiments/ and tests/. unhooked() stays beside kit_check, its first consumer, rather than moving to the package root - two consumers in the same subsystem is not yet shared vocabulary.
2026-08-19: named the second half of this. A push started right after a bd mutation fails at pre-push with 'shape-contracts ... files were modified by this hook' while that hook's own output reads '0 bare-array boundaries'. The hook is read-only (--assert, pass_filenames: false); what actually changed the tree was bd's ASYNC export of .beads/issues.jsonl landing mid-hook-run, and pre-commit blames whichever hook was running. Cost one failed push tonight, and the failure names an innocent gate — so the reader goes looking in devtools for a defect that is not there. Operating rule until fixed: after any bd mutation, git add .beads/issues.jsonl and commit BEFORE pushing. Verified: the identical push passed on the retry once the export was committed.
2026-08-19: the candidate mechanical fix this bead proposed is REFUTED, measured rather than assumed. 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' is synchronous, but it is not byte-equivalent to what bd's async writer produces: exported to a probe file it gave the SAME SET of 318 lines (298 issues + 20 memories) in a DIFFERENT ORDER - sorted, the two files are identical; unsorted they differ on 36 lines. So wiring it in as a pre-push flush would rewrite the tracked file with an equivalent-but-reordered payload on every push, fight the async writer for the ordering, and put a large meaningless diff in every commit. That is worse than the race. Do not reach for bd export here again. What remains viable is a LEGIBILITY guard rather than a flush: the defect that costs time is not the dirty file, it is that pre-commit blames whichever hook was running, so the reader goes hunting in devtools for a fault that is not there. A pre-push check that refuses early and names bd as the writer would convert a twenty-hook misattribution into one line. Blocked on where it can live: .pre-commit-config.yaml is template-owned and carries ZERO '# >>> LOCAL-SLOT' regions (grep -c = 0), so the honest home for it is upstream in sdlc-scaffold, not a hand-edit here. Operating rule stands unchanged in the meantime: after any bd mutation, git add .beads/issues.jsonl and commit BEFORE pushing, and run no bd mutation while a push is in flight.

title: witness_check's cuda tolerance assumes fp16 arithmetic and is 4x too tight for bf16
description:
comp/witness_check.py applies CROSS_PRECISION_FACTOR = 4.0 (line 46) only on the CPU branch. The cuda branch's premise is that arithmetic MATCHES between arms, so any residual difference is kernel nondeterminism and a near-zero tolerance is right. Measured on the card (knee-djk8 leg b): that premise holds for fp16 - three members pass at EXACTLY 0 - and is false for bf16, whose refusals sit at 0.63-2.47x bf16 eps (2^-7 = 7.8e-3), the same 1.6-2.4x band the CPU calibration already measured. So the gate refuses bf16 members for being bf16, not for drifting. The bead knee-djk8 stated this as 'every bf16 member fails', which is both too strong (three pass) and too weak (they pass at exactly 0, not merely inside tolerance).

NOT fixed on discovery on purpose: this is the pre-submission safety gate, and widening a tolerance is exactly the edit that must arrive with its own test rather than beside an unrelated commit. The fix is to derive the cuda tolerance from the arm's DTYPE eps the way the CPU branch does, and the test is the equivalence class that let it survive - a bf16 pair whose difference is one eps.
close_reason: Fixed: tolerance() now derives from dtype eps on both devices (EPS_FACTOR * finfo(precision).eps); the cuda branch is gone because both regimes measured into the same 1.6-2.5x eps band. Three tests: the bf16-one-eps equivalence class, the discrimination check (bound stays 6x under the 0.05 smallest real reading defect), and the mantissa-scaling identity. Commit 7dc6f87.

title: Split the remaining measure/render classes (ServeBench, OutOfFoldOracle, ReaderAgreement)
notes: 2026-08-19 14:49 UTC, c7dc613: ServeBench and OutOfFoldOracle done, along with TieDivergence and CropLaterality in f2f32f0. Only ReaderAgreement remains, and it is the one that needs a decision rather than a move - its report shares _resample with by_label and gap, so splitting it means deciding whether the resampling is part of the measurement or part of the reading. Gates green and 99% coverage on both passes; archmap regenerated in the same commit each time, which is what stopped the pre-push hook rejecting it the way it did twice yesterday.
close_reason:
Four of the five split (f2f32f0 TieDivergence + CropLaterality, c7dc613 ServeBench + OutOfFoldOracle), and the fifth is REFUSED on the mechanism rather than deferred.

The pattern earns its keep only where the render is trapped behind an apparatus: Attribution needs a GPU, StackCoverage the published predictions, SlotTies and TieDivergence and CropLaterality a corpus of DICOMs to walk, ServeBench a loaded member on a card, OutOfFoldOracle both. In every one of those the table could not be exercised without constructing the thing that measures.

ReaderAgreement has no such apparatus. Its whole input is one DataFrame of annotated cells, and tests/unit/kneemri/labels/reader_agreement.py:83 already builds that by hand - every report test there runs today without a corpus, a card or a checkpoint. Its LCOM4 3 is not a measure/render seam at all: the islands are {_resample,by_label,gap,report}, {error_report,errors} and {cells}, which are THREE QUESTIONS (agreement rate, error census, cell construction) that happen to share a table. Splitting a Report off it would buy no testability and would copy a pattern past the reason the pattern exists.

Recorded so the next lcom scan does not re-raise it: ReaderAgreement's LCOM4 3 is accepted, on the same grounds TrainingOptions' LCOM4 5 is.

title: A check that measures nothing reports a clean pass
description:
THE CLASS, not one bug: every check ends with a count and an exit code, and the two are independent, so a collapsed denominator prints the sentence a passing check prints and exits 0. Four occurrences in a week from three unrelated causes: arm_check twice (WSL bash / PowerShell PATH without coreutils - every arm timed out, '0 arms checked, 0 refused'), kit_check for 53 shipped-package commits (pathspec anchored one level down matched no file, so git log named no commit and every stale kit read as current), and the encoder drift gate (a compiled checkpoint whose keys all carry _orig_mod. matched no stock tensor and reported drift 0.000).

FIX: kneemri/denominator.refuse_empty is the one home for the refusal, wired into all five; each caller names its own empty set and its likeliest cause. Live denominators after the fix: 83 runs / 25 closure files / 4 champion members / 17 checkable kernels.

title: [bug] A running chain freezes lib.sh at source time, so a mechanism added mid-session silently skips queued arms
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19. run_train gained _seat_value in 96d7b80 (12:36 local). focal_pool and unfreeze_4 both finished AFTER that commit and neither printed a SEAT VALUE line; centre_tissue, whose chain shell sourced lib.sh at 13:12, is expected to print one.

MECHANISM: bash parses a sourced file ONCE into function definitions held in that shell's memory. A chain is one long-lived shell that sources experiments/lib.sh at launch and then runs arm after arm, so every arm in a chain runs the lib.sh that existed when the CHAIN started, not when the ARM started. run_snapshot deliberately snapshots the arm and the package but points ARM_LIB at the LIVE repo lib.sh - which is safe for editability but does nothing for a chain, because the chain already holds its copy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the failure is SILENT and it looks exactly like a broken mechanism. Reading unfreeze_4's log, the honest conclusion from the evidence is 'seat value does not fire', and the fix one would reach for is in _seat_value. The seat value had to be recomputed by hand for both arms.

OPTIONS: (a) have run_train re-source lib.sh per arm - cheap, but re-sourcing mid-run is the class of thing run_snapshot exists to avoid; (b) stamp the lib.sh commit into each arm's log at run_train entry, so a missing mechanism is attributable in one grep instead of an hour; (c) have a chain re-exec itself per arm. (b) is the cheapest and turns a silent skip into a readable fact; it does not fix the staleness, it makes it legible.

Recorded in experiments/README.md alongside the unfreeze_4 row.
notes: Option (a) landed 2026-08-19 in 24f4ff8: run_train compares the parsed blob to the working tree and re-sources + re-dispatches when they differ, so the CURRENT arm gets the current mechanisms. _LIB_REFRESHING bounds it to one attempt. queue.sh was never affected (fresh shell per arm). experiments/lib_staleness_check.sh proves the decision; the re-source path is not proved end to end because it holds the card.
close_reason: Closed

title: attribution's depth section draws a conclusion from a single window
description:
On band_dense_s2026 the reading was '1 window(s) of 20', so the depth sweep had one window: 'best single window starts at slice 0 (0.8558)', 'range 0.8558 to 0.8558 over 1 windows', 'per-label best window: 1 distinct depths over 12 labels'. It then prints the interpretation line 'one shared depth means a re-weighting of the sampled windows helps every label; several means the only correct answer is to read more of the stack'.

That sentence cannot be true from n=1. With one window every label trivially shares it, so the report states a conclusion the data cannot support, in the same wording it would use for a real result. Same family as the failures arm_check and ledger_check exist for: a vacuous result that reads identically to a measured one.

FIX: refuse the depth section when the window count is 1, the way RecordMix.shared refuses a too-small intersection rather than reporting over the survivors. Print what was asked and why it could not be answered.

Note the slice-cost section below it IS informative on the same run (6 distinct depths over 12 labels, slice 9 carrying 17%) — so only the window sweep degenerates, not the whole axis.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] The card gate sat in run_snapshot, so the documented smoke procedure spent GPU ungated
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 by walking into it. Smoking the new focal_pool recipe the way CLAUDE.md documents it — source experiments/lib.sh, call run_train with --studies 60 --epochs 1 — launched onto a card already running depth_regions_narrow and died with 'CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 366.00 MiB ... 4.84 GiB is free'.

THE HOLE: hold_card was called by run_snapshot, which only a QUEUED arm passes through. run_train is what actually starts the trainer, and it is reachable three other ways — the documented smoke, an ad-hoc one-off, and any script that sources the lib. All three spent GPU with no gate, by construction rather than by accident.

WHY THE NEAR-MISS IS NOT REASSURING: the incumbent survived at 1255 img/s with no STALLED line, but only because the NEWCOMER lost the allocation race. That is luck. The same collision at a smaller footprint is two arms sharing one card, which is exactly the 31.9-GB PCIe-paging collapse the lock exists to prevent — the serialiser would again have been the thing producing the overflow it guards against, the same shape as knee-n7ql.

FIX: hold_card moved from run_snapshot into run_train, which is the ONE point every GPU-spending path crosses, with release_card on every exit path including the failures (a crashed trainer holding the lock would idle the queue behind it). Per call rather than per arm, so a sweep arm calling run_train several times lets another chain interleave between its runs instead of holding across all of them. run_snapshot copies the package and the arm, which spends no GPU, so nothing needed protecting before the trainer starts.

VERIFIED: the identical command that OOM'd now prints 'waiting for another process to release the card: 12369 MiB free, want 18432' and queues.

A switch recipe is smoke-only by construction (decode_smoke_caches builds its sixty-study truncation), so switch_tie reports "UNCACHED switch_tie: nothing decoded at 336px_12sl_last" on every run and always will. title: The six-axis cache construction is spelled by hand three times on the BUILD/TRAIN side
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-18. StudyCache(directory, slices, image_size, routing, reading, first) is written out at kneemri/training/train.py:614, kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py:234 and kneemri/corpus/cache_flags.py:102. All three agree TODAY - checked field by field.

This is the duplication Member.cache() was created to remove on the SERVE side, where three call sites (the oracle, the witness check, the curve) each named a cache by size, depth and router while the member also recorded a crop and a band - so any member that read anything else resolved to the DEFAULT arrays, which exist, load, and are the wrong pixels. members.py:193 states the rule: 'the set of fields that names a cache is not knowledge a consumer should hold'. The build/train side still holds it in three places.

WHAT IT COSTS WHEN IT DRIFTS: a seventh cache axis added to StudyCache.key() and forgotten at one of the three means arm_check reports 'cached' for a cache the run will not open (a queue slot spent discovering it), or build_cache writes under a name the trainer does not ask for.

FIX: TrainingOptions.cache(directory) - train.py and arm_check both hold a TrainingOptions and would call it; cache_flags builds from an argparse Namespace for the build CLI and would keep its own or take the same shape. NOTE it adds a seventh factory method to TrainingOptions (see knee-d2z6, which says the setup-on-the-config residue is deliberate but growing), and it edits the training entrypoint - so gates plus a 60-study smoke, and not between an arm being queued and run.

CacheFlags.cache stays the namespace half (build_cache, build_embeddings, head_trial parse into a bare Namespace). A Protocol collapsing the two was tried and REJECTED BY THE GATES, correctly: fitness reads a second class in cache_flags.py as a second subject, envy reads a method touching 9 foreign fields and 0 of its own as belonging elsewhere. The two halves are pinned equal by tests/unit/kneemri/training/train.py::test_cache instead. Verified: gates green (99% cov), and arm_check over the real queue reports 37 arms, 0 refused, 0 uncached - every arm's reading still names a cache that is on disk. Commit 0acd323.

title: Serve-side read of a recorded config had no mechanical guard - the nine-defect class, from the reader's end
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-18, for the silent train/serve mismatch class (a value recorded in the config, a consumer reading a module default - nine instances counted in MemberRecord's own docstrings, each found AFTER a run by a witness, a refused fingerprint or a lost submission).

The WRITER was already guarded: tests/unit/kneemri/runs/member_record.py::test_payload_takes_each_config_field_from_the_option_of_its_own_name moves one option and demands exactly one stamped field follow (21 shared fields). Nothing guarded the READER, so a key could be stamped correctly and consumed by nobody - which is what happened all nine times.

LANDED: tests/unit/kneemri/inference/members.py::test_every_recorded_field_is_either_consumed_or_declared_unread. Builds the config the WRITER actually stamps (imports its helper rather than copying it), and asserts recorded == CONSUMED | PROVENANCE_ONLY - 27 keys = 20 with a declared serve-side reader + 7 declared unread (ema, rank_weight, pair_memory, report_weight, unfreeze_last, head_lr, backbone_lr: training rules that leave no trace in a forward pass). Then probes each consumed key with a second legal value and demands its reader follow. A NEW recorded field can no longer arrive with no consumer and no stated reason for having none.

TWO OTHER AUDIT RESULTS, written down so they are not re-derived:

  - READING/ROUTING NEED NO LANDED CHECK. StudyCache.key() puts crop, band, router and truncation in the cache FILENAME, so a mis-wired reading is a FileNotFoundError on a memory map, not a silent swap. That is a stronger guard than a comparison and it already exists. Do not add one.
  - Ensemble.slices/decoded_scheme took 'members or self.package.members', so an EMPTY subset silently meant the whole package - a default in two methods whose own docstrings say 'derived, never defaulted'. Unreachable today (reads() groups are non-empty and members[0] would raise first), fixed anyway to 'is None' via Ensemble._asked so an empty subset surfaces as max() refusing an empty sequence / agreed() refusing zero distinct values.
close_reason: Closed

title: Landed guard does not reach the DATA switches: --weight-floor, --calibrated-targets, crop/band/centre/scheme
description: kneemri.training.landed now checks 14 switches across the model, trainer, objective and augmentation. The switches that map to a DATA argument rather than to a policy object are still outside it: Supervision (--weight-floor, --calibrated-targets) is consumed by Targets.load, and the routing/crop/band/centre trio shapes the cache read. RESOLVED IN PART, AND THE OTHER PART IS VOID BY CONSTRUCTION.

Targets now carries the Supervision it was loaded under and answers for it via supervised(); Landed takes the targets as a third authority and Request gained weight_floor/calibrated_targets. wanted() re-derives the floor from the FLAG rather than reading arguments.supervision.floor, so a broken bool-to-value rule in TrainingOptions.supervision is visible at the guard instead of only in the loss.

Recorded because the same reasoning applies to any future data axis: put it in the cache key and it guards itself.
