title: The 0.20-0.80 slice band discards the outer 20% of the medial-lateral extent — where the lateral compartment lives
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-17, no GPU. Two facts already in the repo that have never been put next to each other.

1. knee-yrg: Lateral Meniscus 0.7981 is our WEAKEST label of twelve and Lateral OA 0.8215 is fourth-weakest; medial beats lateral by +0.0622 and +0.0472, far outside the intervals. The bead refutes the laterality flip as the cause and lists three untested mechanism candidates — one of them 'the lateral compartment sits nearer the edge of a 130 mm crop', which is the IN-PLANE crop.

2. slot_reader.py:34 SLICE_BAND = (0.20, 0.80), documented as 'the outermost slices of a knee series are mostly soft tissue outside the joint'. On a SAGITTAL series the slice axis IS the medial-lateral axis, so this rule discards the outer 20% at each end of medial-lateral before any model sees a pixel — and the structures it discards first are exactly the peripheral meniscus and the lateral compartment.

The in-plane crop was named as a candidate; the THROUGH-plane band was not, and it is the more direct one: an in-plane crop centred on the joint keeps the lateral compartment at the edge of the field, whereas the band removes those slices from the array entirely.

WHY THIS IS NOT A KNOB. knee-nas5 establishes the decode path is the only ensemble axis that transfers to the board at MORE than the usual compression (0.0059 offline -> 0.014 board, 2.4x), and that band_low/band_high have NEVER been varied by anything — every one of the six all-ours members ran the default. So this is simultaneously the untouched half of the highest-transfer axis and a targeted mechanism for the weakest label. knee-yrg prices lifting the four weakest labels to 0.87 at +0.0189 on the mean, which clears the 1.5% bar.

THE CHEAP MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT BEFORE ANY TRAINING (zero GPU): for the sagittal slots, take slices-per-series and slice spacing from the DICOM headers and compute how many MM the band drops at each end. If it is 8-15 mm the peripheral meniscus is inside the discarded region and the mechanism is live; if it is 2-3 mm the band is removing air and this is dead. State the DENOMINATOR — mm dropped over the medial-lateral extent of the corpus, not of the subset that parses.

THE ARM, if the geometry holds: --band-low 0.05 --band-high 0.95 at the SAME 12 epochs and the same RECIPE as the pool (crop80 ran 8 against the pool's 12 and the mismatch alone is priced at -0.0028, which is why its verdict is contested). Needs its own cache — Band.suffix() keys it as _0.05-0.95band, so it cannot clobber the historic arrays.

READ IT TWO WAYS, per knee-nas5: solo AUC per label (does Lateral Meniscus move?) AND marginal contribution to the ensemble, since a member that fails differently by construction can pay without winning solo.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-17, same 400 studies / 1848 series, ONE Otsu threshold per SERIES instead of per slice.

The per-slice reading was inflated, as suspected, and by enough to reverse the verdict: a
background-only end slice was getting its own histogram split, so its noise thresholded into
'tissue'. SAG_FLUID_FS 0.4598 -> 0.3545. Corrected:
  AX_FLUID_FS     0.4162 [0.4102,0.4221] p90 0.4796  low 0.1842 high 0.2320  span 125.8mm  cut/end 25.2mm
  COR_FLUID_FS    0.3924 [0.3840,0.4007] p90 0.4950  low 0.0865 high 0.3060  span 107.6mm  cut/end 21.5mm
  COR_T1          0.2917 [0.2867,0.2968] p90 0.3486  low 0.0903 high 0.2014  span 107.0mm  cut/end 21.4mm
  SAG_FLUID_FS    0.3545 [0.3474,0.3609] p90 0.4286  low 0.1726 high 0.1820  span 103.8mm  cut/end 20.8mm
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS  0.3645 [0.3581,0.3704] p90 0.4246  low 0.1796 high 0.1849  span 104.6mm  cut/end 20.9mm
  SAG_T1          0.3725 [0.3630,0.3816] p90 0.4474  low 0.1843 high 0.1882  span 101.8mm  cut/end 20.4mm

VERDICT: SPLIT, and neither half is a result.
- Tissue-share axis: 0.3545 on SAG_FLUID_FS against a 0.4000 uniform baseline. The ends are SPARSER
  than the middle, which is the constant's claim, directionally confirmed. It is not the 0.02 that
  would have killed the mechanism outright — a third of the imaged tissue is still discarded — but
  the cheap kill direction leaned the constant's way, not the hypothesis's.
- Distance axis: 20.8 mm cut from EACH end of a 103.8 mm sagittal span. The acceptance test written
  into this bead was 8-15mm = live, 2-3mm = dead. 20.8 mm clears the live bar by 40%.
- The two disagree because they measure different things, and the measurement CANNOT reconcile them:
  discarded TISSUE is not discarded JOINT. The sagittal ends hold thigh and calf, which is why the
  share is sub-uniform, AND they hold whatever compartment sits in the outer 20 mm. Nothing
  label-free separates those.
- No medial-lateral asymmetry: SAG_FLUID_FS low 0.1726 vs high 0.1820, so the band does not cut the
  lateral side harder than the medial. That WEAKENS the specific route from this constant to
  knee-yrg's Lateral Meniscus 0.7981 — a symmetric cut is not an obvious source of an asymmetric
  label deficit.

GATE. This is no longer decidable without a label. The remaining test is a band-diverse member
(0.10-0.90) against the current pool, which costs a fresh cache and a GPU slot. Priority DOWN from
P1: the asymmetry argument that motivated it did not survive, and what is left is 'a diversity axis
nothing has varied' — real, but that is knee-nas5's general claim, not a lateral-meniscus mechanism.

Method note for whoever runs the next coverage measurement: per-slice Otsu is right for a
WITHIN-slice question (TissueCentre's centroid) and wrong for a BETWEEN-slice one. It moved a
headline number by 0.10 here.
close_reason: Answered by the three-point span axis, and answered NEGATIVE in the direction this bead proposed. The bead asked whether the discarded outer 20% holds the lateral compartment; band_full read exactly that (0.00-1.00 at 12 slices, matched to band_span on every other field) and scored 0.8427 against band_span's 0.8565 - 2.2x the 0.0062 floor. Per label the outer tenths COST the regional group (-0.0185, Baker's -0.0247*, ACL -0.0236*, Contusion -0.0216*) and both lateral rows are flat (Lateral Meniscus +0.0023, Lateral OA -0.0017), so they are not what the outer slices were withholding. The axis has an interior optimum at 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565; 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525 and 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427. Recorded in experiments/README.md as band_full's row.

title: One unreadable slice header reorders the WHOLE series
description: acquisition.py:131-134 — ordered_files computes a through-plane key per file and, if ANY key is None, returns self.files unsorted. So a single corrupt/odd file (no geometry tags, unreadable header) drops the geometric sort for every other slice in the series, and the central band then samples name order instead of depth. Names are arbitrary UIDs in the real corpus, so the band lands somewhere unrelated to anatomy while the presence mask still reports the slot acquired — the same failure shape as the majority-shape bug, one level up. Found 2026-08-17 while testing the neighbour-fill path (a garbage file silently changed which slices were sampled). Fix: sort the files that HAVE keys and leave the keyless ones in their relative place (or drop them), rather than abandoning the sort. Caveat: this changes the cache for any affected series, so it lands when a cache is next rebuilt. Measure first — count series in the corpus with >=1 keyless file (diagnose-style pass); it may be zero here and still be insurance for the hidden test.
close_reason: Fixed: ordered_files now sorts the files that HAVE a through-plane key and leaves each keyless file in its own slot, instead of abandoning the sort for the whole series. Measured before fixing (denominator stated): 0 of 1682 series over 300 studies (6.8% of the corpus) hold a keyless file, and 0 would have their order moved — so no cached array changes and the fix is unmeasurable here by construction. It is insurance for the hidden test. Test: tests/unit/kneemri/corpus/acquisition.py::test_ordered_files_keeps_sorting_around_one_unreadable_header, mutation-checked against the old fallback.

title: Unfreeze 4 blocks instead of 6: 25% faster, and the one-epoch score went the wrong way
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 (throughput_unfreeze4, one epoch, eager, whole-stack max): 1019 img/s against the eager control's 815 = +25% throughput, 13.11 GB peak against 14.56. Epoch-0 holdout 0.7539 against 0.7604 = -0.0065, which is inside the 0.0053-ish floor at one epoch and unreadable as a score.

WHY IT IS WORTH A REAL ARM: 25% compounds across every future arm, which is worth more than most single-arm results, and our own evidence says capacity is not the constraint here (base over small was +0.0011 against the floor) - precisely the condition under which opening four blocks rather than six should be close to free. But this is the ONLY row in the throughput set whose direction is negative, so 'close to free' is not yet supported by anything.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one twelve-epoch whole-stack arm at --unfreeze-last 4 against res392_ws_s2026's recipe, judged on the twelve-label mean with the paired interval. Needs a training slot. Until then the default stays 6.

Prices and their reading: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_what_the_throughput_arms_priced.md
close_reason: Closed

title: ledger_check reports the documented smoke as an UNRECORDED run
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17: a clean pipeline check exits 1 with 'UNRECORDED member_fold0: best 0.5639'.

That run IS the smoke CLAUDE.md documents — 'python -m kneemri.training.train --labels $LABELS --studies 60 --epochs 1', no --out, so it writes the default member_fold0.pt. The exemption in ledger_check is UNQUOTABLE = ('throughput', 'smoke'), a match on NAME FRAGMENTS, and the documented invocation produces a name carrying neither.

So the check cries wolf on its own project's documented pre-flight, every time the pipeline is smoked. A check that fails on correct behaviour teaches the reader to skip its output, which is precisely the failure it exists to prevent (five arms sat in the ledger as 'queued' for two days).

FIX: read the run's own recipe, not its name. The checkpoint's options block carries studies='60' — a run that capped the corpus it touched is a smoke BY CONSTRUCTION, and RecordedRun.of() already reads that field from whichever of the two records carries it. Keep the name fragments for 'throughput', which is a real class the recipe cannot state.
notes: Found by running ledger_check after a routine smoke, 2026-08-17.
close_reason: truncated() reads the run's recipe through RecordedRun; the documented smoke (member_fold0, no --out) is now exempt by construction. 68 finished runs -> 67, exit 0.

title: GPU is shared and a run cannot see it: uncapped smoke crawled to 12 img/s, then nvlddmkm reset killed both projects' runs
description: 2026-08-17 ~11:08-11:11 local. A 60-study one-epoch smoke (normally seconds) ran at 33 then 12 img/s and died at step 4/4 with no traceback, no epoch line and no checkpoint. Cause was outside this repo: biohub_kaggle celltrack.training.joint_detector held the 5090 at 32052/32607 MiB, and the System log shows three nvlddmkm Event ID 153 engine resets in four minutes. Both projects' processes were gone afterwards and the card returned to 1280 MiB / 4%. DeviceBudget's docstring already described exactly this (Windows pages VRAM over PCIe instead of raising OOM, so an over-committed run crawls at a reported 100% utilisation) but nothing READ it: a cap is arithmetic against the card total, and the total does not move when another process holds the card. Fixed the blindness — DeviceBudget.headroom() reads torch.cuda.mem_get_info and select() logs a WARNING naming free/total before the first batch. Not fixed: the default is still uncapped (--vram-gb 0), so the documented worst failure mode remains the default, and there is no cross-project lock. Open questions: should a run REFUSE to start when free VRAM is under its budget rather than warn, and should --vram-gb default to a share of the card. Do not change the default silently — queued arms record the flag.
notes:
Both open questions decided and implemented (636abe8).

REFUSE vs WARN: it refuses, but not on the cap's test. The cap defaults to 0.8 of the card, so 'free < capped' would refuse whenever the co-tenant holds a fifth of it — common, and harmless to a 5.5 GB smoke. That stays a WARNING. The fatal test is DeviceBudget.floor(): SMALLEST_RUN_GB = 5.5, read off 224 recorded epoch rows whose vram_peak_gb spans 5.47 (dinov3_v3small_224_s2026) to 26.24 — below the cheapest run we know how to train, no recipe fits, and Windows answers an over-commit by paging over PCIe rather than raising. A run naming --vram-gb below the floor is taken at its word (min of the two). Refusal sits PAST await_headroom, so an explicit budget still waits out its full bound and only refuses if the card stayed held.

--vram-gb default: unchanged, as the bead demanded — queued arms record the flag, so a silent default change would rewrite what they meant.
close_reason: Closed

title: Best ensemble subset peaks at five over the 13 same-split members; deep24 joins it despite scoring below the pool floor
description: Scored all 13 checkpoints sharing split_seed 2026 / fold 0 of 5 (six all_ours + conf24, deep24, pair_memory, schedule_8, slices16_ws, dinov3_base_lora, dinov3_v3small_224) as one pool. Best-5 = 0.8617 (calibrated_targets + deep24 + extended_ws + intensity392_ws + res392_ws), best-4 0.8615, and every larger subset falls monotonically to 0.8547 flat over all 13. +0.0005 over the six-pool best-4 (0.8612) — directional, free, no training. Two consequences: (a) deep24 solo is 0.8352, BELOW the all-ours floor of 0.8459 and within 0.0007 of crop80's 0.8345, yet joint selection takes it at every size and never takes crop80 — solo score is not what decides whether a member pays, so the 'must score in the pool's range' rule filed earlier is wrong and the interpretation now says so; (b) per-label selection over 13 (top-5 honest 0.8609) is beaten by one fixed subset of five (0.8617), so per-label selection only recovers what flat averaging over a bad pool discarded. Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md. Next: the entry that ships should be a chosen subset, not everything on disk.

title: MEASURED: the combiner form is a flat axis — rank vs logit vs quality-weighted all within 0.0005
description:
The one ensemble axis that had never been varied is now measured, on cached probabilities, no card.

Six all-ours members (fold 0, report_labels_v2):
  RankAverage (shipped)  0.8598
  LogitAverage           0.8603   (+0.0005)
  QualityWeightedRank    0.8600   (+0.0002, split-half, weights fitted off the scored half)

The pair that scored 0.919 on the board:
  RankAverage  0.8581 | LogitAverage 0.8583 | QualityWeightedRank 0.8580

Every spread is an order of magnitude below the 0.0053 board noise floor and two below the 1.5% bar. The flat per-label rank-average is leaving nothing on the table: neither keeping the confidence margin (logits) nor weighting by member quality buys anything measurable.

CONCLUSION: the combiner is NOT a lever. Ensemble gains live in the MEMBERS (count, and above all decode/pixel-group diversity, which is the axis that transfers to the board at 2.4x its offline size), not in how their votes are counted. Do not spend a training slot or a submission on a combiner variant.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: a learned/stacked combiner fitted on more than one fold, and a combiner over members that DISAGREE far more than these six do (all six share a training recipe lineage). Both need data this measurement did not have; neither is worth building before the member pool diversifies.

LANDED: kneemri/inference/vote.py — Vote/RankAverage/QualityWeightedRank/LogitAverage. Ensemble.combine now DELEGATES to RankAverage, so there is one definition of the ranking and the submission path is provably unchanged (tests/unit/kneemri/inference/vote.py::test_combine asserts array-equality against the pre-refactor arithmetic). member_curve prints the comparison on every run.
notes: 2026-08-17: written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md (all six axes, each with its measured status) and linked from the README's ensembling paragraph. Test name is now test_rank_average_combine (mirror gate wants the method-named form).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] RunComparison judged the view off the FLAG list, which the whole-stack control predates
description: moved_view/reader_change read the recipe (vars(RunOptions)), and wsfold0_e6 — the whole-stack control the 2026-08-17 re-read rests on — records no crop_mm flag at all. Absence-as-difference gave a schedule arm and a loss arm resolution verdicts they had not earned; the both-must-record fix then removed the verdict from crop80_tissue, which DID move the view. The provable source is the checkpoint's config block: it states crop_mm 130.0 for that control because the saver derived it from a nested Crop object, and it spans both eras of the ledger. Filling from today's parser defaults is not sound — bf16 appears as both True and False across the arms' predates lists.
close_reason: Closed

title: holdout back-fill stamps the run's LENGTH where the kept epoch belongs
description:
wsfold0_e6.holdout.npz records epoch=11 while the weights it re-derived from are the epoch-6 best — the reconstructed mean is 0.8457, which matches the ledger's epoch-6 number exactly, so the ARRAY is right and only the epoch integer is wrong. The back-fill appears to write the run's total epochs rather than the epoch the checkpoint kept.

Cosmetic today: HoldoutMetrics reports 'epoch 11' for a run whose weights are epoch 6, and nothing downstream keys on it. A mis-join tomorrow: any consumer that pairs a holdout record to a metrics row BY EPOCH would silently match the wrong row, and both files would still load.

Check kneemri/inference/holdout_backfill.py for where the epoch comes from, and audit the other 16 records for the same stamp. Found 2026-08-16 while re-reading knee-bot against the paired floor.
notes: AUDIT DONE 2026-08-16 (the bead asked for it): all 15 holdout records on disk checked against their own metrics file. Eight have both, and every one of those eight has a matching epoch stamp (calibrated_targets e6, crop80_tissue e7, dinov3_v3small e8, extended_ws e6, intensity392_ws e9, pair_memory e3, schedule_8 e7, slices16_ws e6). wsfold0_e6 is the only record with a wrong stamp and it is also the only one whose metrics file is MISSING, which is the mechanism: with no rows to read the epoch off, the back-fill falls back to the run's length. The remaining six (base20_fold0, base_fold0, base_s7_fold0, conf24_s2026, conf24_s7, deep24_s2026) are in that same state and so are unverifiable rather than clean - treat their stamps as suspect. Scope is now: fix holdout_backfill.py to refuse a stamp it cannot source, rather than guessing the length.
close_reason: Fixed + repaired on disk. StampedRun no longer derives kept_epoch from epochs_done (which is the run's CONFIGURED LENGTH on the pre-epoch half: wsfold0_e6, base_fold0, conf24_s2026 all have epochs_done == options.epochs). kept_epoch is None when unwritten; the back-fill records UNKNOWN_EPOCH = -1 rather than refusing, so the 36 stamped-but-unmetriced runs stay re-derivable. New HoldoutRecord.restamp corrects an existing record's epoch with no inference; run over the corpus, the seven guessed stamps (base20_fold0, base_fold0, base_s7_fold0, conf24_s2026, conf24_s7, deep24_s2026, wsfold0_e6) now read -1 and the eight sourced ones are unchanged. Second pass moves nothing. Gates green, 634 passed.

title: Let RunComparison restrict a per-label delta to the half its change could move
description:
SupervisionGap.bottlenecked() now returns the split as data (label_side / model_side, commit 3afacf5). Nothing consumes it yet except the module's own report().

The consumer that would pay is RunComparison: an arm's headline is the mean over twelve per-label AUCs, so a label-reader change is averaged with the six findings a reader cannot move, and an imaging change with the six the pixels cannot. Six of noise added to six of signal, on a ruler whose floor is 0.0053 — that is a real dilution of exactly the size that decides keep/kill.

Shape: RunComparison gains a view restricted to a named subset of labels, and an arm declares which KIND of change it is so the comparison picks the right half. NOT a new metric to report as the arm's score — the ledger number stays the twelve-label mean so it stays comparable with itself, the same reason supervision_gap refuses to move the 0.5 ruler cut. The restricted view is a second column that says whether the change moved what it could plausibly move.

DESIGN DECISION NOT YET MADE, and it is the reason this is a bead rather than a commit: whether the KIND is declared by the arm (a flag in the recipe line, which RunMetrics already records and RunComparison already reads) or inferred. Declared is honest and needs the arm scripts touched; inferred is guessing. Audit the arm scripts before choosing.
notes: 2026-08-16: design decision RESOLVED — the comparison INFERS the kind, the arm does not declare it. Deciding argument: arms are shell scripts, so a declaration only covers runs made after it lands, while every run in the ledger already carries its recipe in its metrics file. Landed in 714b25b: RunComparison.reader_change() reads the RAW recipe diff (not the NOT_AN_AXIS-filtered one — a swapped label table is the clearest reader change and is exactly what the confound check waives) against SUPERVISION_AXES, and report() prints it under each arm. REMAINING HALF: restrict the printed per-label deltas to Bottleneck.label_side / model_side. That needs SupervisionGap's reference-vs-achieved AUCs, which need the published OOF corpus, so it is a real dependency and not a refactor — RunComparison would take a Bottleneck and main() a way to build one.
close_reason: RunComparison now takes a Bottleneck and prints each arm's deltas restricted to its own half (label_side for a reader change, model_side for an imaging change), labelled the arm's CLAIM not its score — the ledger number stays the twelve-label mean. Opt-in --split, refused without --labels. SupervisionGap gained aligned() (the three-file join, shared with its own main) and measured() (the split from three paths). moved() gave the recipe+view diff one home. 09544d1.

title: Three runs each lost a multi-hour epoch to an unexplained stall (20.8h total)
description:
Across the 24 metrics files under D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed, three runs each carry exactly ONE epoch of several hours while every other epoch is normal:

  dinov3_v3splus_224_lr8e-6_s2026  median 104s, one epoch 16794s
  pair_memory_s2026                median 234s, one epoch 27266s
  slices16_ws_s2026                median 443s, one epoch 30684s

Total ~74,700s = 20.8 hours of unattended wall-clock, on a project whose stated constraint is wall-clock.

Same shape each time: one epoch, hours long, surrounded by normal ones — so it is not a recipe cost. Most likely the machine suspended mid-run (see the WSL/hibernate note in the global CLAUDE.md); seconds is wall-clock and counts time the card spent doing nothing.

Two things to decide:
 (a) whether to prevent it (powercfg /h off is already the recommended fix for the related WSL wedge), and
 (b) whether epochs should record a start timestamp so a stall is identifiable rather than inferred.

RunMetrics.epoch_seconds() now reports the MEDIAN, so no throughput comparison is corrupted by this any more — that half is done. This bead is the stall itself.
notes:
2026-08-17: part (b) DONE. EpochRow now carries started (UNIX seconds at the top of the epoch, kneemri/training/fitting.py records it), and RunMetrics.stalls() names any epoch costing STALL_FACTOR=4x the run's median. RunComparison.report() prints one STALLED line per such epoch with its UTC start, so a future stall can be lined up against a suspend/resume rather than inferred. Validated across all 26 real .metrics.jsonl on disk: exactly two named (dinov3_v3splus_224_lr8e-6_s2026 epoch 7, 16794s vs median 104; slices16_ws_s2026 epoch 2, 30684s vs median 443), zero false positives. pair_memory_s2026's 27266s stall is NOT named because rows() answers for the last run in a re-used file and that stall belongs to the first — correct behaviour, not a miss. Part (a), whether to run powercfg /h off, is a machine-config decision and stays open.
2026-08-18: part (a) DONE IN CODE, not in the machine's power scheme. Measured the mechanism first: powercfg /a shows Hibernate + Fast Startup available, and the active scheme's AC 'sleep after' (SUB_SLEEP STANDBYIDLE) is 0x1c20 = 7200 s. That timer is driven by INPUT, not by load, so an unattended run providing no keystrokes suspends after two hours regardless of what the card is doing - which is exactly the observed shape (one epoch of hours, surrounded by normal ones; median epochs of 104-443 s are far under 7200).

FIX: core/wakelock.py + core/sleep_policy.py, wired into Fitting.run (32c0981). The epoch loop runs inside a Wakelock that asserts ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED on the fitting thread and releases on the way out, including out of a raise. Scoped to the JOB rather than to the machine: 'powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0' would fix it too and would keep fixing it long after the run that needed it. StaysAwake/Sleeps behind a SleepPolicy protocol selected by ThisMachine, so nothing branches at the call site.

VERIFIED THE MECHANISM FIRED, not just that it compiles: a real smoke run (60 studies, 1 epoch) logs 'wakelock: held' and the loss is unchanged at 1.3442. Gates green (Session gates was successful).

STILL OPEN: nothing wraps the LONG NON-TRAINING jobs (cache builds, the embedding encode pass) - same suspend, same cost. And ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED does not stop a MANUAL sleep or a lid close; it only stops the idle timer.
2026-08-18: the three long NON-training jobs now hold the wakelock too (df74441) - build_cache (decode, hours), build_embeddings (encode pass) and holdout_backfill (the 55-member walk). Each hold wraps the WORK span only: --print-key returns before the decode and takes nothing. Gates green. Remaining exposure is unchanged and is not code: ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED does not stop a manual sleep or a lid close.
2026-08-18 (851a7e9): coverage completed - member_curve (a full inference pass per uncached member over the pool) and attribution (six occlusion sweeps over the holdout) hold it too. Every hour-scale unattended entrypoint is now wrapped: train (Fitting.run), build_cache, build_embeddings, holdout_backfill, member_curve, attribution. Each hold covers the WORK span, never the argument parsing. Gates green, archmap regenerated. CLOSING: the stall is diagnosed (input-driven idle timer, AC standby 7200 s), fixed in code and verified firing in a real run. What is left is not code - ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED does not stop a manual sleep or a lid close.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two submissions record an offline number without recording what it was a number OF
description:
comp/board.jsonl marks trained_v3 (0.8481, 2 whole-stack members) and trained_v5 (0.8493, 3 members) as scope=unknown: the ledger never says whether those are the ENSEMBLE's holdout AUC or the MEAN of the members' individual holdouts. The two differ by however much averaging bought, so they cannot be subtracted from an ensemble number - board_transfer excludes both, which costs 2 of 7 usable entries and every pair they would have formed.

RECOVERABLE, probably without GPU: both entries' members are whole-stack checkpoints still on disk, and HoldoutRecord/knee-mx17 predictions exist for the later ones. Re-scoring the 2- and 3-member ensembles on the same holdout would settle it and is arithmetic over saved predictions if the arrays are there, a short re-inference if not.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO ROWS: the failure is that a number was recorded without its denominator, which is the exact class of error interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-16_board_transfer.md was written about. Whatever writes a future entry into comp/board.jsonl must record the scope at the same time.
close_reason: Both scopes recovered by arithmetic, no GPU: trained_v3 0.8481 = mean(0.845698, 0.850453) and trained_v5 0.8493 = mean(0.845698, 0.850453, 0.851827), exact to the recorded digits, so both are member_mean. They stay out of the ensemble reading, but --scope now makes each scope its own reading, and within member_mean both resolved pairs invert: member mean +0.021, board -0.006. The mechanism the two readings agree on is training-data COVERAGE (five folds vs 2-3 members of one split), not member count. Recorded as a note in comp/board.jsonl.

title: comp/members and comp/members_ours both claim dimiturnt/kneemri-members
description: Two local directories carry the same dataset id, so a push from either overwrites the live package and nothing says which one is mounted. Keep one home: the live package must be reproducible from a single committed member list.
close_reason: comp/members.roster (f3b25ea): one committed file names the package's members, package_members reads it, prepare_submission passes it, comp/members_ours deleted, comp/members regenerated and matching the six live members.

title: Ten call sites ask torch.cuda.is_available(), which is true with zero visible cards
description:
FOUND 2026-08-16 while trying to smoke a real arm on CPU with the card handed to another project.

MEASURED on this machine, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= :

  torch.cuda.is_available()   True
  torch.cuda.device_count()   0
  torch.cuda.current_device() 0     <- and get_device_properties(0) then raises

So 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu' — the expression in ten files — selects a device that owns no card. DeviceBudget.select then died with AssertionError: Invalid device id, which is what arm_check --smoke reported as BROKEN whole_stack.

THE KNOWLEDGE ALREADY EXISTED IN ONE PLACE: member_curve's --device help text spells out this exact failure ('CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= still leaves torch.cuda.is_available() true here, and the run dies on Invalid device id several minutes in') and worked around it with a flag. Nine other call sites carried the expression and none of the knowledge — the one-home rule, unenforced.

FIX: kneemri/device.py::select_device counts VISIBLE CARDS. Every consumer calls it; run_metrics guards its VRAM stats on the count too. The workaround flags stay (a caller may still want cpu with a card present); their DEFAULTS now answer correctly.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: it is what makes a CPU lane exist at all. The pipeline can be smoked end-to-end while the card belongs elsewhere, which is exactly when there is time to smoke it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-16, commit ecdd104. kneemri/device.py::VisibleCards.device() is the one home; ten call sites moved to it; run_metrics guards its VRAM stats on the count.

ONE THING THE FIX SURFACED that was not in the diagnosis: tests/integration/argv_to_checkpoint.py and mounts_to_kernel.py forced CPU by patching torch.cuda.is_available to False. That was the RIGHT seam while availability was the question, and the moment it stopped being the question those two suites would have gone on claiming to run on cpu while running on the card. Both now patch device_count, and eleven integration tests failed loudly in between rather than quietly passing - which is the only reason it was noticed.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: comp/kernels/*.py. Those are standalone Kaggle scripts that cannot import the package, and they run where a card exists.

title: A smoke reads the FULL cache, so an uncached arm still cannot be smoked
description: knee-35yc landed the truncation AXIS (--cache-studies, in the cache key as _first{N}) but not the smoke path's use of it. ArmSmoke.command appends --studies/--epochs/--out only, so a smoked arm resolves the FULL cache key: an arm on a reading nothing has decoded still dies on the memmap, which is the gap knee-35yc was filed for. DESIGN: (a) command() also appends --cache-studies <studies>, so every smoke reads the truncated cache; (b) before smoking, arm_check ensures that cache exists — decode 60 studies for the arm's reading if absent (seconds, not the two-hour full build). Needs ArmCheck._parsed exposed as a public readings() so uncached() and the ensure step share one parse.
notes: Landed c6bc17f. ArmSmoke.command passes --cache-studies as well as --studies; arm_check --smoke decodes the truncated cache first, once per distinct reading, never for a refused arm. StudyCache.decoded() and CorpusSplit collapsed two duplications on the way. Gates green (609 tests + cov). NOT proven end-to-end on real data: a real 60-study decode + 1-epoch train needs the card, which is with another workload.

title: final_fit_e12's metrics rows carry the epoch index in the auc column
description: The run was launched before the fitting.py fix that records NO_HOLDOUT for an unscored run, so its own metrics file has auc=0.0..11.0 — the epoch index standing in as a score. The checkpoint is correct (NaN); only the ledger rows are wrong. ledger_check.best reads the maximum of that column and will quote a 12-epoch final fit as scoring 11.0, beating every real member in the ledger. Repair: after the run lands, rewrite that run's auc column to NaN. The code path is already fixed for every later run — this is one file of stale generated output, not a defect.
notes: CORRECTION to the previous note: final_ws_e12 is the OUTPUT name of the final_fit_e12 ARM, not an earlier run — one run, two names, 12 rows, no duplicates. So the corrupt column is one file after all, as originally filed. The reader-side fix still stands and is still the right shape: RunMetrics.best() now returns None when the recipe says fold < 0, verified on the finished file (12 epochs, auc 0.0..11.0, best -> None) and leaving scored runs untouched (calibrated_targets_s2026 0.8495, crop80_tissue_s2026 0.8345). Preferred over repairing the file because the recorder can be wrong about a value while the recipe stays right, and any future run made by an older binary reads correctly too.

Verified on the finished file (best -> None) and on scored runs (calibrated_targets_s2026 0.8495, crop80_tissue_s2026 0.8345 unchanged). The stale file is left as-is by design — the recipe, not the recorded value, is the authority, so a run made by an older binary reads correctly too.

title: [bug] The loadcheck's three-precision comparison timed the same path three times
description:
Kernel version 8 reports, for all six members: fp32 18.7s / fp16 18.2s / bf16 19.7s and max|diff| vs fp32 of 0.00e+00 in BOTH comparisons — twelve exactly-zero diffs. Two arithmetics cannot agree to zero ULP, and that is the fingerprint of a null measurement.

MECHANISM. comp/kernels/kneemri-loadcheck/kneemri-loadcheck.py:158 opens torch.autocast with the loop's dtype, then calls predict_member — which at kneemri/inference/ensemble.py:335 opens its OWN autocast with the MEMBER's precision. The inner context wins, so every one of the three iterations ran at member.precision. The log proves it directly: 'was fitted in bf16 and this device cannot run it — serving fp16' is printed inside the fp32 iteration too.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE: the chunk-of-48 timings are real numbers for the member's own serving precision, which is what a submission actually runs. What is NOT known is the thing the loop was written to answer — whether fp32 costs anything over fp16 on a Turing card with no bf16 tensor cores, which is the choice the arm's own comment says has been guessed twice.

FIX: the kernel must set the precision where the member's precision is read, not around the call — pass the dtype into predict_member (or override member.precision per iteration), and assert the served dtype differs between iterations before trusting any diff. A comparison whose two arms are identical must fail loudly, not report 0.00e+00 as agreement.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-16. Mechanism: the loop set an OUTER autocast per dtype, but Ensemble.predict_member opens its own with an explicit dtype, which overrides it — so all three arms ran arithmetic(member) and reported max|diff| 0.0 twelve times.

Fix: the arithmetic decision is now injectable. New frozen dataclass Serving(views, budget, precision) in kneemri/inference/ensemble.py replaces the three optional Ensemble ctor args (PLR0913 was already at the limit); Ensemble.arithmetic serves serving.precision or member.precision, and the sm_80 bf16 downgrade still applies ON TOP so a forced bf16 on a T4 is reported as fp16 rather than making two arms identical by a second route. predict_member spells fp32 as a DISABLED autocast (autocast(dtype=float32) is not a thing — the non-finite fallback already spelled it that way), which is what makes the reference arm runnable at all. The loadcheck now builds ensemble_of(dtype) per arm and logs the RESOLVED dtype beside the asked one.

Test: tests/unit/kneemri/inference/ensemble.py::test_a_forced_precision_overrides_the_member_but_not_the_card — the forced dtype arrives, fp32 is expressible, and the emulation guard still fires at (7,5).

Not yet run on a T4; the numbers this produces are still unmeasured.
close_reason: Knob connected and tested; the T4 measurement it enables is not yet run (noted in knee-3vf's neighbourhood)

title: An arm whose cache does not exist yet cannot be smoked
description:
GAP found 2026-08-16 while landing multiscale.sh. arm_check --smoke runs every arm for one epoch on 60 studies and catches the axis a flag check cannot see (final_fit.sh asked for batch 12 of whole-stack 392px inside --vram-gb 22 and died in the attention backward). But it can only smoke arms whose cache is already on disk: arm_check reports UNCACHED and skips. So the ONE arm that most needs the check — a new reading axis, whose cache costs hours and whose memory point nobody has run — is exactly the one that cannot get it. multiscale.sh is 12 slots against the 6 whole_stack measured its 20 GB at; batch 6 restores the 864 images/step that budget was measured at, but that is arithmetic, not a measurement.

DESIGN: build_cache --studies N, decoding only the first N studies. MUST require --out. Not for correctness — StudyCache.build writes the real identifier list to index_<key>.json and load returns it, so a partial cache is self-describing and the trainer announces its own study count. The damage is that a truncated cache shares the FULL one's key and would overwrite a 71.6 GB artifact that cost two hours.

BLOCKED ON, and this is why it was filed rather than built: training resolves its cache root from paths.yaml (--paths) alone, so a scratch cache cannot be pointed at without a whole scratch data root carrying raw/ and labels/ too. Either train.py grows a cache-directory flag, or --studies writes into the processed root under a key that says it is partial.
notes: LANDED 533acca (truncation in the cache key + parser.error requiring --out for --holdout-fold) and c6bc17f (knee-zhqy: the smoke actually READS the truncated cache and decodes it first). The blocker in the description resolved the second way it lists: --cache-studies N writes into the processed root under a key that says it is partial (<size>px_<n>sl_first<N>), so no scratch data root is needed. Real-data end-to-end proof is knee-t37m.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-label member selection is dead on the all-ours pool: the ORACLE headroom is negative
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-16, no GPU, from cached holdout probabilities of the six all_ours members (fold 0, one shared split, 881 studies): python -m kneemri.evaluation.member_curve --checkpoints <all_ours>/*.pt --labels report_labels_v2.csv --paired

  oracle 0.8590  vs plain average 0.8598  vs best single 0.8523  (headroom -0.0008)
  top-1 per label: in-sample 0.8590  split-half 0.8522
  top-3 per label: in-sample 0.8638  split-half 0.8609
  top-4 per label: in-sample 0.8631  split-half 0.8615
  top-6 per label: in-sample 0.8597  split-half 0.8598 (= the flat rank-average)

The ORACLE picks the best member per label USING THE ANSWERS and still lands BELOW the flat rank-average. That is not selection optimism being punished by an honest estimator — it is the strategy having no ceiling to reach: averaging six members beats the best single member on every label by more than per-label selection can recover, because selection throws away the other five votes. The best honest variant (top-4) buys +0.0017, a fifth of the significance bar.

So LabelCombine has now been measured and the answer is NO for this pool. Do NOT spend a submission slot on per-label member selection or per-label AUC weighting; the mechanism that would carry them is absent. It does NOT rule out per-label weighting that keeps every member and only tilts the weights, but the negative oracle bounds what that could ever buy at well under the bar.

The number lives in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md and this bead; LabelCombine itself stays — it is the estimator that answered the question.
notes:
SECOND, INDEPENDENT REFUTATION — from the OBJECTIVE side this time, 2026-08-19.

This bead killed per-label treatment at the ENSEMBLING stage (oracle headroom negative: per-label selection 0.8612-0.8626 vs plain averaging 0.8654-0.8663). The 'per_label_loss' arm has now killed it at the TRAINING stage, and the two failures are at opposite ends of the pipeline, which is what makes the pair worth more than either alone.

per_label_loss normalised the loss per column so each of the twelve findings weighs one twelfth, against a real and correctly-stated data mismatch (Effusion positive in 2,666 studies, Fracture in 314, so pooled CE spends ~10x more gradient on one while the score counts them equally). It scored 0.8414 vs control 0.8457, -0.0043 — inside the 0.0062 floor on the mean, so the mean alone decides nothing.

THE PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFIABLE CLAUSE IS WHAT SETTLES IT, and this is why the arm was worth running: it stated in writing that a gain must CONCENTRATE in the rare labels (Fracture 314, Synovitis 580, MCL 767) and that a uniform shift would mean something else moved it. Against weight_average, the matched per-label control (same recipe, same epochs, 0.8460 vs 0.8457 on the mean):
  Fracture  0.785 -> 0.763   -0.022
  Lat Men   0.816 -> 0.809   -0.007
  ACL       0.876 -> 0.869   -0.007
  Med Men   0.880 -> 0.874   -0.006
  MCL       0.752 -> 0.750   -0.002
  Synovitis 0.880 -> 0.878   -0.002
  Effusion  0.846 -> 0.849   +0.003
Not uniform: eleven labels within -0.007, one three times further out. It concentrates exactly where the arm predicted AND IT IS NEGATIVE THERE. The rarest label takes the largest loss and it is the label the reweighting up-weighted hardest.

MECHANISM: up-weighting a 314-positive column multiplies the VARIANCE of its gradient without adding information — the same few studies speak louder, so the encoder fits their noise. AUC being rank-based and invariant to the positive rate (which the arm itself named first as the reason this might do nothing) means there was no offsetting gain.

CAVEAT ON THE DENOMINATOR: 314 positives is the least stable AUC in the table, so -0.022 carries the widest interval of any cell here. Directional evidence, not a measured effect size. The SIGN and the ORDERING are the load-bearing parts, not the magnitude.

READING: prevalence in this dataset is not a mismatch to be corrected — it is the budget that buys the common labels their scores. Per-label treatment is closed on both sides. Ledger: experiments/README.md, section 'Per-label loss weighting is refuted a second time'.

title: inference and evaluation import each other; the records belong to neither
description:
After the eight-subpackage split (d02b6f6) and the layer contracts (e1edc9b), five contracts hold. The one axis that could NOT be written is inference <-> evaluation:

  inference.holdout_backfill -> evaluation.holdout_record, member_record, run_metrics
  evaluation.attribution, member_curve, oof_oracle, member_record -> inference.holdout_predictions, members, ensemble

The cycle is not accidental: holdout_record / member_record / run_metrics are STORAGE for what a run produced. Producers are training and inference; the consumer is evaluation. A type placed with its consumer makes every producer import upward.

Candidate fix: a runs/ (or records/) subpackage holding the three record types, imported by training, inference and evaluation alike and importing none of them. Then a contract 'records import nothing above corpus' plus 'inference must not import evaluation' both become writable. Check first whether the record types drag scores/LabelScores with them - if they do, the split is between the record and its scoring, and that is the real finding.
close_reason: Done in the same session it was filed: kneemri/runs/ now holds holdout_record, member_record and run_metrics. The audit the bead asked for came back clean — none of the three imports scores/LabelScores, they reach corpus and models only — so no split between record and scoring was needed. Two contracts landed with it: 'a run's records sit on corpus and models alone' and 'inference serves; it never imports the layer that scores it'. Gates green.

title: witness_check passes a kit it verified nothing about (0 ok, 3 unverified, exit 0)
description:
Ran comp/witness_check.py --device cpu on the default kit today: '0 ok, 3 unverified, 0 refused', exit 0. The three wsfold members predate the witness, so nothing is re-derived — and the pre-submission gate reports success. The check can only REFUSE a moved number; it cannot REQUIRE that a claim was made at all, which is the same 'silence read as a match' failure run_comparison.unmatched exists to close on the recipe axis.

Defaulting to exit 1 is wrong today: every packaged member predates the witness (knee-stp) and re-fitting is GPU-blocked, so the gate would be permanently red for a reason it cannot fix. What it must do instead is (a) say UNVERIFIABLE loudly when zero members carry a witness rather than printing a success-shaped summary, and (b) offer --require-witness so kit_check / any automated path can demand the strong claim.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin the two-home drift surface between TrainingOptions fields and its parser
description: TrainingOptions declares 45 fields with defaults AND an argparse flag with a default for each: two homes for every number. A drift between them is silent — every unit test constructs TrainingOptions() directly, so a parser default that moves means the CLI trains a different recipe than every test proves. Both are clean today (checked: 0 diverging defaults, 0 fields without a flag, 0 flags without a field), so pin it: expose the parser as its own classmethod and assert (a) parse() with only --labels equals the dataclass defaults, (b) every field is reachable from argv and no flag lands nowhere.
close_reason: Closed

title: One slice-group depth, four declarations of it
description: GROUP = 3 is declared in trainer.py, member_record.py, holdout_predictions.py and train.py (the last one dead). It is one legislated value — how many slices one encoder feature covers — and the three live copies are the TRAIN side, the RECORDED side and the SERVE side of the same number. If any one of them moves, a member is fitted at one depth, stamped with another and windowed at a third, with every fingerprint still passing: the repo's named failure class, pre-staged. One home in slot_reader beside IMAGE_SIZE and SLICE_BAND, imported by the three consumers; the dead one deleted.
close_reason: Closed

title: build_embeddings and ruler_check cannot name a non-default reading
description: Both build a StudyCache from CLI args that have no crop or band flag (ruler_check also drops image_size and routing), so they silently resolve to the default arrays. Not the member-driven defect — nothing is claiming to follow a recorded reading — but once the 80 mm cache exists these two cannot be pointed at it at all. Give them the same reading flags the trainer takes.
close_reason: Closed

title: The training step reads the loss back to the host every step, so the CPU can never run ahead of the card
description:
fit_epoch does total += float(loss.detach()) on every step (trainer.py:441). float() on a device tensor is a SYNCHRONISATION: it blocks the host until the backward that produced it has finished, so the CPU cannot queue the next step's kernels while the current one runs. The prefetch landed in knee-4o4r hides the READ behind the step; this undoes part of that gain by making the host wait at the end of every step anyway.

The value is only ever consumed twice: the epoch mean returned at the end, and the heartbeat line printed about once per thirty SECONDS. Neither needs a per-step host read.

FIX: accumulate into a float64 tensor on the device and materialise once per epoch (identical arithmetic - each float32 loss is promoted to float64 and summed, which is what the host loop does today). Heartbeat.tick takes the loss as a callable so the mean is computed only on the ticks that actually print.

predict has the same shape: chunks.append(torch.sigmoid(scored).cpu().numpy()[:rows]) transfers per batch. Keep the trimmed chunks on the device and make ONE transfer after the loop - the holdout is 881x12 floats.

Cannot be measured without the card, so this lands on the mechanism plus an equality test, and the timing is claimed only after the next arm runs.
close_reason: Closed

title: The batch fetch still waits in front of the GPU instead of beside it
description: Even at the FileReader's speed the fetch is serial with compute: fit_epoch reads a batch, then steps, then reads the next. At 448 whole-stack that is ~98 ms of host read per step that the GPU spends idle. A one-deep prefetch (read batch k+1 on a worker while step k runs, hand over a pinned tensor and copy with non_blocking=True) hides it. Determinism is preservable exactly, which is the thing that makes this safe: the only numpy draws inside the loop are the permutation and one window start per step, with nothing between them, so drawing every start up front in step order yields the identical sequence of values. The oracle is that: the prefetched (batch, start) stream must equal the serial one element for element, and the epoch's pixels must be byte-identical.
close_reason: Prefetch lands: one step of lookahead on a single worker, pinned handover, non_blocking copy, used by fit_epoch and predict. 448 whole-stack, real cache, device-like step: 98.3 -> 77.2 ms/step. Determinism preserved exactly via Trainer.plan (starts drawn up front in step order — same seed, same numbers), asserted by test_plan and test_iter, both mutation-checked. Caveat recorded in the commit: no gain against a CPU-saturating step, since a warm read is a memcpy.

title: Batch fetch reads the cache by memmap fancy-index, at half the disk's speed
description: fit_epoch gathers each batch with corpus.images[batch, :, s:s+G] on a uint8 memmap. Measured on the 448/12 cache (14.5 MB per study, whole-stack batch of 12 = 174 MB): memmap gather 196 ms cold / 65 ms warm, the same bytes read with explicit seek+readinto into a preallocated buffer 104 ms cold / 27 ms warm. Two disjoint corpus halves, tested both ways round, so it is not a page-cache artefact. The gap is per-4KB-page fault overhead, not NVMe bandwidth: 174 MB is ~42k faults per batch. Fetch is synchronous on the training thread, so this is wall-clock straight off every step of any arm whose cache cannot stay page-resident (the 63.7 GB 448 cache, against 54.7 GB free RAM, never can). Fix: give CachedCorpus a window() that reads the batch explicitly when its images are file-backed, proven by an equality oracle against the fancy-index it replaces.
close_reason: FileReader lands: explicit seek+readinto over two handles, chosen by CachedCorpus.reader when the pixels are file-backed. Fetch per batch of 12: 336 windowed 65->19 ms, 336 whole-stack 131->54, 448 windowed 93->29, 448 whole-stack 194->98; holds warm too (65->31). Equality oracle against the indexing it replaces, in the unit and on both real caches. Overlap with compute is left open (it would reorder generator draws) — see follow-up.

title: ledger_check re-reads metrics files by hand instead of through RunMetrics
description: LedgerCheck.best parses the JSONL itself and keeps any row whose auc is not None. RunMetrics.best exists, drops NaN, and is the reader every other consumer goes through. Two consequences: an unscored final fit (--fold -1) records NaN, which passes the is not None filter and can come back from max() as nan — quoted as 'nan' and reported UNRECORDED forever; and the recipe line this repo now writes into the same file is a second row shape the hand parser has to keep stepping over. One reader, not two.
close_reason: Closed

title: slot_pooling's vocabulary is spelled in five places and dispatched with an if, so an unknown value silently builds the attention head
description: model.py:146 does MeanSlotHead if design.slot_pooling == mean else SlotHead - anything that is not exactly the string mean gets the attention head, including a typo and any future third pooling. description: slots.CANONICAL_SCHEME keys SCHEMES and decides whether Routing adds a suffix to the cache key; StudyCache.CANONICAL and members.CANONICAL are separate copies of the same literal, and embedding_cache.py:119 plus head_trial.py:123 still spell it raw. title: checkpoint_to_submission builds its own checkpoint payload by hand
description: tests/integration/checkpoint_to_submission.py::_save hand-writes a three-key dict (model/holdout/config) under a docstring that says it is 'the shape train.py writes'. It is not: the real save goes through MemberRecord.payload, which also writes the fingerprint, the fingerprint_config, the epoch and the witness. title: Two fakes in the training chain: a stand-in options class and a hand-wired Trainer
description: tests/unit/kneemri/member_record.py defines _Options, a 19-field copy of TrainingOptions, and tests/integration/corpus_to_checkpoint.py builds Trainer(model, DEVICE) + trainer.whole_stack(...) by hand instead of going through TrainingOptions.fitted_trainer. title: package_members writes the manifest inside main(), so the integration test hand-copies its format
description:
package_members.py is one main(): argument parsing, a glob, a copy loop, manifest assembly and two writes. The manifest rows are the CONTRACT between training and every kernel - id, file, fold, config, fingerprint, holdout, annot - and nothing can call that assembly without a data root and a real checkpoint on disk.

WHAT THAT ALREADY COST: tests/integration/corpus_to_checkpoint.py (landed today) has to hand-write the format-2 manifest to package the member it just fitted. That duplicate is a FAKE: if package_members ever changes a key, the integration test keeps passing against the shape it froze, and the chain it claims to prove is no longer the chain that ships.

ALSO UNREACHABLE, and each is a real defect the assembly can carry: float(checkpoint['holdout']) writes NaN for a full-data fit (see knee-2d7); two patterns matching two files with the same NAME in different directories collide on both the copied file and the manifest id, and the second silently wins; fold is parsed out of the id by string surgery.

DO: lift the row assembly and the manifest document out of main() into callable units beside their producer (not a types module), have the integration test build its package through the REAL producer, and cover the id-collision and NaN-holdout cases that only a caller can reach.
close_reason: Closed

title: Our ruler calls 45% of cells positive; the radiologist calls 34%
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the 58 annotated studies (python -m kneemri.supervision_gap), no GPU.

Binarising the report labels at MIDPOINT=0.5, which is what BOTH our training targets and our local ruler do:

   cut     ours    agree  precision   recall
  0.50    44.7%    79.2%      65.3%    84.6%     <- what we use today
  0.60    44.7%    79.2%      65.3%    84.6%
  0.75    30.6%    82.6%      77.9%    69.2%     <- excludes the reader's mild band
  0.88    10.3%    75.0%      95.8%    28.7%

The radiologist calls 34.5% of cells positive. WE CALL 44.7% - a positive set a third larger than the one the competition scores. Cutting at 0.75 lands at 30.6%, buys +3.4 points of agreement and +12.6 of precision, and costs 15 of recall.

WHY THE GAP IS ENTIRELY ONE BAND: 0.50 and 0.60 give identical numbers, so nothing sits between them - the whole difference is the reader's lowest YES level at 0.68. knee-37f read those cells: they are the report faithfully recording trace, small, low-grade and grade-1 findings the image annotator did not count. Supervision already measures the radiologist agreeing with that level 37.8% of the time.

THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT TO HARD-THRESHOLD THE TRAINING TARGETS. The three YES levels are live signal - the model orders them correctly for 11 of 11 findings (knee-mxj) - and cutting them to binary throws that away. The graded calibration is how to use it, and it exists.

IT IS AN ARGUMENT ABOUT THE RULER. Our local number scores agreement with a positive set a third too large, which is a concrete, quantified mechanism for the local-to-leaderboard compression knee-7d1 measured from the other side (local +0.0107 became +0.020 on the board).

THE TEST, and it is nearly free once a GPU is available: recompute the ledger's local numbers with the ruler cut at 0.75 and check whether they track the leaderboard better than the 0.5 numbers do. We hold six scored entries, so the comparison is real.

DO NOT SILENTLY MOVE THE RULER. Every historical number was computed at 0.5; changing it without recomputing the ledger would make the ledger incomparable with itself, which is the failure the fixed-ruler rule in Targets.pair exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: The six scored entries' local numbers recomputed at both cuts, and whichever tracks the leaderboard better adopted deliberately across the whole ledger.
notes:
TESTED DIRECTLY 2026-08-14, SAME DAY IT WAS FILED, AND THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT SURVIVE. Downgraded P0 -> P2.

This bead argued from a BASE RATE - our labels call 44.7% of cells positive against the radiologist's 34.5% - to a conclusion about our RULER. The direct test asks the question the bead should have asked: on the 58 annotated studies, which cut of the report labels produces a mean AUC closer to the AUC against the radiologist?

  report cut 0.50: 0.8419    |proxy - annotation| = 0.0028   <- the cut we already use
  report cut 0.75: 0.8330    |proxy - annotation| = 0.0061
  ANNOTATIONS    : 0.8391

THE CURRENT CUT IS THE CLOSER PROXY, not the worse one. Both differences are far inside the annotation mean's own interval (+/-0.034 at n=58), so the honest verdict is that the test CANNOT DISTINGUISH THEM - and it certainly does not support the change.

WHY THE BASE-RATE ARGUMENT WAS WRONG, and this is the part worth keeping: AUC measures RANKING, not base rate. The mild band is not noise sprinkled at random - the model ranks those studies BETWEEN the clear positives and the clear negatives (knee-mxj: 11 of 11 findings order the three YES levels correctly). A positive set that is a third too large therefore costs an AUC far less than it costs an accuracy, because the extra positives sit where a ranking metric is least disturbed by them. A base-rate mismatch is a strong argument about a threshold metric and a weak one about a ranking metric, and the competition scores a ranking metric.

AND CUTTING AT 0.75 FLATTERS US: on the full corpus it moves the quoted number from 0.8483 to 0.8721, because dropping the ambiguous mild cases makes the task easier. Adopting it would have raised every number in the ledger while making nothing better - the exact shape of self-deception the fixed-ruler rule exists to prevent.

WHAT SURVIVES: the base-rate measurement itself is real and is now in supervision_gap, and it remains the clearest description of what our labels ARE. What is refuted is the inference from it to a ruler change. The local-to-leaderboard compression (knee-7d1) needs a different mechanism.

title: The decode/forward overlap the docstring promises does not exist
description:
Submission.chunks says: 'Decoded chunks, yielded as they are read so prediction overlaps the next decode's I/O.' It does not overlap. The generator body is

    sized = self.decode(chunk, planes, read)   # blocking
    yield {...}

and Ensemble.predict_members consumes it with a plain . So the sequence is decode(1) -> forward all members on (1) -> decode(2) -> forward on (2). The GPU idles through every decode and the CPUs idle through every forward.

THE FIX: pull one chunk ahead on a background thread, so decode(N+1) runs while the GPU works on N. Saves min(total_decode, total_gpu) off the wall clock, changes no output, and carries no accuracy risk - the arrays handed to each member are identical either way.

COMPOUNDS WITH THE PROCESS-POOL FIX (see the DECODE_THREADS bead): with decode at 0.12s/study instead of 0.27s and hidden behind the forward pass, decode could leave the critical path almost entirely.

NOTE the docstring has claimed this since it was written, which is why nobody looked - a comment asserting a property nothing enforces.
acceptance_criteria: A kernel log where elapsed time is close to max(decode, forward) rather than their sum.
notes: 2026-08-18: the CODE fix has landed — chunks() now submits chunk N+1's studies to a pool that outlives the loop before awaiting chunk N (submission.py:223-236), and the docstring records what the old body did. Only the ACCEPTANCE remains unobservable (needs a hidden-rerun log). Nothing left to implement here.
close_reason: CODE COMPLETE, acceptance unobservable. chunks() submits chunk N+1 ahead of awaiting N (submission.py:223-236) and the docstring no longer claims a property nothing enforced. The criterion - a kernel log where elapsed is max(decode, forward) not their sum - needs a HIDDEN-rerun per-chunk log, which Kaggle does not expose through the API; the visible set is 3 studies and never reaches steady state. Closing rather than holding open: the work is done and no further work would move it. If an efficiency-board runtime ever arbitrates it, reopen.

title: Decode uses 8 threads on a GIL-bound workload - measured SLOWER than serial
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, 96 real studies, warm page cache, this machine (16c), returning the REAL decoded tensors so IPC is paid:

  serial         25.7s   0.27s/study   1.00x
  threads(4)     19.0s   0.20s/study   1.35x
  threads(8)     26.1s   0.27s/study   0.98x   <- THE SHIPPED SETTING, no better than no pool at all
  processes(4)   11.2s   0.12s/study   2.29x
  processes(8)   12.8s   0.13s/study   2.01x

submission.py:37 sets DECODE_THREADS = 8 and justifies it as "above the four available cores on purpose: decoding is dominated by waiting on the mount". THAT JUSTIFICATION IS WRONG: if decode were mount-bound, threads would scale and processes would not beat them. Decode is GIL-BOUND (pydicom parses headers and tags in Python) and eight threads contend badly enough to lose to running serially.

THE FIX: ProcessPoolExecutor at the core count. Kaggle gives 4 cores and processes(4) is the peak measured here. IPC was the obvious objection and it is not real: the benchmark returns the actual bags (a chunk of 48 is about 390 MB) and processes(4) is no slower than returning shapes alone.

CAVEAT ON TRANSFER: measured on local NVMe with 16 cores; Kaggle is 4 cores on a slower mount, so the RATIO may differ. What transfers is the GIL-boundedness, which is a property of the code - and the finding that the shipped setting loses to serial does not depend on the disk.

WHY IT MATTERS: the Efficiency Prize scores total runtime, and decode is the CPU half of every submission.

DESIGN: swap ThreadPoolExecutor for ProcessPoolExecutor in Submission.decode, workers = os.cpu_count(). The worker must be a module-level or static callable (Windows spawn), which the current lambda closing over planes is not.
design: Swap ThreadPoolExecutor for ProcessPoolExecutor in Submission.decode, workers = os.cpu_count(). The worker must be a module-level or static callable (Windows spawn), which the current lambda over  is not.
acceptance_criteria: A kernel log whose per-chunk decode line drops by ~2x at the same chunk size.
notes:
ATTEMPTED THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2026-08-17, and it CANNOT BE MET FROM THE VISIBLE RUN. Pulled every
kernel log via `kaggle kernels output` and read the per-chunk decode lines:

  kneemri-efficient (THREADED decode, LB 0.919)   studies 1-3: decode 5s at [336, 448], elapsed 5s
  kneemri-vote      (PROCESS POOL, LB 0.919)      studies 1-3: decode 5s at [336, 448], elapsed 5s
  kneemri-onedecode (PROCESS POOL)  chunk 1       studies 1-3: decode 5s at [336]
                                    chunk 2       studies 1-3: decode 2s at [336]

Whole-kernel spans on the same visible set: efficient 57.8 s, vote 52.9 s, onedecode 64.5 s, chosen 64.3 s
— dominated by imports and weight loading, and across different member sets, so not a decode reading.

WHAT THIS SETTLES: the threaded and the process-pool build take THE SAME 5 s on chunk 1 at two pixel
groups. Chunk 1 pays pool spawn, so the ~2x cannot appear there, and the visible test set is 3 studies —
it never reaches the steady state where the fix pays. onedecode's own chunk 2 (5s -> 2s at ONE size) is
the only steady-state line in existence and has no threaded counterpart to divide by.

SO THE CRITERION AS WRITTEN IS UNMEETABLE: "a per-chunk decode line dropping ~2x at the same chunk size"
requires two chunks at the same size from two builds, and the visible set yields at most one steady-state
chunk from one build. The arbiter has to be the HIDDEN rerun, whose per-chunk log Kaggle does not expose
through the API — leaving the efficiency board's runtime column as the only instrument, and it prices the
whole entry, not the decode.

The measurement stands on the local benchmark (processes(4) 2.29x, threads(8) 0.98x vs serial) plus the
2026-08-16 evidence that the spawn pool RUNS on Kaggle. This bead is a WAIT, not work: nothing further is
learnable without either a hidden-run log or an efficiency-board runtime for two builds that differ only
in the pool. Do not spend another submission slot on it — the same slot buys a score bet instead.
close_reason: CODE COMPLETE, acceptance unmeetable - the bead's own 2026-08-17 note settles this. The spawn-safe ProcessPoolExecutor is shipped and was observed RUNNING on Kaggle 2026-08-16. The criterion needs two builds' per-chunk lines at the same chunk size from a HIDDEN rerun; the visible 3-study set yields at most one steady-state chunk from one build. The measurement that justified the change stands on the local benchmark (processes(4) 2.29x, threads(8) 0.98x vs serial) and on GIL-boundedness, which is a property of the code and not of the disk. Explicitly NOT worth a submission slot - the same slot buys a score bet.

title: Our three label tables are one ruler - they differ only in training supervision
description:
confident_v2, flatyes_v2 and report_labels_v2 differ in GRADED values on 45% and 27% of cells respectively - and their BINARISED targets are IDENTICAL everywhere: the same 16,058 positives, and the same mean AUC to four decimal places (0.8474 on the published 4-seed OOF).

CONSEQUENCE: they differ only in the supervision they hand training. No choice among them can move an evaluation number, so any experiment framed as 'compare label tables' is comparing training signal alone and must be read that way. Worth recording because the three tables look like three rulers and are not.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded; no action unless a graded-vs-binary evaluation is ever introduced.
close_reason: Closed

title: find_kit spent 248 seconds walking the competition mount
description:
MEASURED by the free loadcheck kernel on 2026-08-14: 't=248.2s kit located at /kaggle/input/datasets/dimiturnt/kneemri-kit/kneemri_src'. Four minutes before a line of ours ran, in EVERY kernel - all seven carried the same copy.

CAUSE: Path('/kaggle/input').rglob('kneemri/model.py') descends into the competition mount, which holds one directory per study and one per series beneath that, and stats every DICOM on the way.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the Efficiency Prize scores TOTAL RUNTIME, and this was our largest single expense - larger than any model choice we have argued about.

FIXED in 35140de: pruned by directory name (train_series/test_series/train_images/test_images) and bounded by depth, in all seven kernels. UNVERIFIED - the next kernel run of any kind will print its own t= line and settle it, at no cost.
acceptance_criteria: A kernel log whose 'kit located at' line is under ~20s.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-17 on the kneemri-encoder v2 log (kit b41059e), read as timestamped JSON rather than as code: t=1.0s 'installing [4 wheels]', t=21.5s the numexpr banner, t=40.4s 'kit b41059e' — the stamp kernel_run prints AFTER locating the kit. So the whole prologue, wheel install and imports included, is 40s, and the locate itself is bounded by the 19s between those last two lines. Against 248.2s measured on 2026-08-14 that is the prune working, and it is the kernel log the bead asked for rather than a fifth reading of the walk. Denominator note: this was a commit run over 3 test studies, but the 248s came from descending train_series, which is mounted the same in both.
close_reason: Closed

title: We consume a rule-engine label table and call it a reader - replace it with an actual model
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-14. We do not run a language model at all. report_labels_v2.csv is a PUBLISHED table we consume; this repo has no code that reads a report and emits a verdict - confident_labels, label_power and reader_agreement all analyse the table. The giveaway is in the data: __conf is CONSTANT per verdict (NO 0.85, UNK 0.05, YES 0.95), which is a rule engine signature and not a model confidence.

The frontier notebook says the same thing about itself: a multilingual RULE-BASED reader, with negation scoped by direction, Turkish and Croatian negators that govern what precedes them, "sin alteraciones" read as explicit normality, and numeric grades interpreted per structure.

WHY THIS IS THE LARGEST MEASURED LEVER WE HAVE:
  - a third of the cells the reader calls positive are not positive to the radiologist (65.3% agreement)
  - the reader captures only a quarter to a third of what the severity words carry, measured as a level gap of 0.03-0.08 against a level range of 0.26
  - and that shortfall is UNIFORM ACROSS LANGUAGES (en +0.078, es +0.064, el +0.055, de +0.047, bg +0.031), so an improvement applies to the whole corpus rather than a slice
  - our local ruler IS these labels, so better labels raise both what we train on and what we measure with

WHY IT IS PLAUSIBLY 1.5%: the leaderboard/local gap already shows label noise attenuating our ruler (knee-7d1, local gains roughly double on the board). Removing a third of the false positives from supervision is not a knob, it is the supervision.

WHAT IT NEEDS: a model that reads a report in seven languages and emits per-finding presence AND ordinal severity, with the reader_agreement CLI as its acceptance test - it has to agree with the radiologist more than 65.3% on the 58 annotated studies, and close no language gap because there is not one to close.

COST AND RISK: it is the expensive branch (a model pass over 4,407 reports, and choosing/hosting the model). The cheap gate already exists - reader_agreement measures any candidate table in seconds - so a candidate can be judged before anything is retrained on it.
notes:
DOWNGRADED FROM P0 TO P2, 2026-08-14, on knee-37f's answer. This bead's value rested on 'a third of the positives we train on are not positives'. Reading the English false positives shows the report ASSERTS the finding in about 15 of 16 - they are trace, small, low-grade and grade-1 findings that the image annotator did not count. A better reader reproduces them.

What survives: the one clear negation miss in 16, the Synovitis under-calling (14 missed, plausibly because synovitis is described obliquely - 'hypertrophy of the synovium', 'thickened synovial tissue'), and the severity shortfall this bead already measured. Those are real and worth a reader eventually; they are not a 1.5% lever on their own.

The work this releases goes to knee-mxj (ordinal severity), which knee-37f now supports by mechanism rather than by hope.

title: Our best member cannot be verified: res392 predates the witness
description:
FOUND while verifying the all-ours package, 2026-08-13. Six members, witness_check on CPU:

    calibrated_targets   ok (0.00244 of 0.0312)
    extended_ws          ok (0.0156 of 0.0312)
    intensity392_ws      ok (0.00162 of 0.00391)
    lora_r8_v3small_224  ok (0.0119 of 0.0312)
    sliceattn            ok (0.00234 of 0.00391)
    res392_ws            UNVERIFIED - no witness
    5 ok, 1 unverified, 0 refused

THE UNVERIFIED ONE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT MEMBER. res392_ws is our best single member at 0.8523 and was trained on 2026-08-12 before the witness landed, so there is nothing to re-derive. It is also the member whose READING is least trivial - 392 px resampled off a 448 cache, the only resampling member in the package - which is precisely the class the witness exists to catch (the decode resolution taken from SlotReader's default was one of the four defects that motivated it).

WHAT STILL COVERS IT, partially: the fingerprint pins the weights, image size and group; its config records train_size 392 and img 448; and both rebuilders now READ that config rather than defaulting (fixed today). So the specific 'rebuilt at the wrong resolution' failure is closed by construction. What is not covered is anything the fingerprint cannot see - the gap the witness was built for.

THE FIX IS ONE ARM AND IT PAYS TWICE: re-run res392 under the current code. It would carry a witness, and it would also pick up --patience (9% of wall-clock), bf16, compile, and the corrected AUC - none of which existed when it was fitted. The score should reproduce within the floor; if it does not, that is itself worth knowing.

UNTIL THEN: the package is 5/6 verifiable and that should be said out loud in any submission note, not discovered afterwards.
notes: STATED OUT LOUD 2026-08-17 in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md ('One member of the pool is unverifiable, and it is the strongest one'), which is the half of this bead that does not need a training slot. Re-measured the same day: witness_check --device cpu now reports 6 ok / 1 unverified / 0 refused — the pool has gained crop80_tissue_s2026 (ok, 0.0152 of 0.0312) since the 5/6 reading, so the unverified SHARE is falling as the pool grows, but res392_ws_s2026 is still the one member no witness covers. Also noted there that the fix stacks with knee-a8x: one re-run at the control's rate buys the witness AND disambiguates the resolution-vs-rate confound.

title: ledger_check: the gates check code, nothing checked a document
description:
BUILT AND PASSING 2026-08-13: kneemri/ledger_check.py reports any run with a metrics file whose best score is quoted nowhere in experiments/README.md. One command, no GPU: uv run python -m kneemri.ledger_check.

WHY. The static gates catch defects in code and NOTHING CHECKS A DOCUMENT, which turned out to be the day's larger exposure: five files were carrying conclusions later measurement had overturned, and the ledger itself held five arms as 'queued' that had run two days earlier. An arm that runs and is never written down is an arm paid for and thrown away, and the next planning pass reads its row as unstarted work.

IT PAID IMMEDIATELY. First run, after I had already spent the afternoon updating that ledger by hand: FOUR unrecorded runs - schedule_8 (0.8429), dinov3 at 224 (0.8057), dinov3 S+ (0.8012), and the killed v2 LoRA arm (0.8127 at epoch 3). All four are now in the table and it reports 15 runs, 0 unrecorded.

MATCHED ON THE NUMBER, not the arm name, deliberately: the table names arms in prose (whole_stack, resolution) while the files are outputs (wholestack_s2026, res392_ws_s2026), and a mapping between them is one more thing to get wrong.

TWO LIMITS, both real:
  - It cannot tell a FINISHED run from a KILLED one. The v2 LoRA arm died at epoch 3 and still left metrics; the row says so, but the tool cannot.
  - It checks that a NUMBER is present, never that the sentence around it is true. Stale interpretation - the other half of what went wrong today - still needs a reader.

NOT WIRED INTO THE GATE. It reads the data root, which CI does not have, so it belongs in the arm-queue ritual beside arm_check rather than in nox.
close_reason: Built, passing, and run again 2026-08-15: 15 finished runs, 0 unrecorded. Deliberately outside nox (it reads the data root); it belongs to the arm-queue ritual beside arm_check.

title: The reader mis-handles negation: report-YES near a negation agrees only 42%
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against the 57 annotated studies, and it names WHAT a better reader has to fix rather than asserting that one would help.

Taking report-YES cells whose finding's own sentence could be located (137 of 311, the rest being non-English or differently worded), and splitting by whether that sentence contains a negation - no, not, without, negative for, intact, normal, unremarkable, ruled out, free of:

    finding sentence      n     radiologist agrees
    no negation         111          73.9%
    CONTAINS negation    26          42.3%

difference 0.316, SE 0.105, z = 3.00, 95% CI [0.109, 0.523] - excludes zero.

So when the reader says a finding is PRESENT and the sentence naming it carries a negation, it is wrong more often than right. 19% of the located report-YES cells are in that state.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE SEVERITY BRANCH. A regex-grade severity extractor was measured to add nothing beyond the existing levels (same session). Negation is the opposite case: it is a KNOWN failure mode of clinical text extraction, it is measurably present here, and it is exactly what a stronger reader is good at and a pattern-matcher is not. It converts 'use a better model' into a specific defect with a measured cost.

TWO LIMITS, both stated rather than buried:
  - The negation detector is crude. 'ACL intact, medial meniscus torn' is ONE sentence carrying both, so some flagged cells are false alarms - which means the true effect on genuinely-negated cells is LARGER than 42.3%, not smaller.
  - 137 of 311 cells located, because the anatomy patterns are English. This holds on the half we can read.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP: re-read only the negated cells with a stronger model and re-measure agreement against the annotations. That is 26 cells in the annotated set and roughly 19% of report-YES cells corpus-wide - a small, targeted re-read rather than a full relabel.
acceptance_criteria: Agreement on negated report-YES cells rises materially after a targeted re-read, measured against the same 57 annotated studies.
notes:
SIZED CORPUS-WIDE 2026-08-13, and it is a SMALLER lever than the agreement gap suggests. I quoted '19% of report-YES cells' - that was 19% of the LOCATED subset, and located is only 36.9% of report-YES.

    report-YES cells corpus-wide          16,129
      finding's own sentence located       5,946   36.9%
