      of those, carrying a negation        1,057   17.8% of located, 6.6% of ALL YES

Down-weighting the negated cells therefore corrects supervision on 6.6% of positives, taking them from about 42% reliable to excluded. That moves the effective label noise on positives by a couple of points at most. Free, mechanism-sound, worth doing when something else touches Targets - NOT a lever, and not to be planned around.

THE MEASUREMENT STILL STANDS: z = 3.00 on the agreement gap, and it names a real reader defect rather than asserting one. What the sizing changes is where the VALUE is. 63% of report-YES cells cannot have their finding's sentence located by English patterns at all, and that is the population a stronger multilingual reader would reach. The negation defect demonstrates the reader HAS extractable errors; the prize is in the part we cannot currently inspect.

DROPPED TO P2. Filed as P1 on a gap measured inside a subset without first checking what fraction of the corpus that subset was - the same shape as reading a per-label delta without its interval, which this session has already corrected twice.

title: Arm-lint: every committed arm should be proven to parse before it costs GPU time
description:
RUN ONCE 2026-08-13, by hand, result: 0 of 22 train arms carry flags kneemri.train would refuse - including --patience and --calibrated-targets added the same day. So nothing is broken today; what is missing is that this cannot be re-checked without redoing the work.

WHY IT IS WORTH A TOOL. This project's most expensive failures are arms that fail SILENTLY or late: arm U printed ARM U DONE after dying at epoch 7, a str.replace that matched nothing left dinov3.sh writing one name for every size, the package snapshot broke uv run and two queued arms died in under a second, and an arm run with no arguments iterated zero times and exited 0 with an empty log. A flag typo belongs to that family and costs a queue slot to discover.

HOW IT WORKS, already proven by hand: source each arm with ARM_LIB pointing at a STUB lib.sh whose run_train prints its arguments instead of training, with a fake uv on PATH and a per-arm timeout. That exercises the REAL shell parsing - which matters, because one past arm died on a quoting error - and yields the exact flag line, which is then handed to TrainingOptions.parse().

NOT BUILT TODAY, deliberately: it needs a home that does not fight the guardrails (devtools/ is template-owned; a kneemri module would need a test that shells out, which the unit-test-size gate may refuse) and that decision deserves more than the ten minutes left in this pass. The stub lib is in the session scratchpad and the recipe is above.
acceptance_criteria: One command that reports any arm whose flags the trainer would refuse, runnable before a queue is armed.
close_reason:
Built: kneemri/arm_check.py + experiments/stub_lib.sh. 31 arms checked, 0 refused, and proven to catch a real typo - injecting --slice-poolng into whole_stack.sh reports 'REFUSED whole_stack: train: error: unrecognized arguments'. One command before a queue is armed: uv run python -m kneemri.arm_check.

IT FOUND ITS OWN FAILURE MODE TWICE WHILE BEING BUILT, which is the argument for it. A bare 'bash' from python resolves to WSL's, which is wedged on this machine, so every arm timed out and the tool reported '0 arms checked, 0 refused' - a clean pass over nothing, exactly the silent no-op it exists to catch. And arms that drive uv run directly (the diversity curve, the cache build) bypass the stub and do REAL work; killing them on timeout leaves the grandchild holding the pipe, so the check hung instead of skipping. The stub now shadows uv with a no-op and the interpreter is named explicitly.

Split so it is testable: invocations() shells out, refused() is pure. The unit gate forbids tests that shell out, and the logic lives in the pure half.

title: comp/kit is generated, gitignored, and inside the type checker's scope
description:
Adding comp to lint_paths (knee-wb9) pulled comp/kit under pyrefly. That directory is BUILD OUTPUT - build_kit.py copies our own packages into it, verify_kit.py keeps it honest, .gitignore excludes it - so the checker was type-checking a STALE COPY of kneemri against the CURRENT one and reporting every refactor as an error at a path nobody edits. It surfaced on the Targets.pair signature change: the old copy passes a float where Supervision is now expected.

RUFF IS FINE - it respects .gitignore, so only pyrefly sees it.

TRIED AND DID NOT WORK: project-excludes in [tool.pyrefly], with both 'comp/kit/**' and '**/comp/kit/**'. Neither suppressed it, so the key or the pattern semantics are not what I assumed for pyrefly 1.1.1 - worth ten minutes with the docs rather than more guessing.

DONE INSTEAD: deleted the stale comp/kit. The gate is clean and nothing is suppressed. This is a real fix for today and NOT a durable one - the next build_kit run recreates the directory. A freshly built kit is an identical copy of the current source so it should type-check, but that has not been verified, and a duplicate package on the search path is a hazard whatever its contents.
design: Either find the pyrefly exclude that actually works, or have build_kit write outside the repo entirely - the kit is a Kaggle upload, not project source, and nothing in the repo needs to read it.
acceptance_criteria: A build_kit run followed by uvx nox -s lint leaves the gate green.
close_reason: Fixed durably: the kit now builds under the data root, out of the repo. My earlier project-excludes attempt could never have worked - pyrefly's own --help says 'if files are specified on the command line, project_excludes in any config files loaded for these files are ignored', and the gate passes explicit paths. The directory had to leave the checked tree, which it also should have on the house rule that data lives out of the repo: it is ~200 MB of weights and wheels.

title: If we place, kneemri-members and kneemri-kit must be PUBLIC before the winner deadline
description:
Rules Sec 8.a: a prize winner must deliver the final model's code and weights, and 'the model weights should be provided as a public kaggle dataset so it is both publicly accessible and linked to the inference/submission code'.

MEASURED 2026-08-13 via the Kaggle metadata API - all three of our datasets are PRIVATE:
  dimiturnt/kneemri-members   private   CC0-1.0    (our trained weights)
  dimiturnt/kneemri-kit       private   CC0-1.0    (our source tree)
  dimiturnt/dinov3-hf         private   other      (third-party pretrained)

PRIVATE IS CORRECT RIGHT NOW and this must not be done early: 5.d forbids private sharing outside Teams, and publishing the weights publicly during the Competition Period would hand the solution to the field for nothing. The rules only require it of a WINNER.

dinov3-hf is a third-party pretrained model, covered by the 2.5.a carve-out for incompatibly-licensed models, so it is NOT required to be open-sourced - though Meta's licence does permit redistribution with the Agreement alongside, which we already ship, so making it public is available if the Sponsor asks.
acceptance_criteria: A checklist item on the final-submission runbook, not an action taken now: flip kneemri-members and kneemri-kit to public if and only if we place.

title: The honest denominator: what is our slot-attention head actually worth?
description:
Stolen from biohub_kaggle a9d1db8, which found its ablation knob had a degenerate zero - a mounted affinity at bonus 0 fell between two modes and produced an EMPTY submission that scored 0.0000 and read as 'the affinity is everything'. Fixing it produced the first honest denominator of that campaign: distance-only 0.7476 against shipped 0.9380, so the learned head is worth +0.19 and any proposal to REPLACE it has a bar while a proposal to ADD to it has a low one.

WE HAVE NO SUCH DENOMINATOR. Every arm here is measured against wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457, which is the full recipe. We have never measured what our own components carry:
  - slot attention (per-diagnosis softmax over six slots) against plain mean-pooling of the slots
  - the ranking term (--rank-weight 1.0) against pure BCE
  - the whole-stack read against a single middle window
Each is one short arm, and each converts a component we ASSUME is load-bearing into a number.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND curiosity: it sets the bar for every future proposal. A new pooling scheme that beats mean-pooling by 0.01 is uninteresting if slot attention already beats it by 0.05; it is the whole game if slot attention is worth 0.002.

CHECK FOR THE DEGENERATE ZERO WHILE DOING IT - that is the transferable half of their bug. Ask of each knob whether its zero is the mechanism's limit or a third mode nobody meant: does --rank-weight 0 give pure BCE, or something neither?
design: One arm per component, all at 8 epochs (schedule_8 measured -0.0028 against twelve for two thirds the cost). Not a sweep - each knob at its LIMIT, once.
notes:
THE FIRST ARM HAD NO KNOB, and the CPU half of this bead is now done (2026-08-13, no GPU).

AUDIT. This bead asks for three denominators and treats them as three GPU arms. Two of the three knobs already existed; the first did not.

  1. SLOT ATTENTION against mean-pooling - NO KNOB EXISTED. StudyDesign carried pool, slice_pooling, anatomical_prior and layer; SlotHead was the only head in the codebase. The arm could not have been run at all, and would have been discovered at the card rather than here.
  2. RANKING TERM at zero - CLEAN, verified by reading train.py:318. 'if self.rank_weight:' falls through to Objective(normalise_by_count=..., per_label=...), carrying the SAME flags the ranked branch does, so --rank-weight 0 is pure BCE and nothing else changes with it.
  3. WHOLE-STACK off - already a flag, already the default.

BUILT: MeanSlotHead, StudyDesign.slot_pooling ('attend' | 'mean'), --slot-pooling, recorded in the checkpoint config by member_record, read back by Member.slot_pooling and HoldoutPredictions.load, and used by MemberPackage's rebuild. Wired to every consumer BEFORE the arm is queued, because a head fitted with uniform pooling and rebuilt with attention loads without complaint - the shape that has cost nine defects, every one found after a run.

THE DEGENERATE-ZERO CHECK IS THE POINT AND IT PASSES. MeanSlotHead overrides ONLY the attention weights; projection, slot embeddings, dropout, readout and parameter count are identical. Two tests hold it there: zeroing the query and prior makes the softmax uniform and the two heads then compute the same function to 1e-5 (so 'mean' is the mechanism's LIMIT, not a third mode), and perturbing query and prior by 10x leaves MeanSlotHead's output bit-identical (so the ablation does not secretly read what it removed).

WHAT REMAINS IS GPU: three arms at 8 epochs, each knob at its limit, once. Nothing about them needs designing now.
AUDIT 2026-08-20: two of the three components this bead asks for are ALREADY PRICED by other work, and only the third needed an arm.

  1. SLOT ATTENTION vs mean pooling - DONE, by the unledgered slotmean run found on 2026-08-19: 0.8406, -0.0051 against wholestack_s2026, 12 epochs. Read on the UNPAIRED bound (the control kept no per-study predictions) and directional rather than a refutation, but the axis is MEASURED once instead of assumed. experiments/README.md line 269.
  2. RANKING TERM at zero - the only one still open, and now queued as rank0_dense (see below).
  3. WHOLE-STACK off - DONE at +0.0147, long since banked into the shipped recipe.

QUEUED: experiments/arms/rank0_dense.sh, chained behind aprior_dense. Single variable --rank-weight 0 against band_dense = 0.8578, 12 epochs at the settled operating point rather than this bead's original 8 (one-cycle makes --epochs a schedule and not a truncation, so the control has to be matched on it, and band_dense is the settled 12-epoch control).

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH A SLOT THOUGH THE TERM WAS MEASURED. recipe.sh justifies the flag as the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms, and those arms are real - but they were read against rank24_s2026 = 0.8272 at 24 epochs, small backbone, before whole-stack and before the band, and there is +0.0306 of recipe on top of that control now. This ledger's most repeated finding is that a lever does not keep its size across operating points (attend_dense +0.0016 at 12 slices became -0.0009 at 20; the density trade reversed direction; crop80_span gave back what the band widening paid for). The mechanism sharpens it: the ranking loss is WITHIN-BATCH pairwise, so its strength scales with the pair count a batch affords - the ledger already relies on this in rejecting the 448 px rung. This arm runs batch 12; rank24_s2026 predates the metrics recorder and kept no recipe line, so its batch is NOT recoverable and the cross-era comparison cannot be made honestly at all.

DEGENERATE-ZERO CHECK: passes, and verified by reading rather than assumed - train.py's 'if self.rank_weight:' falls through to Objective carrying the SAME flags the ranked branch passes, so --rank-weight 0 is pure BCE and nothing else moves with it. Zero is the mechanism's limit, not a third mode.

PLUMBING VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: RECIPE already carries --rank-weight 1.0 and the arm appends --rank-weight 0 after it. argparse last-wins was CONFIRMED by parsing the exact argv (rank_weight = 0.0), not assumed. arm_check --only rank0_dense: 1 arm checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached.

title: DINOv3 belongs at BASE, not small: the distillation story scales with the student
description:
2026-08-12 12:46Z, after the owner asked why we pit v2-small against v3-S/16 at all.

THE ARM WAS BUILT TO ISOLATE THE ENCODER, and it does that correctly: 21.6M against 22.1M params, both 384 wide, 12 blocks, 6 heads, everything else held fixed. As a controlled swap it is right.

AS A LEVER IT IS AIMED AT THE WEAKEST POINT. The argument that made matched-size look sufficient was ours - capacity is not the constraint here, base over small being +0.0011 against a 0.0053 floor (knee-7u5). That evidence is about DINOv2. DINOv3's entire story is distillation from a 7B teacher, and how much of a 7B teacher survives into a 21M student is exactly the quantity that should scale with student size. If v3 has an edge anywhere, ViT-S/16 is the worst place to look for it.

PLAN, in cost order:
  1. v3small at 224 (queued) - a quarter of 336's tokens, so ~15 minutes. It answers a question about US (did our 336 read break a 224-native encoder), not about model size, and it decides which read size a base run should use.
  2. v3base at whichever size 224 vindicates - ~3x the compute of small, so ~3 h at 336, minus the 21% compile just bought. The weights are ALREADY in our Kaggle dataset (vits16 and vitb16 both uploaded), so a base member is submittable the day it exists.
  3. NOT v3large: 300M is 8-10 h an arm here and it is not in our mount.

384 IS DROPPED FROM THE QUEUE, not from the ideas. It tests the grid at 1.7x native extrapolation, which only becomes interesting if 224 shows extrapolation is NOT the problem. Running it before that answer would spend 70 minutes on a hypothesis the cheaper arm can kill.

KEEP A SMALL V3 MEMBER REGARDLESS OF SCORE: differently-failing members are the one thing measured to pay (+0.0092 for four of them), and v3small at 0.807 is cheap to keep in the curve.
notes:
MY DOWNGRADE TO P3 THIS MORNING WAS TOO HASTY, and today's LoRA result is why.

I dropped this to P3 on the grounds that DINOv3-S+ (28.7M, wider) scored 0.8012 against plain v3-S's 0.8080 - 'capacity scaled the WRONG way inside the small family'. That is true and it does not speak to BASE: S+ is a wider SMALL, not the next rung, and it was measured under the fine-tuning recipe now known to cost v3 0.0160 (knee-7ov).

WHAT THE CONFIGS SAY, checked rather than assumed:
    DINOv2-S/14   image_size 518  patch 14  hidden 384  layers 12  registers 0
    DINOv3-S/16   image_size 224  patch 16  hidden 384  layers 12  registers 4
SAME WIDTH, SAME DEPTH. v3-S/16 is not a larger network than v2-S/14 - it is the same size, distilled from a 7B teacher, with a coarser patch that yields 23% fewer tokens at equal pixels. The published DINOv3 advance is concentrated in the 7B teacher and the large distilled variants, so S/16 is the variant where an upgrade is LEAST expected.

SO EVERY v3 NUMBER WE HAVE was measured on the least favourable variant under a recipe that damaged it. That is a weak basis for burying the family, and this bead's premise - that the distillation story needs a bigger student - survives its own counter-evidence.

THE RUN THAT WOULD ANSWER IT: v3-base with LoRA. Not queued without the owner's word, because it is GPU beyond the arm set already agreed.

ALSO UNTESTED FOR BOTH ENCODERS: we read last_hidden_state, the final block. Dense/local tasks often prefer intermediate layers, and v3's Gram anchoring targets patch-level structure specifically. Cheap to test and it applies to v2 as well.

title: Intensity augmentation REFUTED at 392: 0.8459 against the control's 0.8523
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 11:47Z. experiments/arms/intensity_augment.sh, 12 epochs, fold 0, whole-stack, max pooling, 392 px read off the 448 cache — identical to res392_ws except for --intensity-aug (gamma/blur/contrast/noise on top of the geometric augmentation both share).

  res392_ws_s2026     0.8523   geometric augmentation only
  intensity392_ws     0.8459   + gamma/blur/contrast/noise
  delta               -0.0064  against a 0.0053 noise floor

BEHIND AT EVERY MATCHED EPOCH, not just at the end: e2 0.8156 vs 0.8231, e5 0.8409 vs 0.8477, e7 0.8452 vs 0.8523-peak. The arm's own header predicted this shape and named the mechanism: intensity augmentation buys invariance to contrast and noise, and our supervision is thin enough (report-derived labels, 3.5k studies) that spending capacity on invariance costs more than the invariance is worth. MRI intensity is also not arbitrary — sequence contrast IS the signal for several of the twelve targets, so flattening it destroys information rather than nuisance variation.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: it does not refute intensity augmentation at a larger data scale, nor with a milder schedule. It refutes it AS CONFIGURED, on this corpus, at this supervision level.

IT IS STILL A MEMBER. 0.8459 is the second-best single member we have, it reads 392 like res392 (same pixel group, no extra decode), and it fails differently by construction — a model trained under contrast jitter makes different mistakes than one that never saw it. Diversity is the one thing measured to pay here (+0.0092 for four differently-failing members), so it goes into the diversity curve rather than the bin.
close_reason: Refuted AS CONFIGURED and correctly scoped by the bead itself. The endpoint delta (-0.0064 against a 0.0053 floor) is marginal on its own; what carries it is being behind at every matched epoch (e2 0.8156/0.8231, e5 0.8409/0.8477, e7 0.8452/0.8523), with a named mechanism - MRI sequence contrast IS the signal for several of the twelve targets, so flattening it destroys information rather than nuisance variation. Retained as a diversity member, which is where it goes next.

title: Three of the five OneCycle knobs are PyTorch defaults nobody chose
description:
AUDIT prompted by the owner asking what scheduler we use. It is OneCycleLR, whose anneal_strategy defaults to 'cos' - so the project already has cosine, inside one-cycle, and there is no separate cosine path.

OURS, with a measured reason: max_lr per parameter group ([head 1e-3, backbone 8e-6, now 4e-5]) and pct_start=0.15. The justification is real and recorded - at a CONSTANT rate our five folds peaked at epochs 13/13/10/12/11 and gained ~0 over their final five, so a run that improves to 60 epochs is training on a decaying rate rather than training longer.

PYTORCH DEFAULTS, never chosen by us:
  anneal_strategy='cos'
  div_factor=25        -> the run STARTS at max_lr/25
  final_div_factor=1e4 -> the run ENDS at max_lr/250,000, i.e. effectively zero for the last stretch

WHY THIS IS WORTH A LOOK GIVEN TODAY: the session's pattern is that every constant inherited rather than measured has turned out load-bearing once it got a flag - the encoder rate (5x helped), the unfreeze depth (uninterpretable at the inherited rate), the slice count, the group thickness. div_factor is the same shape of thing: with the rate finding suggesting the encoder was frozen too hard, a warmup that STARTS the backbone at 4e-5/25 = 1.6e-6 - below the inherited constant rate - deserves questioning.

NOT QUEUED, deliberately. The rate effect is not yet confirmed single-variable (arm S), and sweeping a schedule parameter before the effect it interacts with is established is exactly the stage-gate error this project has already paid for once.

ALSO NOTED, and it affects a running arm: because OneCycle is defined over total_steps, arm T (36 epochs at 4e-5) stretches the whole cycle rather than merely adding duration - warmup goes 3.6 -> 5.4 epochs and the decay slows to match. It tests schedule SHAPE and duration together. That is the right thing to ship, but it must not be read as 'more epochs helped'.
notes:
AUDIT FINISHED 2026-08-13, no GPU. All three unchosen defaults are now characterised, and the useful finding is not any one of them.

MEASURED at our exact settings (peak 8e-6, pct_start 0.15, 12 epochs x 291 steps):
    div_factor 25        -> the backbone STARTS at 3.2e-7
    final_div_factor 1e4 -> it ENDS at 3.2e-11, which is zero for any practical purpose
    anneal_strategy cos  -> as this bead already said, we have cosine inside one-cycle

THE THING THAT MATTERS IS THE INTEGRAL. Summed over the run:
    OneCycle at peak 8e-6   total 0.01405
    constant 8e-6           total 0.02794
    OneCycle delivers 50.3% of it, at a MEAN rate of 4.02e-6.

So when this project moved from a constant 8e-6 to OneCycle(max_lr=8e-6) it HALVED the total backbone movement while calling it the same rate. Anyone reading '8e-6' in both regimes is comparing two different amounts of learning, and the same halving applies to every arm quoted by its peak: the 5x rate arm at 4e-5 delivers a mean 2e-5, which is 2.5x the old constant rather than 5x.

IT IS A FRAMING CORRECTION, NOT A DEFECT. OneCycle's value is the warmup and the anneal, not the integral, so half the area does not mean half the learning - and the schedule measurably works (schedule_8 at two thirds the length costs only 0.0028). What is wrong is quoting a PEAK as if it were a rate.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH ACTING ON, cheaply: if the peak is worth about half a constant, the peak that reproduces a constant that worked is roughly twice it. That is one arm, and it is the honest version of the 'div_factor deserves questioning' this bead opened with.
close_reason: All three defaults characterised and the framing corrected: OneCycle at peak 8e-6 delivers 50.3% of constant 8e-6's total learning rate. Quoting a peak as a rate is what was wrong, not the defaults.

title: Decide the epoch-selection read policy: 3 windows, or document the mismatch
description:
AUDIT. The slice stack is read three different ways in one project:
  - TRAINING LOSS: one RANDOM 3-slice window per step (trainer.py:282), same start for every study in the batch.
  - EPOCH SELECTION: Trainer.predict reads the MIDDLE window only.
  - DEPLOYMENT (submission, ruler_check, attribution): 10 OVERLAPPING windows, averaged.

So the epoch kept as 'best' is chosen under a policy the shipped model never uses.

MEASURED, across seven checkpoints holding both numbers: overlap beats middle by a near-uniform +0.0156 (min +0.0127, max +0.0172). Ranking is essentially preserved - one swap, deep24_s2026 vs ep24_fold0, which sit 0.0008 apart and are tied in any case.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, one benign and one not:
  BENIGN: our comparisons are not distorted, so no recipe decision made this session is invalidated.
  NOT: every local number understates deployment by ~1.6%, which is LARGER than any single method change measured today (ranking +0.005, base +0.0085, 8->24 epochs +0.0068). TTA is the biggest single contributor we have, and it was already in the submission path rather than being a finding.

WHAT IS STILL UNTESTED: whether epoch SELECTION within a run would choose a different epoch under the deployment policy. That needs per-epoch states, which we do not keep. The near-uniform gain (spread 0.0045) suggests mostly not.

FIX OPTIONS: score epochs on 3 windows (first/middle/last) rather than 1 - a cheap approximation that removes most of the mismatch; or accept the mismatch and document it. Full 10-window scoring per epoch would add ~10x the eval cost to every epoch, which is not worth 0.0045 of ranking fidelity.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-13, superseding my note earlier today. I wrote that whole-stack members 'lose' this bead's +0.0156 because they read one window, and called it a P0. Measured: rotation TTA on a whole-stack member buys +0.0003 to +0.0009, not the +0.0156 the analogy predicted (knee-2wg, refuted and closed).

The reasoning was wrong in an instructive way. Window TTA averaged over ten different SLICE DEPTHS, so what it bought was seeing more of the stack - not averaging as such. A whole-stack member already integrates every depth through its elementwise max, so it ABSORBED that gain rather than forfeiting it. Whole-stack's +0.0147 and window TTA's +0.0156 are the same mechanism counted once each.

What stands from this bead is unchanged and was always the useful part: comparisons among whole-stack members are undistorted, and for those members the deployment reading IS the training reading.
close_reason: Decided: the mismatch is retired by whole-stack, not by a scoring change. Trainer.whole_stack sets window = every slice, so Trainer.predict's middle is 0 and epoch selection reads exactly what the submission reads (trainer.py:585-606, now documented there). The 3-window fix was a cheap approximation of a policy gap that only exists for WINDOWED members, and every member we ship is whole-stack. Nothing to build.

title: A queue gate fired on a file written at BUILD START, not completion
description:
chain13 waited on index_336px_20sl.json to decide the 20-slice cache was ready. build_cache writes that index at the START of the build (timestamp 11:47, while the log still read 3600/4407), so the gate was already satisfied and the arm would have begun the moment the GPU freed - training on a 59.7 GB array still mostly zeros.

It would NOT have crashed. It would have produced a plausible, wrong number for the slice-coverage question, which is the failure mode this project keeps meeting: the run completes and the result is quietly meaningless.

Caught before firing only because chain12 still had ~65 minutes left. Requeued on 'CACHE BUILD COMPLETE', which build_cache logs as its final line.

RULE, same family as knee-74x and knee-b02: a readiness gate must key on a marker the producer writes when it FINISHES. An output path proves the job started, never that it ended.
close_reason: chain13 re-gated on 'CACHE BUILD COMPLETE'; chain14 now asserts every checkpoint path exists before spending GPU. The rule (gate on a completion marker, never on an output path) is recorded here and applied.

title: The kit was stale AND had lost its wheels; both guards caught it
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-11. comp/kit had drifted from kneemri/: backbone.py, ema.py, targets.py, train.py, trainer.py all differed and objective.py was missing entirely. The wheels were gone too - build_kit rebuilds from scratch and drops them unless run WITH --wheels, which comp/README already warns about.

BOTH GUARDS WERE VERIFIED BY BREAKING THEM, not by reading them:
- publish.py refused with the exact file list, exit 1, BEFORE authentication (its docstring's claim, confirmed in both directions: after the rebuild it clears staleness and stops at the missing token instead).
- verify_kit.py, with a wheel removed, said 'missing wheel: jaxtyping (kernel will fail at import)' and exited 1; green again on restore.

So this needed no fix - the design is right and it worked. Recorded because the SYSTEM is what deserves the credit: the kit is gitignored (no duplicated source in git), it goes stale by construction on every kneemri/ change, and the gate sits at publish time where it is fail-safe. Auto-rebuilding on commit would HIDE the drift rather than catch it.

Kit rebuilt and verified; nothing published - that is the owner's call.

STANDING RULE: after any session that touches kneemri/, run 'uv run python comp/build_kit.py --wheels <dir>' then 'uv run python comp/verify_kit.py' before any submission.
close_reason: No fix needed - both guards were verified by breaking them and the standing rule already lives in comp/README.md:52-66, which is where it is read. Nothing left in the tracker.

title: DINOv2-large: the rung above the public frontier
description:
Every strong public notebook stops at base. The reason is the scored kernel's T4, which constrains INFERENCE only - training runs on our own 5090, and metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/large/1 exists (1.2 GB, 300M params, 1024-wide).

WHY THIS AND NOT ANOTHER KNOB: our own ladder says capacity and training time are the only two levers that have ever cleared the 0.0062 noise floor (small->base +0.0085, 8->24 epochs +0.0068, and they ADD: base@20 = 0.8255 vs small@8 = 0.8081). Every knob-sized idea we have tried has landed inside the floor. Large is the next rung on the one axis that pays.

RISK, stated upfront: VRAM at batch 12 (base used 13.7 of 32 GB; large is ~3.5x the parameters). If it OOMs the arm must NOT silently drop to batch 6 - we already paid for that confound once, when base ran at batch 6 against batch-12 baselines and had to be killed and requeued.

SECOND RISK: a large member may not fit the Efficiency kernel's runtime budget. That is fine and it is why two kernels exist - the accuracy entry and the efficiency entry are separate submissions, and 347 of 897 teams carry an efficiency score strictly below their public best.

Queued as /tmp/chain9.sh behind the depth bracket.
notes:
THE PREMISE IS STALE, 2026-08-13, and it is the whole argument for this arm.

This bead says 'capacity and training time are the only two levers that have ever cleared the noise floor' and 'every knob-sized idea we have tried has landed inside the floor'. Both were true when written. Since then:
    whole-stack reading   +0.0147   adds no parameters
    392 px resolution     +0.0066   adds no parameters
    DINOv2-large          +0.0021   3.5x the parameters, 185 s/epoch against ~50 (knee-7u5)
The two biggest gains this project has measured are EVIDENCE, not capacity, and the one large-encoder measurement we already have is inside noise while costing 3.7x the wall-clock. knee-7u5's reading - that the binding constraint moved from capacity to supervision - is now supported by three arms rather than one.

THE T4 RISK THIS BEAD RAISES IS ANSWERED and is not a reason either way: a 1024-wide member gets 324 images per forward from the width-scaled budget, which is 0.61 GB of weights plus 1.15 GB of activations = 1.76 GB against the T4's 15.8. Large fits inference comfortably (knee-d16).

DROPPED TO P2. Not refuted - large has never been run under whole-stack, and the +0.0021 was measured windowed at 24 epochs before any of the coverage work. But it is no longer the next rung on 'the one axis that pays', because that axis turned out not to be capacity.

title: tests/e2e is still empty
description: The testing policy in CLAUDE.md specifies three layers; integration is now filled with the checkpoint-to-submission chain, e2e is still an empty directory. An e2e smoke would decode one REAL study from D:/data, build the cache, run a member and write a submission row - which is the only layer that would catch a DICOM-reading or slot-routing regression. It must skip when the data root is absent so CI stays green, which is also why it was not written blind: a test that always skips is worse than no test because it reads as coverage.
close_reason: tests/e2e/submission_smoke.py: four real studies through cache -> member -> prediction -> submission columns, plus a cache/model shape agreement check. Skips when the data root or a member is absent.

title: Queue scripts must use python -u and a real process-kill path
description: Two operational defects cost time this session. (1) Piping train stdout through grep buffers it, so a 45-minute arm showed NO epoch lines and progress could only be inferred from the .partial checkpoint mtime; python -u fixes it and is now used in the chain script. (2) pkill does not exist in this Git-bash environment - it fails with 'command not found' and the failure looks like success in a compound command, so an earlier 'kill the queue' silently did nothing. Use PowerShell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process + Stop-Process -Force, matching on CommandLine. Both are why a confounded arm ran for 7 minutes before being caught.
close_reason: python -u is in the chain scripts; the kill path is Get-CimInstance Win32_Process + Stop-Process -Force matched on CommandLine. Both applied.

title: Non-English reports: weaker labels and a 0.016 score gap on 54% of the corpus
description: DEFLATED, do not build the parser on this evidence. The gap survives restricting to confident labels (0.0119 all vs 0.0117 at conf>=0.7), so it is not simply ruler noise. BUT scanner model predicts report language almost deterministically (MAGNETOM Avanto fit 0 percent english over 262 studies, Optima MR450w 100 percent), the between-manufacturer spread (0.8020-0.8256) is LARGER than the language gap and does not order by english share (best group is 50 percent english), and field strength shows nothing (1.5T 0.8159 vs 3.0T 0.8156). Language is confounded with site. Subgroups are small (111-223) so the manufacturer ranking is not itself established. A nine-language label parser targets the one reading the evidence does not isolate.
close_reason: DEFLATED and the analysis is the deliverable. The 0.0119 gap survives restricting to confident labels, so it is not ruler noise - but scanner model predicts report language almost deterministically (Avanto 0% english over 262 studies, Optima MR450w 100%), the between-manufacturer spread 0.8020-0.8256 is LARGER than the language gap and does not order by english share (best group is 50% english), and field strength shows nothing. Language is confounded with site, subgroups are 111-223 so even the manufacturer ranking is not established, and a nine-language parser would target the one thing the evidence cannot isolate. Do not build it.

title: Two seed members on disk have an unrecoverable recipe
description: seed7_fold0.pt and seed13_fold0.pt were trained by an inline queue whose flags were not saved and whose script is gone. Checkpoints recorded image geometry but not one_cycle/weight_floor/intensity_aug, so neither can be matched to a seed-2026 counterpart and neither can serve as a noise floor on its own. train.py now writes an 'options' block (str-valued, since every loader uses weights_only=True and it refuses Paths). If a clean noise floor is needed, run three seeds under one explicit recipe rather than trusting these two.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-17, won't-fix, and the remedy is dead by decree rather than unfinished. This bead's only proposed action was 'run three seeds under one explicit recipe' as a noise floor; the owner has since banned seeds and folds outright ('seeds and folds - its the same thing, tried slightly differently'), so that arm will never be run and the two checkpoints will never gain a matchable counterpart. The PREVENTION already landed: train.py writes a str-valued 'options' block, so no member fitted since can lose its recipe. The two files are inert - grep finds them only as string fixtures in tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/package_members.py, never in the served pool. Nothing left to do.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rebuild the kit whenever kneemri/ changes, not only when weights change
description:
A kernel run died on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kneemri.submission'`. The kernels had been refactored to import a newly extracted module, the MEMBERS dataset was pushed with the new weights, and the KIT — which is what actually carries our source into the kernel — was not.

`comp/verify_kit.py` exists precisely for this and takes a second to run. It was skipped because the change felt like it was 'only in the kernels', which is exactly backwards: the kernels are a bootstrap that imports the kit, so a change to either is a change to both.

CHEAP FIX AVAILABLE: make the push path refuse to run a kernel against a stale kit. `publish.py kernel` could call the same drift check `verify_kit.py` performs before pushing, so the ordering cannot be got wrong by remembering. Filed rather than done because the immediate cost was one kernel run and pushes are unlimited — but it will recur every time a module is extracted.
close_reason: publish.py now runs verify_kit's drift() in main, before auth, on every subcommand

title: Scale to 20 members (5 folds x 4 seeds) — buys rank, teaches nothing
description:
The one difference we KNOW separates the two ensembles: theirs is 20 members (5 folds x 4 seeds), ours is 5. At ~12 epochs a member costs ~5.5 min, so 15 more is ~80 minutes, and members are nearly free at inference (20 members cost 575 s of kernel time against 5 members' 542 s — the fixed cost dominates).

Deliberately ranked BELOW the schedule and the diagnostic. It is the most predictable gain available and the least informative one: it would raise the leaderboard number while leaving every open question exactly where it is. Its real value is giving the other changes a stable ensemble to be measured against, so run it AFTER the recipe is settled, not before.
notes:
WHY THIS IS NOW THE PRIORITY, and how to measure it cheaply (2026-08-11).

The largest KNOWN difference between our 0.868 submission and the 0.888 graft is member count: 5 against 20. But the two also differ in per-member quality (0.8269 against their 0.8398), so the 0.020 leaderboard gap is a mixture of both and neither is attributable yet.

THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT BE TAKEN FROM WHAT WE HAVE. Our five members are five different FOLDS, so four of them trained on fold 0's holdout — ensembling them there would score a model on studies it was fitted on. Member count has to be varied with the fold held fixed, which means SEEDS.

QUEUED: two extra seeds for fold 0 (30 minutes), giving three members on one holdout. That yields the marginal-member curve — single member, then two, then three — and the shape of that curve says whether going to twenty is worth 2.5 hours of GPU or whether it saturates at four or five. Rank-averaging is the combiner, as the metric demands.

Ranked above further label work because arm A came back flat: the label lever is unproven on the model's own measurement, while the member lever is the one difference we KNOW separates our submission from the better-scoring one.
SEED VARIANCE IS +/-0.012, WHICH RETROSPECTIVELY WEAKENS MY OWN ABLATION CONCLUSIONS (2026-08-11).

Fold 0, identical recipe, identical data, only the seed differing:
  seed 2026   0.8202
  seed 7      0.8323     (+0.0121)

Every single-fold ablation I ran this session has an effect size FAR below that spread:
  intensity augmentation  +0.0019
  better labels           -0.0008
  both together           +0.0001

I reported those as 'null' and closed two issues on them. The honest statement is weaker: AT SEED 2026 the effects are small, and a single matched pair CANNOT RESOLVE an effect six times smaller than the run-to-run spread. 'Not detectable at n=1' is not the same as 'null', and I wrote the stronger claim.

WHY MATCHED SEEDS DID NOT SAVE IT, which is the subtle part: matching the seed fixes the initialisation and the data order, but every arm changes the random STREAM — augmentation draws differ, so the arms diverge stochastically much as different seeds would. Matched-seed is not paired in the way it looks.

WHAT SURVIVES: the five-fold result (+0.0107, every one of five folds improving) is a paired comparison across five independent splits, and five-for-five is not seed scatter. The bug fixes stand.

WHAT DOES NOT: the 2x2. To resolve a +0.002 effect against a +/-0.012 spread needs roughly (0.012/0.002)^2 ~ 36 paired runs, which at 15 minutes each is nine hours for one cell. That is not worth it for an effect that small — the correct conclusion is 'too small to matter at our current distance from the frontier', and the experiment should not be repeated bigger.

THE PROJECT'S OWN RULE SAID THIS: 'once a result works, multi-seed; never read signal into single-seed scatter'. I applied the first half and skipped the second.

SILVER LINING, and it is a real one: a +/-0.012 seed spread means ENSEMBLING SEEDS should pay well, because averaging independent runs of this variance is exactly what rank-averaging is for. That makes the member-count experiment more promising than it looked, not less.
VOID — THE MEASUREMENT WAS LEAKY, AND THE BUG WAS OURS (2026-08-11).

`train.py` built the fold split from the TRAINING seed: ReportFolds(folds, arguments.seed). So the extra seeds did not re-train the same setup on the same split — they trained on DIFFERENT splits. seed 7's fold-0 holdout shares 192 of 909 studies with seed 2026's.

CONSEQUENCES, all of them mine to retract:
1. 'Seed variance is +/-0.012' (0.8202 / 0.8323 / 0.8282) is unfounded — three numbers on three different holdouts of different difficulty, not three samples of one quantity.
2. The marginal-member curve (+0.0053 for the second member, +0.0018 for the third) is VOID: it scored seed 7 on seed 2026's holdout, 717 studies of which were seed 7's training data. That is what produced an implausible 0.8807 for a member that logged 0.8323 in its own run.
3. The correction I wrote to the interpretation document — downgrading the ablations against a +/-0.012 noise floor — rested on (1) and has itself been corrected.

THE BUG FAILED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION, which is why it was worth catching: leakage makes numbers BETTER, so nothing looks wrong until a value is implausible enough to question. 0.8807 was implausible only because a matched measurement of the same member existed at 0.8316.

FIXED: --split-seed is now separate from --seed and defaults to 2026, so the split is a property of the corpus rather than of the run. A test asserts that changing the model seed does not move the split.

STILL UNMEASURED, and to be redone with the fix: the run-to-run noise floor, and the marginal value of a member. Both need seeds that differ ONLY in initialisation.
close_reason: Curve measured on the recovered ruler, three seeds, one split: 1 member 0.8204 [0.8171-0.8233], 2 members +0.0018, 3 members +0.0007. Best SINGLE member (0.8233) beats the 3-member ensemble (0.8229). Ensembling buys ~0.002 for 3x inference. Caveat: these differ only by seed on one fold, so it is a LOWER bound - the submitted 5-fold ensemble also varies training data.

title: comp/SUBMISSIONS.md: method-tuple naming + coverage grid
description:
Mirror the biohub convention: kernels named for the method tuple from a closed vocabulary, one subdir per method, and a coverage grid recording what has been tried vs what has not. The slug says which method it is; a new version of one slug is that same method retrained.

WHY: without it, submissions become an unlabelled pile and the 5/day budget gets spent re-running things whose result is already known. It is also where a grafted score is recorded AS a graft.
notes:
THE LEDGER'S MISSING HALF IS FILLED, 2026-08-13. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md stopped at 2026-08-11 and was missing FIVE of the nine entries - including both numbers that matter most: the 0.894 fusion (our best board position) and the 0.500 (a slot spent on a T4 OOM that wrote no submission, so the deleted fallback scored the sample table). A submission record missing the entry that cost a slot is the one it most needed to hold.

Added with their local numbers, plus a section reading the six SCORED entries together, because separately they look like noise and together they isolate one variable:
    1 member   holdout 0.8518 (our best ever)  ->  LB 0.868
    2 members  0.8481                          ->  0.882
    3 members  0.8493                          ->  0.882
    5 members  0.8269                          ->  0.888
    20 theirs  0.8398                          ->  0.888
    23 fused   mixed                           ->  0.894
The best single model this project has produced loses to five much weaker ones by 0.020, and a third member of our OWN recipe bought nothing while a different recipe bought +0.006.

WHAT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR - a method-tuple naming scheme and a coverage grid - is still open. What is done is the RECORD, which was the part that could mislead a spend decision.
close_reason: Closed

title: Combine members by rank, not by probability
description:
The score is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs, invariant under any strictly increasing map, so calibration and thresholds are worth exactly nothing.

Averaging raw probabilities lets the most confident model dominate; averaging RANKS combines the only information the metric reads. Applies to member ensembling and to TTA pooling (logit-averaging is a geometric mean of odds, probability-averaging an arithmetic mean of risk - they order studies differently).
close_reason: Implemented and shipped: ensemble.py:110-116 ranks per label via argsort().argsort(), normalised, then means over members. Docstring at ensemble.py:7-8 carries the reason.

title: Members carry their preprocessing; verify by fingerprint before use
description:
A trained member is only reproducible together with the reading that produced it: resolution, crop, slice-order rule, laterality rule, slot-fill predicate, and the stand-in for a slice that will not decode. NONE of those change a single tensor shape.

So a member fitted under one reading and run under another loads cleanly, runs, and returns a submission computed from the wrong image. Ship the reading WITH the member, and have each member answer a seeded question whose expected answer travels with it; a mismatch stops the run rather than being averaged into a submission.

Group members by the pixels they need so one decode serves every member sharing it.
close_reason: Implemented and PROVEN: members carry their config, StudyModel.fingerprint answers a seeded question, and the graft-verify kernel reproduced 20/20 stored fingerprints at worst max|diff| 4.65e-06 against a 2e-3 tolerance. Members are grouped by pixel_group so one decode serves all sharing it. The submission path stops on a mismatch.

title: Backbone ablation: DINOv2 vs medical-pretrained
description:
Every public notebook mounts metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/small/1. Alternatives are already packaged as Kaggle datasets: RadImageNet ResNet-50, MedicalNet ResNet-50 (3D), BiomedCLIP.

The field defaulted to DINOv2 with no visible evidence against domain-matched medical pretraining. Natural-image SSL may well win, but it is untested here, which makes this a cheap and uncrowded axis once a harness exists.

NOTE: no internet in kernels - a backbone must be a MOUNTED Kaggle model, never a download.

title: Graded targets + confidence as sample weights
description:
Reports are graded, annotations are thresholded: "small joint effusion" can sit against a NEGATIVE annotation because the annotator marked only significant ones. So "term present => positive" is wrong by construction; grade the mention (trace / unqualified / marked) instead - and it costs nothing, because the metric reads only order.

Carry a per-finding confidence as a sample weight so a report that never mentions synovitis pulls weakly on that head rather than asserting a negative. Weight the image-annotated studies above every derived row - they are the only labels read from the images.
close_reason: Both halves shipped: targets.py carries graded scores (docstring 'Graded, not thresholded') and per-(study,target) confidence as loss weights, with annotated studies at W=3.0. The floor on top is knee-9sy, measured and closed.

title: Synovitis is 84.2% UNK and Fracture 56.4% — the biggest supervision hole in the corpus, and it does NOT predict our scores
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, over ALL 4,406 corpus rows. Every one of the twelve columns is populated
on every row, so these are rates over the corpus, not over a subset that happened to parse.

  label              UNK%    NO%   YES%
  Synovitis          84.2    2.6   13.2
  Fracture           56.4   36.5    7.1
  Lateral OA         33.1   42.3   24.7
  Medial OA          25.5   37.7   36.7
  Contusion          20.8   49.8   29.4
  PF OA              18.5   36.3   45.2
  Lateral Meniscus   10.0   64.5   25.4
  Effusion            9.9   29.6   60.5
  MCL                 9.8   72.8   17.4
  ACL                 8.1   64.1   27.8
  Medial Meniscus     5.7   41.1   53.3
  (Baker's Cyst absent on a column-name mismatch, not a missing measurement.)

WHERE THIS CAME FROM. The user challenged the label-contest pilot's headline — MCL is our worst label
and had 0/100 contested cells — with "that's unknown, if our worst labels were just not found in the
reports". Agreement on ABSENCE is not evidence of correctness, and it is failure mode 2 of that very
pilot. So it was measured rather than argued.

THE OBJECTION FAILS FOR MCL AND ACL, at the sharpest point. They are the two labels with zero contested
cells and they carry the LOWEST UNK rates of all eleven, 9.8% and 8.1%. MCL's 72.8% NO rate is the
highest in the corpus: the reports address the medial collateral ligament and call it intact. The reader
agreeing with that is agreeing with a real statement, not with a silence. So the pilot's conclusion
holds — supervision is not what bounds MCL.

IT RELOCATES AND LANDS HARDER. 3,710 studies carry no synovitis information and 2,485 carry no fracture
information. Over half the corpus is silent on fracture. That is a supervision hole far larger than the
pilot's 4.0% contest rate, and a contest cannot see it — a contest only scores cells where the reader
made a call.

AND IT DECLINES TO EXPLAIN OUR SCORES, which is the part worth keeping. If missingness capped
performance the ordering would show it. It inverts:
  Synovitis  worst coverage in the corpus (84.2% UNK)  ->  0.873, mid-pack, above seven other labels
  MCL        third-best coverage (9.8% UNK)            ->  0.788-0.793, worst of the twelve
So the hole is real, it is much bigger than the contest rate, and it is NOT the current bound.

MECHANISM FOR WHY IT COSTS LESS THAN IT LOOKS. Under --weight-floor (shipped in RECIPE) an UNK cell is
not dropped: it trains at value 0.28, weight 0.2875 — a soft negative. Synovitis's 13.2% positives are
learnable against a quiet negative background, which is what 0.873 on 84% missing data looks like.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY PRICE IT, and it is not a re-read — the reports genuinely do not contain the
information, so a better reader cannot recover it:
  (a) the AUC ceiling per label given its UNK share, computed on the 57 image-read annotations, which
      are the only cells where the truth is known independently of the report;
  (b) whether the soft-negative treatment of UNK is better or worse than dropping those cells, which is
      a matched arm and NOT one this bead should assume the sign of;
  (c) whether the ~0.87 Synovitis number survives on the annotation ruler or is an artefact of scoring
      against a holdout that inherits the same 84.2% silence — this is the one that could invert the
      whole reading above, and it is the FIRST thing to run.

Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md, section "The objection that
'0 contested' might just mean 'never mentioned' — measured".

P3 rather than higher: it is a ceiling question, not a floor question, and (c) is cheap enough that it
should gate any further work here.
notes:
ITEM (c) RUN 2026-08-20, and it CORRECTS THE EVIDENCE IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION while leaving the conclusion standing. Tool already existed: kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap, on report_labels_v2.csv, 58 annotated studies / 696 cells.

THE TWO POINTS I ARGUED FROM BOTH FLIP ON THE ANNOTATION RULER:
  Synovitis  report holdout 0.873  ->  annotation ruler 0.7378  (2nd worst of twelve)
  MCL        report holdout 0.788  ->  annotation ruler 0.8798  (4th best of twelve)
So the ~0.87 Synovitis number does NOT survive -- it falls 0.135 -- and it was in part an artefact of
scoring against a holdout that inherits the same 84.2% silence, exactly as (c) suspected. The specific
inversion this bead's description leans on ('worst coverage scores mid-pack, best coverage scores
worst') is a property of the REPORT ruler and must not be quoted again.

BUT THE CONCLUSION HOLDS, on twelve points instead of two. UNK share against annotation-ruler AUC:
  Synovitis 84.2% -> 0.7378 | Fracture 56.4% -> 0.8861 | Baker's 45.9% -> 0.9547 | Lateral OA 33.1% ->
  0.7099 | Medial OA 25.5% -> 0.9504 | Contusion 20.8% -> 0.8421 | PF OA 18.5% -> 0.8005 |
  Lateral Meniscus 10.0% -> 0.6497 | Effusion 9.9% -> 0.9453 | MCL 9.8% -> 0.8798 | ACL 8.1% -> 0.8640 |
  Medial Meniscus 5.7% -> 0.8498
  spearman rho = 0.014 (t = 0.04, df 10), pearson r = -0.111.
The best-scoring label carries 45.9% silence; the worst carries 10.0%. Missingness does not order the
findings on the ruler that counts either.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. rho = 0.014 over TWELVE points with each AUC drawn from ~58 studies cannot exclude a
moderate relation -- it fails to detect one, which is weaker than showing none. Per-label SE here is
~0.04-0.06 (label_power), so no single row above should be read to better than a few points, and the
2nd-worst / 4th-best ranks for Synovitis and MCL are themselves inside that noise. What survives is the
absence of an ORDERING, which is a claim about all twelve together and is the only thing twelve points
of this quality can support.

ITEM (a) IS NOW LARGELY ANSWERED TOO by the same run: supervision_gap's 'labels' column IS the report
label used as a predictor of the radiologist. Synovitis 0.6870 labels vs 0.7378 model -- the model
BEATS its own supervision by +0.0508 despite 84.2% silence, which is the mechanism this bead proposed
(an UNK cell trains as a soft negative, not a dropped one) confirmed on the annotation ruler.
ITEM (b) is untouched and is still a matched arm.

title: The labeler rulebook has three undecided conventions that produce 36 of 48 known label errors
description:
FOUND 2026-08-20 by the 100-report contest pilot (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md).
Filed separately from knee-mxj because this is a RULEBOOK defect, not a reader defect: none of the three
needs a better model, a re-read, or a GPU. They need a decision written down.

THE PILOT'S NUMBERS: 1,200 cells, 48 contested. 36 of the 48 trace to just two of the conventions below,
and a further 9 cells were parked as UNCERTAIN by the third.

(1) NO STABLE RULE FOR WHAT A NORMAL-BONE SENTENCE DENIES — the largest single source.
    The same template gets opposite answers across studies:
      tr, signal-only:   'sinyal intensiteleri dogaldir'  -> Fracture NO in 008/037, UNK in 032/046
      bg, structural:    'normalna forma'                 -> Fracture NO in 054/085, UNK in 007/036
    A signal statement and a structural statement deny different things, and the rulebook does not say
    which. This is also where the entire multilingual excess lives (bg 12.5%, tr 7.7%, hr 6.3% against
    en 2.7%) — those three languages compress bone and cartilage into one boilerplate clause, so the
    ambiguity fires more often there. It is a SENTENCE SHAPE, not a language deficit.

(2) A FINDING THE REPORT NEVER NAMES, ANSWERED NO — 23 cells, almost all Fracture / Contusion / Baker's,
    the findings a normal knee report simply does not mention. The bias is ONE-WAY: the reader fabricates
    denials, never positives. And the damage is a WEIGHT error, not a sign error: such a cell trains at
    value 0.08 / weight 0.85 where the rulebook puts it at 0.28 / weight 0.05. A cell that should be
    nearly switched off is trained at near-full confidence. PROPOSED RULE: unmentioned = UNK, never NO.

(3) OSTEOCHONDRAL LESION -> COMPARTMENT OA IS UNDECIDED — UNK in 018/022/052, YES in 015/044/054/061.
    9 cells parked as uncertain purely because the convention does not exist. Pick one and write it.

ALSO OBSERVED, smaller and worth recording before it is lost: BILATERAL OR COMPARTMENT-UNSPECIFIED SPANS
ANSWERED FOR ONE SIDE ONLY, 6 cells. Study 037's 'Medial ve lateral menisküste grade II dejenerasyon'
scored the medial and left the lateral UNK — the lateral is named in the very sentence used for the
medial. A span that names both compartments should answer both.

WHAT THIS IS WORTH, stated honestly so nobody plans around it. The pilot priced the WHOLE label axis at
+0.006 on the unweighted mean of twelve — at the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, a twentieth of the project
bar — and correcting label VALUES has been tried once and lost 0.0020 (calib_span). So this is P3 and it
is NOT a scoring lever. It is filed because the diagnosis was paid for, because a rulebook decision is
cheap and permanent, and because any future reader work would otherwise rediscover the same three
questions from scratch.

ACCEPTANCE: the three conventions written into the labeler rulebook as explicit rules. NOT a re-read of
the corpus — see the interpretation for why that pass is not worth taking.

title: Some commits fail once on 'files were modified by this hook' while every gate reports clean
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-20, twice in one session. A commit fails with three hooks marked Failed — importlinter-gate, arch-fitness, astgrep-gate — each with the SAME reason line, '- files were modified by this hook', and each with its own output reporting CLEAN:

  Contracts: 11 kept, 0 broken.
  INFO devtools.graph.fitness: architecture fitness: clean (0 god-modules / cycles / god-files; 0 advisory)
  INFO devtools.astgrep: ast-grep: clean (module shape)

So nothing is actually wrong with the code. Re-running the identical commit immediately afterwards succeeds first try, both times.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD AT P3 RATHER THAN IGNORING: this is the exact failure shape CLAUDE.md warns about — the twenty-odd Passed lines scroll past and the Failed lines are hundreds of lines up, so a commit verified by the tail of its own output reads as landed when it is not. It has already cost three silent no-op commits in an earlier session. The cost here is small (one retry) but the FAILURE MODE is the expensive one, and a recurring benign red makes the gate less likely to be read when it goes genuinely red.

DIAGNOSIS IS UNCONFIRMED. .beads/issues.jsonl shows as modified during the failing runs, including one where no bd command had been issued since the previous commit, which points at a beads daemon rewriting the jsonl while pre-commit is running — a race, which would explain why it is intermittent (one of three commits in this session passed first try with bd mutations staged). Not verified. .grimp_cache/ is gitignored so it is not the cache.

NEXT STEP: run the three hooks manually with the jsonl untouched and see whether the modification reappears; if it is the beads daemon, the fix is either an exclude in the hook config or ordering, and the pre-commit config is TEMPLATE-OWNED by sdlc-scaffold, so the change goes upstream and comes back through copier update rather than being hand-edited here.

title: The intensity augmentation block costs at most 0.8% of an arm, not the 15% first measured
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20 from the two arms' own metrics files, which record per-epoch `seconds`. aug_long and band_dense_long are a matched pair differing only in `intensity_aug`, so the epoch-time delta IS the block's cost.

  band_dense_long  median 363 s/epoch  (n=24, range 363-376, very tight)
  aug_long         median 417 s/epoch  (n=5,  range 389-429)
  delta            +54 s/epoch, +14.9%, +21.6 min over a 24-epoch arm

WHERE IT GOES. kneemri/training/augmentation.py is already vectorised and on-device — every transform draws from one torch.rand(n,...) and probabilistic ones are applied by MASK (out = do*transformed + (1-do)*original) rather than a Python branch. That is the documented, correct choice for batch throughput, and its price is that a blur with blur_probability=0.2 is COMPUTED on 100% of the batch and then thrown away for 80% of it. Same for gamma at 0.3. So the 15% is real GPU work, not a data-loading stall.

CONTENTION HYPOTHESIS CHECKED AND NOT SUPPORTED. aug_long's epoch times scatter over 40 s where band_dense_long's sit inside 13 s, which looked like CPU contention from other work on the machine during the arm. The wall-clock windows refute it: the fastest epoch (1, 389 s) and a slow one (2, 421 s) both ran while the machine was otherwise idle, and the two epochs that overlapped a nox gates run (3 and 4, 429/417) bracket that same range. Read the scatter as natural variance, not as a cost I am imposing.

IS IT WORTH FIXING. Not obviously. Gating blur/gamma on whether the mask has ANY true entries would recover most of it only when a whole batch draws below threshold, which at batch size n is rare; genuinely skipping per-sample means a Python branch per image, which is the thing the vectorisation exists to avoid. The honest options are (a) accept 15% as the price of the block, (b) index-select the subset the mask selects, run the transform on that subset, and scatter back — one gather/scatter against a full-batch conv, which is a real win at p=0.2 and a loss at p=1.0. (b) is the only one worth measuring and it must not change the RNG draw ORDER, which augmentation.py's docstring says is what makes a member's pixels reproducible.

FILED NOT CLAIMED: no fix attempted, no arm gated on this. It is a number to have before anyone argues about whether the intensity block earns its time.
notes:
THE PRICE THIS BEAD WAS FILED ON WAS MOSTLY SOMEBODY ELSE CPU. Re-measured 2026-08-20 over 13 aug_long epochs against all 24 of band_dense_long, a pair whose recorded recipes differ in exactly one field (intensity_aug True/False, every other key byte-identical):

    aug_long          n=13  median 392  min 366  max 429
    band_dense_long   n=24  median 363  min 363  max 376

MEDIAN gap +29 s (+8.0%), not the +54 s (+14.9%) this bead was filed on - that figure came from a handful of early epochs and did not survive more of them. But the medians are the wrong statistic and the SPREADS say why: the control varies over 13 s across 24 epochs, aug_long over 63 s across 13. A constant-work vectorised block cannot produce five times the variance; a contended machine can. ps -ef shows two celltrack proxy_eval CPU jobs at 7-8 CPU-hours each plus a dozen biohub_kaggle log watchers, all from other projects, competing with the dataloader.

MIN AGAINST MIN is the least-contended estimate available: 366 against 363, +3 s an epoch, +0.8% - and that comparison is BIASED AGAINST the block, since the control has 24 draws to find a low minimum and aug_long only 13. So the true cost is at most 3 s an epoch.

WHICH VINDICATES THE DOCSTRING I WAS IMPLICITLY DOUBTING. Augmentation._intensity records 18.7 ms against 19.0 ms a step for the enabled path against a guard, on a ~1.15 s step - about 1.7%. This bead +14.9% contradicted it by an order of magnitude, and I treated the docstring as the unrepresentative number (different shape) rather than treating my own measurement as the contaminated one. The docstring was right.

CONSEQUENCE, and the point of closing rather than re-scoping: the optimisation this bead proposed - index-select the masked subset, transform, scatter back, preserving RNG draw order - targets a share of 0.8%, on the ENABLED path only, which today is one arm whose own result is still undecided. Not worth the risk it carries: the whole ledger matched controls depend on identical augmentation, and a scatter/gather rewrite is exactly the kind of change that silently perturbs a draw. Reopen only if intensity augmentation earns a permanent place in the recipe AND the block is re-measured on an idle machine at a real training shape.

STANDING LESSON, bigger than the bead: an epoch-time delta measured while other projects hold the CPU is not a measurement of the flag. Take mins, not medians, or take the measurement when the machine is ours.

(This reason replaces an earlier one in which unescaped backticks were command-substituted by the shell and pasted a ps -ef dump into the ledger. Never put backticks in a bd reason written from bash.)
close_reason: Re-measured 2026-08-20: the intensity block costs AT MOST 3 s an epoch (+0.8%), not the 54 s (+14.9%) this bead was filed on. aug_long n=13 median 392 min 366; band_dense_long n=24 median 363 min 363, recipes differing in exactly one field. The medians are contaminated - control spread 13 s, aug_long spread 63 s, and ps -ef shows two celltrack CPU jobs at 7-8 CPU-hours plus a dozen biohub_kaggle watchers competing with the dataloader. Min against min is the least-contended estimate and is biased AGAINST the block (24 draws to find a low minimum against 13). That vindicates Augmentation._intensity own docstring (18.7 ms against 19.0 ms a step, ~1.7%), which I had implicitly doubted. The proposed index-select/scatter optimisation therefore targets a share of 0.8% on the enabled path only, against a real risk of perturbing an RNG draw the whole ledger matched controls depend on - not worth it. Reopen only if intensity augmentation earns a permanent place in the recipe AND is re-measured on an idle machine. STANDING LESSON: an epoch-time delta measured while other projects hold the CPU is not a measurement of the flag; take mins, not medians. Full working is in this issue notes.

title: final_ws_e12 recorded its epoch index into the auc field; the run has no score and no predictions
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 while auditing runs-on-disk against the ledger.

D:/data/.../final_ws_e12.metrics.jsonl has twelve epoch rows in which auc == epoch exactly (0.0, 1.0, ... 11.0) and no per_label key at all. The loss column is healthy and monotone (1.1992 -> 0.5774 over the twelve), so the run TRAINED; what failed is the recorder, which wrote the epoch index into the score field.

IT CANNOT BE RECONSTRUCTED FROM DISK. Every other run of that era kept a .holdout.npz that HoldoutMetrics.of can rescore from - this one did not (only .metrics.jsonl, .partial and .pt). So the only path to its number is re-scoring final_ws_e12.pt against the holdout on the card, which is GPU work and therefore queued behind arms, not done inline.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE RUN: a metrics file whose auc field is well-formed nonsense passes every reader we have. RunMetrics.best would happily return auc=11.0 as this run's best epoch, and any comparison against it would quote 11.0 as a score. The ledger never named this run so nothing downstream was corrupted, but nothing DETECTED it either - it surfaced only because a name-matching audit went looking. Worth an assert in the recorder or a range check where scores are read (an AUC outside [0,1] is not a number any reader should accept).

SCOPE NOTE: this is one file and a pre-existing era's bug, not a live defect - current runs record correctly (band_span's rows this hour are well-formed). Priority is the range check, not the historical run.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-19: the filing claimed `RunMetrics.best` would return auc=11.0 for final_ws_e12 and that every reader accepts it. Both halves are wrong, checked against the code rather than assumed. run_metrics.py:274 already guards it — the run recorded fold -1, a run that held nothing back cannot have a best epoch, and best() returns None for final_ws_e12 AND final_fit_e12 today. The other three readers of auc are guarded too, two by that same best(), and LabelStability by requiring per_label, which the corrupt rows do not carry.

What the audit DID find in the same sweep is a different defect and it is now fixed: LabelStability.best parsed the metrics file itself and took a maximum over every line, missing the last-run-group rule RunMetrics.rows() exists for. pair_memory_s2026 is the case on disk (12 epochs peaking 0.8353, then 4 peaking 0.8155) and it contributed the profile of an overwritten checkpoint to the stability correlation. Delegated to RunMetrics.rows(); the across-holdout median rank correlation is unchanged at +0.51, so the recorded conclusion survives the fix.

Remaining scope of this bead is therefore SMALLER than filed: not 'readers accept a nonsense AUC' but 'the guard is a recipe lookup, so a corrupt file whose recipe does NOT record fold<0 would pass'. final_fit_e12 is that shape (no fold in its recipe) and returns None only because it recorded no rows at all. A range check on auc in [0,1] would close it by value rather than by provenance. Downgrading to P3 — no reader is wrong today.
close_reason: Closed

title: An EMA of the weights is kept for the FINAL FIT only: +0.0013 directional, free
description:
weight_average scored 0.8460 vs control 0.8457 — flat, and its pre-registration says that is the EXPECTED result, not a disappointment: keeping the best epoch by holdout score is itself an average over the trajectory, so an EMA was predicted to help LEAST here and MOST in the final fit, where no holdout ranks epochs and the last one is kept by construction.

The mean is therefore the wrong read. Its own stated targets were the best-to-last gap and the last-epoch value:
  control          best 0.8457  last 0.8394  gap 0.0063
  weight_average   best 0.8460  last 0.8407  gap 0.0053
Gap shrinks 0.0010, last epoch +0.0013. Both far under the 0.0062 floor, so NEITHER IS A RESULT.

VERDICT (the significance bar applied literally): directional, mechanism-sound and free — one extra weight copy, no extra step time, no measured throughput cost. So KEEP IT for the final fit, where there is no holdout to select on, and do NOT spend a slot on it, rebuild a member for it, or plan around it.

It does not rescue the banned seed/fold axis it was scouting for: damping the last few hundred steps recovers about a fifth of the 0.0062 three-seed spread — a knob-sized piece of a floor-sized problem.

ACTION when a final fit is next built: pass --ema. Nothing to do before then. Ledger: experiments/README.md, 'An EMA buys nothing where a holdout picks the epoch'.

title: Report length as a free auxiliary target (rho ~0.5 with finding count, model never sees it)
description:
Measured 2026-08-19 (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-19_report-length-is-severity.md): report length predicts the number of positive findings inside EVERY language, rank corr +0.42 (en) to +0.85 (tr), Q4-Q1 of +2.2 to +5.5 findings a study. Verified on the 57 annotated studies to be real severity rather than reader harvesting: calls per study rise with length (+0.506) while precision does not fall with it (67.6/63.9/64.3 by tercile, a spread under one binomial SE).

So it is a cheap, language-independent, reader-independent severity proxy that the IMAGE model never sees. Candidate: regress log length as an auxiliary head. One scalar per study, reuses the ReportSupervision plumbing already in the trainer (--report-weight / --report-vectors path).

NOT a finding and not priced. Nothing measured says it moves the score; what is measured is that the signal exists and is free to construct. Gate it behind a smoke plus one short arm against rate_wholestack (0.8525) before it takes a queue slot.

title: READERS=4 buys ~9% of a 448px epoch — measured in step time, not just GB/s
description:
knee fetch follow-up, MEASURED 2026-08-18. fetch_bench said the trainer's narrow-window read peaks at four handles (1.39 vs 1.06 GB/s). Open question was whether Prefetch hides that. It does not.

448 px, batch 12, 600 studies (476 train), 1 epoch, --recompute-activations --vram-gb 26, narrow window (no --whole-stack). Handle counts INTERLEAVED 2,4,2,4,2,4 so cache warming cannot name a winner:

    READERS=2 : 22, 23, 21 s   (mean 22.0)
    READERS=4 : 20, 20, 20 s   (mean 20.0)

Round one (4,2,2,4) agrees on its warm arms: 22/21 at two vs 19 at four; its first arm was 47 s cold.
Loss identical to four decimals in all ten runs — the reader changes how bytes arrive, not what is computed (the equality oracle in tests/unit/kneemri/corpus already asserts this).

DENOMINATOR: 9% is of a WARM epoch — 600 studies fit in RAM. A full-corpus epoch reads colder, where the fetch term is larger, so 9% is a floor on the saving, not a ceiling.

Constant already shipped at 4 (commit d8b52e4). This bead records the step-time confirmation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fetch throughput: the windowed read peaks at 4 handles (measured), whole-stack at 2
description: MEASURED 2026-08-18 with the new kneemri.corpus.fetch_bench on the 336px_12sl cache. Windowed read (3 of 12 slices, one seek per slot): 0.72 / 1.06 / 1.39 / 1.31 GB/s at 1/2/4/8 handles; reproduced with arms reversed over different rows at 0.77 / 1.25 / 1.43 / 0.92. Whole stack (one seek per study): 0.67 mapped, then 1.06 / 1.35 / 1.35 / 1.38. READERS raised 2 -> 4 in commit d8b52e4; the equality oracle against MappedReader still passes and the 60-study smoke returns the same loss 1.3441, so no number the trainer produces changed. OPEN QUESTION, not measured: what fraction of a real step the fetch is at 448 px and batch 12 - the win is on the host-side term only, so its size in STEP time is unknown until a full-size arm is timed with and without. Re-run the bench on any new cache before trusting the constant: --width for the branch, --offset for fresh rows, --reverse against arm-order effects.

title: Five training switches no committed arm exercises: --pool, --anatomical-prior, --normalise-by-count, --tie, --head-lr
description:
Measured 2026-08-18 by diffing TrainingOptions' 48 flags against every --flag appearing under experiments/**.sh: 13 are never passed by any arm or script. Eight of those are legitimately unarmed (--paths, --seed, --split-seed, --folds, --cache-studies, --bf16 and --band-low/--band-high are defaults, smoke plumbing, or set by the cache builder rather than the trainer). Five are real switches with no coverage on the card: --pool (cls_mean vs focal — the ledger records that before its wiring no arm could select focal AT ALL, and none does now), --anatomical-prior (last used in LEGACY_COMMANDS.md, not in any live arm), --normalise-by-count, --tie (the router; every arm takes the default first-maximal) and --head-lr.

Consequence: arm_check --smoke proves 'every committed recipe survives a real epoch', which is only true of the paths the arms take. These five are landed-checked and stamped but never RUN, so a break in them surfaces at the queue, not at the smoke. Either an arm exercises each (which also answers whether the knob is worth anything) or the knob is dead weight the vulture gate cannot see, because it is reachable Python that argparse references.

Repro: python - <<'EOF'
import pathlib, re
from kneemri.training.train import TrainingOptions
flags = {f"--{n.replace('_','-')}" for n in vars(TrainingOptions())}
text = chr(10).join(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8') for p in pathlib.Path('experiments').rglob('*.sh'))
print(sorted(flags - set(re.findall(r'--[a-z0-9-]+', text))))
EOF
notes: Answered by execution 2026-08-18 and closed off mechanically: all five never-run switches (--pool focal, --anatomical-prior, --normalise-by-count, --tie last, --head-lr) reach a written checkpoint at 60 studies / 1 epoch. The defect was that nothing was watching, so switch_coverage.py now partitions every TrainingOptions field into armed / covered / written-off, a unit test asserts the partition is total, and arm_check --switches runs the recipes. Commit fd26930.
close_reason: Closed

title: --unfreeze-last has no landed-check because LoRA legitimately ignores it
description: StudyModel.parameter_groups honours unfreeze_last only when no adapters are present -- under LoRA every block carries one and the depth argument does not apply. So a naive observed-vs-asked check on open blocks false-positives on every LoRA arm. Wanted: model reports the count of blocks holding a trainable parameter, and Request maps the ask through the adaptation mode rather than through the flag. Deferred because the ambiguity is a design question, not plumbing.
close_reason: Closed

title: KernelRun logs the overlap it was ASKED for, not the one any member used
description: 2026-08-17. FILED ON A REFUTED PREMISE, corrected here. Original claim: solo ran overlap=True while trio ran False, so solo confounded the member-count curve. WRONG. Member.window (kneemri/inference/members.py:385) gives a whole_stack member ONE centred window and never reads the flag at all. Every member in the current pool is whole_stack, so solo v3 and v4 predict identically and the count curve was never at risk. The proposed fix was worse than the bug: flipping the default to False silently disables overlap for WINDOWED members, where tests/integration/mounts_to_kernel.py:130 asserts it is worth +0.0156 — the strongest number in the repo, and the 20 CC0 members in the fusion entry are windowed. Reverted; the default stays True. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is small: kernel_run.py:148 logs 'serving: ... overlap=%s' from self.overlap, i.e. the REQUEST. No member reports what it did. That log line is the entire reason a non-difference read as a confound and cost a re-push. Fix: log the realised decode (windows per member, or whole_stack vs windowed) rather than the request, so the log says what happened.
close_reason: Closed

title: kit_check counts commits over the whole package, so inference-inert code refuses a kit
description: 2026-08-17: kit_check refused with '3 commit(s) behind in kneemri/core' for 84b47c6 / ee0322e / c4756c6 — all three purely additive measurement code (git diff --stat 6f93554..HEAD -- kneemri core = 2 files, 266 insertions, 0 deletions: band_coverage.py plus an Acquisition.through_plane_mm property). Nothing the kernel imports changed. The check measures commit DISTANCE over the declared packages rather than over the import closure the kernel actually loads, so any analysis module landing in kneemri/ blocks a kit that is byte-identical where it matters. Cost today: a manual diff on submission day to prove a refusal was spurious. Fix: compare the kit against the transitive import closure of the kernel entrypoints, or hash the shipped files, instead of counting commits over the package. Until then a refusal needs the diff read before it is believed — and a refusal that is ALWAYS overridden is a check that will one day be overridden when it is right.
close_reason: KernelClosure: kit_check now judges drift over the entrypoint's 23-file import closure. 12 spurious commits behind -> 5 real ones on the same stamp.

title: ruff format has been clean for the whole tree and is still advisory — graduate it upstream
description:
@
MEASURED 2026-08-17: `uv run ruff format --check kneemri core tests devtools` reports `206 files already
formatted`, 0 drift. The gate philosophy in CLAUDE.md is "a check starts advisory, and once the code is
clean it GRADUATES to enforced" — this one has met the bar and has not moved.

The blocker is ownership, not the number. `noxfile.py:41` is template-owned:

    session.run("uvx", RUFF, "format", "--check", ".", external=True, success_codes=[0, 1])

Graduation is dropping `success_codes=[0, 1]` there (and the matching CI/pre-commit invocation), which is
