an sdlc-scaffold edit, not a kneemri one. Do NOT hand-edit it here to make it enforce — fix upstream and
`uvx copier update`.

Cost of graduating: zero today, which is exactly when a ratchet is free to tighten. Cost of NOT: format
drift re-enters silently and the next person pays a whole-tree reformat diff on top of whatever they were
actually changing.

Note the scope difference to check before enforcing: nox runs `format --check .` (the WHOLE repo, dot),
while the 206-file clean reading above was over `kneemri core tests devtools`. Re-measure with the bare
dot before flipping, in case a root-level or generated file drifts.
@
close_reason: duplicate of knee-rqi4; the measurement and the noxfile line moved into that bead

title: batch/start/width travel together across study_cache and window_reader — Window already exists
description: cohesion.data_clumps finds one clump: (batch, start, width) with 5 supports across kneemri/corpus/study_cache.py and kneemri/corpus/window_reader.py. kneemri/inference/members.py already has a Window type (starts, width, size) expressing the same idea on the serving side, so the corpus side is passing a decomposed Window by hand. Unify on one Window at the package root or beside its producer; DRY plus it removes the argument-order failure mode (start and width are both ints). Measured 2026-08-17 via cohesion.data_clumps.
notes: WON'T FIX — audited 2026-08-17, the case is already made in code. window_reader.py:22 argues (batch, start, width) travels as three parameters DELIBERATELY: it is a slicing expression, not a noun. Nothing stores one, returns one, or decides from one; Prefetch holds the schedule that produces them; and Window in inference.members is a DIFFERENT thing (a member's read plan, starts/width/size). A value object here would name an argument list on the inner loop and still be unpacked in the same two places. The detector cannot see a docstring, so this clump will be re-reported on every cohesion run - that is the detector's limit, not a debt.
close_reason: Closed

title: TrainingOptions is six unrelated configs in one dataclass (LCOM4=6)
description: cohesion.lcom reports TrainingOptions at LCOM4=6 — the highest in the tree — with six disjoint method clusters: {adaptation, fitted_trainer, objective, reports} / {band, crop, reading} / {routing} / {supervision} / {sampled} / {fitted_model}. This is the object every training arm is configured through, so the clusters are what an arm actually varies: a READING (band/crop/reading), a SUPERVISION, a ROUTING, and a FIT. Splitting along the measured cluster boundary would make an arm declare which axis it varies instead of setting fields in one flat bag, and arm_check could then assert per-axis. NOT to be done while a training slot is pending — it touches every arm definition. Measured 2026-08-17 via: python -m devtools.run kneemri core --report cohesion.lcom
notes:
AUDITED 2026-08-17 (read train.py:41-160 and 422-540, not greps about it). The LCOM4=6 is two different things and only one is debt.

NOT DEBT — the derived views. The clusters {crop, band, reading}, {routing}, {supervision} are
properties over a FLAT field set, and the flatness is load-bearing: parse() is
cls(**vars(parser().parse_args())), so every flag must land as a scalar field while everything
downstream wants the pair. Each of those properties carries a docstring saying exactly that, and two
of them exist because member_record once stamped a MODULE CONSTANT where the run's own value belonged.
A config object with derived views has no method-field cohesion by construction — LCOM cannot score
this class kind, the same way the data-clump detector could not score window_reader (knee-wjsd).

REAL, BUT DELIBERATE — config plus factory. adaptation/objective/reports/fitted_model/fitted_trainer
build policy objects, which IS a second responsibility. It is there on purpose: main was accumulating
a statement per switch, and 'the run's SETUP is a different job from the run's LOOP' (train.py:499).
The extraction was the fix; the residue is that setup landed on the config rather than beside it. A
RunSetup collaborator taking the options and owning the five factory methods would satisfy both, and
would cost the options_to_policies test its current walk over fitted_trainer/fitted_model — which is
the mechanism that catches a flag reaching no policy, so it must move with them, not be dropped.

P2 -> P3 and NOT NOW. This edits the training entrypoint, the standing instruction is to keep the
pipeline ready for a train command at any moment, and the change buys structure rather than score.
Do it between arms, never before one, and re-run the 300-study smoke plus gates after.

2026-08-18: a SIXTH factory method landed on this class deliberately — TrainingOptions.requested(device),
commit 5d06690 — and it is worth saying why, because it moves the LCOM4 the wrong way on purpose. The
pre-flight landed check's own input was seventeen hand-copied `field=arguments.field` lines inside main,
i.e. the guard against silent mis-wiring was itself unguarded at its input: a crossed wire like
weight_floor=arguments.calibrated_targets parses, type-checks and runs, and the guard then clears a run
for a switch nobody asked for while refusing it for one it did. Putting the transcription on the options
object is what let a test walk it ONE-HOT (move one flag, demand exactly one request field follow) without
a card, a corpus or an encoder download — the same argument this audit already accepted for
objective/reports/fitted_model, 'so the choice can be checked without a GPU'.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RunSetup MOVE: six methods to take, not five, and requested() must travel with them
for the reason stated above about the options_to_policies walk — a test that catches a flag reaching no
policy has to move with the methods it walks, never be dropped.

PROCESS NOTE, since this bead is where it happened: the 2026-08-18 note was first written with a shell
command substitution meant to preserve this audit, the substitution errored, and bd cheerfully replaced
the whole field with the new text alone. Restored from the session transcript. --notes REPLACES; build
the full text first and pass it whole.
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18 (after commit 5d06690): TrainingOptions is LCOM4=4, no longer the tree's highest — OutOfFoldOracle is, at 5. The clusters are now {adaptation, fitted_model, fitted_trainer, objective, reports, requested, supervision} / {band, crop, reading} / {routing} / {sampled}, i.e. requested() and supervision JOINED the factory cluster rather than adding one. The number this bead was filed on has moved on its own, and the residue is the derived-view shape this bead's own audit already classified as NOT DEBT. Staying P3; the RunSetup move buys structure, not a number, and the training entrypoint has to stay ready. Read this report as a diff, not a queue (knee-xbuv).

PROCESS: bd update has --append-notes, which is what the 2026-08-17 destroyed-notes incident needed. --notes still REPLACES.
close_reason: Landed. kneemri/training/run_setup.py:36 RunSetup owns the factory cluster (adaptation/requested/objective/reports/model/trainer); TrainingOptions keeps only the flag-reading methods (routing/crop/band/reading/cache/supervision). The mechanism the notes said must MOVE with them did: tests/integration/options_to_policies.py:24 imports RunSetup and walks its trainer/model policy methods (lines 124, 137), so a flag reaching no policy still fails at the commit that adds it.

title: Upstream: scaffold CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md misdescribe the gate stack
description:
sdlc-scaffold graduated shape_contracts to --assert (noxfile gate list, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml all pass --assert; ci.yml even carries the comment 'Was advisory; graduated once cardiac proved a real ml tree stays clean'), but the rendered CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md gate list still says '**shape-contracts** (advisory) ... Migrate boundaries, then graduate to --assert to block.'

title: The 448 cache's own rungs are buyable now: 420 px fits at UNCHANGED batch 12, 448 px at batch 9
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17, one epoch on 400 studies, fold 0, whole-stack + compile + activation checkpointing + bf16, --vram-gb 28 on a card with ~2.8 GB already held by another tenant. Scores are NOT the point here; these are memory and wall-clock only.

  392 px, batch 12 (the shipping recipe):  20.46 GB peak,  733 img/s,  55 s/epoch
  420 px, batch 12:                        23.42 GB peak,  618 img/s,  89 s/epoch
  448 px, batch  9:                        20.00 GB peak,  560 img/s,  88 s/epoch
  448 px, batch 10:                        22.19 GB peak,  523 img/s,  93 s/epoch
  448 px, batch  6:                        13.43 GB peak,  511 img/s,  98 s/epoch
  448 px, batch 12:                        OOM in six seconds (25.2 GB allocated, 28 GB cap)

WHAT THIS CHANGES. experiments/README.md:370 records '392 already holds 28.4 GB of a 32 GB card while 448 OOMed outright' and concludes that 'buying the next rung would mean a smaller batch, which changes the ranking term's within-batch pair count and stops it being one variable'. That was true of the recipe as it stood. It is not true of the recipe as it stands now: activation checkpointing (2026-08-17, -29% throughput for 3.6x memory) took 392/batch-12 from 28.4 GB down to 20.5, and the headroom it freed buys 420 px at the SAME batch 12. The confound the ledger names — a resolution arm that also changes the batch and therefore the ranking term's pair count — does not apply to 420.

WHY IT MATTERS. Resolution across the image plane is the one cause of the 0.054 frontier gap (knee-jk3) that survived testing; breadth across sequences was refuted at +0.0002 and the 12-of-36 slice cache at no cost. 336 -> 392 is also the largest single measured jump we have (+0.0066, confounded with the encoder rate). The rung above it has been sitting behind a memory wall that no longer exists, and nothing needs decoding: the cache is already 448 px, so --train-size 420 reads it with no rebuild and no new disk.

THE ARM TO RUN when a training slot is free: the shipping whole-stack recipe with --train-size 420 --batch 12, twelve epochs, fold 0, against res392_ws_s2026 (0.8523) on the same holdout. One variable. At 1.6x the wall-clock of the 392 arm.

448/batch-9 is the rung after that, and it does move the batch — read it only if 420 pays.
notes:
2026-08-19: dropped P1 -> P3. The bead's own 2026-08-18 note already retired it — the rungs were bought as RESOLUTION rungs and that axis measured flat (+0.0002, knee-a8x) — so it was sitting in bd ready above work that has a live mechanism. The MEASUREMENT stays valuable and is why this is parked rather than closed: 420 px at unchanged batch 12 is a one-variable arm that costs nothing to decode, so if some other axis ever needs more image plane, the memory wall is already known to be gone. It needs that reason first.
2026-08-19: the axis is now flat TWICE, not once. The 2026-08-18 refutation was the 336->392 step at 8e-6 (+0.0002). The same step at 4e-5 was already on disk unread as a pair — lr4e-5_ws_s2026 (rate_wholestack's storage name) vs res392_ws_s2026 — and reads MEAN -0.0002, with run_comparison confirming the only recipe change is image_size 336->448, train_size 0->392. Two independent rates, both flat against a 0.0062 floor. Stays P3 and parked for the same reason: the memory measurement keeps its value, the resolution reason is now refuted rather than merely unsupported.

title: ruff format --check is labelled advisory but BLOCKS every commit
description: The pre-commit hook 'ruff — format check (advisory)' fails the commit when a file would be reformatted, so it is enforced in practice and advisory only in its label. That mislabel cost three silent no-op commits on 2026-08-17 before the cause was found: the twenty Passed lines below it hide the one Failed line, and the label says it cannot be the blocker anyway. Either graduate it honestly (drop '(advisory)' from the hook name, since the repo is already clean) or make it non-blocking. Template-owned (sdlc-scaffold): fix upstream, not here.

Re-measured here first with the bare dot as this bead asked: 'uv run ruff format --check .' -> 244 files already formatted, 0 drift. Scaffold suite green (14 unit, 85 e2e / 2 skipped). NOT YET PULLED HERE: needs 'uvx copier update', which rewrites this repo's gate config and is a deliberate step, not one to take while a queue may be armed. Local CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md still say 'format --check advisory' and become wrong at that update.

title: Advisory gate blocks are triaged: read them as a diff, not a work queue
description:
Every `uvx nox -s gates` run prints three advisory blocks that have now been read and triaged three
times in three sessions, each time reaching the same answer. Written down once so the next sweep does not
pay for it again — and so that if one of them ever becomes a real finding, the change from THIS baseline
is what gets noticed.

STATE AT 2026-08-17: 29 LCOM4 classes, 1 data clump, 13 recurring string literals, 2 repeated key-sets.

DECIDED NO, WITH REASONS:

  - DATA CLUMP `batch, start, width` (study_cache.py / window_reader.py). Already answered in the code
    it flags: `window_reader.py:22` says the three travel as parameters rather than one request object
    DELIBERATELY. The detector cannot read the comment; the decision stands.
  - LCOM4 ON CONFIG CARRIERS. `TrainingOptions` (6) is a config object — its fields are read by different
    consumers by construction, which is what LCOM4 measures and what a config is FOR. Same for
    `OutOfFoldOracle` (6) and `StackCoverage` (4): facades whose methods each answer one question about
    one corpus. Splitting them buys a smaller number and more files.
  - MAGIC STRING LITERALS. `utf-8` (25x), `cpu`/`cuda` (29x), `nan`/`inf` are stdlib vocabulary. The
    CSV column names (`StudyInstanceUID` 10x, `train_series`, `fold`) fail LOUDLY on a typo — pandas
    raises KeyError — so a constant buys spelling, not safety. The only silent-failure candidates are the
    DICOM keywords (`ImagePositionPatient`, `ImageOrientationPatient`, read through `getattr(header, ...,
    None)`), and those already live in one file behind `_ORDER_TAGS` in `acquisition.py`.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: a NEW entry in any of the three blocks, or a count that moves. The advisory
blocks are useful as a diff against this baseline, not as a work queue — treating them as one is how a
sweep turns into cosmetics, which the house rule forbids ("the linter is a bug-finder, not cosmetics").
close_reason: Recorded decision, no actionable residue. Closing keeps them searchable without sitting in ready.

title: Mount coverage is only checked when someone passes --kernel; nothing runs it before a slot
description: 74a5881 added MemberPackage.mounts + KernelSources + 'verify_members --kernel <kernel-metadata.json>', which refuses an entry whose kernel does not declare the encoders its members need. It is OPT-IN: a submission built without that flag gets no check at all, and the five committed pre-flight checks (arm_check, ledger_check, kit_check, kit_check --mounted, witness_check) do not call it. Two ways to close it: (a) have witness_check or the kit build resolve the kernel directory it is shipping for and run the comparison itself, which needs a link from an entry to its kernel-metadata.json that does not exist today; (b) a repo-level test that every kernel in comp/kernels declares the mounts of the members its script names, which needs parsing the member names out of each kernel script. (b) is a real gate and cheap; measured 2026-08-17, three of the ten kernels (graft, graft-verify, solo) run named subsets, so the parse is what makes it non-trivial. Not urgent while submissions are paused.
notes: Closed by mount_check (e918164): sweeps comp/kernels, parses KernelRun via ast, compares to KernelSources. First run REFUSED kneemri-solo — strongest(1) over a package holding lora_r8_v3small while the metadata declared DINOv2 only; metadata fixed. 6 ok / 4 skipped (graft, graft-verify, fusion, probe build no KernelRun) / 0 refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: pytest crashed mid-run once during gates (exit -1 in tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py), passed on rerun
description: 2026-08-17 10:20 UTC. 'uvx nox -s gates' died with 'Command uv run pytest tests --cov --cov-report=term-missing failed with exit code 4294967295' (-1, a process crash rather than a test failure) while printing tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py — no traceback, no failure summary. Reran the file alone (46 passed) and the whole gates session (green, 3 minutes, 98% coverage) with no code change between, so it is a flake, not a regression. kit_check's tests shell out to git via subprocess, which is the only external process in that file and the obvious suspect (a transient git.exe failure on Windows would surface as a crash of the pytest process only if it took the interpreter down, so this is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis). Worth catching properly if it recurs: run pytest with -p no:randomly and --maxfail=1 -x under 'faulthandler', and check the Windows Application log for the crash record. Filed rather than fixed because one occurrence gives nothing to fix.

title: Serving path: compile or not, decide on a measurement
description:
Training compiles by default since 2026-08-17 (-21%/step). Serving (kneemri/inference/ensemble.py forwarded/predict_member) does not, and should not be switched on blind:

- forwarded() halves rows on torch.OutOfMemoryError. Under dynamo the OOM comes back wrapped in InternalTorchDynamoError, which that except clause does not catch -> the kernel dies and writes no submission. That is the exact failure class two submissions were already spent on.
- Every distinct (rows, window.width) shape is its own graph. The ragged last chunk alone doubles the count, and the OOM retry adds more, each rebuilt under memory pressure.
- Compile time is measured on THIS machine (2.2 s, 9950X3D). Kaggle gives 2-4 slow cores; the per-graph build there is unmeasured and could exceed what the fused kernels save.

Decide with a local measurement first: one member, one chunk, eager vs compiled wall-clock on the 5090, plus graph count. Only if the gain is large AND the OOM path is made compile-safe (catch the wrapped error, or torch._dynamo.disable on forwarded) is this worth the entry risk.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 on the 5090, res392_ws_s2026 (dinov2-small, 6 slots x 12 slices at 392 px), via the new committed CLI `python -m kneemri.inference.serve_bench`:

  4 studies:   eager 188.2 ms  compiled 143.4 ms  -24%   compile 9.5 s   payback 212 passes  graphs 1
  48 studies:  eager 2269.2 ms compiled 1767.6 ms -22%   compile 13.0 s  payback  26 passes  graphs 1

VERDICT: NOT worth adopting as written. The steady-state win is real and matches training's -21%, but it is bought per MEMBER: 13 s of compilation, repaid only after 26 kernel-sized chunks = ~1,250 studies THAT MEMBER predicts. A package of six members needs the hidden test to be that large six times over before the entry is ahead, and the ragged final chunk is a second shape (a second graph, a second build) that this bench does not charge either arm for.

And the 5090 number is an UPPER BOUND on the T4's. Compilation buys mostly kernel-launch overhead, which is a smaller fraction of a slower card's pass; the build itself runs on 2-4 Kaggle cores against 16 here, so the payback threshold moves the wrong way on both terms.

The blockers in the description stand and would have to be cleared first anyway (wrapped OOM in forwarded). Leaving open at P3 rather than closing: if the whole-package serving ever becomes the deadline binder, re-run the bench at that member mix and re-read these numbers.

title: The scaffold's render-format test is blind to the one long literal it exists to catch, so every generated noxfile.py ships an E501
description:
FOUND 2026-08-17 while chasing the single remaining ruff finding in this repo's advisory whole-tree run:

  uvx ruff@0.15.13 check . --statistics  ->  1  E501  line-too-long

The line is noxfile.py:14, `SELECT = "F,B,I,T201,...,TID251"` — 274 characters against a 120 limit.
noxfile.py:152 (the batched `--gate` list) is a second at 164. Both are single string literals, which
`ruff format` cannot split, so they persist through any amount of formatting.

WHY THIS IS A BUG UPSTREAM AND NOT A NIT HERE. sdlc-scaffold has a test whose stated job is exactly
this: tests/unit/test_scaffold_consistency.py::test_python_templates_render_exactly_as_ruff_would_format_them.
Its docstring says it covers both directions, and names ours — "`--select E501` catches the long line
ruff cannot split (a long string literal), which formatting alone leaves alone."

It cannot see this line. `_render` builds a CONCRETE context (project_name, packages, lint_paths,
jscpd_paths, coverage_floor, plus _PINNED_VERSIONS) and `ruff_select` is NOT in it. Jinja renders an
undefined as the empty string, so the template's `SELECT = "{{ ruff_select }}"` becomes `SELECT = ""`
— 13 characters. The longest line in any generated file is replaced by the shortest one before the
E501 check ever runs. The test reads green, and every consumer's noxfile carries the violation as
advisory noise forever, which is precisely the "can carry a violation forever as report noise"
condition that same docstring says this test exists to defeat.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE plus one wrap, both upstream:
  1. tests/unit/test_scaffold_consistency.py `_render` context gains
     "ruff_select": copier_default("ruff_select")  — copier.yml:157 holds the real 274-char default,
     and copier_default() is already imported and used for the pinned versions.
  2. template/noxfile.py.jinja emits the select wrapped, e.g. `SELECT = ",".join((...))` with one rule
     per line via `{% for rule in ruff_select.split(",") %}`. This also makes a rule's arrival or
     removal a one-line diff, which the current 274-char literal does not.

THE `--gate` LINE IS NOT WORTH THE SAME FIX, and the reason is the interesting half. Wrapping it the
same way BREAKS tests/unit/test_scaffold_consistency.py::test_every_enforced_gate_is_wired_into_all_three_runners:
`_enforced_gates` finds gates with `re.finditer(r"--gate[\"',\s]+([\w,.]+)", text)`, which reads the
single token after --gate. Against a joined tuple it captures `.join` and reports all ten real gates as
"wired in ci.yml and pre-commit only" — measured, that is the exact failure it printed. That detector is
a genuine safety net (a gate it cannot SEE is indistinguishable from a gate that is not wired), so the
gate literal should stay one string until someone teaches the regex the joined form. Recorded so the
next person does not rediscover it by breaking the test.

SCOPE NOTE: filed, not fixed, for the same reason as knee-1rax — noxfile.py is template-owned
(.copier-answers.yml pins sdlc-scaffold v1.27.1) and the scaffold is a DIFFERENT REPO. I started editing
it and the owner stopped me, correctly: "fix upstream" says where a fix belongs, not that this session
should walk into another repository unasked. Both changes above were written and REVERTED
(sdlc-scaffold is clean at 948217f on dev); nothing was committed or pushed there.

title: uvx nox -s gates passes on files that pre-commit then refuses: ruff format is advisory in one and enforcing in the other
description:
HAPPENED TWICE on 2026-08-16, both times after a clean gate run. 'uvx nox -s gates' runs 'ruff format --check .' with success_codes=[0, 1] (noxfile.py:41), so format drift is ADVISORY there and the session still reports 'Session gates was successful'. The pre-commit hook runs 'ruff format' for real, rewrites the file, and aborts the commit. The documented merge gate therefore says green on a tree that cannot be committed, and the fix is to run 'uvx ruff format <files>' and commit again — cheap, but it costs a full gate cycle to discover, and the whole point of the gate is that passing it means you are done.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: noxfile.py is TEMPLATE-OWNED (sdlc-scaffold, .copier-answers.yml pins v1.27.1), and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a gate config is not hand-edited to pass — the fix goes upstream and comes back through 'copier update'. There is also no local knob: .copier-answers.yml has no format-enforcement answer.

THE UPSTREAM FIX, one line: drop success_codes=[0, 1] from the 'ruff format --check' call so it blocks, which is exactly the scaffold's own graduation rule (advisory until clean, enforced once clean). This repo IS clean — every gate run this session passed format on everything except the file being added — so it graduates today.

ALTERNATIVE if the scaffold wants format to stay advisory in CI: make pre-commit's format hook advisory too. Either is consistent; the current split is what is not.
notes: Same fix as knee-rqi4: upstream sdlc-scaffold dev 09f6bf8 drops success_codes=[0, 1] from the nox 'ruff format --check' call and '|| true' from CI, so the two runners stop disagreeing with pre-commit. Pending 'uvx copier update' here.

title: Prove the truncation axis end-to-end on real data (needs the card briefly)
description:
knee-35yc put truncation in the cache key and knee-zhqy (c6bc17f) made the smoke read and decode the truncated cache. Both are proven by unit + integration tests on synthetic series. What has NEVER run is the real thing: a 60-study decode out of D:/data raw, followed by a 1-epoch train arm reading it.

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of the axis is that an arm on a reading nothing has decoded gets smoked instead of dying on a memory map forty minutes into a queue slot. A synthetic 32px corpus does not exercise the DICOM walk, the plane table of the real split, or the memory-map shapes the trainer opens.

HOW: python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check --smoke --smoke-studies 60 against a real arm file. Expect under a minute of decode plus about two seconds an epoch. Card time is small; it just cannot run while the GPU is lent out.

ASSERT: the artifact written is <size>px_<n>sl_first60 and the FULL cache's mtime is unchanged (the 71.6 GB artifact is what the key exists to protect).
notes:
PROVEN 2026-08-16, AND WITHOUT THE CARD. arm_check --arms <one-arm-dir> --smoke <out> --smoke-studies 60 ran whole_stack end to end under CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= : the truncated cache 336px_12sl_first60 was decoded from REAL DICOM (SAG_FLUID_FS 59/60, COR_FLUID_FS 56/60, AX_FLUID_FS 60/60, SAG_FLUID_NOFS 33/60, COR_T1 36/60, SAG_T1 34/60, studies with no slot at all 0/60), the trainer mapped it, and one epoch completed: 'ok whole_stack'. So the decode path, the truncated-cache naming, the cache-to-trainer contract and the smoke's own plumbing are all proven on real data - which was this bead's whole ask.

TWO THINGS THE RUN ALSO MEASURED. It took about seven minutes of wall clock for decode plus one epoch of ONE arm, against ArmSmoke's 600 s per-arm timeout - so a single arm fits on CPU and the full 35-arm smoke does not. And it only ran at all after knee-0jb3: the first attempt died as 'BROKEN whole_stack: AssertionError: Invalid device id', because torch.cuda.is_available() is true here with zero visible cards.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN: nothing about the recipe's memory behaviour, which is the axis the smoke exists for and which only the card can answer.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rotation TTA on whole-stack members is noise (+0.001 mean)
description: member_curve --tta on the all_ours pool, three members measured before the run was killed to free the GPU: calibrated_targets 0.8493 -> 0.8498 (+0.0005), lora_r8_v3small_224 0.8215 -> 0.8236 (+0.0021), sliceattn 0.8473 -> 0.8482 (+0.0009). Mean ~+0.0012 against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil noise floor. MECHANISM: whole-stack members already see every slice at 336px canonical orientation; a small rotation resamples the same tissue rather than exposing a view the member lacked. This is the same class of result as knee-eeo (overlap TTA on whole-stack members: nothing). WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: TTA over a genuinely different FIELD OF VIEW (crop scale) rather than a different sampling of the same one.

title: The loss triple (logits, scores, weights) travels as three arguments through five sites
description: devtools.cohesion.data_clumps flags {logits, scores, weights} across kneemri/training/objective.py and kneemri/training/trainer.py, 5 supporting sites: Objective.__call__, Objective.cross_entropy, RankedObjective.__call__, RankedObjective.ranking, Trainer.loss (a pure pass-through), plus head_trial. They are one value - what the model said beside the weighted reading that judges it - and knee-mxj's ordinal objective will want to add a field to it rather than a fourth argument to five signatures. Give it a type in objective.py (the module that defines what a loss reads), drop the Trainer.loss pass-through, and let the existing objective unit tests plus tests/integration/argv_to_checkpoint.py prove the loss is unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: the label analyses reach up into inference and evaluation
description:
labels/ holds both the target vocabulary (targets.py, the base everything reads) and analysis entrypoints that consume finished predictions: ruler_check -> holdout_predictions/members/prediction_cache, ruler_transfer -> ensemble/oof_oracle, label_combine -> ensemble/scores, supervision_gap -> oof_oracle/scores.

So labels/ is two things at once: a base vocabulary and a set of top-of-stack studies. No contract can be written over it while both live there, which is why the layer contracts in e1edc9b are silent about labels.

Options to weigh (do NOT bucket by kind - that is what the principles forbid): move the analyses beside what they analyse (ruler_* and supervision_gap are evaluation studies of the labels, not label machinery), or accept labels/ as top-of-stack and move targets.py down to corpus/ since it reads the report table. The second is smaller and may be more honest: targets ARE part of the corpus.
close_reason: Done: the four studies (label_combine, ruler_check, ruler_transfer, supervision_gap) moved to evaluation/, labels/ now imports models alone, and a contract says so. The bead's second option — moving targets.py down to corpus — was rejected on inspection: targets imports kneemri.models.model for TARGETS, so it would have made corpus import models and broken the base-layer contract.

title: run_comparison --labels on the wrong CSV dies with a pandas KeyError, not a sentence
description: LabelPower.positives() indexes '<target>__verdict' straight out of the frame, so handing it the competition train.csv (the obvious guess for 'the label table') raises KeyError: 'ACL__verdict' from inside pandas after a nine-frame traceback. The user learns nothing about WHICH file is wanted. The right table is labels/report_labels_v2.csv. Same shape as the errors this module already distinguishes elsewhere (a missing metrics file vs an empty one): say which file was handed over and which columns it lacks.
close_reason: Closed

title: Slice padding clusters six copies of the deepest slice, which only attention pooling can feel
description:
RECORDED, NOT FIXED - the defect is documented in slot_reader._sample_indices' docstring and was never a bead, so nothing would surface it at the moment its trigger arrives.

WHAT IT IS: _sample_indices spreads linspace over the 0.20-0.80 band, DE-DUPLICATES, then pads by repeating the last index. For a series with fewer slices in the band than asked for, that gives [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,7,7,7,7] - six copies of the DEEPEST slice - where plain linspace would have given evenly spread duplicates [1,1,2,3,3,4,4,5,6,6,7,7].

WHO FEELS IT: max pooling is duplicate-invariant, so every member using it is unaffected, and the compute is identical either way. ATTENTION pooling is not: six copies of one slice take six shares of the softmax, so the deepest slice of a shallow series is weighted 6x. sliceattn_s2026 is a live member on that path.

HOW BIG: 8.3% of series hold fewer than twelve slices in the band (measured, 60 studies / 315 series). And 'linspace without the dedupe' was swept in the router work and came back BIT-IDENTICAL on the studies tested (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_their-router-not-ours.md), which is consistent with it - those series were deep enough for the dedupe never to fire.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED NOW: changing it changes the CACHE. That invalidates ~300 GB of decoded arrays and every member fitted on them, and no fingerprint would catch the difference because the pixels move without any shape or config changing. The right time is the next rebuild undertaken for another reason - which knee-c5n's SSL corpus would be.

TRIGGER: before any cache is rebuilt, decide this deliberately rather than inheriting it.

title: HoldoutSlab.arrays materialises the whole holdout (12.8-22.8 GB) for consumers that walk it in batches of 8
description:
AUDITED 2026-08-15, NOT IMPLEMENTED - recorded so the finding is not paid for twice.

kneemri/holdout_slab.py arrays() copies corpus.images[self.holdout] whole: 881 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices x 336^2 is about 12.8 GB, and 22.8 GB at 448 px. Its main consumer, HoldoutPredictions.predict, then walks that array in BATCH = 8 chunks; ruler_check.py:114 and attribution.py:343 do the same gather directly. Since knee-sf4k the corpus has corpus.window(batch, start, width), which serves exactly those chunks by explicit file read - so the slab could stream instead of materialise, at about half the wall-clock and a fraction of the resident memory.

WHY IT IS P3 AND WAS DECLINED ONCE: these are analysis CLIs, not the training loop. The win is roughly 14.5 s to 7 s on a read, which is below the project bar for spending a session on. Worth doing when someone is already in these files, not worth a trip of its own.
close_reason: Closed

title: slot_fallback is a config field with no implementation, written as a constant and read by nobody
description:
VERIFIED IN CODE 2026-08-13, re-filed out of knee-t92 so it does not close with that arm's refutation.

members.py:42 declares 'slot_fallback: bool' in the member rules; member_record.py:179 writes it as a hardcoded False; members.py reads it back into the dataclass. NO CODE ANYWHERE ROUTES A FALLBACK SERIES INTO AN EMPTY SLOT - the only other occurrences are test fixtures copying the same literal.

It documents the PUBLISHED members' rule rather than one of ours, which is a legitimate reason for the field to exist in a member record. The defect is that it reads as a behaviour flag: a future reader may set it True and expect routing.

IF A FALLBACK IS EVER BUILT, the semantic cost surfaced by the 2026-08-12 audit stands: the head learns 'slot k is this view', so substituting a different sequence into slot k makes that slot mean two things, and the presence mask stops distinguishing ABSENT from SUBSTITUTED - which is information the model currently has.

P3: it is inert today. The fix is either an implementation or a docstring saying it describes the published members and is not ours to set.
close_reason: Closed

title: Graft residual: the tie rule is fixed, and the rest needs sign structure at n=hundreds
description:
WHAT THIS WAS. Two independent measurements of one imperfection, both from the graft (knee-exd): our
pipeline reproduced the published members' own out-of-fold predictions only to max|diff| 0.025, and the
graft scored 0.888 public on the SAME 20 published members whose public forks sit near 0.899 — identical
weights, so ~0.011 is what our data layer costs.

WHAT IS SETTLED (2026-08-14, `interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_their-router-not-ours.md`):

  - THE TIE RULE WAS ONE CONTRIBUTOR AND IT IS FIXED. `tie=last` reproduces them far better than our
    `tie=first`: 0.0252/0.0061 vs 0.1277/0.0236 on 16 contested studies, replicated on 4 of 4 published
    members across 3 seeds. The confirming detail is that `corr(residual, series_count)` falls from
    +0.647 to -0.070 — the series-count signature WAS the tie-break and nothing else. It is a per-member
    reading axis (`Ensemble.reads`, `MemberPackage`), never a global switch, because our own members were
    fitted under first-maximal.
  - TEN OTHER AXES WERE SWEPT AND OURS WON EVERY ONE: antialias, three percentile variants, per-slice
    percentiles, the linspace dedupe, VOI LUT, crop rounding, overlapping windows, slice order. Our
    decode is already theirs on each. Cross-device float difference is ~5e-6, three orders too small.
  - The routing IS load-bearing (`tie_divergence.py`: 96% of contested slots hold genuinely different
    pictures) — that is a fact about the router, not about the graft gap.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is a smaller and better-posed question than the one this bead was opened with: on
40 unselected studies, 32 still disagree above 0.01 against the 1e-6 a faithful pipeline reaches. The
tie rule is worth about a third of the mean residual. The remainder is probably NOT one thing —
sub-pixel crop placement, uint8 quantisation and float accumulation order can each contribute a little,
and none is separately findable at n=40.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD MOVE IT: hundreds of studies rather than forty, and the residual's per-target
SIGN structure rather than its magnitude — sign separates a head/pooling difference from a pixel one,
which magnitude cannot. It is inference-only against frozen published weights: no training arm, no
submission. It is also NOT on the critical path any more — knee-k5kk measured that the grafted members
now COST score against an all-ours pool, so closing this residual buys fidelity to members we no longer
ship. Keep it as a diagnostic of OUR data layer, not as a graft repair.
notes: 2026-08-17 AUDIT: this description is STALE — both remaining steps are done and the hypothesis is REFUTED. `SlotTies.disagreeing_order` (one CSV read) shows the frame order of train_series.csv IS the sorted-UID order for all 4,407 studies, and `Study.from_directory` probes sorted(directory.iterdir()) whose names ARE those UIDs — same input order, both rules keep the first maximal by slice count, so the two pipelines choose the SAME series in every contested slot. The 1,100 rivalries are opportunity never taken. STEP 2 was also built and run (kneemri/evaluation/tie_divergence.py): 96% of contested slots hold genuinely different pictures, so the routing IS load-bearing and a future change to it would move real images — but that is a statement about the routing, not about the graft gap. The 0.011-0.025 residual must live in the other candidates: window policy, laterality, crop geometry, interpolation. Order lesson recorded in slot_ties.py: the 4,407-header census answered whether divergence was POSSIBLE, the one-CSV read answered whether it HAPPENS, and the second strictly dominates and was available on day one.

title: Attention-MIL degenerate attention is a named failure mode with published fixes
description:
ANSWERED by measurement 2026-08-11, and the answer is that the literature does NOT transfer.

The pre-registered test was: 'if withholding any single slot barely moves the number, the collapse is real AND harmless, and the literature does not apply.' Occlusion on base+ranking, 400 holdout studies:
  AX_FLUID_FS   +0.0193   <- the only slot outside the 0.006 noise floor
  COR_FLUID_FS  +0.0094
  SAG_T1        +0.0067
  SAG_FLUID_FS  +0.0056
  COR_T1        +0.0053
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS +0.0042
  spread 0.0151

READ IT HONESTLY, both ways. The collapse is REAL - axial carries 2-4x any other slot, matching the +0.127 attention/anatomy correlation measured earlier. But five of six slots cost less than the noise floor to remove, so the model is not catastrophically single-instance either; it is one dominant slot plus five marginal ones. Withholding the dominant slot costs 0.0193, which is larger than any single method change measured in this project - so the collapse is not FREE either.

WHY THE PATHOLOGY FIXES STILL DO NOT APPLY: ASMIL and AttriMIL treat bags of thousands of instances where attention collapse discards almost all evidence. We have SIX. A stabiliser that spreads attention over six slots is spreading it over slots that measurably carry less, which is not obviously an improvement - and the anatomical prior, which forced exactly that, already measured neutral (0.8073 vs 0.8081).

DOWNGRADING to P3 rather than closing: the papers are still unread, and the one thing that would change this reading is if a stabiliser helps for a reason other than anatomy-correctness. Not worth GPU while knee-am4 (border) and knee-ghd (depth) are open - both are larger effects on the same model.
close_reason: ANSWERED by measurement 2026-08-11: the literature does not transfer. Left in_progress for two days with no work; closing rather than carrying it.

title: Ordinal severity is the supervision that compounds with the ranking term
description:
OBSERVED in report_labels_v2: the labels are NOT binary. Verdict -> value: NO 0.08 (22,298 pairs), UNK 0.28 (14,445), YES 0.68 (6,461) / 0.82 (6,427) / 0.94 (3,241). Three graded levels already exist inside YES.

THE CONNECTION THAT MAKES THIS WORTH DOING: the pairwise ranking term is the ONLY component that consumes that gradation - its pair weight is relu(s_i - s_j), so a 0.94-vs-0.68 pair carries real signal. BCE mostly pulls both toward 'present', and our local evaluation binarises at MIDPOINT=0.5 and collapses the three levels entirely. Ranking is also the loss change that measured positive in 3/3 matched arms.

So finer severity is not just 'more supervision' - it compounds specifically with the mechanism that works, because the competition metric is a RANKING metric and severity is exactly a ranking signal. A model that knows a severe tear outranks a subtle one is being trained on the quantity being scored.

TWO SEPARATE UPGRADES, often conflated:
  (a) BETTER TEXT ENCODER for the auxiliary embedding target (knee-*, report supervision). Ours is sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 - a general paraphrase model, not medical. multilingual-e5-large or BGE-M3 are stronger multilingually; medical AND multilingual is rare, which matters across twelve languages.
  (b) BETTER READER producing ORDINAL targets - meniscal grade 1/2/3, mild/moderate/severe OA, partial vs full-thickness tear - rather than three certainty levels. This is the branch the label-FILTERING refutation explicitly did not kill: resolving a row is the opposite operation to striking it.

CHEAP FIRST TEST for (b) before any reader work: check whether the existing three YES levels carry ORDINAL information at all, by measuring whether studies labelled 0.94 are ranked above 0.68 studies by a trained model more often than chance. If the current levels are pure LLM certainty rather than severity, a reader upgrade has to supply real severity; if they already track severity, the gradation is a live signal we are only half-using.

NOTE the evaluation limit: our local ruler binarises at 0.5, so a finer target cannot be scored locally as ordinal - it can only be scored by whether it improves the binary AUC. That is the right test anyway, since the competition scores binary annotations.
design:
AUDIT (2026-08-16, targets.py + report_language.py, read not grepped):

WHAT EXISTS. The reader emits FIVE levels (0.08 / 0.28 / 0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94) and they are used as one number that is simultaneously the target VALUE and, through Supervision, the confidence WEIGHT. Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT already proved the levels carry real per-study information: agreement is monotone across a span of 0.58 (4.1% -> 95.8%) and the reader's __conf column is constant per verdict, so the gradation is not certainty noise. What it also proved is that four of five VALUES sit outside their own interval, all too high.

THE DEFECT THIS BRANCH FIXES. One scalar is carrying two different things. 'Small effusion, definitely present' and 'large effusion, possibly present' both land near the middle, and they are opposite studies: the first is a confident LOW grade, the second an uncertain HIGH one. The ranking term reads relu(s_i - s_j) off that scalar, so every pair between the two is either dropped or ordered backwards, and the confidence weight cannot separate them because it is derived from the same column.

THE DESIGN. Have the reader emit TWO fields per (study, label) instead of one: an ordinal GRADE (absent / mild / moderate / severe, from the report's own severity vocabulary — report_language.SEVERITY already holds the multilingual patterns) and a CERTAINTY (how sure the report is that the finding is there at all). Grade becomes the target value; certainty becomes the loss weight. That is exactly the split targets.py's own docstring argues for — 'confidence is a weight, not a value' — applied to a reader that currently cannot honour it because it emits one column.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS WITH knee-3oix. The pair weight relu(s_i - s_j) is the only consumer of gradation, and pair memory multiplies the number of graded pairs the term ever forms. A better-separated grade axis and more pairs drawn against it are the same mechanism from two ends.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT, before any training: re-run kneemri.evaluation.ordinal_signal on the NEW grades against the 58 image-read annotations. The current reader scored 12/12 above chance on the graded band. A split that is real must beat that on the same 58 studies and the same denominator — if separating grade from certainty does not raise it, the split is bookkeeping and the arm is not worth a slot. Fit calibration on the annotations, score on the fold-0 report holdout, as Supervision already does, so the ruler stays independent.

COST, stated: one LLM pass over 4,407 reports. Not started unattended — the gate above runs on the 58 annotated studies and can be checked on a small sample first.
notes: The rulebook half of this bead is now its own issue: knee-wfkk (P3), carrying the three undecided conventions the pilot found — normal-bone denial scope, unmentioned-finding = UNK not NO, and the osteochondral-lesion convention. Filed separately because none of them needs a reader, a re-read or a GPU.

title: bd dolt auto-push fails on every write: the git remote has no dolt refs
description:
Every bd write prints: 'dolt auto-push failed: push to origin/main: Error 1105 ... git ref not found: refs/dolt/remotes/origin/dolt/data/<uuid>'. beads runs in EMBEDDED mode here (no Dolt server), so 'bd dolt show' is unsupported and .beads is not a dolt repo directory.

IMPACT IS COSMETIC-BUT-NOISY, not data loss: .beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked and committed, which CLAUDE.md already names as the durable record ('the Dolt engine is gitignored'). Issues are safe. But the session-completion protocol calls 'bd dolt push', and that step can never succeed as configured.

TWO OPTIONS, NOT TAKEN because they change the owner's issue-tracker sync strategy:
  (a) disable the dolt auto-push and rely on the git-tracked jsonl, then drop 'bd dolt push' from the protocol;
  (b) initialise the dolt refs on the remote so the push has somewhere to land.

Owner's call - flagging rather than changing it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-13 with one line: bd config set dolt.auto-push false. The warning is gone from every write, and it had been firing on all of them - roughly thirty times today alone.

THIS BEAD CALLED IT THE OWNER'S CALL because it framed the choice as a sync STRATEGY. It is not: option (a) was 'rely on the git-tracked jsonl', and that is already how this repo works. CLAUDE.md states it plainly - '.beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked; the Dolt engine is gitignored' - so the jsonl is the durable record, it is committed on every push, and nothing was ever reaching a dolt remote to be lost. Verified after the change: issues.jsonl still updates on every write and still shows modified in git status.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SESSION-CLOSE PROTOCOL, which lists 'bd dolt push' as a mandatory step: that step could never succeed as configured and should not be in a checklist that says work is not complete without it. The git push of issues.jsonl is what actually persists the issues.

The config change itself is tracked - .beads/config.yaml shows modified - so it travels with the repo rather than being a local quirk that the next machine has to rediscover.
close_reason: dolt.auto-push disabled; the git-tracked issues.jsonl was always the durable record and still updates. Not a strategy decision - option (a) in this bead was already how the repo works.

title: archmap costs one extra commit+push cycle - by design, and the CRLF premise was wrong
description:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-11, after hitting this twice in ten minutes and actually reading the hook.

WHAT I ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: graph.json re-dirties after every commit with NO content diff, purely from archmap writing CRLF against an LF blob, leaving a permanently dirty tree.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING: .gitattributes already carries '* text=auto eol=lf', so the normalisation is handled - after a commit+push cycle 'git status' comes back CLEAN, verified twice today. The CRLF line in the output is git's normal normalisation notice, not a defect.

The friction that remains is REAL but INTENTIONAL. The archmap hook is pre-push, not pre-commit, and .pre-commit-config.yaml:151-155 states why: commits stay fast, the graph refreshes once before the push that deploys, and if it drifted the hook stages the regen and BLOCKS - 'commit it and push again (the diff stays your reviewable architecture-erosion signal; auto-committing in a hook can't join the in-flight push)'.

So a push that changed any module costs one extra commit+push. That is the price of the architecture-erosion record being a reviewable diff, and it is only paid when the architecture ACTUALLY changed - not every push.

DOWNGRADED P2 -> P3 and left open only as documentation. Do NOT 'fix' this by moving the hook to pre-commit or auto-committing in the hook: the first slows every commit for a signal needed once per push, and the second is what the comment explicitly rules out. Template-owned in any case - it would belong upstream in sdlc-scaffold, not here.

title: The three advisory cohesion engines are clean against this tree; their one concrete hit is pre-argued
description:
Swept 2026-08-20 with 'python -m devtools.run kneemri core --report cohesion.complexity,cohesion.lcom,cohesion.data_clumps'. Recorded so the sweep is not repeated and its findings not re-litigated.

DATA CLUMPS - 1 hit, and the code already answers it. 'batch, start, width' travel together across 5 sites in study_cache.py and window_reader.py. window_reader.py:37 argues the case explicitly: it is a slicing expression, not a noun the codebase says anything about - nothing stores one, nothing returns one, nothing decides from one; Prefetch already holds the schedule that produces them, and Window in inference.members is a different thing (a member's read plan). A value object would add a type to name an argument list, on the inner loop, and still be unpacked in the same two places. NOT CHANGED. The engine is right that the clump exists and wrong that it is a defect.

LCOM4 - 36 classes at >=2, and the great majority are false positives of the metric rather than findings. A class whose methods are one connected component plus one independent lazy property reads as LCOM4=2: Member has 23 methods in one component and {cache} alone; MemberRecord is {payload, read_size, recipe} plus {witness}. Filing 36 beads off this would be filing noise. The only entry whose shape is arguably real is TrainingOptions at LCOM4=5 ({band, crop, reading} / {routing} / {cache} / {supervision} / {sampled}), and even there the disjointness is what a builder of sub-config objects looks like by construction - the five components ARE the five sub-configs it hands out, which is the design rather than a violation of it.

COMPLEXITY - 839 functions, max radon CC 15 (corpus/diagnose_laterality.py:32 resolve_one), four at 13, the rest at or below 12. No gate violation: ruff C901 is the enforced engine at CC 10 and lint passes, radon and McCabe simply count differently. Nothing to fix, but resolve_one is the highest and it is correctness-critical corpus code, so it is the first place to look if laterality ever misreads.

CONCLUSION: no actionable finding. These three are worth re-running after a large refactor, not on a cadence.
close_reason: Sweep done and recorded in the description; no actionable finding, nothing to carry forward.

title: Resume-from-partial is NOT wanted: a half-resumed arm is not comparable to the arms it is ranked against
description:
Recorded so a later session does not build it after a killed run.

A run killed mid-recipe (driver reset, co-tenant OOM, reboot) loses its compute: Fitting.keep writes a .partial holding the best epoch's WEIGHTS, and a restart begins from the pretrained encoder at epoch 0. That looks like a missing feature. It is not one.

Correct resume needs optimiser moments, the OneCycleLR position, the EMA shadow and both RNG streams — none of which the payload carries, and AdamW state alone is 2x the parameters written on every improving epoch. Resuming from weights ALONE is a different recipe: it re-warms a schedule that had already annealed, so the arm's ledger row would name a recipe the arm did not run, and its number could not be compared with the arms it is ranked against. The experiment ledger is the thing being protected, not the wall-clock.

The real mitigation is upstream and is already built: DeviceBudget.await_headroom waits for the card rather than starting into a held one, and capped() now bounds the allocator by default (knee-lx8u). A killed arm gets rerun.

Revisit ONLY if arms grow past ~2h, where losing one run costs more than the ledger ambiguity — and then save the full optimiser+schedule+EMA+RNG state, never the weights alone.
close_reason: Recorded decision, no actionable residue. Closing keeps them searchable without sitting in ready.

title: TrainingOptions LCOM4 6 is a false positive — decided not to split
description: The cohesion explorer reports TrainingOptions at LCOM4 6 with clusters {adaptation, fitted_trainer, objective, reports}, {band, crop, reading}, {routing}, {supervision}, {sampled}, {fitted_model}. Read it before acting: the class is argparse's dest-name DTO, and every cluster is already a value object it COMPOSES (Routing, Crop, Band, Reading, Supervision, Adaptation) via a property, precisely because parse builds the dataclass straight from flat flags while everything downstream wants the pair. Low cohesion is the correct shape for a flags DTO whose job is to fan one flat namespace out to several policies; splitting it would put the fan-out somewhere with no name for it. Recording the decision so a later session does not re-derive it and churn. Revisit only if a cluster grows behaviour of its own rather than more flags.
close_reason: Recorded decision, no actionable residue. Closing keeps them searchable without sitting in ready.

title: Reader clump (batch, start, width) — decide once whether it becomes a request type
description: The last advisory data clump: (batch, start, width) travels through StudyCache.window, WindowReader.read, IndexedReader.read, HandleReader.read/_fill, prefetch.py — 5 sites. Bundling into a request value would silence the detector; against it: this is the training input hot path (a 174 MB batch read), the triple is not inseparable the way Predicted's was (batch = which studies, start/width = which slices, and callers loop start with width fixed), and Window (starts, width, size) already owns the slice-policy vocabulary at the serving side. Recorded so it is decided once rather than re-audited: leave as-is unless a fourth parameter (e.g. a stride or a slot subset) needs to join, at which point it becomes a request type together with the reason.
close_reason: Recorded decision, no actionable residue. Closing keeps them searchable without sitting in ready.

title: FileReader reopens the cache file per batch: measured, costs nothing, do not 'fix' it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 so it is not re-derived. FileReader._fill opens the cache with path.open per call - two opens per batch, about 580 per epoch - which looks like an obvious thing to hoist into a thread-local handle held for the reader's life.

Benchmarked on the real 448 px cache, 12-study batches, 25 steps, disjoint halves of the corpus per variant and the order swapped:

  width  3   open-per-batch 27.2 ms   held 26.0 ms
  width  3   (order swapped) 10.1 ms  held  9.4 ms
  width 12   open-per-batch 90.9 ms   held 93.2 ms
  width 12   (order swapped) 44.5 ms  held 43.5 ms

Under a millisecond either way at width 3, and held LOSES at width 12 in one of the two orders. Open is not on the cost curve; the read is. Keeping the per-call open, which is what makes the handles trivially thread-safe.

Closing immediately - the value here is the recorded negative, not the work.
close_reason: Closed

value: Kit rebuilt locally to 3ccf191 on 2026-08-18 (was 2 commits behind, missing the ensemble empty-subset fix 8811efa and the unfreeze-last fix 88ac72f). kit_check now reports 0 behind. NOT UPLOADED - the push is a manual, user-gated 'kaggle datasets version -p D:/data/.../kit -m <msg> --dir-mode zip'. Any submission before that upload runs the OLD code.

MEASURED 2026-08-15, CPU only, no bead: keeping a per-thread open file handle in FileReader buys NOTHING over reopening the cache per batch. On the real 448px cache, batch of 12, disjoint study pools and both orders run to cancel page-cache warming: width 3 -> open-per-batch 10.0/10.1 ms vs held 10.2/9.9 ms; width 12 (whole stack) -> 41.9/46.1 ms vs 42.6/46.7 ms. Within noise in every cell, and the held reader is SLOWER in half of them. The open() syscall is invisible next to ~43 MB of reads (~1 GB/s). Do not re-litigate handle lifetime as a training-throughput lever; the read path's cost is bytes, not handles. Bench: scratchpad/handle_bench.py.

Training-step perf audit 2026-08-17: the host-side per-step work is exhausted as a wall-clock lever. Measured on a 5090 at the whole-stack shape (batch 12, six slots, twelve slices, 448 px), against a ~1.15 s step: augment_bag totals 10.4 ms (to-float 1.7, _warp 3.5, _intensity 2.0, back-to-uint8 3.5) = 0.9%, and EMA update was 2.9 ms = 0.25%. Both fixed (afcbffb skips disabled intensity ops, 15.5 -> 2.0 ms; 261f728 makes EMA one _foreach_lerp_, 2.90 -> 0.23 ms). What is LEFT is 5.2 ms of uint8<->float round trip in augment_bag, which is a numerics AND fingerprint change for 0.45% and is not worth it. Together with the earlier reader finding (READERS=2, ~108 ms read against the step, ~10x slack), nothing outside the encoder forward/backward is worth more than ~1% now. The next real lever is the model or the precision, not the loop.
bd update --append-notes appends (newline-separated); --notes REPLACES the whole field. Use append for audit trails on a bead - the 2026-08-17 destroyed-notes incident was avoidable.

GPU memory on this Windows machine (measured 2026-08-13). PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True IS A NO-OP - torch prints 'expandable_segments not supported on this platform' at startup. Three arms carried it and none was ever helped by it. AND --vram-gb CAPS PYTORCH'S ALLOCATOR, NOT THE DEVICE: driver context and kernel workspaces sit on top, so a 30 GB cap on a 32.6 GB card leaves no headroom and Windows PAGES GPU MEMORY OVER PCIe instead of raising OOM. The run then crawls at 40 img/s against ~1000 while nvidia-smi reports 100% utilisation - 25x slower, 1.75 h/epoch. 26 GB is the cap that leaves the driver its room and every healthy arm uses it. A cap only converts thrashing into a clean OOM if it leaves headroom; set too high it PERMITS the thrashing it was meant to prevent. Diagnose by img/s, never by utilisation.

Checkpoint config has TWO guardable ends, both now mechanical: the writing end (member_record walks each option -> stamped field of same name, one-hot, count pinned at 21) and the reading end (tests/integration/checkpoint_config_to_readers.py AST-scrapes every config.get("key") in kneemri/ and demands a fresh payload stamps it - 20 reads across inference/members.py, models/model.py, evaluation/attribution.py, evaluation/encoder_drift.py). Both proven to bite by crossing a wire. The fingerprint cannot catch either defect: it is checked against the member's OWN reading, so a wrong-but-consistent rebuild passes.

Fold and seed ensembling are BANNED by the owner (2026-08-11). They buy variance reduction, not signal, and each member costs a full run on 80% of the corpus. The 5-fold layout was never a decision here - it was copied from the published manifest we replicated ('20 members, 5 folds x 4 seeds', commit ea726fb). Replace with: ONE model fitted on every study (--fold -1, which keeps the last epoch because there is no holdout to rank by), EMA for the variance the seed ensemble used to average away, TTA at inference. Arms measure on fold 0; only the final fit uses all data.

H2D hoist in fit_epoch buys NOTHING - the per-step supervision copies are free (2026-08-18). Hypothesis: corpus.mask / targets.scores / targets.weights are copied host->device per step from PAGEABLE memory, which is synchronous on the default stream. Mechanism CONFIRMED in isolation: a microbench behind 8 queued 4096x4096 mms measures 21.5 ms host-block for three pageable copies vs 0.03 ms pinned/device-resident. It does not matter. Real-loop A/B on a synthetic 96-study corpus (batch 12, 6 slots, 12 slices, 336 px, dinov2-small, bf16, best-of-5 epochs): eager 85.7-88.8 vs 85.0-85.8 (~1.4%); COMPILED, with the loop faithful line-for-line including the heartbeat, 68.18/66.96 vs 67.80/68.02 - NO delta at all. Host-block is not wasted GPU time when the card is saturated. FAULTY-TEST NOTE ON MYSELF: my first hoisted arm silently dropped heartbeat.tick and read 67.23 vs 70.40 (3-4.5%), which looked like it crossed the bar; the whole delta was the missing line plus scatter. An A/B arm must be faithful line-for-line, not just in the part under test. WHERE THE STEP ACTUALLY GOES, compiled: aten::mm 22.1%, addmm 21.1%, efficient_attention_backward 17.9%, forward 9.2% - over 70% is encoder arithmetic, and both aten::copy_ (7.3% eager) and upsample_bicubic2d (2.6% eager, HF position-encoding interpolation) drop OUT of the top-18 under torch.compile because inductor folds them. Confirms the 2026-08-17 audit: nothing outside the encoder forward/backward is worth more than ~1%. The next real lever is the MODEL or the PRECISION, not the loop - stop auditing fit_epoch.

Manifest fields recorded-vs-read (audited 2026-08-15, commit b002c87): every MemberConfig field now has a live consumer — img/slices/group/slots/crop_mm/centre/tie/band/pool/variant/whole_stack/encoder_layer/bf16/train_size/slot_pooling/slice_pooling/witness. The four ReadingRules fields (order/lat/slot_fallback/decode_fill) were deleted, not honoured, because no flag could produce a second value. When adding a manifest field, wire its consumer in the same commit: the record-by-constant, read-by-nobody shape has cost this repo four bugs.

SEEDS ARE BANNED, exactly as folds are (owner, 2026-08-12): 'seeds and folds - its the same thing, tried slightly differently'. This covers multi-seed runs, seed ensembling, seed-twin members in an ensemble, AND arms whose purpose is to measure what a seed buys - measuring a banned method still spends the loop on it. There is also a mechanism reason not to want them: the noise floor is the holdout's SAMPLING error (Hanley-McNeil predicts 0.0053, seed spread measured 0.0062, knee-2rx), so re-running the same recipe cannot move what the same 881 studies with the same 62 Fracture positives will report. Allowed instead: ONE run per recipe, EMA within a run, TTA at inference, and ensembling across DIFFERENT MECHANISMS (resolution, slice count, pooling, slot scheme) since every arm is fitted on the same fold-0 split and is directly averageable.

The measure/render split is justified by an APPARATUS, not by an LCOM number. Split a class into X + XReport only when the render is trapped behind something expensive to construct - a GPU, a corpus of DICOMs, a loaded checkpoint, the published predictions - so that the table cannot be exercised without building the thing that measures. Five classes earned it (Attribution, StackCoverage, SlotTies, TieDivergence, CropLaterality, ServeBench, OutOfFoldOracle). ReaderAgreement did NOT: its whole input is one DataFrame the test already builds by hand, so a split buys no testability. Its LCOM4 3 is three different questions sharing a table, and is accepted as-is, like TrainingOptions' LCOM4 5 (a config with disjoint accessor clusters is what a config is). cohesion.lcom is an advisory pointer, never the reason.

torch.compile must not be applied on a CPU device: dynamo's has_triton() probe indexes a CUDA worker-properties cache the CPU trace never filled and raises IndexError: list index out of range, so a compiled CPU forward DIES rather than running slow. Found 2026-08-17 when compilation became the default and eight argv_to_checkpoint integration tests plus test_compile_encoder failed at once. Fix: TrainingOptions.fitted_model takes the device and compiles only when device.type == 'cuda'.

2026-08-18: LB 0.924 (kneemri-rate), new best, prior 0.919. Clean single-member A/B: kneemri-chosen (res392+intensity392+calibrated+sliceattn) 0.918 vs kneemri-rate (same three + lr4e-5_ws_s2026) 0.924. The swapped-in member is the control recipe at encoder rate 4e-5 instead of 8e-6, +0.0068 solo on the fold-0 holdout. Solo holdout gain predicted the board gain (+0.006); the joint-subset search predicted +0.0013, five times too small. Membership priced by SOLO strength is the axis; the joint-subset ruler underprices it.

Host-side data loading is NOT a training wall-clock lever, measured 2026-08-16 on images_448px_12sl.npy (4407,6,12,448,448). FileReader whole-stack read of a batch of 12 = 165 MB: 1 thread 145.8 ms (1.11 GB/s), 2 threads 108.1 ms (1.49 GB/s), 4 threads 113.3 ms (1.43 GB/s). So READERS=2 is re-validated on the current drive, and 4 is still worse. Against a wholestack_s2026 step of ~1.15 s (336 s epoch, batch 12, ~292 steps) the 108 ms read is ~9% of a step, which Prefetch's single thread and one step of lookahead hide with ~10x margin. Do not spend time on more reader threads, a deeper prefetch queue, or a DataLoader rewrite - the step is GPU-bound and the host side already has an order of magnitude of slack. (The window_reader docstring's 2.27 GB/s at two threads was measured under different drive conditions; the ORDERING it justifies still holds, the absolute number does not reproduce today.)

Kaggle submission mechanics, learned by paying for each (2026-08-11). The competition slug is rsna-knee-abnormality-detection - a WRONG slug answers 403 from ListSubmissions, which reads like a permissions problem, not 404. A code submission needs an explicit -v <kernel version>; without it CreateCodeSubmission answers 403 rather than naming the missing field. Submitting while the kernel is still RUNNING answers 400 - the run must be COMPLETE. Kaggle allows only TWO concurrent GPU sessions, so a third kernel cannot even be pushed. ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json works; the KGAT bearer token in ~/.kaggle/access_token expired 2026-07-23 and returns marketing HTML instead of 401. Run dataset commands from INSIDE comp/ (-p comp/members mangles the temp path on Windows).

RUNAWAY-PROCESS RULE, earned twice in one night (2026-08-14/15). Any job expected to exceed a few minutes MUST run in the BACKGROUND with a hard `timeout` INSIDE the backgrounded command. Foreground is NOT safer: the harness caps a foreground command at 10 minutes and SIGTERMs the WRAPPER, while `uv run`'s python child survives on Windows (not in a killable process group) and keeps every allocation - one orphan held 15.86 GB and 9,519s of CPU. Verify survivors by CPU TIME, never by process age or a StartTime window: a 30-second-old process cannot hold 9,000 seconds of CPU, and that one comparison found both orphans instantly while a StartTime sweep reported zero.

SUBMISSION POLICY (updated 2026-08-13). Stop spending slots on 'maybe it is better'. Mechanics: 5 per day resetting 00:00 UTC, unused slots DO NOT roll over (saving cannot bank them - it only avoids waste), and only 2 Final Submissions count for judging, chosen deliberately at the deadline rather than by last-submitted. THE GATE: an entry must first be justified OFFLINE by kneemri.member_curve on the shared fold-0 holdout, which costs nothing. TWO DIFFERENT BARS, do not conflate them: 0.894 is the best entry we have ACTUALLY SCORED (23 fused - our 3 whole-stack plus the 20 published CC0 members) and is what a new entry must beat to be worth a slot; 0.888 is the best from OUR OWN weights alone and is the number to quote as ours, because the fused entry is mostly theirs (our three members bought +0.006 over their twenty). A candidate that beats 0.888 and loses to 0.894 spends a slot to move us backwards. Submit only when the offline number predicts a gain over 0.894, or when the question genuinely cannot be answered offline. Do not record a daily count in a standing note - it goes stale overnight and reads as current.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by band_span, the fourth corner. The span x density 2x2 IS additive on the mean: span +0.0039 at 12 slices and +0.0038 at 20, density +0.0014 at 0.20-0.80 and +0.0013 at 0.10-0.90, interaction ~0.0001, and the sum matches band_dense's observed +0.0053. The earlier non-additivity was inferred from the per-label signature and asserted of the mean, which three cells could not support. What is true is narrower and better: the SIGNATURE is not additive because the levers move different label populations - span buys REGIONAL (+0.0079 vs focal +0.0011: ACL, Contusion, Baker's, Effusion), density buys FOCAL (+0.0036 vs regional -0.0019: Synovitis, PF OA). All cells fold 0, 4e-5 whole-stack, all deltas under the 0.0062 floor, so directional.

The 'filtering looked like pruning' defect: a skip-list applied to rglob's RESULTS reads as a prune in review and prunes nothing — the walk has already descended by then. It hid in four places across the package and kernel scripts (knee-tg9, e0ae10a) after the kit finder had supposedly fixed it. Grep for 'rglob' plus a set-intersection on .parts to find the rest; the only real fix is os.walk with directories[:] mutation (kneemri/mounts.py).

kaggle CLI dataset upload fails from the Bash tool ('No such file or directory: ...\.kaggle/uploads\D_/...json' - it mangles the drive prefix into a temp path it never creates). Run kaggle dataset/kernel pushes from the PowerShell tool with native backslash paths; same command succeeds there.
